So, it's not just post-Brexit, it’s a wider thing then?

Right, that was a lovely dinner. Roast chicken really hits the spot, doesn't it? Though, honestly, I think I could probably eat a whole dessert buffet right now. Can we have chocolate cake? With extra strawberries! No! Chocolate! With sprinkles  and  chocolate buttons! Alright, alright. This is a serious decision. Clearly, we need a democratic vote. But first, let's talk about how much things  cost  in real life, compared to Monopoly. Do you think a real house costs more or less than Park Lane? Much,  much  more! Lots and lots more. You need  loads  of money! More than all the money in the box?

Right, this is officially the worst playlist ever. No offence, but this is… all a bit beige, innit? Like, where’s the energy? We're going to the Lakes, not a library. Beige? Seriously? I’ll try to keep an open mind. As long as there's a decent pub nearby. I need a proper pub meal after all this driving. Something with a huge Yorkshire pudding. There  is  a pub. The "Old Boot Inn".

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘im, decided the rose bushes needed a 'trim' with Mrs. Henderson’s garden shears. Nearly gave the poor woman a heart attack, he did. She was out there sunnin’ herself. You can’t stay cross for long. Innocent mischief is one way to put it. I had to spend a good hour untangling the shears from the rose stems. And calming Mrs. Henderson down. She wasn’t best pleased. Biscuits, anyone? Ginger nuts, your favourite, George? Always room for a ginger nut, Margaret. Thank you, love. So, what’s the gossip then, Albert? Anything happening down at the social club? Not much, thankfully. Old Man Hemmings is still on about his prize marrow. Says it’s a record-breaker. Honestly, it just looks like a slightly larger than average marrow to me. Hemmings and his marrows. It’s a yearly ritual. It gives him something to live for, doesn't it? Besides, it’s a good excuse for a bit of friendly competition. Friendly is a strong word when Hemmings is involved. He takes that marrow very seriously. I was talking to Derek, the postman, this morning. He reckons Hemmings has been measuring it every hour on the hour. That's Hemmings all over. Still, keeps him active, I suppose. Better than sitting around moaning about the price of everything. Things are going up and up, no matter what they say on the news. You're not wrong there, George. The cost of bread alone! I remember when a loaf was… well, you wouldn’t believe it now. It's a different world entirely. Remember when we could get a pint for… Now, now, Margaret, let’s not start on the price of a pint. That’ll just get us down. I was thinking, actually, about the garden. It needs a proper tidy up. Winter's done a right number on it. You fancy getting your hands dirty, Albert? Your back won’t like that. Remember last year?

…and honestly, the packaging is the thing I’m most stressed about now. It  needs  to look good, but sustainable packaging is…well, it’s expensive! And frankly, a lot of it looks…beige. Like I’m selling mud, not a luxurious face oil. Beige is the enemy, definitely. Luckily, I've been down that rabbit hole for the soaps. Remember how long it took to find those biodegradable stickers that didn't smudge? It’s a nightmare. What are you thinking? Glass? Plastic alternatives? I  want  glass. It feels more…premium? But the weight! The postage costs will be ridiculous. And the risk of breakage… I’ve been looking at these sugarcane-based plastics, but they don’t quite have the same feel. It’s just… everything has a compromise. Ooh, what about those aluminium tins? They’re recyclable, look quite nice, and aren’t too heavy. I saw someone using them for solid perfume on Etsy. Might be worth a look. They’d work well for a balm too, wouldn’t they? That’s a good shout, actually. I hadn’t thought of aluminium. I was so focused on bottles and jars. I need to make a spreadsheet, honestly. Dimensions, weight, cost per unit... I’m a language teacher, not a logistics expert! Though, teaching teenagers arguably prepares you for anything. True enough! You're essentially negotiating with tiny, hormonal diplomats all day. Speaking of spreadsheets, how are the pre-orders going? Have you had much of a response to the Instagram campaign? I know you were worried about reach. It’s…slow. Not disastrously slow, but slower than I’d hoped. I think the algorithm is working against me. I boosted one post, spent a tenner, and it barely made a dent. I think I need to look more at targeted ads, but I’m terrified of throwing money at it and getting nothing back. I get that. Facebook ads are a black hole. What about working with some micro-influencers? Those smaller beauty bloggers might be more affordable and reach a really engaged audience. I’ve had good luck sending free samples in exchange for a review for the soap business. That’s a brilliant idea! I hadn't really thought about that. Who do you use? Any recommendations? Someone who isn’t… overly filtered? I want authentic reviews, not just perfectly posed pictures. There's @glowingskinwithsoph on Instagram – she’s Birmingham based, actually, which is handy.

…and honestly, the price of butter, Derek! It’s outrageous. Utterly outrageous. Five pounds for a block? When I was a girl, you could get a whole pound of butter for… well, I can’t even  remember  how much, it was so little. It's just everything going up and up, isn't it? You’re telling me. I saw petrol at 155.9p a litre this morning. Fifteen-five-nine! It’s daylight robbery, plain and simple. They blame it on everything and nothing, don’t they? Ukraine, the weather, the phases of the moon probably. Exactly! It all feels like excuses. And the news… oh, don’t even get me started. All doom and gloom. I switch it off more often than not these days. It's just… wearing. I understand. I try to keep up with things for school, you know, so I can at least talk to them intelligently about current events. But even  I  find myself needing a break. The kids are so cynical now too, it’s hard to inspire any sort of optimism. Children are always more attuned to things, aren’t they? They see right through it. Though, you always did have a knack for reaching the difficult ones. Remember young Michael Davies? The one who refused to speak a word for an entire term? Oh, Michael. Yes, a challenging one. He just needed someone to listen, didn't he? I sat with him during lunch, just  sat , for weeks. Didn’t push, didn’t pry. Eventually, he started telling me about his dog. A little Jack Russell called Buster, if I recall. Buster! That’s right. And then he blossomed. You had a gift, Derek. A real gift. Such a shame you’re thinking of retiring so soon. They’ll be lost without you. It's not that simple, Maggie. It’s the paperwork, honestly. The constant hoops they make you jump through. Accountability this, data that… It’s taken all the joy out of it. I spend more time filling out forms than actually  teaching . And truthfully… my knees aren't what they used to be. That walk from the car park is becoming a mountaineering expedition. Oh, Derek. Your knees have been complaining for years. You should have had that operation. They said it might only give me a few years of relief, and the recovery is… extensive. I’m trying to weigh it all up.

Honestly, the central heating’s been a nightmare all week. It keeps deciding it’s summer, even when it’s freezing outside. I'm starting to think it's deliberately mocking me. Aye, tell me about it. Ours is doing the same. You'd think, in this day and age, a thermostat would just  work . I’ve been having to run the electric heater in the living room just to feel vaguely warm. Though, Brenda keeps saying I'm wasting money. Brenda always says that, doesn’t she? It’s her superpower. Mine’s currently attempting to wrestle the fairy lights onto the tree. A truly Herculean task, considering how tangled they are. Fairy lights always win. It's a fundamental law of the universe. Like entropy, or the inevitability of needing  another  screwdriver. Speaking of which, I spent the afternoon trying to fix Old Man Hemmings’ garden gate. He swore it was a simple hinge adjustment. Three hours later, and I’m pretty sure I’ve re-engineered the entire structure. Oh, re-engineering things… that sounds about right. I tried to put up the shelves in the spare room last weekend. Let’s just say it involved a lot of swearing and a slightly wonky result. I'm beginning to suspect I’m less a researcher and more a glorified shelf-installer gone wrong. It's the tools, isn't it? You need the right tool for the job, and half the time I end up using a butter knife or something. I’ve got a neighbour who’s got  everything . Honestly, his shed is like a hardware store. Keeps offering to help, but I feel bad asking. My dad’s the same. Always has the perfect tool, perfectly organised. Drives my mum mad. He’s already started talking about his retirement plan, which is apparently entirely centered around building a workshop bigger than our house. Retirement… That feels like a lifetime away. Though, I did have a rather alarming conversation with my Head of Department this week. Apparently, getting funding for my research is becoming…challenging. She casually mentioned ‘alternative career paths’. Oh, that's rough. Bureaucracy can be a killer. Sometimes I think being self-employed is easier, even with the feast-or-famine cycle. At least  I'm  the bureaucracy. Though trying to convince people a handcrafted wooden badger is a worthwhile Christmas present can be… a struggle.

Honestly, Mum, this roast is  amazing . You’ve really outdone yourself. Though… are these the ‘good’ knives? They feel a bit… flimsy? Flimsy? They’re perfectly fine, love. You’re used to your ridiculously oversized chef’s knife at home, aren’t you? This is perfectly normal cutlery. It’s not oversized! It’s… ergonomically designed. And I just feel like the blade’s bending a bit when I'm trying to get through the Yorkshire pudding. It's a national treasure, it deserves a proper knife! Oh, lass, don’t go on so! It’s just a knife. Yer father’s been using that set for donkey’s years. They’re perfectly good, and sturdy enough. Aye, your mother’s right. We’ve had that set since… well, since before you were born, Emily. Survived many a Sunday roast, they have. I know, I know. It’s just… I was helping Dad clear out the attic last week, and we found a whole box of Grandma’s silver. It’s beautiful. Why don't we use that for special occasions? Grandma’s silver? Isn’t that locked away somewhere? I thought Dad said it was too valuable to risk getting scratched. Valuable and sentimental, that silver is. Your Grandma adored that set. She used to polish it every week, religiously. Said it reminded her of her mother. Aye… your Nana… a proper woman, she was. Never let a speck of dust settle. Used to make the best crumble y’ ever tasted. Exactly! And wouldn’t it be lovely to… try and keep that tradition going? Dusting the silver, I mean, not necessarily the crumble. Though I’m rubbish at baking. It's… it’s a bit of a palaver, Emily. Polishing silver. Takes hours. And honestly, it's easier with younger eyes. My hands aren't what they used to be. He’s right. It’s lovely in theory, but it’s a lot of work. Plus, we've got Sophie and Ben coming next week. Do we really want to be worrying about polishing silver when we’re trying to entertain? I suppose not. It’s just… it feels a bit sad, letting it sit in a box. Remember when we were little and we used to try and sneak into the dining room and play with it? Dad always caught us. Oh, I remember! You two were little terrors!

Honestly, this day has been… one of  those  days. You know the kind? Everything feels like wading through treacle. Mmm-hmm. Like when you try to build a really tall Lego tower and it keeps falling down? Precisely. Though mine involved spreadsheets and passive-aggressive emails instead of Lego. Mrs. Henderson decided  today  was the day to rewrite the entire marketing budget proposal. Again. Why? Didn't she like it before? She liked it well enough. She just… had a  feeling . Apparently, a feeling that the font size was ‘disrespectful to the numbers.’ Honestly, I nearly choked on my coffee. Disrespectful to the numbers? That's silly! Numbers don't  have  feelings! You are absolutely right, darling. Utterly, completely silly. But try telling  her  that. It’s always best to just nod and smile and… rearrange the font size. It buys me time, at least. Anyway, enough about work. It's ruining my appetite. How was school? Did you have fun with Poppy today? It was okay. We did painting, but Leo kept getting paint in my hair. Miss Davies had to wash it out. Oh, Leo! That little rascal. I'm glad Miss Davies sorted it out, though. Nobody wants to go home with a rainbow-coloured head. Speaking of going home, are you getting excited about the skiing? Only… forty-something days to go now! REALLY?! Is that all? I’ve been counting! Will it be really, really cold? Colder than last Christmas? It will be cold, yes. But we’ll have all the proper gear – hats, gloves, scarves, the warmest coat you’ve ever seen. And we’ll be whizzing down mountains so fast, you won’t even notice the cold! Will I be able to do the black run this time? Daddy said maybe if I practiced more on the nursery slopes. That’s the plan. We’ll start slowly, with the greens and blues, build up your confidence. And maybe, just maybe, if you're a super-star skier, we can attempt a little bit of the black run towards the end of the week. But no promises! Safety first. Okay. But I  am  a super-star skier! I didn't fall over  once  on the little slope at Milton Keynes Snowdome! Didn’t you? I seem to recall a rather spectacular tumble involving a snow angel impression… That was  intentional ! I was practicing! Of course you were.

Honestly, Food Tech is  ruining  my life. Mrs. Davies is obsessed with pastry. Pastry! Who even  likes  pastry that much? You say that, but you demolished that apple crumble last week. Don't lie. That was… strategic. I needed energy for the History essay. It was a fuel source, not enjoyment. And anyway, this week it’s choux pastry.  Choux  pastry! It’s just… air and disappointment. I’m pretty sure mine looked like deflated footballs. Mine resembled slightly squashed slugs, so you're not alone. At least it wasn't éclairs, those are actively evil. Remember Bethany's attempt last year? It ended in a kitchen covered in cream. Oh god,  yes!  Mrs. Davies was not impressed. She still brings it up as an example of ‘what  not  to do.’ Anyway, it's just… everything's building up, innit? Food Tech, Maths homework, Mr. Harrison breathing down my neck about my English analysis… Tell me about it. He’s convinced we’re all secretly planning to misunderstand  Romeo and Juliet . Like we  want  to get bad grades. Speaking of Maths, have you even started the trigonometry questions? I’m completely lost. Don’t even. I stared at the first one for twenty minutes and it just… blurred. I think I need a YouTube tutorial. Or maybe just to pretend I've got a really bad headache. Headaches work sometimes. Although Mum always sees right through them. She's got a sixth sense for homework avoidance. Are you thinking about what you want to do after GCSEs though? It's looming closer, isn't it? Ugh, don’t remind me. Everyone's talking about A-Levels, or apprenticeships, or… I don't know. I was thinking maybe Spanish? Spanish? Really? That's… unexpected. I thought you were more of a French person. I  was . But then, I was talking to Lizzie’s cousin, she's doing her year abroad in Seville, and she said it’s amazing. And the culture… and the food! Apparently, the tapas are incredible. Plus, I reckon it’d be useful. Loads of companies want people who can speak Spanish, don’t they? Yeah, that’s true. It's definitely a good skill to have. I'm leaning towards Psychology, I think. It just… makes sense? Trying to figure people out, that sort of thing. Though A-Level Psychology sounds  intense . It does. My older cousin did it.

…and honestly, darling, the  audacity  of it all! Leaving poor old Doris standing there, all ready with the Victoria sponge. Honestly, people have no manners these days. But never mind that now. You said you went to the cinema last week? What did you see? Oh, yeah! I went to see ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once’. It was… a lot. ‘Everything Everywhere All At Once’? Sounds dreadful. Is it one of those… superhero things? All boom and bang, with not a plot in sight? Not really. It's got action, yeah, but it's mostly… existential. About a Chinese-American woman doing her taxes and then discovering she has to connect with versions of herself in alternate universes to prevent a great evil. Good heavens. Sounds utterly bonkers. Like something from that Doctor Who programme, isn't it? All time travel and saving the world. Although, even  that  made more sense, sometimes. It's definitely bonkers, but brilliantly so. Michelle Yeoh is incredible in it. Honestly, she’s just phenomenal. It’s funny, sad, and visually stunning all at the same time. Michelle Yeoh… the one who was in that James Bond film, wasn’t she? With Pierce Brosnan? That's the one! She's a proper action star, but this is a completely different role for her. It's really showing off her range as an actress. It's not just about the fighting, it’s about… well, about regret, and family, and finding meaning in chaos. Meaning in chaos. Sounds exhausting. I prefer something a bit… simpler. You know, a good old-fashioned romance. Something with Colin Firth, perhaps. Or maybe that Tom Hanks does so well. A nice happy ending. None of this universe-jumping business. Gives me a headache just thinking about it. I get that. Sometimes you just want comfort viewing. But this actually did have a surprisingly heartwarming core. It’s about a mother and daughter relationship, and how they struggle to understand each other. It reminded me a bit of… well, of us, actually. Oh, don't you start on that now. You and me have always understood each other perfectly well. Despite your…modern tastes in films. Though I must say, you always had a peculiar taste. Remember when you insisted on making me watch that black and white one, with the French chap and the accordion? Oh god,  Breathless ? Don’t remind me.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic was  horrendous  getting here. Took me nearly an hour and a half from Hitchin. I swear, the M1 is just one giant car park these days. Oh, you Southerners and your motorways! It’s never a quiet ride, is it? You should try navigating the A38 round here during rush hour. That’s a proper white-knuckle experience. At least you had a nice drive  to  the motorway, all those pretty countryside bits. Pretty countryside obscured by a constant stream of lorries blasting fumes, maybe. It’s stressing me out just thinking about the drive back. I was considering the train, but then all the disruptions… it feels like a gamble either way. Aye, the trains aren't much better. They’re always ‘engineering works’ or ‘signalling failures’. Typical. Still, better than risking life and limb on the roads. So, how was the school week? Any particularly… vibrant students this week? Vibrant is one word for it. Year 10 are gearing up for their GCSEs, so the drama is dialed up to eleven. Trying to explain the subjunctive mood to teenagers who are more concerned with TikTok trends is… challenging. The subjunctive mood, eh? Sounds important. I always preferred a good, straightforward ‘yes’ or ‘no’ in court, myself. No room for interpretation. Though even  that's  getting harder these days, with everyone wanting to argue the toss. I can imagine! You must see everything, being a court usher. Does it ever… get to you? Hearing all those stories? Oh, love, it does. It really does. You build a bit of a shell, you know? You have to. But some cases stick with you. Especially the ones involving children. It's awful. Still, it’s a job, isn’t it? Pays the bills. Speaking of bills… did you manage to sort out that leaky gutter? You mentioned it last time. I did, eventually. Cost a fortune! Honestly, I think the handyman just charged me extra because I’m a woman and look like I don’t know anything about roofs. It’s so infuriating. It is! They always try it on. You need to get a few quotes, next time. Don’t be afraid to haggle. Your Grandad always said, “Never pay full price for anything, Elsie.” He was a shrewd one, your Grandad. I wish I’d inherited his shrewdness! I’m terrible at that sort of thing.

Honestly, the air smells…different today. Less exhaust, maybe? Or is it just me being overly sensitive after a day of grading endless essays on post-structuralism? You’re not imagining it. They've been doing some work on the main road, diverting traffic. More noticeable when you're used to the constant hum, I suppose. And yes, post-structuralism  will  do that to a person. Anything particularly dreadful amongst the student submissions? Oh, the usual. Several who clearly think Derrida is a brand of coffee. One who attempted to apply Foucault to…TikTok dances. It was…ambitious. How was your afternoon? Did Professor Zhang actually manage to understand the nuances of our proposed collaborative project? Understand is a strong word. He  acknowledged  them. Mostly by nodding politely while periodically checking his phone. I think the concept of a jointly-run module on British Romantic poetry, entirely delivered in English to Chinese students, is still a bit of a leap for him. He’s worried about engagement, I think. Rightly so. It's a big ask. We need to really sell the benefits – the immersive language experience, the direct access to ‘authentic’ cultural understanding… that sort of thing. Maybe bring in some examples of successful Anglo-Chinese academic collaborations? I'll do some digging tomorrow. Good plan. I've got the initial syllabus drafted, at least. Wordsworth and Coleridge, obviously. A bit of Keats, maybe Shelley if we're feeling brave. The trick will be avoiding analysis that’s  too  steeped in Western critical theory. I don't want to completely lose my head in explaining things they simply won't get. Exactly. It needs to be accessible. Speaking of accessible, are you remembering to pick up milk on the way? I completely forgot to ask you this morning and we're down to the dregs. Milk. Always milk. Yes, I put it on the list. Along with… …soy sauce. We’re out of soy sauce. Apparently, my attempt at stir-fry last week was deemed “acceptable but lacking…oomph”. Those were your exact words, I believe. They were. It needed oomph. You were too hesitant with the seasoning. It's practically a crime against culinary art. Honestly, it's like you’re afraid of flavour. I am not afraid of flavour! I'm…respectful of flavour. It’s powerful stuff! Anyway, anything else on the shopping list? Did you want more of those biscuits you’ve been obsessed with?

Right, so, Operation Babysitting is a go for Saturday then? I've checked with Mrs. Henderson, and she’s happy to pop round around six. That gives me just enough time to… attempt this Victoria sponge before heading to The Crown. But  six ? That’s ages away! Will Mrs. Henderson read us a story? A really long one? Yeah! And can we have biscuits  with  the story? Not just after. We'll see about biscuits  with  the story, you two. Mrs. Henderson always does a brilliant story, doesn’t she? And yes, a long one. Perhaps about a dragon? She did a very good dragon last time. Now, are you two finished scavenging? I need the counter space. I’m checking for sprinkles! For the cake! It needs sprinkles. All the cakes need sprinkles. Sprinkles are a very good idea, Lily. Remind me again, how many friends are coming over on Saturday? I completely lost count when Sarah started listing everyone from her book club. Loads! More than when we had a party for my birthday! And are we having pizza? More than your birthday party… that’s a lot of people! Yes, pizza is definitely on the menu. Though I was thinking of making some of those little sausage rolls too. Remember how much everyone loved them at the school fair? Sausage rolls are good. But can we help make them? I’m  very  good at putting the sausage in the pastry. You are indeed a sausage roll specialist, Lily. And you, Sam, you're good at... supervising! Making sure the sausage rolls don't escape. I’m a sausage roll guard! I can wear my pirate hat. Excellent. A sausage roll guard wearing a pirate hat. It’s a look. Right, while I tackle this cake… Anyone noticed how long your hair is getting? It's practically down to your shoulders, Sam. It is! You need a haircut, Sam! You look like a lion! I  like  my lion hair. It's lovely, darling, but maybe just a trim? Your mum mentioned booking you in with Mr. Davies next week. He’s very good with little boys' hair. Remember how he made that cool design when we had a summer cut? Oh yeah! The one with the swirly bits! Can he do swirly bits again? We’ll have to ask! And speaking of looking good… I’ve been thinking about that photoshoot for the school newsletter.

Honestly, this canteen food is criminal. Criminal, I tell you! Like, who decides these combinations? Pasta  and  chips? It's a culinary betrayal. You’re dramatic, Liv. It's a Tuesday. Lower your expectations. Besides, I’m trying to be vaguely healthy. Mum would have my hide if she knew I was living on chips and pasta. She's already judging my life choices from three hundred miles away. Oh, I’m sure your Mum’s judging everyone’s life choices. She's a force of nature, isn't she? No offence. Still, look at that pasta. Is that… broccoli  and  sweetcorn? Together? Someone needs to be fired. No offence taken! She just… cares. And yeah, the canteen's a bit of a wild west. But it’s cheap, innit? Which, let's be real, is all that matters when you’re a broke student. Speaking of broke… are you still on for that thing Friday? The student night at Pryzm? Pryzm? Oh god, yes! Desperately. I need a night where I don’t think about Shakespeare and quadratic equations. Though, knowing my luck, I’ll probably end up debating the merits of iambic pentameter with someone. You  would . Honestly, you’re the only person I know who can make a night out sound like a revision session. It's a skill! Keeps things interesting. What are you wearing? I’m thinking black. Always a safe bet. Maybe with… some glitter? Ooh, glitter's good. I was thinking something vaguely sparkly? It’s been ages since I’ve actually made an effort. Uni life is basically leggings and oversized hoodies at this point. Mum would  definitely  judge that. Tell me about it. My Nan keeps asking me if I'm eating properly. She sends care packages filled with biscuits and digestive aids. Bless her. It's… a lot. That’s sweet, though. My Lola does the same, but hers are mostly dried mango and weirdly specific herbal remedies. Last time she sent me a whole bag of something that was supposed to ‘clear the complexion’. It smelled like old socks. Oh my god! No way! That’s amazing. You need to document that. Imagine the Instagram caption: "Lola’s complexion clearing remedy – smells like regret." I did take a picture! It's buried somewhere on my phone. Honestly, it was the colour of mud. She swore it worked wonders. I think I just politely thanked her and hid it under my bed.

…and honestly, the seagulls were  mental . Proper dive-bombing you for your chips, like. I've never seen anything like it. Blackpool's bad, but Skegness is on another level. Skegness, eh? Living the high life, Liv. Though I can picture it. Coastal towns and aggressive gulls go hand-in-hand. Much better than my 'holiday' which consisted of helping my dad fix the roof. Again. Sounds…productive, Ben. I spent my week attempting to become one with a yoga mat. Not entirely successfully. Sustained a minor hamstring injury trying to do a headstand. Oh, you daft lad! You and your fancy yoga. Me mam would say you just need a good bit of gardening to sort you out. Gets you grounded, she says. Your mam's a wise woman, Liv. Literally. Gardening is good. Though I suspect my attempts at gardening would result in something resembling a post-apocalyptic wasteland. Speaking of grounding, have you seen that new nature documentary on BBC Earth? "Untamed Lands”? It’s brilliant. Oh aye, I caught a bit of it. The bit with the snow leopards? Proper beautiful. Though I’m still hooked on "Taskmaster". Greg Davies is a national treasure. Honestly, I've snorted my tea more times watching that show than I care to admit. "Taskmaster" is addictive. It's the perfect antidote to, well, everything. Especially stressful engineering projects. Did you see the one where they had to move digestive biscuits across the room using only their feet? Oh god, Alex Horne’s face! Pure despair. It's brilliant how they take genuinely absurd challenges and make them so compelling. Much better than most of the stuff on Netflix, honestly. Although, I did get sucked into that Korean survival game show… "Squid Game". Bit intense. "Squid Game" was…something. A bit much for my liking, though. I prefer something I can switch my brain off to. Like, I'm currently re-watching "Great British Bake Off". Comfort viewing. Plus, I get ideas for baking. My attempt at a Victoria Sponge last week was… passable. Passable is good! Baking is a skill. I once tried to make macarons. It was a disaster. They looked like tiny, multicoloured hockey pucks. You tried macarons? That’s ambitious. Mine usually end up cracked and resembling something vaguely resembling a cloud. We should have a bake-off. Liv, you bring the passable Victoria sponge, I'll attempt something equally disastrous, and Tom... well, Tom can judge, since he's clearly the domestic god.

…and honestly, Doreen, that telly picture just ain’t what it used to be. All fuzzy ‘round the edges, even when young Mark came and fiddled with it. Says it's the aerial, but I reckon it’s just getting old, like the rest of us. Oh, Arthur, you  always  say that. You said the same about the one before. Mark knows what he’s doing, he’s good with those things. It’s just you don’t want to admit you can’t see as well as you used to. Now, now, Doreen. No need to be sharp. Just stating a fact. Speaking of Mark, he’s still on about that trip to London, isn't he? Wants to take the little ones. Aye, he mentioned it. Says he’s found a hotel deal. Trying to avoid the school holidays, apparently. It’ll be a nightmare getting around, though. London’s…well, London. Nightmare’s a good word for it. Remember when we took young Emily to see the horses at the Royal Windsor Horse Show? Cost a fortune just to park, and then we were squashed in like sardines. Lovely horses, mind. Real beauties. Used to go to the races at Yarmouth, back in the day. Proper fun. Arthur and his horses. You'd think we lived on a farm! Though, you were quite the fan, weren’t you? Always had a little flutter. A little flutter keeps life interesting, Doreen. Anyway, London. I don’t know if it’s worth the hassle. And the cost! It’s not like it used to be. Everything’s gone up. He's trying to be sensible, your son. He’s looked at a youth hostel in Cornwall as a cheaper option for next year, instead of a proper holiday. He says the kids wouldn’t mind. A youth hostel? Oh, my. That sounds…rustic. I remember one we stayed in, back in the fifties, in the Lake District. It was drafty and the breakfast was awful. Still, it was adventure, I suppose. Adventure? More like misery! No, give me a proper hotel any day. This selling houses business, it’s all getting to me. Every other advert on the telly is about selling your home. Happens even on the football! It's the market, isn't it? People downsizing, or needing the money. It's a reflection of things, I suppose. I've got a couple of parents who are thinking of moving closer to their children, which is nice.

Honestly, Leo was  incredibly  fussy this morning. Like, full-on screaming the house down for a good hour. It’s exhausting. Oh, tell me about it. Elsie was like that yesterday. I thought I’d never get her to settle. It’s just… relentless, isn’t it? Especially when you’ve tried everything. Bottle, boob, rocking, singing, walking… you name it. Everything! I actually tried that white noise app again. Remember that? We were convinced it was going to be a miracle cure. Oh god, yes. The rainforest sounds. Elsie just stared at me like I was mental. Though, to be fair, she looks at me like I’m mental most of the time these days. It's the sleep deprivation, I swear. It’s definitely the sleep deprivation. I feel like I’m walking through treacle. How  are  you coping? You look… remarkably composed, considering. Composed is a strong word. It’s just… I’ve sort of accepted I’ll never have a full eight hours again. And Mum’s been a lifesaver, honestly. She's here most afternoons, just letting me have a proper shower, or a chance to drink a hot cup of tea. Mum's amazing. She really is. I wish she lived closer, I could really use a Mum-afternoon right now. Dad just… doesn’t  get  it. He keeps saying things like “Just let him cry it out.” Honestly! Oh, men. They're all the same. My dad tried that with Elsie. He genuinely couldn’t understand why I wasn't happy with that solution. “It worked for you, didn’t it?” he said. As if it’s a one-size-fits-all solution. Exactly! It's like, they weren't the ones spending three hours trying to get a tiny human to latch properly! Speaking of which… how’s breastfeeding going? You were a bit worried at the start, weren’t you? It’s… better. It was really rough for the first few weeks. Cracked nipples, Elsie refusing to latch, me just crying into my muslin cloths. It was awful. I almost gave up and switched to formula, but I talked to the lactation consultant and she was brilliant. Showed me different holds, and how to get a better latch. That’s good. I tried to breastfeed Leo for a bit, but it was a disaster. He just wouldn’t take it. He preferred the bottle, which is… fine, I suppose.

Honestly, did you  see  what happened with that council vote last night? They’re going ahead with the new bypass, right through Farmer Giles’ land. It’s appalling. He’s been there for generations, you know. Mmm, saw something about it. Another classic case of progress over people, isn’t it? Though, to be fair, that A21 is a nightmare. Something  has  to be done about the traffic. It's on Twitter, everyone’s having a go. Loads of people are organising a protest. Apparently, Giles is pretty resigned to it though? Said he's too old to fight it anymore. Poor man. That's just... heartbreaking. Makes you wonder what all the point is, building all these things if it just makes everyone miserable. Exactly! And the disruption it’ll cause. Remember when they did the roadworks by Mum’s? She couldn’t get to the shops for weeks. It's always the little people who suffer. Oh, and speaking of suffering, who’s taking Winston this morning? He’s been giving me the ‘I need to go’ look for the last half hour. I can do it. I need a bit of fresh air anyway. Promised myself I'd get out and deadhead those roses before it gets too warm. They're looking absolutely dreadful, you know. Covered in aphids. Oh, good. You and Winston are a good team. I've got a deadline looming for that website copy – that new garden centre out near Challock. They want it all by lunchtime. Honestly, garden centres! It's all 'rustic charm' and 'seasonal delights’… it’s exhausting. Sounds like you, darling. Always turning something simple into a literary masterpiece. Now, did anyone remember to put the bins out? Recycling is today. I did! Before I started prepping breakfast. Though, I swear, the bin men are getting cheekier. They didn't even bother putting the bins back properly last week. Just left them sprawled all over the pavement. Typical. No respect these days. It’s that generation… I tell you. Though, maybe they're just rushing, trying to get everything done. Speaking of rushing, you two heading to Sarah's on Saturday? Her fortieth is fast approaching. Yes, booked a taxi. It’s going to be mayhem, isn’t it? Sarah always throws a good party. I’m still trying to decide what to wear. Everything feels a bit… wrong, after being in scrubs all week.

…and honestly, Miss Davies just  loves  to make the maths tests ridiculously hard. Like, it’s not about understanding the concept anymore, it’s about spotting the trick she’s hidden in the wording. Did you have that problem with question three? The one about the…the converging series? Ugh,  question three . Don't even get me started! I spent ages on that. I think I ended up just writing down everything I vaguely remembered about series, hoping something would stick. It looked like a mess, probably. Did you manage to… you know, actually  do  it? Sort of. I remembered something Mr. Harrison said about a similar example last term, but I had to really wrestle with it. He's much better at explaining things, less…determined to make us feel inadequate, you know? He actually wants us to  get  it. Totally! Miss Davies is brilliant at maths, don't get me wrong, but sometimes I think she forgets what it’s like to be learning it for the first time. It’s like she's speaking a different language. Speaking of different languages, Gran was showing me her stamp collection again yesterday. Honestly, it's massive. She's got stamps from everywhere! Oh wow! Gran’s stamp collection is legendary. Remember when she showed us the one from… was it Bhutan? The one that actually smelled of flowers? Yes! That was amazing. She said it was because they used natural dyes in the ink. She knows  everything  about stamps. It’s kinda cool, actually. She was telling me about the science behind creating the adhesives, and the different paper types they use to prevent fading… It made me think, that’s actually really interesting science. That  is  cool. It’s funny how you can find science everywhere, isn’t it? Even in stamps. I'm supposed to be doing a project on plant adaptations for biology, and I'm stuck. I was thinking of doing something on carnivorous plants, but it feels… overdone? Carnivorous plants are cool, though! But you're right, everyone always does Venus flytraps. What about something on how plants adapt to the cold? Like, the way some trees in Canada can survive freezing temperatures. Hmm, that’s a good idea. I saw some amazing pictures of frost-covered trees in Canada when Auntie Helen went last year. We have to focus on local plants too, though, don't we?

…and then young Timmy, bless 'im, he just  screamed  the place down. Absolutely howled. Didn’t like Reginald one bit. Reginald ‘ere, see? Oh, Arthur, you and your puppets. Honestly. Timmy's a sensible lad, probably just didn't understand. It  is  a rather…lifelike rat, isn’t it? Lifelike! It’s artistry, Mavis! Pure artistry. I made ‘im meself, you know. Found the felt at a car boot sale in Attleborough. A right bargain, it were. Three bob a sheet. Used to be a proper knack to these things, puppet-makin’. Not like now, with everything bought in a shop. Afternoon all. What horrors is Reginald inflicting on the neighbourhood today? Horrors? Reginald’s a sweetheart, Peter! Mavis is bein’ difficult. Says he frightens the children. Well, Arthur, a rat puppet  does  have a certain…impact. Though I expect it’s the artistry Mavis objects to, not the rat itself. Don’t wind me up, Peter. I appreciate the effort, Arthur, truly. It just doesn’t scream ‘cuddle buddy,’ does it? Speaking of things needing a bit of adjustment, are you still meaning to get your eyes tested, Arthur? You were squinting at the telly last night. Oh, that. Well, I was watchin’ that programme about handbell ringing. The patterns they make, you see, they’re quite small on the screen. And fiddly. Proper fiddly. I was tryin' to follow along, y’know, see how they hold the bells. Handbell ringing? That’s a new one, Arthur. I thought your hobbies extended to slightly unsettling puppets and…well, mostly resting. Restin’ gets boring, Peter! And handbell ringing… it looked peaceful. And clever. They were up at that church in Bury St Edmunds, apparently. Got quite a good reputation, that team. I was thinkin’, maybe, just maybe, I could give it a go. Honestly, Arthur. You on a handbell team? It'd be a sight. Though, it would get you out of the house. And stop you making more…friends. Now, Reginald's a good listener! Anyway, I don’t think I’d be very good at it. You need a bit of…dexterity, don’t you? And I'm not as nimble as I used to be. Keeps tellin' me, this body does. You’d manage. You’re surprisingly coordinated for someone who spends most of their days animating rodents. Still, the eye test is a good idea. I can drive you, if you like.

…and then Professor Davies just kept going on about post-structuralism! Honestly, I think he enjoys hearing himself talk more than actually  teaching  us anything. Right, another latte then? This one’s gone down a treat. Sounds about right. Davies was always a bit of a windbag, even when  we  were students, all those years ago. Still, good to have a cuppa in here, eh? Feels…normal. It’s been ages since we just sat and properly chatted. It really has. Uni's been hectic. But needed this. It's nice to just  be  in Bolton. Especially in a proper café, not one of those chain places. Remember when this used to be, like, the only decent café in town? Venice? Oh, aye. Before all the coffee shops started popping up like mushrooms. This place was  the  place to be seen. Your Grandad used to bring me here for a waltzer and a slice of Victoria sponge after our shifts at the hospital. He loved a good waltzer, your Grandad. Oh god, I can picture him! A waltzer and sponge cake, classic. It’s mad to think how much has changed. Do you remember when there weren’t even traffic lights on Deakins Lane? Don’t I just! You'd have to practically sprint across. And the market…it was completely different. More…proper, you know? All local stalls, proper butchers, fishmongers. Not everything pre-packaged and imported. It feels a bit soulless now, doesn't it? Though, that Italian deli they’ve got is decent. Maybe we should grab something from there later? I’m starving after that lecture. Good shout. They do a lovely prosciutto and rocket sandwich. Though, it's not quite the same as the stuff my mum used to make. She’d bring back bits and bobs from when she visited Italy with your Grandad. Said she learned all the secrets to making proper pasta sauce from a little nonna in Naples. She was a legend, your mum. Always making something delicious. Speaking of Italy…we’re actually doing a module on Venetian history next semester. It’s supposed to be really good. All about the trade routes and the Doge’s Palace. Oh, Venice itself? That’s fascinating. It's a city built on water, isn't it? Must have taken some doing. I always wanted to go, but…life just kept getting in the way.

…and honestly, the leg press felt impossible yesterday. Like, genuinely questioning all my life choices during set three. Did you see Mark trying to spot me? He looked terrified I was going to pancake him. Oh, Mark. He’s all bravado until someone actually needs saving. I saw him trying to look busy over by the dumbbells. Probably preemptively bracing for impact. You were going  heavy  though, weren’t you? I stuck to a lighter weight, feeling a bit off after that awful sleep. Too heavy, maybe. My quads are screaming at me now. But I’m trying to build up before…well, before the holiday. Need to feel at least marginally confident in a bikini. Which reminds me, are you  still  considering Greece? Definitely Greece! Booked the flights last week, actually. Staying in Santorini, a little village called Oia. Apparently, the sunsets are insane. It's ridiculously expensive, though. I might need to take out a small loan just for the cocktails! Oia! Oh my god, photos look incredible. Worth the loan, I reckon. I’m still leaning towards Portugal. Cheaper, and I’ve always wanted to try surfing. But then again, Santorini… decisions, decisions. How long are you going for? Ten days. Late July. You should come! Seriously. We could do the whole sunset-watching-cocktail-drinking thing together. There’s a bit of hiking too, if you get bored of the beach. Hmm, tempting. Very tempting. I’d need to check work, but I could potentially swing it. I've got that ridiculous project deadline looming, but my boss is pretty understanding. It’s just… things with Liam are still a bit messy, and the idea of being around couples on holiday feels… draining right now. Oh, still? Honestly, you're better off without him. Remember that time he turned up to your birthday dinner wearing  those  sandals? The ones with the socks? A crime against fashion and good taste. You deserve someone who at least understands footwear basics. Oh god, don’t remind me. The sandals. A truly traumatic experience. It's not  just  the sandals, though. It’s just… the constant needing to explain myself. And he always brings up my ex, Ben. Like, consistently! It's infuriating! Ugh, the Ben card. Classic control tactic. You need to tell him to park it. Seriously. Anyway, enough boy drama. How's work? Still battling endless spreadsheets? Bupa is driving me insane at the moment.

…and honestly, the sheer exhaustion is something else. Little Leo decided 3am was a perfectly acceptable hour to make his grand entrance. Completely ignoring the carefully laid plans, of course! Though, Sarah was wonderful, absolutely stoic. Still, she's knackered. Ah, newborns. No respect for schedules, are they? Reminds me of trying to get a meeting with de Gaulle. Utterly immovable object, that man. Though, at least  he  had a reason for being awake at odd hours. Congratulations, Penelope. A grandson! Splendid. Is he a proper English boy, born and bred? Oh, yes, very much so. Born at St. Thomas’s. Though, Sarah did briefly consider going to France to have him. She’s been doing a lot of research into maternity care over there. Apparently, it’s quite…different. More holistic, she said. I was horrified at the thought of navigating a French hospital bureaucracy, frankly. France! A fascinating country, horrifying bureaucracy notwithstanding. I spent a good deal of time there, you know, chasing threads for the book. The property laws are a labyrinth. You can’t just  build  anything, even if you own the land. And the enterprise… so much red tape. Though, they are masters of protest, aren’t they? I’ve crossed paths with a few anarchists in my time, usually near the Sorbonne. Highly articulate, surprisingly polite, and utterly convinced the world is about to end. Anarchists? Goodness. Sarah was talking about how affordable property is in certain regions, tempting as it might be. I can't imagine having to deal with "highly articulate" protests when all I want is a quiet garden. We had a French couple staying at the B&B last summer, delightful people, but they were utterly baffled by London. The lack of…planning, they said. Everything felt so haphazard. Haphazard is a polite word for it. They’ve a point, you know. Though their own planning can be rather…rigid. Speaking of haphazard, did you hear about Chichester Cathedral? Utterly dreadful about the spire. Collapsed, or part of it did. Oh, no! That’s awful. I haven’t. What happened? Apparently, the masonry was failing. Something to do with the materials and, believe it or not, the original architect, a fellow called Porden. Seems his calculations weren’t quite as sound as everyone thought after all these centuries. They're assessing the damage now. It’s a tragedy for the building, of course, and a reminder that even the most magnificent structures are fragile.

Honestly, this sweet and sour chicken is… questionable. It tastes like it’s been sitting under a heat lamp since Tuesday. You always say that about Chinese food, Leo. You're such a snob. It's perfectly alright. Good even. Besides, it’s cheap and cheerful. And Mum insisted we came here. She did, didn’t she? Said it was a ‘family favourite’. I think ‘convenient because it’s five minutes from Gran’s’ might be more accurate. Yeah, Gran's already quizzing me about my mock results. She keeps asking if I’m applying to Oxbridge. Like, Gran, I'm trying to pass Physics, let alone get into Oxford! Tell me about it. My Aunt Carol cornered me and started asking about university prospects. I haven’t even  decided  what A-Levels I’m taking properly yet! It’s a bit much. It’s the family curse, innit? Everyone’s got an opinion and they're all desperate to live vicariously through us. Speaking of A-Levels, how’s History going, Raj? You were stressing about that Tudor essay last week. It’s…a process. I think I finally got my head around Henry VIII’s wives. It's just remembering  which  head got chopped off and when. Honestly, it’s like a morbid soap opera. Sounds exciting. I wish I had a soap opera to study. Mine is just…numbers. And formulas that make absolutely no sense. You're telling me. I’m considering dropping Further Maths. It’s genuinely sucking the joy out of everything. I swear, if I see another integral… Don’t you dare! Mr. Henderson will have your hide. He's obsessed with that stuff. Remember when he spent twenty minutes explaining the philosophical implications of calculus? Oh god, yes! And the way he got all misty-eyed talking about Euler. It was bizarre. He’s…intense. But he does make it kinda interesting, though? Like, when he relates it all to the universe or something. Makes you feel small, but in a good way? Small and confused. That’s how I feel. Anyway, enough about the horrors of education. Anyone seen the new issue of ‘Nova Force’? The storyline is getting properly mental. No way! Is Captain Stellar finally going to confront the Shadow Syndicate? I swear, they’ve been building that up for like, six months. I haven’t had a chance to grab it yet.

Honestly, this house is  full  to bursting. Jonathan’s birthday is next week, and trying to find a space to even  put  his presents is proving…challenging. It's not just the presents, is it? It’s everything. Decades of everything.      Tell me about it, Agnes. It’s the same at our place. Though, to be fair, most of  our  clutter is probably school projects young Thomas has insisted on keeping. He’s convinced that lopsided pottery penguin is a masterpiece.      It  is  a masterpiece! I put a lot of effort into that penguin. And it's not clutter, it's… archival material.      Archival material? Right. Well, we're not exactly planning a museum here, Thomas. Mum’s right, we need to thin things out. Especially before the party. I was thinking we could tackle the spare room this afternoon? It’s basically a repository for things we haven’t looked at since the 90s.      The 90s weren’t  that  long ago, dear! Though, I do agree, a good clear-out is always beneficial. Makes you realise just how much…  stuff  one accumulates over a lifetime. It's amazing how brands get you hooked, isn’t it? I remember when Kendal Mint Cake was just…Kendal Mint Cake. Now there's Kendal Mint Cake  biscuits , Kendal Mint Cake  chocolate , even Kendal Mint Cake  lip balm !      Oh, don't even get me started on branding! When I was a girl, you bought butter, full stop. Now you’ve got ‘luxury spreadable’, ‘countryside butter’, ‘extra creamy…'. It’s all marketing nonsense and costs twice as much. I still get most of my groceries from Booths, they haven’t gone mad with all that fancy labelling… yet.      Booths are lovely, aren’t they? Though, getting there from Darlington is a bit of a trek. I have to admit, sometimes the convenience of the supermarket wins. Even if it means battling through aisles of unnecessary choices. Speaking of groceries, have we sorted the cake for Jonathan? I was thinking Victoria sponge. Classic.      Victoria sponge is perfect, Mum. I’ve already ordered it from Mrs. Higgins, the baker down the road. She does a fantastic job, and it’s proper sponge, none of this dry, mass-produced stuff.      Can it have extra jam? And maybe some fresh strawberries?      Of course, darling. Extra jam and strawberries. Your father always loved a generous dollop of jam on his Victoria sponge.

Honestly, I’m  dreading  options week. It's like, everyone else has it all figured out - ‘Oh, I’m going to do triple science, obviously!’ – and I'm just… blank. Like a total void where future career paths should be. Tell me about it! It’s proper stressful. My mum keeps going on about needing to think practically. “Something with good job prospects, darling.” As if  I  know what has good job prospects at fifteen! What are you leaning towards, even a little bit? I don't know! I like… art. But my grandma keeps saying, “Oh, lovely dear, but how will you  earn a living ?” Honestly, it's the same thing with music. I’m actually getting pretty good at clarinet, you know? Mr. Davies says I have potential. Ooh, really? That’s brilliant! But yeah, the ‘earning a living’ point is always thrown at creative stuff. It’s infuriating. My older cousin tried to be a photographer and she had to give it up and become a paralegal. A  paralegal ! She was so gutted. See?! That’s what I’m scared of. Becoming a sensible, boring adult doing something I hate. Though, being a paralegal probably pays well. Speaking of jobs, have you seen what some YouTubers make? Like, proper money. Oh, don’t even get me started on YouTubers! It's ridiculous. Little kids filming themselves opening toys, and they are rolling in it. Though, it's hard work, I reckon. Constant content, editing... And all those comments. True, true. The comments section is a  bog . Seriously. Filled with trolls. I was watching this beauty guru the other day and some bloke was just… horrible. Why do people  do  that? I know, right? It's awful. I tried to get into blogging once, just about fashion and stuff, but I couldn't deal with the potential for negativity. I deleted it after a week. It felt like… too much pressure. Good for you. Honestly. It's not worth it. Anyway, back to options. I was thinking maybe Geography? It's... useful. You can learn about places. Geography’s not bad. Sarah's doing it, and she says it's really interesting, especially the stuff about climate change. But she also says the fieldwork is a  nightmare . Apparently, the last trip involved a lot of rain and midges. Oh, brilliant. Midges are the  worst . Okay, slightly less appealing now.

…and that robin, bold as brass, nicked a crumb right off the bird table while I was fillin’ it. Didn't even flinch. They’re gettin’ too used to us, they are. Back in my day, a robin wouldn’t come within ten foot. Aye, they do. Reminds me o’ old Man Hemmings down the lane. Used to feed the squirrels biscuits, right out of his hand. Ended up with ‘em followin’ him everywhere, little blighters. Even into the village shop, apparently. Caused quite a stir, that did. Oh, the stories you two tell! It's lovely to hear them. It feels like a different world sometimes, doesn’t it? Everything's so… rushed now. No time for watching the wildlife, or lettin' squirrels raid the shops. It is, isn’t it? Though, I’m trying to use some citizen science apps to track the local bird populations. There's this one, iNaturalist, that’s quite interesting. You can log what you see and it helps build a database of species distribution. iNaturalist, you say? Sounds a bit fancy for an old engineer like me. I’m still gettin’ my head around this new telly remote. Keeps changin’ channels on its own accord. Drives me mad, it does. And don't even  mention  trying to understand this computer my granddaughter left. Me neither, Roy. Computers are the devil’s work, mark my words. Give me a good book any day. I was readin’ up on the history o’ this land, actually. Did you know, before Norwich was Norwich, it was a Saxon settlement? A right important one, apparently. Built on the river, for trade, like most places were. Ooh, interesting! I always loved history. Did you know Harrow was part of Middlesex historically? It wasn't even part of Greater London until the expansion. It's fascinating how borders shift and change over time. It’s funny how local history is so often overlooked. Everyone focuses on national events, but there’s so much richness in understanding what happened right here, on your doorstep. The Norwich story is particularly good, with the Norman influence afterwards; the cathedral is stunning. Aye, the cathedral's a beauty. Though, I've always preferred the Roman ruins further south. Spent a bit o' time down that way workin' on a road project years ago. Terrible traffic, though. You wouldn’t believe the state of some o’ them roundabouts.

…and honestly, Doreen, this new headmaster at Costessey Junior, young Mr. Finch, he’s all about ‘experiential learning’ now. Experiential! Sounds right fancy, don't it? But what it  is , if you ask me, is letting them run wild in the woods pretending to be badgers. My granddaughter, little Maisie, comes home covered in mud every other day. Oh, you and your Maisie. She's a lively one, that girl. Though I do agree, this 'experiential' nonsense… it sounds exhausting, for both the children  and  the teachers, if you ask me. When I was helping out at Harrow High, it was chalk and talk, and that was that. Perfectly good enough for us, wasn’t it? Morning, you two. Biscuits? And actually, experiential learning isn’t necessarily a bad thing. It  can  be quite effective, if implemented properly. Engaging different learning styles and all that. Though I’ll admit, the badger bit does sound a little…ambitious. Ambitious is one word for it, Kevin. I said to my son, “They’ll be building dens next!” He just patted me on the head and said something about fostering creativity. Creativity! When what she needs is learning her times tables. Times tables are crucial, Arthur, absolutely crucial. Though having said that, I remember young Jamie – little terror he was – couldn't grasp division to save his life. Tried everything. Gave up in the end. He’s doing alright now, runs a successful plumbing business, doesn’t need division for that, does he? Funny how things turn out. I had a student like that, utterly baffled by fractions. Now she’s a brilliant architect. Turns out spatial reasoning was her strong suit, fractions weren't essential. Speaking of essential, have either of you had a delivery this week? I've been waiting on a new garden gnome. A garden gnome? Good heavens, Kevin. You’re a teacher, a man of books and learning…and you’re collecting garden gnomes? Don't judge me, Arthur! The wife likes them. It’s a simple pleasure. The delivery driver, though, was a right character. Tried to leave it with Mrs. Higgins next door. Said my number 3 was confusingly similar to hers. Number 3! Honestly, the youth of today can’t even count. They're all glued to those blinking phones, aren’t they? Tweeting and TikTokking and whatever else they do. I tried to understand it once, my grandson was showing me.

Aw, look at it comin’ down proper now. It were just flitty bits a minute ago, but now it’s a right blizzard. Proper Sunderland weather, this is. Makes you miss home, doesn't it? Even if home is freezing. Miss the grey? Nah, I’m good. Cambridge snow is… picturesque. Sunderland snow is just  cold . And damp. And probably covered in something industrial. Though, I must admit, it does look nice on the garden. Did you manage to get the winter bedding planted yesterday? Aye, I did. Nearly froze my fingers off, mind you. Those pansies looked a bit peaky, though. I’m worried they won’t survive a proper hard frost. You think I should have put more compost in? You always put too much compost in, love. You’re convinced everything needs smothering in the stuff. They’ll be fine. It’s Cambridge, not the Arctic. Speaking of surviving things… have you seen what Brenda’s doing for her hen do? Oh god, don’t even  start . I saw the group chat. A murder mystery weekend in… Skegness? Skegness! Honestly, it’s like she’s deliberately trying to make it the most beige weekend imaginable. I know! And she’s making everyone dress up as their ‘spirit animal’. I’ve been assigned a sloth. A  sloth . I’m a PhD student researching particle physics, not a particularly slow-moving mammal! Oh that’s brilliant. Honestly, Brenda. Her taste is… questionable. Still, at least it’ll be a story. It’s not exactly Phil’s stag do, is it? Quad biking and a wrestling match? He'll be bruised for a month. Honestly, I’m worried for the blokes. Especially old man Henderson from accounts. He’s going to pull a muscle just  getting  into the quad bike. I’m actively avoiding eye contact with Phil about it. Wise move. So, hen do versus stag do… who do you think will have a worse hangover on Sunday? Phil, definitely. He can't handle his beer. He’ll be claiming it was the adrenaline. It'll be a classic. Anyway, enough talk of impending doom and dodgy hen parties. Have you been giving any more thought to where we should go on holiday this year? I have! I was looking at Italy again. Tuscany, maybe? We talked about it last year. Proper sunshine, good food, lovely scenery… Tuscany sounds lovely.

Now this… this is a proper roast, this is. Not like some of the things you get these days. All foam and no substance, innit? Though mind, your mother always ‘as made a good roast. Always ‘as. Oh, don’t start, Arthur. You say that every time. And it  is  good, isn’t it dear? Lovely and tender. Though a bit more gravy wouldn’t ‘ave gone amiss, if you ask me. It’s genuinely delicious, Grandma. Honestly. Perfectly cooked. And the Yorkshire puddings are incredible. They’re light as air! Absolutely. I've been trying to replicate a Yorkshire pudding like this for  years . It’s a dark art, isn't it? It seems so simple – flour, eggs, milk – but getting the rise is… elusive. Elusive? It’s all in the fat, young man. Beef dripping, that’s what you need. None of yer sunflower oil nonsense. Beef dripping and a ‘ot oven. My mother, she used to get it from the butcher, straight from the roasting joints. Proper stuff. Nowadays, it's all… processed. He’s right you know. It used to be so much simpler. Everything local. Farmer Giles down the road with the beef, old Mr. Henderson with the veg… You knew where your food came from. It's that traceability people are craving now, I think. That's part of what drives the whole 'slow food' movement, isn't it? Knowing the origins, supporting local producers… It's more meaningful than just grabbing something off the supermarket shelf. Exactly. We were talking about it with our students last week. The detachment from food production is a huge issue. They’ve grown up thinking chicken just  appears  in plastic packaging. They haven’t a clue about the process, let alone the ethics. Ethics? What ethics are there in a chicken? It’s for eatin’, innit? Though I suppose… I suppose they do treat ‘em better now than they used to. Used to be battery farms, dreadful things. Never could stomach the thought of it. Oh, Arthur, do let's not talk about battery farms at the dinner table. It ruins my appetite. Remember Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning leeks? She grew them in the allotment, huge things they were. You could knock someone out with one. I remember! You used to tell me stories about her, Grandma. She sounds like she was a character. Allotments are making a comeback, aren’t they?

Honestly, Mum, this is  exactly  how my Grandma used to make it. It's…comforting. Almost suspiciously so. Did you get the recipe from her again? Now, don't go accusing me of culinary espionage, love. It's a classic roast! Though, your grandma  did  have a knack. She never measured a thing, just a pinch of this and a dash of that. Drove your grandad mad, trying to recreate it. It’s really good, actually. Best roast I’ve had in ages. Better than anything I attempt, that's for sure. My flat still smells faintly of the burnt offering I called a ‘spaghetti bolognese’ last week. Aye, a good roast. Reminds me of Sundays back in Sale. Your mother always laid on a spread, didn't she? Even when we were scrimping. Though, the gravy wasn’t  quite  this smooth back then. Dad! You're not saying Mum's gravy has improved with age? That's fighting talk. Just observing, lass, observing. It’s gotten…refined. I’ve always said, a good gravy can save a mediocre roast. A bad gravy can ruin a perfectly good one. Used to be, gravy was made with the pan drippings and a bit of flour. Simple. None of this fancy cornflour nonsense. Gave it a proper flavour, it did. Used to have to chase the cat away from the roasting tin, that one was a menace. Oh, don’t even  start  with the cats, Dad. Remember Winston trying to steal the turkey off the carving board during Christmas ‘87? Absolute chaos. I wasn’t even born yet! But I’ve heard stories. Sounds like a yearly tradition. It pretty much was. The family Christmas spectacle of feline larceny. Speaking of tradition, Mum, are you still planning on getting a new kitchen? I was thinking about the colours, and… Oh, no, darling, not this again. Your father is quite firm on keeping things as they are. He says he knows where everything is. It's true. I've lived with that kitchen for thirty years. Don't want to be wandering around lost, trying to find the biscuit tin. But it's… orange! And avocado! It’s a time capsule of questionable decorating choices. You could at least get new worktops? It’s just…a little dated. He’s got a point though, changing things up can be stressful. Remember when we tried to rearrange my nan's living room?

…and honestly, the feedback from the beta testers on ‘SkillSwap’ has been…well, a mixed bag. Mostly positive, thankfully, but the universities are hesitant. They  like  the idea of students gaining practical skills through micro-internships with each other, but they’re terrified of the accreditation side of things. Hesitant is an understatement, knowing academic bureaucracy. It’s the ‘what ifs’ that get them, isn’t it? What if someone’s skill assessment is wildly inaccurate? What if a student ends up doing effectively paid work and it messes with funding models? Exactly! I tried to explain it’s not about replacing the curriculum, it’s  supplementing  it. Real-world application, peer-to-peer learning... building a portfolio beyond just essays and exams. You know, the kind of stuff I wish I’d had access to when I was at Leeds. All theory, very little actual doing. It’s a good idea, Ben, genuinely. But universities are institutions, encased in tradition. Remember when I tried to get them to even  consider  incorporating more creative writing exercises into the history curriculum? "It doesn't align with the assessment objectives," they said. As if exploring historical events through narrative is somehow…less valid. Oh, tell me about it. I ran into similar resistance with the initial pitch for ‘FlowState’ – the productivity app. “Too disruptive,” they called it. Now it’s got millions of users and is featured in  Forbes . Sometimes you just have to build it and prove it works. That's easier said when you're building an app than when you're trying to change entrenched academic practices. Though, I did stumble across this incredibly clever thing online yesterday… it's a TikTok account, believe it or not. A physics teacher is doing all these demonstrations using household objects, set to viral audio. It's attracting a huge audience. Seriously? A physics teacher on TikTok? That's…unexpected. Send me the link. Maybe there's a lesson in there. People respond to engaging content, regardless of the subject. We need to  show  the universities the benefit, not just tell them. I will. It's @PhysicsFunTime, I think. He's brilliant. He explains complex concepts in such a simple, visually appealing way. Honestly, it makes me feel like I've been teaching history all wrong. All droning lectures when I could be recreating battles with LEGO! Now  that  I’d pay to see.

Honestly, this risotto is  fighting  me tonight. It’s supposed to be creamy, not… gluey. Sounds about right for a Tuesday. Risotto is a commitment, Liv. You’re a brave woman. Anything good on your phone? Just endlessly scrolling through TikTok again? No! Well, a little. But mostly I was looking at cottages in Cornwall. Remember how we said we wanted to do a proper Cornwall trip next summer? Not just a day trip to St Ives dodging tourists. Oh, good. Yes! Cornwall sounds amazing. I need a proper beach holiday. Been a long time. Anything catching your eye? Somewhere ridiculously remote with a pub in walking distance is the dream. There’s a really cute one near Padstow. Tiny, stone cottage, looks like it’s practically  on  the beach. It's a bit pricey, obviously. Thinking we could maybe split it with Sarah and Ben? They were talking about needing a break too. That's a good shout. Padstow’s lovely, though it  is  a bit foodie-focused. Might be a bit overwhelming if we just want to chill. Remember that little village we stumbled across in Dorset last year? Charmouth? That was perfect. Ooh, Charmouth was good. Very Jurassic Coast vibes. Although, I think Cornwall feels… further away, you know? More of an escape. This risotto is definitely not helping my escape fantasies. I swear it's getting worse. It's the stress of being a project coordinator, darling. You’re always juggling a million things. How was work today? Still battling with the Henderson contract? Don’t even  start  me on Henderson. He’s requested another five revisions, all utterly pointless. He just likes to see his name in lights, honestly. I’m starting to suspect he actively enjoys making my life difficult. It’s exhausting. You have a bad day at work, you can actually  help  someone. I just move numbers around on a spreadsheet. Hey, that's not fair to yourself. You’re good at what you do! And honestly, some people need a lot of hand-holding. That’s just…people. Still, sounds draining. My day was… eventful. Old Mr. Davies had a bit of a wobble this afternoon. Just feeling really lonely, you know? Happens a lot. Oh, bless him. You're such a good nurse, you really are. It must be hard, dealing with that stuff day in, day out. It’s just… heavy.

Oh, look at this one, Chloe. You were  tiny ! Honestly, a right little button. This was Brighton, wasn't it? Your dad insisted on building a sandcastle the size of a small bungalow. Ruined his back, he did. Oh my god, I completely forgot about that trip! I just vaguely remember being covered head-to-toe in sand. And Dad groaning. He always overdid it. Though, to be fair, he  did  make spectacular sandcastles. Spectacular? That’s a strong word, dear. Ambitious is more like it. And messy. Very, very messy. Still, good times. He loved taking you all to the seaside. It was his thing. You were always so good at paddling, weren’t you? No fear. I think I just didn't realise the sea was… big. I was too busy collecting shells. Funny the things you remember. How are things with Mrs. Higgins next door? I haven't had a chance to pop round for ages with work being so hectic. Oh, poor love. She's not been well. A bit of a chest infection, apparently. Old age catching up with her, I suppose. I’ve been taking her a bit of soup, just to check on her. She misses Arthur something awful, you know. It'll be ten years next month since he went. Can’t believe it. Ten years… That's a long time. She really did adore him. I remember him always having sweets in his pocket for me when I was little. He was a softie, that one. Always spoiling you. Said you reminded him of his granddaughter, Sarah. Though, Sarah lives all the way up in Scotland now, doesn't she? Never see her. Life just... scatters everyone, doesn’t it? It does. It’s a bit depressing when you think about it. Everything feels so… transient. Especially with work. I’m juggling so much at the moment. We're launching that new product line next quarter, and the suppliers are being… difficult. Honestly, getting them to meet deadlines is like pulling teeth. Suppliers, eh? Always a headache. Your father was the same, always complaining about his suppliers when he was running the shop. "They don't understand the value of good service anymore!" he'd say. He'd rant for ages. It's the same now, honestly. They promise the earth, then deliver… well, not the earth. More like a handful of dust.

Right, honestly, this is  way  better than student halls. Proper atmosphere, innit? Though I still can’t believe how early they start flogging stuff over here. Seven in the morning! I was still dreaming about gravy at that hour. Gravy is always on your mind, isn’t it, Lottie? It's charming, though. And yes, it’s a vast improvement on the grey concrete of campus. I actually managed to sleep past eight for once. Which is a miracle. Did you manage to decipher what that woman was saying about the peaches? My French is… well, it’s definitely a work in progress. Decipher? Ha! I just nodded and smiled a lot, then pointed. Worked a treat. Honestly, I think she was trying to tell me they were from a specific valley or something. It's all a bit beyond me. I'm sticking to pointing at pastries. Less opportunity for miscommunication. Speaking of which, how’s the uni work going? You seemed a bit stressed on the train. It’s…fine. It's just, the stats module is really kicking my backside. It’s all about hypothesis testing and p-values and stuff. It’s so frustrating because the  idea  makes sense – trying to prove something scientifically. But applying the actual mathematical methods…it feels like guesswork half the time. Do you remember Mr. Harrison in sixth form, trying to explain that stuff? Vaguely. Mostly I remember trying not to fall asleep during his lectures. Physics weren't my strong suit, to put it mildly. I was all about the creative stuff, remember? Art and English. Much more forgiving when you get things a bit wrong, or interpret things your own way. Are you getting any help? A little. There’s a study group, but it's mostly people who already  get  it, showing off how clever they are. It's not massively helpful. I was thinking of emailing the lecturer again. It feels a bit pathetic, admitting I'm struggling, but… Don't be daft. It's  not  pathetic. Everyone struggles. Honestly. It's part of learning. And lecturers are supposed to  help , remember? That's literally part of their job description. Plus, you're miles smarter than you give yourself credit for. Honestly, you were always the one who'd pick up on things I completely missed. You always said I overthought things. No, you just  thought  things. There’s a difference.

…Honestly, it was  huge . I mean, genuinely, the size of my hand. Crawling across the landing, right outside the bathroom. Nearly gave me a heart attack. Oh, you and spiders, eh, Brenda? You go all to pieces. I swear, they sense fear. It’s why they come for  you . That’s ridiculous, Doreen! They don't  sense  fear. It’s just… well, it's a spider! A big, hairy one! And our house isn't usually like this. We’ve never had many spiders before. Never had many, you say? You live in the countryside, dear. Spiders  come  with the countryside. Same as the mice. You’ll be finding a little field mouse in the pantry next, mark my words. Don't even  say  that! I’m still a bit traumatised from that incident last autumn. Remember when one got into the airing cupboard and… well, let’s just say it wasn’t a pleasant discovery. My husband, David, had to deal with that one. He’s the practical one, thankfully. He’s a good man, David. Proper handy around the house. My Barry? He'd scream louder than you, Brenda, if he saw a spider. Though he's good for other things, bless him. And mice… they're sneaky little things. They won't come out when you're looking, will they? Just when you're settling down with a cuppa and a biscuit. Exactly! It’s the  principle  of it. The invasion of privacy! And the thought of them… running around. I’m a clean person, Doreen. I like things tidy. You are, you are. This house is always immaculate when I come. Though, you know, a little bit of…nature…isn’t so bad. I like the birds, myself. Oh, the birds are lovely. We have a robin that comes to the bird feeder every morning. Such a cheerful little thing. And the blue tits are regulars too. David built that feeder, you know. He's quite the carpenter when he puts his mind to it. Barry tried to build me a bird table once. Ended up looking like a wonky shed. Nearly took my eye out with a splinter. Had to get rid of it in the end. Still, he meant well. That sounds like Barry. Bless him. It's nice to have a bit of wildlife, isn’t it? As long as it stays  outside . Though, even the birds can be a nuisance.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork after Mum died was just… relentless. It felt like every single organisation needed a death certificate, and then three forms completed in triplicate. You wouldn't believe it. It was almost a full-time job on top of everything else. Oh, darling, you’ve no idea. My Arthur…well, dealing with his things was bad enough, but Mum -  her  paperwork was a nightmare. She collected everything! Bills from the 1950s, old grocery lists… I spent weeks sorting through it all. It’s almost like they  want  to make it harder when you’re grieving. Exactly! And then trying to piece together everything for the probate. It was all so confusing, particularly with the house. She’d been meaning to update the will for years, you know? Kept putting it off. Luckily, it was straightforward in the end, but the worry… My Arthur was the same, bless him. Always meaning to. Always “tomorrow.” I nagged, of course, but you know how men are. Still, it all got sorted. Tell me, with your Mum… you mentioned a disease? Was it quick? No, not at all. It was… cruel, really. Vascular dementia. It started subtly, just little memory lapses. Forgetting where she’d put her keys, repeating stories. But then it progressed so rapidly. The last year was particularly difficult. She didn't really  recognise  me towards the end. It was heartbreaking. It felt like losing her bit by bit, long before she actually went. Oh, that’s awful, dear. Dementia is a terrible thing. It robs them of everything, doesn’t it? And it’s so hard on the family, watching that happen. My sister’s husband had it. It took five long years. Just… a shell of his former self. It was. And she was such a vibrant woman, Mum. Always busy, always involved in everything. Head of the Women's Institute, volunteered at the hospital, organised every village fete. It's just... hard to reconcile that with the person she became. Have you always lived around here, in Stevenage? I know you were originally from Bristol, but… No, not always. Bristol's always been home in my heart, mind you. Grew up right there, practically on the docks. My father worked at the docks, unloading cargo. Tough life it was. But we were happy. Then Arthur – he was a teacher, like yourself – got a post at a school in Luton.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Fresh air, no marking… and look at that! Oh, wow. Is that…? A hot air balloon? Quite a long way up, isn’t it? It is! Spotted it a few minutes ago. Makes you wonder where they’re heading. Probably somewhere far more exciting than grading undergraduate essays, that’s for sure. Though I do rather enjoy the theoretical debates we get in the postcolonial literature seminar… sometimes. ‘Sometimes’ being the operative word. I’m still recovering from that deconstruction of  Heart of Darkness  last week. Honestly, some of those students take things a little  too  seriously. Oh, you say that, but you were the one championing the argument about Marlow being a complicit… well, you know. Alright, alright, I got carried away.
