It's the Norfolk air - gets the blood flowing, the theories bubbling! Speaking of bubbling… did you see Old Man Hemmings’ sheep were out again this morning? Nearly caused a pile-up on the A140. Oh,  those  sheep. Honestly, they’re more adventurous than most people I know. And Hemmings just lets them wander. He says it’s their ‘natural inclination’. Natural inclination to cause traffic chaos, perhaps. Reminds me of Barnaby, actually. Remember when he chased that pheasant all the way into Mrs. Gable’s prize-winning rose bushes? How could I forget? She didn’t speak to us for a week! Poor Barnaby just looked so pleased with himself, tail wagging, pheasant feathers stuck to his nose. He’s a menace, that dog, but an adorable one. I keep thinking we should get another one, a companion for him. Another dog? Seriously? Our lives are already hectic enough. And remember the expense! Food, vet bills… It adds up. I know, I know. It's just… he seems a bit lonely when we’re both at the university. And he does get so exuberant on walks. Another dog might tire him out a bit. Plus, a little puppy chaos would be… fun. ‘Fun’ is one word for it. ‘Expensive’ and ‘time-consuming’ spring to mind too. We haven't even discussed that camping trip you were suggesting. That's  another  expense, and I’m not convinced sleeping on the ground is my idea of relaxing. Especially with the midges out here. They're vicious. It wouldn't be roughing it! I was thinking a glamping pod, somewhere with proper beds and… crucially… midge netting.

Honestly, this weather is just  doing  my head in. One minute it’s glorious sunshine, the next it’s threatening to pour. Makes planning anything impossible. Aye, you’re tellin’ me. Proper British weather, innit? Always keeps you guessing. Reminds me of trying to predict attendance at the gyms some days. You never quite know what’ll walk through the door. Had a real surge last week, then… nothing. I imagine. People’s motivation waxes and wanes, doesn't it? Similar to language learning, actually. You get a burst of enthusiasm, then the grammar hits, and… poof! Gone. I'm teaching a new evening class, beginners’ Italian, and I'm already bracing myself for the September drop-off. Italian, eh? Fancy that. Always wanted to learn a bit of Italian. My wife and I did a week in Tuscany a few years back. Beautiful place. Couldn’t get past ‘Buongiorno’ and ‘Grazie’ though, unfortunately. That's a good start, though! Seriously. It’s all about baby steps. The biggest problem I find is people wanting to be fluent  immediately . They think it's like downloading an app. Sounds about right! Everything’s instant these days. No patience for putting the work in. It’s the same with fitness, you know? Everyone wants the six-pack abs after a week. I spend half my time managing expectations, and the other half explaining progressive overload. Progressive overload? Right. Buildin' things up slowly. Start with what you can manage, then gradually increase the intensity or weight. You can't just jump in at the deep end. Good coaching technique, really. Applies to most things, I reckon. That’s actually remarkably insightful. It  absolutely  applies to language learning. I try to explain that to students all the time. It's about consistent, small gains. Building a foundation before tackling complex sentences. I even use a sort of ‘fitness’ analogy sometimes - ‘warming up’ with basic vocab before ‘strengthening’ grammar muscles. See? Told ya! I’ve always thought there’s more crossover between different disciplines than folk give credit for. You learn a few things managin’ ten gyms across the Midlands, let me tell you. It's all about people, really. Getting them to believe they can achieve something. Speaking of the Midlands, have you been to Birmingham much? I occasionally pop in for theatre trips. It's had a bit of a renaissance, hasn’t it?

Right, that’s a proper brew. Thanks, love. Though I still say your nan makes it better, doesn't she, Arthur? She puts a pinch of bicarbonate of soda in, you know. Gives it a bit of…oomph. Aye, she does. Always has. Says it takes the tang out of the water. Scientific, she calls it. Though I reckon it’s just habit after all these years. Bicarbonate of…what now? Sounds disgusting. Don't be rude, lad. Your Great-Grandma knows a thing or two about a good cuppa. She's been making 'em for longer than you've been alive! And it  does  make a difference. Honestly. Though, young folk, they wouldn't know good tea if it slapped ‘em round the face. Now, now, Margaret. Don’t go starting on the youth of today. He's probably just absorbed in his… what  are  you looking at anyway? Is that more of those TikToks? Just…stuff. Friends sending memes. It's easier than explaining it, honestly. Memes? Is that like those pictures folk send on the computer? With words on ‘em? Yeah, kinda. They're jokes, mostly. Little videos or pictures. It's just…funny. Funny, is it? Well, I remember when funny was a good knock-knock joke! Used to drive your grandfather, God rest his soul, absolutely mad with ‘em. Oh, you and your jokes, Margaret. Remember the one about the scarecrow? How could I forget? "Why did the scarecrow win an award?"… "Because he was outstanding in his field!" Arthur nearly choked on his tea that day! Aye, you always did have a knack for the silly ones. It were a welcome change from all the serious talk, with the fishing and the work. Speaking of work, I’ve got a mountain of GCSE papers to mark next week. Honestly, the things these kids write. You wouldn’t believe it. Some of them can't even work out percentages. It's worrying, I tell you. Properly worrying. GCSEs are stressing me out already. Mock exams are next month. I’m proper bricking it. Oh, now don't you worry yourself sick. You’re a bright lad, you are. Just put your head down and do your best. And remember your times tables. That's where most of ‘em fall down, you know. Back in  my  day… Now, now, Dorothy. Don’t go on about “back in your day”.

Right, are you  sure  this is the right way, love? This looks… awfully narrow. And I haven't seen a sign for the village hall in ages. Relax, Elsie. Satnav says we’re spot on. It’s taking us the scenic route, that’s all. Apparently, avoiding the A66 saves us about ten minutes, and look at the countryside! It’s gorgeous. Though I admit, it  is  a bit… lane-y. Scenic route? Scenic route for a van carrying a full ceilidh band’s worth of instruments? That sounds like a recipe for disaster, more like. Remember Old Man Hemmings’ gate? We nearly took his whole wall out trying to get a delivery van through that. That was one time, Elsie, and Hemmings had been meaning to replace that wall for years. Besides, this is different. The satnav knows what it’s doing. It’s got… algorithms. Algorithms! Oh, don’t give me that. Algorithms don't know sheep from swedes. A good map, and a bit of common sense, is what you need. I swear, this technology is turning people daft. My Year 9s can’t tell time without their phones, and half of them think Darlington is in France. You're a tough critic, you are. Though I agree about the time-telling… it’s worrying. Still, the band are relying on us to get them there on time. Old Man Tiber – the fiddle player – will have a right fit if he’s late for soundcheck. He's got a temper like a stirred hornets’ nest, that one. Aye, Tiber. He’s a character. Though he always smells faintly of wood shavings and mothballs. Wonder what he gets up to when he’s not fiddling. He mentioned something about making bird boxes last week. Probably. He’s a proper craftsman, I think. Always tinkering. Speaking of tinkering, I finally managed to fix that broken loom you had. The shuttle was jammed. Oh, bless you, love! You did? That’s brilliant! I was going to have to take it to that shop in Barnard Castle, and they charge the earth. I was hoping to get a new scarf done before the winter. It's getting chilly now, isn’t it? Proper autumn weather. It is. Had a bit of a downpour this morning. Forecast is looking grim for the weekend, actually. Not ideal for a wedding, is it? Poor Sarah and David.

Honestly, that site… it’s even worse than the photos suggested. The light’s all wrong, and the existing brickwork is just… sad. It’s going to need  so  much work to get it to a liveable standard. Tell me about it. I was already bracing myself after seeing the brief, but being  there … it feels almost wilfully depressing. Old Man Hemmings really did pick the most challenging one, didn’t he? Part of me thinks he just enjoys watching us squirm. He absolutely does. He probably gets a little thrill out of our panicked late-night design sessions. Though, I will say, the potential is there. If we can get the light right, and play with the internal spaces… it could be really special. That's what I keep telling myself. Speaking of special… did you see Chloe last night? At Ben’s party? Oh,  Chloe . Yes. Looking particularly radiant, as always. Still seeing that musician, Leo? Apparently. They looked… entwined. It’s all very bohemian. Honestly, I’m starting to think she only dates people who own at least three vintage guitars. You’re probably right. She has a type. Though Leo seems… nice enough. A bit too intense for my liking, but nice. How’s your sister, by the way? Last I heard she was absolutely swamped with work. That’s putting it mildly. She’s in a right state, actually. The firm she joined after graduating is… brutal. 80-hour weeks are the norm, and she’s being completely micromanaged. She called me yesterday, practically in tears. Keep saying she’s questioning if architecture was the right choice. Oh, no! That’s awful. That’s precisely the kind of environment that makes people lose their passion. Remind her why she loved it in the first place? All those models she used to build as a kid… I tried. She’s just feeling so… useless, apparently. Her boss keeps rewriting her designs, saying they’re “too conceptual”. It’s soul-crushing. I told her to maybe start looking around, but she’s worried about appearing disloyal so early on. It’s a tough one. Loyalty is admirable, but not at the expense of your mental health. Maybe she should talk to someone in HR, or even a mentor if she has one. She did say she considered HR, but she's worried it will make things worse. It's a really small firm, everyone knows everyone.

…and honestly, the traffic on the A1 was  brutal  this morning. Absolutely brutal. I left with what I thought was plenty of time, and still nearly missed that meeting with Harrison Steel. Honestly, people just don't seem to understand the concept of merging anymore. It’s every man for himself. Ugh, tell me about it. Even getting into Grantham yesterday was a nightmare. Old Mrs. Higgins was trying to do a three-point turn on Beckingham Lane for a solid five minutes. Held everyone up. Five minutes?! Goodness gracious. That's… dedicated bad driving. I swear, they should re-test everyone over forty. Just to make sure they still  remember  how to indicate. Mum! That’s a bit harsh! Though… you do have a point. Dad’s driving is… an experience. Don’t I know it. Thankfully, he mostly sticks to village roads now. Less carnage that way. Anyway, enough about vehicular chaos. How was your weekend? Did you end up going to that exhibition with Liam? The one at the gallery in Norwich? Yeah, it was good! Really interesting. He’s… good at picking out stuff like that. Something different. It wasn’t what I’d normally go for, all very conceptual, but he explained it all and I actually really enjoyed it. We had lunch afterwards, down by the river. It was lovely, finally some decent weather. Oh, that sounds delightful. Liam sounds like a good influence. Is everything… going well with him, then? You’ve been a bit quiet about it lately. It’s… good. It's still fairly new, and we're just taking things slow. He's really busy with uni at the moment, loads of deadlines. It’s hard to find time to just…be. I understand. That’s perfectly normal. University is demanding. Don’t put too much pressure on yourselves. It's important to have your own space too, you know? Don't lose track of your friends. Speaking of which, have you heard from Chloe? She hasn’t been replying to my messages. She’s been a bit MIA, yeah. I think she’s really throwing herself into the drama society. Apparently, they’re doing a massive production of ‘A Midsummer Night’s Dream’ and she’s got a pretty big part. She’s been at rehearsals every night. Oh, that's wonderful for her! She  always  loved Shakespeare. Remember when we tried to get her into that summer course at the Globe when she was fifteen?

…and honestly, the ‘dynamic team environment’ bit just feels so… empty, doesn’t it? Like they’ve just copy-pasted it from every other job description ever written. Oh,  absolutely . It's corporate speak for “we work long hours and expect a lot.” Though, to be fair, most places  are  looking for someone who can blend in. You’ve got to play the game a little. Are you stuck on the covering letter, then? That's usually the worst bit. Stuck is… a strong word. More like circling, tentatively, like a nervous shark. I've got the skills, I  know  I’ve got the skills. It's just… articulating them in a way that doesn't sound like I'm bragging, or underselling myself. You’re good at this, aren’t you? Making things sound… impactful. Radio voice and all that. Guilty as charged. Years of making the mundane sound fascinating. Look, let’s break it down. What specifically are they asking for that makes you hesitate? Read me the bit you’re wrestling with. Okay, right. It’s this: “Demonstrable experience in creating engaging content for diverse audiences, with a proven ability to adapt style and tone to suit different platforms.” Ugh. ‘Engaging content.’ It feels so… vague. It  is  vague. But it's radio producer code for “can you make people listen/watch/read?” Think about your language teaching. You are  constantly  adapting your style. You have to explain complex grammar to a beginner then discuss post-structuralism with an A-level student. That's adapting style and tone, right there! I suppose so. It just doesn't… feel like ‘content creation’ in the media sense? I'm used to thinking of it as facilitating learning. Same difference! You're crafting narratives, you're building understanding, you're keeping people interested and actively involved. That’s all content creation. Just frame it differently. “Utilised pedagogical expertise to create engaging and accessible learning materials… adapted communication style to cater for a diverse range of learning needs and abilities…” See? Sounds good, posh even. Posh. Yes. It does. But will they understand what ‘pedagogical’ means?! Probably not, but it shows you've got a vocabulary! They’ll skim it, looking for keywords. ‘Engaging’, ‘diverse’, ‘adaptable’ – tick, tick, tick. Don’t get bogged down in trying to write the perfect sentence, just make sure you’re hitting  their  needs. What about the job itself?

…and honestly, the thought of another quarterly report genuinely makes my skin crawl. Five years at the top, building that digital marketing agency, and now… I just feel…empty. Empty is a strong word, David. You were brilliant at it. You built something  amazing . It’s understandable to feel a bit lost now you’ve sold it, though. Like, what  now ? It's a big shift. Exactly! What now  is  the question. I keep circling back to this pottery idea. Remember how much I enjoyed that weekend workshop we did in the Cotswolds? The feel of the clay, the process… it felt…grounding. I do remember. You were surprisingly good. And surprisingly messy! You had clay  everywhere . But seriously, pottery? That’s… a significant departure from multi-million pound deals, isn't it? It is. But the deals felt… hollow. This feels… real. I’ve been doing some research. There’s a real demand for handmade ceramics, especially unique pieces. I'm thinking small-batch, online store, maybe some local markets. No pressure, no investors, just… making things. That sounds…lovely, actually. Peaceful. Though “small-batch” still implies  some  business acumen, doesn't it? You can’t just fire up a kiln and hope for the best. You’ll need a business plan. Oh, trust me, the planning stage has begun. I’ve been sketching out costs - kiln, clay, glazes, website, packaging… it adds up quickly. I was thinking maybe we could use some of the sale money to rent a small studio space? Somewhere with good light, ideally. We definitely have the capital. And a studio is a good call, the house is lovely, but not exactly suited to turning into a pottery workshop! Have you looked at spaces around here? I know a couple of the parents at the school rent studios for their art. I could ask around. That would be amazing, actually. Thank you. I’ve started looking online, but word-of-mouth is always better. What about you? You're nearing the end of your sabbatical, aren't you? Still unsure about going back to teaching full-time? I am. Honestly, this house-sitting, having the freedom to just…  be  has been incredible. It’s made me question everything. I really enjoy working with the kids, don't get me wrong, but the bureaucracy, the endless meetings… it’s soul-destroying. You’ve mentioned wanting to do something with tutoring before.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is lovely, Margaret. You really shouldn’t have. Though, I  did  suggest it when you asked what everyone fancied… Nonsense, dear. A bit of good cooking keeps the spirits up. And it’s not as if  I  do much these days beyond pottering. Though I did spend the morning trying to explain to young Leo here that vegetables don’t magically disappear if you hide them under your jumper. Found one! It was hiding! A strategic hiding place, I daresay. Reminds me of my own attempts at avoiding Brussels sprouts as a boy. Utterly fruitless, of course. Your grandmother was a woman who knew her nutrition. Leo's got your determination, Arthur. He fixes his gaze on something he doesn’t want, and you could move mountains trying to change his mind. It's exhausting. It's not helped by the fact he's picked up this thing of saying "No!" to absolutely everything. Speaking of things he’s decided he doesn’t like… have you seen Ben’s facial hair lately? It’s practically a Viking helmet. Oh, the beard? Yes. Quite… substantial. He’s been letting it grow for months now, hasn’t he? Says it’s ‘a look.’ Honestly, at his age, you’d have thought he’d know better. A mid-life crisis manifested in follicular form. Perfectly understandable. Though I recall my own youthful experiments with a rather ill-advised moustache. Didn’t last long. My wife informed me it made me look like a villain in a silent film. Oh, Arthur! You always were one for a bit of drama. It’s just… it’s all a bit  much , and I feel like I don't even recognise him. We haven’t had a proper evening out, just the two of us, since Leo was born. And when we do, he spends the entire time talking about… well, I don’t even know  what  he talks about. Crypto-currency? Some obscure football team? It's not conducive to romance. That’s the trouble with these modern distractions, isn’t it? They suck you in. They take over your world. When I was teaching, I remember young fathers barely attending parents’ evenings because of work commitments or… well, online games. It's a worrying trend, the disengagement. Mummy, more pie! Coming right up, darling. See, Margaret? That’s where  my  engagement is – ensuring this one gets enough to eat.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the car park passes at the doctors is just ridiculous, isn’t it? They’re saying you need a pass now, even just to drop someone off. It’s like they  want  people to be late for appointments. Oh, don't even get me started on that! I drove Mum down last week, and nearly got a ticket. Luckily, the attendant was having a fag break, but honestly! It's supposed to be a service for the community, not a revenue-generating scheme. It's the same with everything these days, isn’t it? Everything’s about money. Reminds me a bit of that referendum, actually. Don't. Please. I've had enough political chat for one lifetime. It just… it still gets to me, you know? Seeing how divided everyone became. Even at the village fete last weekend, you could feel the tension. Old Mr. Henderson, usually so cheery, was practically spitting feathers at young Tim from the bakery over Brexit! Oh, Henderson! He'll argue with a post. Still, it  was  a messy affair. Do you think things will ever settle down? I miss the days when we didn’t have to think about all that with every cup of tea. Remember when our biggest worry was whether the WI was winning at the flower show? Good times. Simpler times. Speaking of which, how's your piano playing coming along? Are you still tackling that Chopin nocturne? Oh, goodness. It’s…a work in progress. Let’s just say my fingers aren't as nimble as they used to be. And it’s harder to find the time with everything at school. Little Jamie’s got a school play next month, you know. He’s absolutely terrified he’ll forget his lines. He’s all nerves! He's such a sweet boy, though. Just like his dad was at that age. Aw, that’s lovely. He'll be brilliant, I’m sure. They always are, aren’t they? Even when they’re convinced they’re going to mess it up. It makes you think of Sarah, doesn't it? That school play she was in… playing the fairy queen. She was so proud. Oh, Sarah. It feels like a lifetime ago. Remember how she used to drive us all mad practicing her lines? Up and down the stairs, stage directions and everything. She always wanted to be an actress.

Aye, it’s grand tae get oot here, eh? Beats staring at a screen any day. Though, ironically, I’ve been glued to the bloody thing all morning. You and half the world, I suspect. What's got your attention this time? Not another Twitter storm, I hope? You get yourself so worked up over that platform. No, not a storm, exactly. More… observing. I’m trying tae figure oot how best tae leverage X – still cannae bring myself tae call it that – for work. We’re trying to push engagement with this new campaign, and the boss is convinced social media’s the key. The boss, eh? Always has a new bright idea, does he? And you’re the one who has to translate bright ideas into something resembling a strategy. Precisely! And it feels like a moving target. It was Instagram stories last quarter, now it’s all about short-form video and trying to tap into these… 'trends.' Honestly, half the time I don’t even  understand  the trends. This one about people pretending to be NPCs? Absolutely baffling. Oh, I’ve seen that! It's… a commitment to the bit, I suppose. Look, for the engagement side, I've found X, despite all its… quirks, is still pretty powerful for reaching a niche audience. Especially if you’re quick to respond to things, jump on relevant hashtags. It’s all about being part of the conversation, not just shouting  at  it. That's what I’m trying to get my head around. It’s not enough to just  post  anymore. It's about actively engaging, but then that takes time, resources… and frankly, a thicker skin. Some of the replies I’ve seen are… choice. Aye, the ‘choice’ ones. That's the downside, isn’t it? People feel emboldened to say things online they’d never dream of saying face-to-face. But you learn to filter it out. Mostly. I mostly use it to share academic articles or comment on research. It's surprisingly effective for connecting with other academics, even if half of them are arguing about methodology. See,  that  I can understand! Practical application. Mine’s more… trying to make plumbing supplies seem exciting to the general public. It’s a challenge. Honestly, sometimes I envy your world. Talking about theoretical physics feels a lot safer than trying to explain the benefits of a new type of sealant.

Honestly, this risotto is  fighting  me. It's either too dry or a swamp. There’s no in-between, apparently. Risotto is a commitment, Liv. You knew that going in. It's like…relationship level effort for a Tuesday night meal. Don’t even  start  with the relationship analogies. I just want something vaguely edible before I collapse. How was your weekend, by the way? You were very quiet when you got back from seeing Ben. Ugh. Complicated. Good, mostly. He took me to that new Italian place near the station – the one everyone’s raving about. The food was amazing, genuinely. But…he spent the entire evening talking about his ex. Seriously?  Still ? How long has it been now? Six months? Six months and three days, to be precise. Apparently, she’s “finding herself” in Bali and he’s deeply concerned about her spiritual wellbeing. I mean, good for her, but…it’s just a bit much, you know? It felt like I was on a date with three people. Oh, Chloe. That is… exhausting. You deserve better than being a sounding board for someone else's emotional baggage. Did you say anything? I tried! Gently. I was like, “That sounds tough for her, Ben, but maybe we could talk about…us?” And he completely pivoted to how she used to hate spicy food and he’s now rediscovering his love for it because she’s not there to complain. Oh my god. That is… impressively self-absorbed. You need to ditch him. Seriously. I’m half tempted. But he’s really lovely when he's not comparing me to a woman currently perfecting her downward dog in Ubud. I just…I don't know. It’s easy to get caught up in wanting to 'fix' things. It's a nurse thing, I think. You’re not a fixer, you’re a fantastic person who deserves someone who appreciates you for  you , not as a proxy for someone else. Honestly, it sounds like you're doing all the emotional labour. You're probably right. Work's been hectic too. Old Mr. Henderson's been having a really rough time, and then we had that incident with the patient who… You don't need to hear about that. It's just…challenging sometimes. Hey, you’re amazing at your job. You always are. But you don’t have to carry the weight of the world on your shoulders.

Right, this is proper good, this is. You’ve outdone yourself, love. Honestly. Though, I still say you put too much garlic in everything. Oh, don’t start, Dad. A little garlic never hurt anyone. And honestly, you’d complain if I  didn’t  put garlic in things. It’s become your ironic complaint. She has a point, Arthur. It's a tradition now. Besides, it smells delicious. Speaking of traditions… have we actually finalised anything about George’s visit? It’s only a week away. That’s what I wanted to bring up, actually. I’ve been thinking. He’s still… well, you know. A bit all over the place. I’m worried about him being left to his own devices for too long. Particularly with… the voices. Dad, we’ve talked about this. He’s been seeing Dr. Davies regularly, and he's managing. He  wants  to come and spend time with us, to be normal. We can’t treat him like a porcelain doll. I’m not suggesting we do! Just… perhaps a bit of oversight. Maybe he could stay with us the whole time, rather than bouncing between us and Sarah's? It’s a small house, but it would be easier to keep an eye on things. And it would be nice for him, a bit of familiarity. That's a good thought, actually. Sarah's got the kids and all the chaos. It might be a bit much for George. Although, I will say, little Leo adores his Uncle George. Keeps asking when he’s coming to build Lego. It  would  be easier. And frankly, I’m worried about him driving all that way on his own. Remember what happened last time? He got utterly lost and ended up in… was it Exeter? Don't remind me. Took me three hours to talk him down and get him redirected. He swore he was following the signs for Holsworthy, but... well. Honestly, I don’t trust his spatial awareness anymore. Right, okay. So, we suggest to George he stays here? We’ll have the spare room ready. We can’t promise to babysit him, Arthur, but we can definitely make sure he's comfortable and has someone nearby. That’s all I ask. Just knowing someone is around. It helps me sleep at night, you know? He’s a good lad, George, just… easily unsettled. We know, Dad.

…and honestly, Arthur, I’m tellin’ ya, this subjunctive mood is killin’ me. Killin’ me dead. I’ve been at this Spanish for nearly a year now, and it still feels like tryin’ to nail jelly to a wall. A year, is it? Blimey. Well, you’ve got more dedication than I ever had. I gave Duolingo a go, remember? Lasted about a week. Too much green owl nagging, I think. Nagging owl! That's a good way to put it. But it's not just the grammar, though the subjunctive  is  a beast. It's the sheer volume of it all. Remembering all the different verb conjugations… it’s a proper workout for the brain. You were always good at maths, numbers, that sort of thing. Languages just don’t… click for me the way they used to. Well, quantity surveying  was  all about numbers, I suppose. Tidying them up, making sure they added up. Bit different to remembering if "ser" or "estar" is the right one! Though, I always thought learning a language should be more…immersive. I’ve always fancied going to Spain and just  living  there for a bit. Pick it up naturally, like the kids do. Immersion is brilliant, in theory. But I’m not sure I could just swan off to Barcelona for six months, Arthur. My students would revolt! I've tried the immersion thing at home, mind. I put Spanish radio on while I’m marking essays. Honestly, 90% of the time it just feels like background noise. And the newsreaders talk so fast! Right? It’s all just a blur. I was reading something the other day, about how some countries, like… well, Spain actually, with Catalan, they effectively  need  to be bilingual. Kids are learning both languages from practically birth. Makes it so much easier, doesn't it? It does, doesn't it? Imagine… it’s just built in. I was reading about that too. It's not just Spain, is it? Belgium with Flemish and French, Switzerland with…well, everything! It's practically the norm in so many places. It makes me wonder, why is it so hard for us Brits? We're supposed to be good at languages, aren't we? Supposed to be. That's a good one. I think it's a bit of a myth, personally. We’re a bit… isolated, aren’t we? Historically. Island mentality, I reckon.

Right, okay. I  think  this is everything remotely related to… well, everything. Honestly, Dad, you’re a hoarder of statements. It’s impressive, really. Hoarder? Now, that’s a bit harsh, isn’t it? I just like to be prepared. You never know when you’ll need an old bank statement. Especially with these online accounts… always something going wrong. Remember that time with the fraudulent transaction? Vaguely. Seems like a lifetime ago. And that’s exactly why paper trails are less helpful now! Everything is digital. We need to get this scanned, Dad. Seriously, the amount of paper… it’s a fire hazard. I’ve got that little scanner at my place, we could knock it out this evening? Scanning…sounds fiddly. And what about all the confidential stuff, eh? Banking details and all that. I don’t entirely trust these computers, you know. They’re always getting hacked. Dad, it's more secure than leaving them piled up in a spare bedroom, believe me. Encryption, passwords, the whole shebang. I’m pretty good with that sort of thing, remember? It’s part of what I do, analysing language data… lots of digital security involved with corpus linguistics. Making sure datasets are protected and all that. Corpus…what now? Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. You and your fancy degrees. Still, good to know you know what you’re doing. It's just... I saw something on the news yesterday about identity theft, and it spooked me. Fair enough. We’ll be careful. Look, let's just focus on the important stuff for now. Bills, statements… anything pre-2010 we can probably shred. Unless you think you need proof of purchase for something ancient? Hmm. There's this one from… oh, goodness, 1998. It's for a flight to Malaga. Your mum and I, for our anniversary. We booked through Thomas Cook, can you believe it? They're still going, aren't they? Not really. They had a bit of a collapse a few years back. It was all over the news. But Malaga, nice. Mum always loved Spain. That reminds me, have you booked your trip to Crete yet? You were talking about it last month. I was supposed to. I found a really good deal online, but then… well, the website looked a bit dodgy. Lots of pop-ups, spelling mistakes… I just couldn’t bring myself to enter my card details.

Right, I’m officially stressing about petrol. Did you even  look  at the prices back there? Absolute daylight robbery. Seriously, six quid for a full tank feels like getting mugged. Dramatic as ever, Elsie. It’s not  that  bad. Though yeah, it's definitely creeping up, isn't it? I filled up yesterday, and it was…substantial. Hertfordshire prices are usually a bit higher anyway, compared to up North I imagine? A  bit  higher? You’ve no idea, lad. Sunderland petrol stations are…competitive, shall we say. They have to be, with everyone needing to get to Newcastle or down to Teesside for nowt. Six ninety-nine a litre used to be scandalous, now it’s practically a bargain. This was easily over seven-twenty. Seven twenty?! Blimey. Makes me appreciate the company fuel card a little bit more, actually. Though even then, you start to question every unnecessary journey, you know? Like, do I  really  need to drive to that site meeting an hour away when I could Teams it? Exactly! It’s the principle of the thing as well. They know we’re reliant on our cars, so they just hike up the prices. It’s infuriating. And it’s not like wages are going up to match. Tell me about it. Consulting’s alright, but…inflation’s a beast. Still, at least  I  don’t have to navigate the A19 every day. That road is a death trap. Don’t even START me on the A19. It’s a constant stream of lorries and people trying to merge at the last minute. The amount of times I’ve screamed at the radio… it’s a wonder my vocal chords haven't given out. And the bikers! Honestly, they think it’s a racetrack. The bikers are a pain, aren't they? I saw one the other day, absolutely  flying  down the M1. Weaving in and out of traffic like they're auditioning for a stunt show. It’s reckless! They don’t seem to have any regard for anyone else’s safety. My grandad used to be a biker, though. Proper old-school, leather jacket, greasy hair, the whole shebang. He’d be horrified at some of the youngsters now. He always said it was about respect for the machine  and  the road. That's fair. I suppose there's a difference between enjoying a ride and just being dangerous.

Right, so, your coaching session tomorrow…did Marcus give you any pointers on that forehand slice? You were looking a bit… strained last time, darling. Yeah, he mentioned it. Said I was getting too wristy. It feels weird trying to hit  down  on the ball when I usually try to lift it. The slice is all about deception, isn't it? Makes the ball stay low, messes with their rhythm. I remember watching Federer do it…almost felt like he wasn’t even trying, but the ball just died at their feet. Oh, don’t get your father started on Federer! He'll be recounting stories of Wimbledon for the next hour. Remember that match against Nadal in 2008? The final? Absolutely breathtaking. Mum, seriously? Tennis talk again? It’s just a sport. “Just a sport”? Oh, come  on . It’s artistry, strategy, athleticism…it’s everything! And you’re getting rather good at it yourself, you know. Marcus seems pleased with your progress. He’s right, you are improving. He said your serve has gotten significantly faster, didn’t he? And your footwork. That’s key, really. Like a boxer. Always moving, always anticipating. He said it was "less clumsy." Which isn't exactly a glowing review. And my serve is fast because I just…throw the racket at the ball. It's not exactly graceful. Well, sometimes brute force works! But Marcus is trying to teach you control, finesse. Think about Alcaraz. He’s got power, yes, but look at the spin he gets on the ball. It's insane. Alcaraz is a phenomenon, though. A bit like a young Nadal was. That raw energy, that willingness to fight for every point… it's inspiring. Though, personally, I always admired Djokovic’s consistency. The man is a machine. Djokovic is  boring  though. He just…wins. There’s no drama. Alcaraz is exciting. He actually  looks  like he's having fun out there. That’s a fair point. Djokovic is a bit… clinical. Though, you can't deny his dedication. Have you seen the lengths he goes to with his dietary regime? Apparently, he only eats certain foods at certain times of day. Absolutely obsessive. I read an article about it. He’s almost…scientifically optimized his body for tennis. It's a little unnerving, frankly. I prefer players who seem to just enjoy the game. Like Kyrgios? Oh, Nicholas.

Honestly, these sprouts are… an experience. Like, a green, tiny cabbage experience.      Liam! Don't be rude. Your Grandad loves sprouts. And they're good for you. Just eat a couple.      Mum, leave him. He’s a growing lad, he needs his… whatever it is young people eat these days. Probably just energy drinks and regret.      Regret sounds about right, considering the state of his room last time I checked. And Maisie, you're not exactly a picture of health yourself, living on noodles and instant coffee.      Now, now, Dave. Let the children enjoy their Christmas. Though I do agree about the sprouts, Sharon. A bit…overdone, aren't they?      They’re perfect! I parboiled them  and  roasted them. Honestly, you can’t please anyone. Did anyone notice the napkins? Doreen brought them.      Oh my god, are those… are those supposed to be angels? Because they look  exactly  like little white underpants.      Liam! Oh, that’s brilliant. They really do! Doreen and her… choices.      Doreen does have a unique eye. Remember that ceramic cat she gave us? The one with the wonky eye?      Don’t even  mention  the cat. It’s in the shed, ‘resting’. Anyway, have you all started your Christmas shopping yet? I’ve almost finished, just need a few bits for your Dad, Dave.      Footie socks, as always. You know me too well. I'm alright for gifts, actually. Done most of mine online. Less hassle than battling it out in the shops.      I prefer going to the shops. You see people you haven’t seen all year. Though it's getting so expensive isn’t it? Everything is going up.      It is. I'm on a student budget, so I've been making all my presents this year. Thankfully there's a crafty shop in town that I got supplies from. It's cheaper and more thoughtful.      I'm skint. I was hoping for a new gaming headset, but I doubt that's happening.      We’ll see, Liam. Don’t count your chickens. Are we all agreed on turkey next year? Or are we switching it up?      Turkey is tradition. Though I’m not opposed to ham.      Turkey's lovely, but honestly, all that carving… someone needs to help me next year. My arms aren’t what they used to be.      I can carve! I helped Mum last year. Though I nearly lost a finger.      You and a breadknife are a dangerous combination, Maisie.

Honestly, this week has been  mental  at work. We’re trying to roll out this new project management software and everyone is just… resisting it. Like it's personally offensive. Oh, people and change, eh? Always a drama. Sounds like you're dealing with a lot of Luddites. You’d think after all this time, people would be used to new systems. It’s the learning curve, love. Nobody  likes  having to learn something new, especially not when they’ve been doing things one way for twenty years. It feels like admitting they're not already experts. Reminds me of trying to get old man Hemmings to use GPS on the farm. Nearly had a heart attack. It's not just the learning curve, Dad. It's that they think  their  way is best, even when it's demonstrably less efficient. And then they complain about being overworked! I spent half of yesterday explaining the benefits of shared calendars. Shared. Calendars. Oh dear. You sound like you're banging your head against a brick wall. Is your manager being supportive? She's... diplomatic. Which basically means she tells me to be patient and "encourage buy-in". It’s corporate speak for “good luck, you're on your own”. Honestly, I’m seriously considering looking for something else. The pay is alright, but the stress isn't worth it. Don't rush into anything, sweetheart. Jobs are hard to come by these days. Have you spoken to Sarah about it? She always has a good perspective. I haven’t, actually. I've been avoiding her a bit, to be honest. Things are a bit… awkward at the moment. Awkward? What’s happened with Sarah? I saw her at the supermarket last week and she seemed perfectly cheerful. It’s complicated. We had a… disagreement. About Mark. Remember Mark, from university? Vaguely. The one with the terrible taste in music? That's the one. Well, he messaged me last week – out of the blue, after like, five years. Just saying he was in town and wanted to catch up. I mentioned it to Sarah, just in passing, and she… completely lost it. Lost it how? She accused me of actively seeking him out, of  wanting  to see him. Said I clearly still had feelings. It was ridiculous! I just said I’d politely decline, and she was acting like I’d betrayed her or something.

Right, onions are softening nicely. Though honestly, this whole ‘stir-fry’ thing feels… underwhelming. We usually do something a bit more substantial on a Friday, don't we? It's been a long week, love. Substantial feels…effortful. Besides, we had that enormous roast on Sunday. My arteries are still recovering. Speaking of recovering, how did the appraisal go? You seemed a bit tense this morning. Oh,  that . It was…predictable. More box-ticking than actual conversation. Apparently, I need to "demonstrate more proactive engagement with digital workflows." Honestly, I’m transcribing audio files, not launching rockets. What digital workflow could  possibly  be more efficient than listening and typing? Sounds like Brenda is just justifying her existence. She’s always been a bit…enthusiastic about the new software. Did you at least get a decent pay rise out of it? A 'cost of living adjustment'. Which, as far as I can tell, is a polite way of saying 'we'll give you enough to stop you actively starving'. Want to order a pizza instead? I’m losing faith in the stir-fry. Now you’re talking. Though, have you seen the new Marks & Spencer food hall? They’ve revamped it. Apparently, their pizza range is…ambitious. Ambitious? M&S pizza? That sounds…terrifyingly expensive. But go on, tell me. What kind of ambitions are we talking about? Lobster and truffle oil ambitions? Possibly. I saw one with fig and prosciutto.  Fig and prosciutto . On a pizza! It was fifteen quid. Fifteen quid! Good lord. We’re moving swiftly into artisanal pizza territory. We could get a perfectly good takeaway for half that price. Though, I did see they have a new range of ready meals…a sort of slow-cooked beef ragu. Hmm, tempting. But back to more important matters. I was reading an article today about equine welfare, specifically regarding the racing industry. It’s…grim. Honestly, it makes you question the entire sport. Oh dear. Don't start that. You know I try not to think about it. It's a bit like the Walking Dead; I know it’s popular, but I just can’t bring myself to watch it. Far too depressing. Have you finished the crossword? I've been stuck on 17 down all day. “Ancient mariner’s lament .” I had a go. I think it’s ‘sea shanty’. Sea shanty! Of course! You’re a genius. You always are.

Honestly, I've been staring at my wardrobe for a solid half hour and I still have  no  idea what to wear. This is a disaster. Sounds familiar. I did the exact same thing. Ended up grabbing the first vaguely presentable thing I could find. Which, in my case, is this… questionable floral number. You’d think having a wardrobe full of clothes would  help , wouldn’t you? Tell me about it. I’m going for comfy. Black jeans, a nice top, and trainers. I'm predicting a lot of dancing, and I  will not  be the one hobbling home. Comfort is key, honestly. I’m in jeans and a jumper. Layers are your friend when you're bouncing between pubs and… wherever we end up. Though, I did try to squeeze into these boots… big mistake. My feet are already killing me. Boots are always a bad idea, love. Always. Trust me, I learned that the hard way last year. Nearly twisted my ankle on that cobbled street near The Botanist. See, this is what I'm wrestling with! Do I attempt a heel? I’ve got these new ones, the black strappy ones, but they’re… ambitious. And then there’s the whole ‘drinking and heels’ equation. A recipe for disaster, if you ask me. Oh god,  don’t  do heels. Seriously. You know you'll be regretting it by 11 pm. I once tried wearing platforms on a night out and ended up nearly taking out a poor waiter. Not a good look. Platforms are even worse! You lose all sense of proprioception, or whatever it's called. You just become a wobbly tower of potential disaster. Speaking of disaster, anyone else panic-bought something utterly ridiculous online and now regrets it? I may have purchased a sequin bodysuit… purely on a whim. It’s currently lurking in a carrier bag, judging me. A sequin bodysuit?! Oh, I need to see that. Honestly, you’re a legend. Oh, that’s amazing! Though, not as bad as the time I bought a feather boa. Don't ask. So, definitely no heels then? Sensible shoes it is? Absolutely no heels. Unless you're planning on sitting down all night, it's just not worth it. Think about the walking! We'll be traipsing all over town, aren't we? Heard there's a new place opened up near the docks.

Honestly, David, Mrs. Patterson at work is  killing  me. She’s decided I need ‘more initiative’. As if I’m not already running the director’s life! It’s just…she's one of those people who needs to be seen to be managing, even if everything is perfectly fine. Ah, the classic ‘micro-manager’. They’re a special breed, aren’t they? Reminds me of old Mr. Henderson at the council. Used to rearrange my stapler three times a day. What exactly does ‘more initiative’ even  look  like in your job, then? Anticipating the director's needs before  he  even knows them? Pretty much! She suggested I start proactively researching potential venues for the Christmas party. In…April. As if I don’t have enough on my plate. It’s like she thinks I spend my day twiddling my thumbs. It just makes me feel so… undervalued. Well, you  are  brilliant at what you do. Honestly, you're the most organised person I know. Remember that time you planned our anniversary trip to Italy with a week’s notice? Logistical masterpiece. She’s probably just insecure. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking… about that whole soulmate thing. Oh, here we go. You and your philosophical ramblings over morning coffee. What sparked this one? Just… well, I was reading something online, and it got me wondering. Do you really believe in it? This idea that there’s one ‘perfect’ person out there for everyone? I used to. Properly believed, the rom-com, destiny kind of stuff. Then I realised life's a bit messier than that. I think it's more about finding someone you genuinely connect with, and  choosing  to build a life together. Finding someone you can tolerate even when they leave their socks on the floor. Fair point on the socks. But isn’t there something… comforting in the idea that there's  someone  designed for you? Like a missing piece of a puzzle? Maybe. But I think we’re all a bit jig-saw-shaped, y’know? We fit with lots of people, just in different ways. And sometimes, the ‘perfect’ fit isn’t necessarily the most exciting. Though, I suppose, we've done alright, haven't we? Alright is an understatement. You're my favourite jigsaw piece. It’s just… sometimes I wonder what it would have been like if I’d taken that job in America, back in the nineties.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of paperwork for that one client is ridiculous. It’s like they actively try to make things difficult. I swear, sometimes I think accounting exists purely to torment sales people. Sounds about right. Government work isn’t exactly a walk in the park either. It’s just…different difficult. Endless forms, but for completely different reasons. Everything has to be justified three times over, and you still get questions. You two and work. Always complaining! Though I do sympathise, honestly. My department’s been a bit of a nightmare since Brenda went off sick. She handles all the holiday requests and…well, people tend to take the mickey if no one’s keeping an eye on things. Three requests for a month in Bali  already ? In November? Bali in November sounds lovely, actually. Though I can see your point. People will push it, won’t they? It’s the British way. Is Brenda alright, by the way? What happened? She’s got a bad back. Something about lifting a box of files. Honestly, the storage in that office is a health and safety hazard waiting to happen. I’ve been meaning to sort it, but… you know how it is. Always something else. Sounds rough. Mum, you should really push for a proper ergonomic assessment over there. Seriously. And maybe get that air conditioning fixed? It was boiling in there when I popped in last week. Absolutely, darling. I have mentioned it, several times. It’s just… getting things done at that company can feel like pulling teeth. They’re very careful with spending, which is fair enough, but sometimes it’s penny-wise, pound-foolish. It’s not just the air con though, it's the whole building– did I tell you about old Mr. Henderson's funeral? It was lovely, really. Such a well-respected man. No, I hadn't heard. Oh dear. He was a fixture in the community, wasn't he? Always tending to the flowerbeds by the church. He was. And the graveyard itself… it’s beautiful. All those old tombstones, some dating back hundreds of years. You get a real sense of history, standing there. It’s funny, isn't it? How we spend so much time avoiding thinking about death, and then cemeteries become these strangely peaceful places. I’ve always found them a bit creepy, if I’m honest.

Right, so, Liam’s decided he's moving  again . Honestly, that's the third place this semester. Third! You'd think finding a decent room in this city wouldn’t be rocket science. No way, seriously? What’s up this time? Did his housemate start collecting taxidermied badgers again? Because that was a bit much, even for Liam. Oh, I heard something about that. Apparently, it wasn’t the badgers themselves, it was the  smell . He didn’t, like, properly…prepare them. Oh, God. That's… Liam, innit? No, it’s something about the landlord. He found out Liam was having, like, regular DnD nights. Apparently, ‘excessive gathering’ breaches the contract? Can you  believe  it? DnD? That's a new one. Though, I can see a landlord being a bit sketched out by a bunch of people chanting in a living room. My landlord just cares that rent’s paid on time, which, thankfully, isn’t usually an issue. Though, this tax return stuff is stressing me out. Have either of you even  looked  at it? Don't even mention it! I left it 'til the last minute, naturally. Mum keeps going on about how I need to be sensible with money, like I haven't got a student loan hanging over my head and a part-time job that barely covers the cost of beans on toast. She’s convinced I’m going to end up living in a cardboard box. It’s very encouraging, you know. My mum just sighs and tells me to ask my dad. He’s an accountant, so he sorts it all out for me. It feels a bit… dishonest, letting him do it. But honestly, I'd be lost without him. It’s all just numbers and forms and jargon. It  is  a mess. And then you get stuff like capital gains tax, which sounds completely made up. Like something out of a fantasy novel. Speaking of fantasy... did you see the football on Saturday? Absolute shambles! Don’t even! I had to leave the pub early, I was so embarrassed. Old Man Hemmings was grinning like a Cheshire cat. He's been going on about how Barrow is a proper footballing town for years, and now they've actually beaten City, he’ll never let me live it down. Oh no! You're doomed. Hemmings is terrifying. He’s the reason I avoid the chip shop on match days.

Honestly, this is  amazing . Way better than anything you get back ‘ome, eh Mam? Though, I still reckon Bolton’s chip shops are undefeated. Oh, don’t even start, love. You always come back to the chippy. This is lovely though, innit? Beautiful place, Croatia. Never thought we’d end up ‘ere, did you? Though, I still miss Maggie. Who’s Maggie? The dog? No, silly lad, your Auntie Maggie! She'd have loved this. Said she always wanted to come to Croatia. Remember how she used to go on about it? Oh, yeah… vaguely. Was she the one with the… loads of cats? She had a  thing  for cats, that’s true. And a questionable collection of garden gnomes. It's a lovely family tradition, isn’t it? These holidays. A little bit of sun, good food, and escaping the… well, the general British gloom. Though, even in Croatia, I suspect the buses run late. It’s practically a national sport. You’re telling me! Trying to get around London on public transport is a special kind of torture. At least ‘ere they seem… calmer. Less shouty. Speaking of torture, how are you finding uni, love? Settled in alright? Still doing all that… coding? Yeah, it’s good. Hard work, obviously. Coding’s a nightmare sometimes, but I’m getting there. There’s this one bloke on my course, though, covered head to toe in tattoos. Proper full sleeves. Bit intimidating, y’know? Cool! Can he get a job then? Mum says tattoos are a bit… much. Oh, don’t listen to your mother, she’s from a different generation. It’s just self-expression, isn’t it? I've seen doctors and nurses with tattoos these days. It doesn't define 'em. I've known some right lovely lads with tattoos, worked with 'em at the hospital. Exactly. It’s becoming quite commonplace. Though, I do wonder about the long-term implications. Will they regret them in 30 years? He says he’s a digital artist, so it fits the vibe. And he's really good at it, apparently. Better than half the art students. Can  I  get a tattoo when I’m older? We’ll talk about that when you’re eighteen, pet. And even then, we’ll see. It’s a permanent decision. What about school? Are you still moaning about Mr. Henderson and his history lessons? He’s alright, I guess.

…Right then. That was… a proper holiday, that was. Bit of a trek getting back though, wasn’t it? All those blinking motorways. It was lovely, George. Absolutely lovely. Cornwall suits you, you know. You seem to… brighter. And honestly, the YHA at St Ives? Beautiful spot. Though a bit hilly for my liking! These pictures are fantastic, actually. You two look so relaxed. And that lighthouse! The one at Land’s End? Stunning. I’ve only ever seen it on postcards. Oh, that lighthouse! A proper beast, that was. Climbed right to the top, I did. Nearly blew me away, wind was fierce. Reminded me a bit of old Mrs. Higgins, always had a gale force personality that woman. Though she weren't made of granite, thankfully. George, honestly! Always comparing everything to someone you knew from Costessey. But yes, it  was  windy. I was more worried about you on those coastal paths, though. Such a drop! Nonsense, Ethel. Got my wits about me. Though nearly tripped over a crab once. Scuttled sideways at me, it did. Gave me a right fright. Remember when young David used to collect them, Ethel? On Cromer beach? Oh, David. Always with a bucket and a net. He’d bring home the strangest things, wouldn't he? Remember that starfish? And he insisted on keeping it in the bathtub... Sounds like a typical childhood! Mine was more about getting into trouble at school, I’m afraid. Though I did try to be a ‘naturalist’ for a week, collecting bugs. That ended badly. For the bugs, mostly. School… Hmph. Waste of time, mostly. All that learnin’ and what good did it do me? Never needed quadratic equations to mend a fence, y’know? Though I suppose  you  put it to good use, didn’t you, Arthur? Being a teacher and all. It has its moments. Certainly more fulfilling than some jobs. Though sometimes I wonder if I actually  taught  anything, or just kept thirty teenagers quiet for an hour. Don't be so modest, Arthur. You've had a positive influence on so many lives. I've heard parents in the village talking about you for years. Speaking of trips… I was thinking, maybe next year… we could do that “Yorkshire in a Day” thing? I saw it advertised. Apparently, you get to see the Dales, the Moors, and a bit of Whitby all in one go.

Oh, this is proper good, this is. You’ve outdone yourself, ANON. Honestly, better than my nan’s, and she makes a cracking lasagne, she does. Yeah, it’s… nice. Proper filling though, innit? I could eat a horse after that shift today. Been shiftin’ bricks all day, non-stop. Feels good to just  sit  down, y’know? It  is  good, ANON. Seriously. You never cease to amaze me with your culinary skills. Though, I still maintain your gravy is the real star of the show. What did you put in it this time? A hint of red wine? ANON: Guilty! Just a splash. I figured, it's Friday, we deserve a little treat. And you two look like you both needed one. Leo, you look completely knackered. Knackered is an understatement. Old Man Hemmings was on my back all day about the speed. Like I  want  to rush building a wall, right? Safety first, and all that. Tell me about it. Work’s been a nightmare this week. Had a bridezilla on Wednesday who decided she absolutely  needed  peacock feathers on every single table, the day before the event. Peacock feathers! Where am I supposed to even  get  peacock feathers on a Wednesday afternoon in Doncaster? Peacocks? Seriously? That sounds… challenging. It's always the wedding events, isn’t it? Everyone thinks they’re wedding planners just because they’ve watched a few episodes of that show with the scary lady. You have no idea. And then her mother started chiming in with ‘suggestions’. Honestly, I nearly walked out. It’s just… stressful. I’m starting to think I need a holiday. Somewhere far, far away from tulle and table settings. Sounds mental. I’d rather be layin’ bricks all day than dealin’ with all that. Least bricks don’t talk back. Though, bricks  are  heavy. Have you been seeing anyone new, Leo? You've been a bit quiet lately. Still seeing… what was her name? Chloe? Nah, Chloe and me called it quits a few weeks back. It just... didn't click y’know? Too much drama. She wanted me to be all different, go out more, be all fancy. I’m happy with a pint down the pub and a game of darts, really. Ooh, sorry to hear that, love. It's always rubbish when things don’t work out. You deserve someone who appreciates you  as  you are. Not trying to mould you into somethin’ you’re not.

Honestly, I'm  still  exhausted. Barcelona was amazing, don’t get me wrong, but five days of solid sightseeing takes it out of you. How was your weekend? Quiet, I assume, being the saint you are and working? Quiet-ish. Had a particularly rough patient on Friday night, so Saturday mostly involved collapsing on the sofa. Worth it though, knowing I helped. Barcelona sounds incredible though! You were going on about the Sagrada Familia for weeks leading up to it. Was it as breathtaking in person? Breathtaking is an understatement. Pictures genuinely don’t do it justice. It's… overwhelming. And the Park Güell! It was like stepping into a fairytale. I spent ages just wandering around, people-watching. Did you watch any TV at all? I missed the finale of 'Happy Valley'. Oh no! I completely forgot. I meant to record it, but the shift was mental. I’ll have to find it on catch-up. Was it good? Everyone's been raving about it. And back to Barcelona... you said “solid sightseeing”. Did you just do the tourist trail, or did you discover any little hidden gems? Mostly the tourist trail, I’ll admit. We did a walking tour which was brilliant, and the Gothic Quarter was amazing, just getting lost in those little streets. We found this tiny tapas bar, completely packed with locals, and the food was insane. Proper authentic stuff, not the tourist-trap paella. We attempted to go to a flamenco show, but it was booked solid. Apparently, you need to book ages in advance. Ugh, that’s so frustrating. Tapas sounds amazing though. I’m craving something other than hospital canteen food! How was the boyfriend? Did he behave himself? Last time you went away with him, there was that… incident with the lost wallet. Don't remind me! He was  perfectly  behaved, thankfully. He even remembered to pack the adapter, which is a minor miracle. He’s actually been really sweet since we got back, offering to do the washing up and everything. It’s almost suspicious. Oh dear. Maybe he feels guilty about the wallet? Or maybe he's realised if he wants more Barcelona trips, he needs to up his game. Honestly, you deserve someone who remembers adapters  and  keeps track of their belongings. You’re right. I know. It’s just… he’s a good guy, you know? Anyway, enough about my love life.

…and honestly, dealing with fourteen year olds arguing about TikTok trends  all  day just drains you, doesn’t it? It’s not the academic side, it’s the… the  drama . Endless, pointless drama. Tell me about it. I thought starting my own business would be drama-free. Ha! Turns out, convincing adults to part with their money is just a different flavour of teenage angst. At least they usually  have  the money. That’s… a very good point. What exactly  is  your business, again? I think we only briefly touched on it back at the hotel. Something tech-related, wasn’t it? Yeah, it is. It’s a software company. We develop apps – mostly for small businesses, helping them manage their inventory and stuff. It started, honestly, because my mum runs a little bakery in Ealing, and she was drowning in spreadsheets. I just thought, there  has  to be a better way. That’s lovely! A very practical beginning. Bit different from teaching history, which… well, let's just say the direct practical application isn’t always immediately obvious. Although, I do harp on about learning from the past, you know? Trying to avoid repeating mistakes. Doesn't always sink in with the TikTok generation though. I bet. My mum still mostly uses paper and pen, actually. Digital native I am not, apparently! She says it’s ‘more reliable’. It’s a battle. But that's how it began. It grew from there. I did the typical graduate thing – tried to get a 'proper' job at a bank – lasted about six months. Soul-destroying. Oh dear. A bank? You seem… vibrant. I can’t quite picture you behind a desk in a grey suit. Exactly! It was awful. Everyone seemed so… disengaged. And the whole structure felt so… rigid. I come from a fairly entrepreneurial family, you see. My grandfather ran a market stall, selling fruit and veg. My uncle had a taxi firm. It’s in the blood, I think. I realised I needed to  build  something, not just… maintain something. That makes sense. I come from a long line of teachers, actually. My mother, grandmother, great-grandmother… It felt almost obligatory, to be honest. And I enjoyed it, initially. Being able to spark an interest in history, to get them thinking… that's fulfilling. But the bureaucracy now… the endless paperwork, the constant changes to the curriculum… it's a weight.

Honestly, I’m dreading going back to that house. It's just…a lot right now, innit? Still on about Liam leaving his dirty plates for a week? Thought you were over that by now, love. You went on a right ramble about it last Tuesday. It’s not  just  the plates, Ben! It’s the principle of the thing. It’s the constant mess, the passive-aggressive notes… Honestly, living with him felt like being perpetually stuck in a mildly irritating argument. And now it’s just…Sarah. Alone with her essential oils and her ‘healing crystals’. Sarah's not  that  bad. She's just… into her stuff. And lets be honest, a quiet house sounds pretty good after Liam's bass rattling through the walls at 3am. Remember that time he decided to learn the electric guitar? I’m actively trying  not  to remember that time. It was traumatic. But Sarah... she’s just…presently unsettling. She keeps offering me sage “to cleanse my aura.” And she talks to her plants. By name. It's a bit much, even for me, and I used to collect Beanie Babies. Right, well, Beatrice the bear was a serious commitment, wasn’t she? But yeah, Sarah's a bit…out there. I think she genuinely believes the crystals are doing something. Remember when she tried to "align our chakras" before your exam? Don’t even  start . I nearly failed because I was too busy trying to figure out where my root chakra was supposed to be! Look, it’s not that I dislike her, it's more that I don’t understand her. And I need a housemate I can, you know, actually  relate  to. Someone who understands the importance of a clean kitchen and doesn't think a full moon affects the WiFi. Fair enough. It's a strange balance, isn’t it? Finding someone you can live with. It's not just about cleanliness, though. It's about compromise. Liam was a nightmare for mess, but he was always up for a night out. Sarah’s quiet, yeah, but she's always happy to share her herbal teas. Herbal teas that smell suspiciously like potpourri, you mean. I swear she’s trying to turn our kitchen into a Victorian apothecary. Have you spoken to her about it at all? Like, subtly hinted at maybe keeping the crystals…contained? I tried, briefly.

Right then. That’s a load off me shoulders. Queue was awful at the butcher’s, absolutely  awful . Old Mrs. Higgins was in front, taking ten minutes to decide between two sausages. Two! Like there’s a world of difference. Oh, don't start on Mrs. Higgins, Arthur. She’s a sweet woman, just a bit… deliberate. And you know how she likes her Cumberland sausages. Did you get the bread I asked for? The seeded bloomer? Seeded bloomer, seeded bloomer… Yes, yes I did. Right here. . Though I say, they’re getting smaller these loaves, aren't they? Used to be you could feed a family on one of them. Now it’s just a mouthful each. Inflation, I suppose. Everything’s going up. They are a bit on the small side. Still, better than that spongy white stuff they try to pass off as bread sometimes. Did you remember the milk? And the biscuits for your tea? Milk, yes. Two pints. And digestives. Your favourite. Though I tried to suggest gingernuts, you know. A bit of spice. You’re always so… predictable with your biscuits, Marjorie. Predictable is good, Arthur. Predictable means reliable. I like a digestive with my Earl Grey. It’s a comfort. Speaking of comfort, how are your knees doing after all that walking? I told you we should have taken the bus. They’re… protesting, let’s say. Not as sprightly as they used to be, are they? Though I managed to hold me own. Didn’t need no help from you, even though you kept hovering. Honestly, Marjorie, I’m not an invalid yet. Hovering is caring, dear. And you nearly tripped over that uneven paving stone outside the greengrocer's. I saw it happen! I was just being prepared. Besides, I wanted to admire young David’s display of plums. Beautiful they were, a lovely deep purple. Plums? You and your plums. Always fussing over the fruit and vegetables. I just need something to gnaw on with me tea. Honestly, it’s like you’re preparing for a royal banquet, not a simple supper for two. Well, a simple supper deserves nice ingredients, doesn't it? And I'm making that potato and leek soup you like so much. It will warm you up nicely, with this chill in the air. That sounds lovely, actually. Your soup is always top-notch. Much better than anything you get in those fancy restaurants.

Right, that’s a proper brew. Always better at your Mam and Dad’s, isn’t it? Though, don’t tell ‘em I said that. They'd never let me live it down. Yeah, it’s decent tea. Better than school dinners, anyway. Though that’s not exactly a high bar. School dinners were grim, lad. Grim. When Arthur and I were youngsters, it was mostly spam and watery cabbage. You lot are spoiled rotten with your choices. Aye, spoiled. Though I remember one dinner lady, Mrs. Higgins, used to sneak us extra custard. She had a heart of gold, that woman. Custard, eh? Luxury! Speaking of luxury, I’ve been meaning to ask, Dad, are you still having trouble with the telly? You mentioned last time you couldn’t get Now TV working. Oh, that confounded thing. Aye, still a bother. Keeps asking for a password, and I swear I’ve tried every combination imaginable! It’s all this modern technology, you see. Back in my day, you had one button, you turned it on, and Bob’s your uncle. I can have a look later, Grandad. I’m alright with that sort of stuff. It’s probably just cached data or something. Oh, you’re a clever lad, aren’t you? Always with your computers and your gadgets. Arthur used to take things apart just to see how they worked, then couldn’t put ‘em back together. Drove me round the bend. Well,  someone  had to understand how the world ticked, didn’t I? Though, admittedly, a few bits and pieces never quite made it back into working order. Remember that clock, love? The one your Auntie Brenda gave us? Don't even  start  on that clock, Arthur! It was a beautiful mantelpiece clock, and you ended up with springs and cogs scattered across the living room floor! She never forgave us. Sounds like a disaster. Disaster is putting it mildly! Brenda was furious. She said Arthur had a knack for demolishing perfectly good things. Now, about this week, are you two thinking of coming down to Hull for Friday night bingo? Oh, Mam, you know I have marking to do. GCSE papers don’t mark themselves, unfortunately. It’s a mountain of quadratic equations and geometry proofs. Dreadful, honestly. Though the pay keeps me in biscuits, so I suppose I shouldn't complain. Aye, the marking. A thankless task.

Right, so, this collagen stuff… honestly, I'm starting to think it’s all a load of marketing guff. My nan swears by it, says it’s done wonders for her joints, but she also believes in homeopathy. So… Nah, I’ve heard alright things. A mate of mine, proper into his fitness, uses it in his protein shakes. Says it helps with recovery. Though, knowing him, he probably also polishes his dumbbells every night. Recovery from  what  though? You two are barely capable of a leisurely stroll without needing a lie-down. Don’t get me started on the gym obsession. It's all performative. Harsh, Leo. Some of us actually  enjoy  trying to not resemble overripe avocados. Speaking of performing, have you seen that new tech? The Neuralink thing? Elon’s gone completely bonkers. Implanting chips in brains… Bit dystopian, innit? Reminds me of that Black Mirror episode… the one with the memory storage. Imagine losing all your embarrassing uni moments to a faulty update. God, the thought. My deleting history is long enough as it is. Speaking of uni, anyone heard from old Manby? Haven’t seen him post anything on Insta for ages. Last I recall he was going through some serious drama with that girl, Chloe. Manby? No, not a peep. He always did have a knack for disappearing off the face of the planet. Remember that time he went “off-grid” for a week and turned out to be volunteering at a llama sanctuary in Wales? Oh,  that  week. He told everyone it was a spiritual retreat. Llama sanctuary suddenly sounds less impressive. My mum was asking about him actually. Said she hasn't had a Christmas card from him in two years. She's convinced he's joined a cult. Your mum thinks everyone's joined a cult, Leo. Remember when she was convinced Mr. Henderson, the postman, was a member of the Freemasons? Classic. Still, it’s weird, isn't it? Losing touch with people like that. We all seemed so close at uni. Now it feels like… years ago. Actually, it  is  years ago. Bloody hell. It is a bit sad, yeah. Though some people you're better off without, to be honest. Remember Darren? The one who wore those… well, those  things  he called shirts? Oh god, the Hawaiian shirts. And the socks with sandals. The man was a walking fashion disaster.

Right, so, shopping list. Mum, are we still needing paracetamol? My head's been pounding a bit since… well, since the mosquito decided my arm was a buffet. Aye, put it on, love. And some antihistamine cream for that bite, you poor thing. It’s proper swelled up. Did you try that lavender oil I told you about? I did, it helped a little with the itching, but it’s still angry looking. Honestly, I don’t get why they even  exist , mosquitoes. Just…pointless, vicious little blighters. You shoulda just squashed it, then. Easy. Now, now, young man. Not everyone has the…resolve…to engage in immediate insecticidal action. Some of us prefer a more passive approach. Like, say, a fly swatter. Passive? You call waving a plastic thing around like a madman ‘passive’? It’s just delayed gratification for the squashing impulse! And honestly, Dad, you're terrible at it. You usually end up beating the furniture more than the bug. That’s a gross exaggeration. I’m merely…adjusting my technique. It’s about trajectory, you see. And swiftness of hand. Oh, here we go. The Consultant explains fly swatting. Honestly, John. Anyway, back to the list. Milk, bread, eggs… Need anything special for tea tomorrow? I was thinking a shepherd’s pie. Can we have chips with it, please? And gravy. Loads of gravy. Always. You live for gravy, don’t you? Speaking of living for things… has anyone seen what the Bolton Wanderers’ situation is? I saw a headline about a potential takeover but didn’t have time to read it. Oh, it’s all a bit messy, actually. A consortium is trying to buy the club, but there's a lot of back and forth with the current owners. Seems they’re dragging their heels. Typical. It's always something with Wanderers, isn’t it? It’s like the universe specifically targets us for footballing disappointment. Don't start on that now, lass. You'll get yourself all worked up. It’s just a game, at the end of the day. Though I admit, it's been a bit rubbish to watch lately. Rubbish is an understatement. We’re getting battered every week! We need a new striker, proper good one. Like Haaland, but… cheaper. A perfectly reasonable request. Easily attainable. You know, when I’m advising companies, I often use football clubs as an analogy for… Oh, here we go  again .

Honestly, P.E. is  the  worst. Mr. Davies made us do shuttle runs today. Shuttle runs! Like, what is this, the 1980s? Everyone was practically collapsing. Ugh, tell me about it. Ours was badminton, which sounds okay, but then he made us do drills for like, forty minutes. Forty minutes of hitting a shuttlecock back and forth. My arm feels like it’s going to fall off. Did you see Chloe nearly take out Mrs. Peterson with her racket? No! Seriously? Chloe’s a menace. Though, fair play to her for aiming at Peterson. She was  really  going on about the importance of proper technique. It's like, chill out, we’re just trying to have a laugh. Speaking of laughs, did you see that new video from ‘Sci-Guys’? The one about the exploding gummy bears? No! Exploding gummy bears?! Oh my god, I need to watch that. They’re so good at making science actually…fun. Unlike Mr. Henderson. He just drones on about osmosis. Osmosis! Who even cares about osmosis? Everyone should care about osmosis! It explains loads of stuff. Like why your fingers go wrinkly in the bath. But yeah, Henderson's a bit… monotone. He barely looks at us when he's talking. It's like we're a room full of potted plants. Totally! And the way he asks questions? "Can anyone  explain  the process of cellular respiration?" Like, no, Henderson. We’re 15, not qualified biochemists! It's intimidating. School is just… a lot. Have you seen what Maisie’s been posting on Instagram? It's all perfectly filtered selfies and 'relatable' quotes. It's so fake. Oh, don’t even get me started. It's like, she lives for the 'aesthetic' now. Remember when she used to just post pictures of her dog? Now it’s all perfectly curated 'vibes'. I know, right? And she’s been hanging around with Jess and Lily a lot lately. They’re so obsessed with those beauty Youtubers. I saw Jess trying to contour her nose like NikkiTutorials the other day. It looked… alarming. Oh dear. They really take that stuff seriously. It's a whole world I don't get. I'd rather spend my time drawing, honestly. Do you think Mr. Clarke would actually let us do a mural in the art room? I was thinking something with like, bioluminescent plants. Ooh, that’s a good idea!

Ugh, honestly. This is  brutal . I think this cold is actively trying to dismantle my internal organs. Sounds delightful. You’ve been sounding like a foghorn for the last twelve hours. Plenty of fluids, yeah? And resting? Cambridge is hardly the place to be traipsing around when you’re feeling poorly. Fluids, yes. Mostly tea, if I’m being honest. And a concerning amount of lemon and honey. Resting… well, I  tried  to work, felt guilty otherwise. Research doesn’t exactly do itself, even when your head feels like it’s full of cotton wool. Though honestly, staring at spreadsheets when you can barely focus feels… pointless. Pointless is a good word for it. You need to prioritise. Remember what happened last time you tried to power through? Ended up needing that doctor's appointment  and  a week off. It's just not worth it. Don’t remind me. That was… unpleasant. I swear, I think I had a mild form of food poisoning on top of everything else. Remember that dodgy takeaway near the lab? Oh god, yes. The one that looked like it hadn’t seen a health inspector in decades? I specifically told you not to go there. Honestly, you and your quest for the perfect Friday night curry… Hey! It smelled amazing! And I was starving! And it tasted… alright until about an hour later. Anyway, that’s ancient history. It's just, feeling grotty always makes me think about all the things I should be doing to be healthier. Like, I really should get the new booster. The updated COVID one? I had mine last week. Bit of a sore arm, but nothing major. You’re right though, it’s a good idea. Especially with winter coming. And given your track record this year… Don’t start. I feel like I’ve spent half the year battling some sort of lurgy. It’s just… hospitals make me so anxious. Even thinking about them… it’s the  waiting . And the smell. Honestly, it's awful. I know. It's not a fun place to be. But think of it as preventative, not reactive. It’s a quick jab, and it significantly lowers your risk. Plus, think of all the research you  could  do if you weren't perpetually sick. You’re employing logic. That's… unfair when I feel this rubbish. Speaking of things I shouldn’t be doing when sick… I was channel-hopping earlier and came across that ridiculous antiques show.

Right. “Quixotic.” Twenty-two points. Honestly, Dad, you let me have the ‘X’. I suspect a little favouritism. Nonsense, Eleanor. It was a perfectly legal play, and you earned it. Besides, someone needs to keep the score down, you're running away with this. Honestly, you and your vocabulary. Where  do  you learn all these words? It’s not from transcribing legal documents, is it? It  is  a good word, Eleanor. Though rather… pessimistic, isn’t it? All this talk of impractical dreamers. Not the spirit one wants to encourage in young people. Though I suppose, looking back, a few of my students were rather quixotic in their ambitions. Remember young Alistair Finch? Wanted to single-handedly save the rainforests with a ukulele. Alistair Finch! Good Lord. A lovely boy, frightfully untalented musician, bless him.
