Especially with the roof repairs still looming. Have you spoken to Graham about getting quotes again? He promised he would last week. Graham is… Graham. I left a note on his desk. He’s currently obsessed with some pigeon nesting on the fire escape. Says it’s a rare breed. Honestly, sometimes I think he spends more time observing avian life than managing the building! That sounds about right. I’ve caught him chatting to sparrows before. But seriously, the roof. We need to get that sorted before winter sets in properly. We don’t want another leak like last year. Remember the chaos that caused with the art exhibition? Don't remind me. Mrs. Dubois nearly had a fit. Thankfully, her paintings weren't  completely  ruined. It led to a very awkward conversation about insurance. Anyway, back to the hall. I’m thinking we could possibly squeeze the pottery classes into the small meeting room, but it’s a bit cramped, and it’s where we keep all the spare chairs. We could look at getting some folding chairs then? Something we can easily put away. I saw a good deal online the other week, and we could even get some nice colourful ones - brighten the place up a bit. It's all looking a bit beige at the moment, isn’t it? That’s not a bad idea. Brighten things up  and  solve a practical problem. Add it to the list. Speaking of lists, I was thinking about the storage room. It’s such a mess in there. We really need to have a proper clear-out.

Oh,  this  is proper comfort food. Honestly, I forgot how good a proper roast dinner could be. South Africa does lamb well, but roast potatoes…they're just not the same. Too much rosemary usually, and not enough crispy bits.      See? I  told  you Hereford was a good shout for a cottage. Proper countryside, good pubs, and clearly, someone who knows their way around a kitchen. Though, admittedly,  someone  did most of the work.      Hey now! I just provided the… expertise. You two were excellent peelers and parsnip-choppers. Don't undersell the importance of good prep! Besides, I needed a break from restaurant kitchens. This is therapeutic.      Mmm. This gravy is… exceptional.      Gravy  is  the key, isn’t it? My mother used to say a good gravy can solve most of life’s problems. She wasn’t wrong. Though she always made it with a splash of sherry. Liam, do you think a bit of sherry would have elevated this already delightful gravy?   Liam:   Dai, you and your sherry! It’s a classic, but I was going for a more traditional, beefy flavour. Though… I wouldn’t rule it out for next time. I did use a good red wine reduction, though.      Oh, red wine is lovely. Makes everything taste fancier, doesn't it? It's a good job I drove, otherwise, I'd be having a glass with this. Always loved a Sunday roast, even when my kids were little terrors, demanding Yorkshire puddings the size of their heads.   Sarah:   Yorkshire puddings… another thing we struggle with in South Africa. They just come out flat and sad. It's a science, isn’t it? The fat needs to be  smoking  hot. I tried once, and nearly set off the smoke alarm.   Rhys:   You're not alone! I’ve had a few Yorkshire pudding disasters. Remember that one Christmas, Mum? They resembled… well, let’s just say they didn’t resemble Yorkshire puddings.   Dai:   Ah, yes. That was the year we ate turkey sandwiches for a week to compensate. Your mother, Bronwen, she's a genius with a casserole, but baking isn't her forte. She  can  make a mean bara brith, though.   Bronwen:   Oh, here we go. Always the bara brith! Yes, I can make a good bara brith. It's a national treasure, after all. But honestly, I’m more of a savoury person. Give me a good cheese and onion pie any day.

…and honestly, the traffic was  brutal . Like, I aged five years just getting from the A19 to Durham. You wouldn't believe it. It was all slow-moving, tail lights, the whole shebang. Durham, eh? Visiting family again? Aye, mam and da’. Just a quick weekend. Da' was on about needing help with the garden – says his back’s playing up again. Though knowing him, it’s probably an excuse to get a brew and a biscuit out of me. Sounds about right. Dads are experts at that sort of thing. Mine's convinced he can’t change a lightbulb without endangering himself these days. And Durham's lovely, though, isn’t it? Really different vibe to down south. Oh, it is. Proper history, you know? It's beautiful, but a bit…slow. Everything down here feels so  fast  paced. You're always rushing. You wouldn’t catch anyone having a proper chat in a queue in Sunderland like you might in Harpenden. Probably not. We're all too absorbed in our phones, I suppose. Speaking of fast paced, how's work? Still wrestling with that massive text corpus? Wrestling is a good word for it. It's… a lot. We’re trying to tag everything for sentiment analysis. Apparently, knowing whether people are generally positive or negative about… garden gnomes… is vitally important to  someone . It's bizarre. It wouldn't hurt to have a holiday, honestly. Garden gnomes? Seriously? That confirms my suspicions that some of these data science jobs are just made up on the spot. You  need  a break. Remember how we were talking about Italy? Italy? Oh, aye! Florence. I was looking at flights last night, proper getting lost down a rabbit hole. It’s just…expensive, isn’t it? Even with a bit of saving, it feels a world away. It is, admittedly. But we could look at going shoulder season. September maybe? Fewer tourists, slightly lower prices. Plus, the sun's still decent. We could go wine tasting in Tuscany, eat loads of pasta… You're talking my language now. I saw a documentary about Florence the other day. All beautiful art and amazing food. Honestly, it made me wanna chuck it all in and become a gelato maker. You'd be a world-class gelato maker, I reckon. Although I suspect the corpus of data on gelato flavours would be equally bizarre. So, Italy aside, how’s Liam doing?

…and honestly, the whole thing with Mum’s appointment just felt so  rushed . They seemed determined to get her in, scan her, and get her out. No real explanation of what they were looking for, you know? Just “routine check-up”. Routine at her age feels a bit…ominous, doesn’t it? Ominous is right. They do that, don’t they? Like cattle. My sister, bless her, had a similar thing with her knee. They diagnosed arthritis in five minutes flat. Five minutes! She was practically begging the doctor to actually  look  at her. Exactly! And then trying to get follow-up information… it’s a nightmare. I’ve been on hold to Addenbrooke’s for nearly an hour three times this week. It's infuriating. Though, to be fair, they did say the scan results would go directly to Mum’s consultant. Consultants. They’re the worst for being unreachable. Mine… well, I had a bit of a scare last year, something they found on a chest x-ray. Took me a week to actually  speak  to him. A week of worrying myself sick. Oh dear, that sounds awful. It’s the uncertainty, isn't it? That’s half the battle. And with Mum… well, it's brought everything up, really. Dad’s passing, you know, it wasn’t… sudden, but it was quick. It didn't give anyone time to prepare. This feels different. There's a sense of… finality hanging over it, even before we know what's wrong. I understand that. My Nan, when she went... it felt like a relief, if I’m honest. She’d been poorly for so long, and she was in pain. But even knowing that, the actual  emptiness  afterwards… it knocked me sideways. It’s funny, isn’t it? How people grieve in such different ways? My brother, he barely said a word. Just went quiet. Oh, that’s so typical of David. He clams up. Always has. Mum’s worried about him, actually. She keeps saying he's not processing it properly. She’s trying to get him to talk, but he just shrugs her off. Says he's ‘fine’. Men, eh? Honestly. My husband’s the same. When his Grandad died, he just threw himself into work. Didn’t shed a tear. I kept asking him if he was okay, and he’d just say “Busy, love”. It's a generational thing, I think.

Right, that was lovely. Honestly, Sarah, your roast chicken is consistently  excellent . Even better than my mum’s, and I never thought I'd say that! High praise indeed, love. She’s a domestic goddess, your Sarah. And this Pinot Grigio…spot on with the chicken. A far cry from the stuff I get given at work ‘dos’, let me tell you. Mmm. Chicken was good. Leo! Put the phone down, darling. We’re having a conversation. It’s called ‘family time’. Remember that? Sorry. Just…checking something for school. History project. It's boring. History  is  pretty dull. Unless it’s about Romans or Vikings. Then it’s alright. How’s the proofreading going? Still drowning in student essays? Oh, you have  no  idea. It’s term time, which means a tidal wave of panicked undergraduates trying to meet deadlines. Honestly, the grammatical errors... I’ve started to see them in my  sleep . Though, the marketing side is picking up, thankfully. A local brewery wants me to revamp their social media. That’ll be a nice change of pace. Pictures of beer aren't exactly taxing to look at, are they? A brewery eh? Sounds good. More interesting than deciphering ‘their, there and they’re’ for the millionth time. My lot at work are driving me mad with a new logistical issue. We’re trying to get a shipment of components to the factory, but there’s been a hold up with transport. It’s all a bit chaotic, to be frank. What kind of components? Is it…car stuff? Actually, yes. It  is  car stuff. We supply parts for a new electric vehicle model. It's…complicated. Cool! My Dad’s really into cars. He’s always talking about bhp and torque and stuff. I haven’t got a clue what he means. Oh, bless him. That’s a classic Dad conversation. We're going to have to schedule some work experience for you boys. Perhaps something a little more engaging than essays. Leo, you’ve always been good with your hands…maybe engineering? No way. Too much maths. I’m thinking…something to do with computers? Coding, maybe? Coding is good, excellent actually. Huge demand for skilled coders. Though it requires focus, right? You need to be able to sit and concentrate for hours. Speaking of focus…remember that skiing trip we talked about? I was looking at chalets in Austria, and there’s one that looks absolutely perfect.

Honestly, looking back at these photos from Japan is making me ache to go back. Remember that little ramen shop in Kyoto? The one with the incredibly grumpy chef? Oh my  god , yes! The one where you tried to ask for extra noodles in Japanese and he just stared you down like you’d insulted his ancestors? It wasn’t  that  bad. He just… didn’t appreciate my enthusiasm. Though, I'm pretty sure “more noodles” ended up sounding like “I want to wrestle a carp.” It definitely had that vibe. Still, the ramen  was  amazing. And the whole city felt like stepping into a different world. I keep meaning to properly learn the language. I got as far as politely asking where the toilet is, which, let's be honest, is pretty essential. You’d be good at it. You pick up languages so quickly. I just… struggle with the politeness levels. It's terrifying. One wrong honorific and you've potentially caused an international incident. Speaking of learning things, did you ever finish that online photography course? Almost! I got stuck on the section about long exposure. It sounded so theoretically simple, but trying to get a decent shot without everything blurring into oblivion was… challenging. I've been meaning to practice. We’ve got a good spot down by the river, haven’t we? We do. Though, truthfully, everything around here is currently Badger-centric. Badger-centric? What do you mean? Old Man Hemmings next door is convinced he has a family of badgers living under his shed. He’s spent the last week building a sort of… badger observation post? It's a ridiculous little structure made of pallet wood and old netting. He offered to let me photograph them. No! Seriously? That’s amazing. And slightly concerning. Is he… feeding them? Apparently, he leaves out bowls of peanuts. I think he’s trying to lure out the 'patriarch'. He's named him Barnaby. Barnaby the Badger. I can’t. That's hysterical. Maybe if I bring my long exposure kit, I can get a dramatic, shadowy shot of Barnaby enjoying a peanut. It would be art! “Badger Noir” – the exhibit writes itself. You’re on. Though, I suspect Barnaby won't be posing. They’re remarkably elusive, those little blighters. Last night, I was trying to get some star trail photos, and the only movement I got was a rustling in the bushes and a lot of snuffling.

Right, honestly, that brisket is  something  else, Anya. Seriously. You’ve outdone yourself. It’s…it’s like my Nana used to make, but… better? I didn't even  know  brisket could taste like this. Oh, stop it, Leo, you’re making me blush! It’s my great-aunt’s recipe, passed down. Loads of paprika, a tiny bit of marmalade… the secret ingredient, don’t tell anyone. It’s a proper Jewish kitchen staple really. Did you ever get any good food in Ireland? When you were backpacking? Ireland… food wasn't the  point  of Ireland, if you know what I mean. It was more about… avoiding responsibility and contemplating the existential dread of graduating. Though, I did have some decent stew. Very rustic. And I did try black pudding. Once. “Rustic” is a polite way to put it, Leo. Black pudding’s an…experience. I've got a couple of Irish regulars at the cafe, they swear by it with everything. Speaking of experiences, did anyone see that photo Ben posted of himself skinny dipping in the Irish sea? Skinny dipping? Crikey! That's cold, even for a Brit. Fair dinkum, I wouldn’t touch the water over there with a ten-foot pole. It’s practically glacial. Though, I did do a bit of ocean swimming in Cornwall last summer. Relatively warm, comparatively speaking. Ben, you madman! I saw! It was tagged to me, naturally. He looked absolutely blue. And said something about “embracing the wild Atlantic.” Typical Ben. Did you at least have someone on lookout? Apparently, Chloe’s brother, Jamie, was ‘on lookout’. Mostly filming, though, apparently. He said it was for ‘posterity’. Honestly, the things that bloke does… It reminds me of that time we nearly got arrested for trying to climb Nelson’s Column. Oh god, don't  remind  me. My mum nearly had a heart attack when I told her. You two are relentless. You know, I was thinking, this brisket... it's better than anything I serve at the café. I need to get you to share that recipe, Anya. We could do a Jewish-inspired specials night. Actually, I've been trying to find a good recipe for rugelach. It’s proving elusive. Ooh, rugelach! That’s a tricky one. Do you want the apricot or chocolate kind? It’s all about the dough, honestly. My Nana used to swear by using cream cheese.

Honestly, I still can’t believe you’ve never been on Nemesis at Alton Towers.  Never . It’s practically a rite of passage. Look, I appreciate the cultural significance, alright? But dangling upside down, being whipped around like a ragdoll… it just doesn’t appeal. I’d rather spend my time, you know, actually  thinking  about things. Like…the inherent flaws in current border security protocols. Right. From rollercoasters to geopolitical strategy in one smooth transition. You’re something else, you are. And don’t pretend you don’t yell on The Mummy at least a little bit. Okay, okay, the Mummy is different. It’s dark, it’s enclosed… it’s vaguely archaeological. Relatable! But Nemesis? That's just…aggressive. Speaking of aggressive, have you seen the latest figures on attempted crossings? It’s a mess, honestly. The system is  so  overburdened. It is, isn’t it? It's awful what some of those people are going through. And the rhetoric around it all is just… exhausting. Anyway, back to more pressing matters. I’ve been trying to explain to my team the appeal of  Baldur’s Gate 3 . They think I've lost it spending my evenings meticulously planning character builds. Oh, they wouldn't be the first to think that. But seriously,  Baldur’s Gate 3  is a masterpiece. The level of choice…the narrative complexity… It's basically interactive storytelling. Have you rolled a dark urge character yet? Don’t even  start . I’m trying to play a relatively lawful good cleric and the dark urge whispers are relentless. It’s terrifying. It’s like the game is actively trying to corrupt me. Which, honestly, is probably what’s happening to my brain after all these hours. That's the beauty of it! It's testing your moral boundaries. It's…philosophical! It’s a far more enriching experience than, say, screaming your lungs out on a metal beast. You wound me. Although, have you seen that new ride they’re building at Thorpe Park? The Hyperion X? It’s supposed to be absolutely mental. Higher than Oblivion, faster… all the superlatives. See, this is what I mean. This relentless pursuit of bigger, faster, scarier. Isn’t there a point where it just becomes… pointless? Like, don’t you just feel sick afterwards? Sometimes. But sometimes it’s exhilarating! It’s a release. A good adrenaline dump. It’s not thinking about grant applications and statistical significance for a couple of hours.

…and honestly, the blisters are  brutal . I didn’t realise how much pressure you put on your palms when you’re learning to row. It's not like cycling, is it? You think you're just… pulling. Oh, darling, rowing is a whole other beast. I tried it once, years ago, with a friend’s husband. Thought it would be all Henley-on-Thames and gentle gliding. Turns out it’s mostly awkward flailing and a very red face. Did you at least manage to stay  in  the boat? Mostly. There was one… incident. Let’s just say I provided some unintentional entertainment for the other beginners. And the instructor had to fish me out. It wasn’t dignified. I’m thinking maybe kayaking would have been a better choice. Less to go wrong, you know? Kayaking is lovely. I did a bit of that in the Lake District a few years back. Beautiful, but you  need  the right gear. I got absolutely soaked, even with a waterproof jacket. Reminded me of that trip to Scotland with your Auntie Maureen. Remember she insisted on a floral summer dress, despite the forecast? Oh, God, yes! The picture is still legendary. She looked like a very disgruntled, very damp peony. She refused to acknowledge it was raining, insisted it was “atmospheric moisture”. And then complained for a week afterwards about catching a cold. She was a character, that one. I still miss those phone calls. Always full of stories, completely unfiltered. It's strange, isn’t it, how long it took us to actually  meet  her side of the family? Mum always said there was… distance. Distance is putting it mildly. It was practically a feud. Apparently, there was some disagreement over Grandad’s will. Something about a particularly valuable stamp collection. Mum never really talked about it. It was only after she passed, and I started digging through old letters, that I realised how fractured things were. I finally met Cousin David about five years ago. It was… awkward. We both just sort of circled each other, trying to find common ground. That sounds exhausting. It’s good you made the effort, though. Family is family, even the slightly estranged bits. Speaking of family… have you heard anything more about Uncle George? I know you were worried. Not much, sadly. Mum spoke to Auntie Carol yesterday. He’s… not doing well. They’ve started palliative care.

Dad, honestly, it's just…stressful. Like, all of it. And I keep getting these really weird texts from Liam. Just dots and dashes. Dots and dashes? Is he taking the mickey, lass? What’s he on about? I asked him what he meant and he just sent back more! I think… I think he's trying to send messages in Morse code? He says it's ‘secure’. Honestly, it’s more annoying than secure. It takes ages to decode! Morse code! Good grief. Kids these days. Back in my day, ‘secure’ meant writing it in invisible ink with lemon juice. Simpler times. You should just tell him to text you normally. What did you get back, anyway? Anything important? Just… "Meet me at the usual". Which is helpful, considering the ‘usual’ is anywhere within a five mile radius of the city centre. It's probably about results day, isn't it? Everyone's being all cryptic. Aye, probably. They're all nervous, same as you. Don't let it get to you too much, alright? Whatever happens, happens. You've worked hard. Speaking of things getting to you, you still using that phone I got you? Vodafone giving you trouble again? It’s fine, yeah. No signal problems  yet . But the battery life is shocking. I have to carry a portable charger everywhere. And the camera is… well, it's not great. I saw Chloe's new phone, and the pictures are amazing. Phones these days. All bells and whistles. When I got my first mobile, it was brick-sized and could barely make a call. Remember how we used to have to actually  remember  numbers? Now everyone’s glued to their screens, thinking the phone remembers everything for them. My memory's going, though, I’ll admit. Can't even remember where I put my glasses half the time. You left them on top of the glass water bottle this morning. Again. Did I? See? Told you my memory's shot. Still, better than relying on all these fancy gadgets. Anyway, no stressing over phones. Are you sorted for stationery? Pens, paper, the works? You'll need it all when you get to uni. Nearly. I’ve got most of it, but I need a new set of highlighters. And a proper folder, not just a flimsy plastic one. I was looking on eBay actually, saw a really good one.

… Honestly, this dissertation is killing me. Absolutely killing me. I’ve been staring at this screen for eight hours and I’ve written, like, two coherent sentences. Tell me about it, man. I’m drowning in readings for Professor Davies’ module. He expects us to have absorbed the entire history of post-structuralism  before  next week. It’s mental. Davies, yeah, he’s a proper academic, innit? Lives in a world of his own. But my problem isn’t the reading, it's actually  writing  the thing. I keep getting distracted. YouTube rabbit holes, mostly. Did you see that video of the robot trying to make a perfect omelette? No way! A robot omelette? Send me the link. But seriously, you gotta lock yourself away. Library, coffee shop, somewhere that isn’t your room. This place is too comfortable. Too many distractions. Plus, remember what happened last time you tried to work here? The FIFA tournament raged on 'til 3 AM. Don’t remind me. Lost a fortune to Liam, I did. But it’s just… hard to focus. I keep thinking about… well, about getting out of here. Like, properly out. You mean after uni? You’ve never really talked much about what you wanna do after, have you? Always just assumed you'd drift into something in tech, right? Yeah, that was the plan. But lately… I’ve been obsessed with Japan. Honestly, obsessed. I’ve been watching travel vlogs, learning basic Japanese on Duolingo, the whole shebang. Japan? That's a bit random, bruv. What sparked that? I don’t know, really. It just… looks incredible. The culture, the food, the tech… even just the  order  of everything. London’s chaotic, yeah? But Tokyo looks… pristine. Efficient. And I’ve always been into Japanese video games, so maybe that’s played a part. I can see that. I’ve always fancied going to Japan myself. The food alone would be worth the flight. Ramen, sushi… man, my mouth’s watering just thinking about it. But it’s expensive, isn’t it? Ridiculously. That’s the problem. I was thinking, maybe a teaching assistant thing? Like, teach English over there? I’ve been researching it. Apparently, the pay isn’t amazing, but it covers rent and living expenses, and you get a visa. Plus, it’d give me a chance to actually  live  there, learn the language properly, you know?

Oh, this one! This was taken at Buckfast Abbey, wasn’t it? Just a couple of weeks ago. Honestly, the gardens were looking  stunning . Did you manage to get any good pictures, Margaret? I did, actually. Mostly of the bees, though. They were all over the lavender. Properly buzzing! You know how I am with bees. Old Mr. Henderson would have  loved  to see them. He always kept a little patch for them in his garden. Henderson? Good man, Henderson. Kept a meticulous ledger, that one. Always paid his taxes on the dot. Unlike some… Oh, Granddad, don’t start on politics first thing! It's a Sunday afternoon. Though, I  did  see something on Facebook about… well, apparently there’s a new documentary about David Cameron and offshore accounts. Honestly, the audacity! Facebook, eh? I still don’t entirely trust it, you know. Too much… information. And people putting  everything  online. I saw Brenda next door posting pictures of her dinner last night. Honestly! That  is  Brenda. But it’s handy for keeping up with everyone, isn’t it? Especially the family. Saw little Emily’s dance recital video. She’s getting so big! Speaking of things growing, my hip is definitely  not  getting any younger. Though I managed to get the car MOT’d yesterday, that was a palaver. Young man at the garage tried to tell me I needed new tyres. Rubbish! Plenty of tread left on them. Just trying to fleece an old man. Oh, those garages! Always finding something. Did you argue with him, Arthur? You’re a stubborn one, you are. Stubborn? I simply pointed out the facts! And reminded him I've been driving longer than he’s been alive. He backed down quickly enough. Though my back was aching something awful afterwards. Getting in and out of that car is becoming a real chore. That’s why I was thinking... Remember how we talked about maybe doing a cruise next year? Something a bit easier than driving all over Europe? The Mediterranean, perhaps? I saw a really good deal to Italy and Greece. All-inclusive, so you wouldn’t have to worry about a thing. A cruise… hmm. I’ve always been a bit wary of those. All that being stuck on a boat. And the insurance! It would cost a fortune just to insure Arthur’s hip! My hip is perfectly insured, thank you very much!

Honestly, you two look  relaxed . Proper relaxed. Did Belgium live up to the hype, then? Mum, you were so stressed about the driving beforehand. Relaxed is an understatement, love. It was… restorative. Though, ‘stressful’ is putting it mildly about the driving. Your mother nearly had a coronary the first time we hit a roundabout. They’re  everywhere ! And massive. Don’t even get me started on the roundabouts, David! Honestly, I thought we were going to end up in a ditch more than once. And the sat nav… Oh, the sat nav! It kept trying to take us down what were essentially bike paths! Oh no! Did it really? You know Dad, he trusts a sat nav more than his own instincts. That's putting it nicely. I was convinced it was deliberately trying to sabotage the holiday. Kept sending us through these tiny, cobbled streets in Bruges. I swear, one wrong move and we’d have lost a wing mirror. Worse, it didn’t account for the different road markings. Everything’s a bit… looser over there. And the lanes! So narrow! I was constantly worried about scraping the car. And the speed limits kept changing. One minute 50, the next 30… completely random! Sounds chaotic, honestly. But worth it for the waffles, I presume? I saw pictures, they looked incredible. Were they as good as everyone says? Oh, darling, the waffles were  divine . Proper Belgian waffles, with everything on them. Strawberries, chocolate, cream… I’m putting on weight just thinking about it. We went to this little place in Ghent, and they had a waffle bar. A whole bar dedicated to waffles! And the chocolate, don’t forget the chocolate. I brought you some, actually. It’s in the bag. Don’t tell your brother, he’ll want it all. Oh, brilliant! Thanks Dad. That’s very thoughtful. I’ve been craving something sweet all day. What about the other food? Was it mostly just waffles and chocolate? No, no, they did really good mussels. We had them in Brussels, with frites, of course. And the beer! They take their beer very seriously. David tried a different beer with every meal. It’s a national pastime! And a very good one, I might add. The service in the restaurants was a bit slower than we’re used to, though. You had to really flag someone down if you wanted another drink.

Right, I  think  this is finally thickening up. It smelled promising, but honestly, after last week’s ‘attempt’ at risotto - which, let’s be honest, resembled wallpaper paste - I'm not holding my breath. Wallpaper paste is a bit harsh, darling. It was… enthusiastically creamy. And you were experimenting! That’s what good cooks do. Though perhaps less enthusiastically next time. What  is  this, anyway? Smells vaguely… autumnal. It’s supposed to be a butternut squash and sage soup. I saw Delia Smith do it on the telly, looked simple enough. And definitely less risk of turning into a solid block than risotto. She made it look so effortless, didn’t she? Everything she does looks effortless. Delia makes breathing look effortless. She’s a national treasure. Although, I suspect there's a whole team of people fluffing her cushions and pre-chopping the onions off-camera. Speaking of autumnal, did you see Fiona posted pictures of her garden? Absolutely  covered  in chrysanthemums. Oh, Fiona and her chrysanthemums! Always meticulously arranged. She’s very…aesthetic. It’s lovely, don’t get me wrong, but I’m more of a wildflower sort of person. A bit chaotic, like me. Speaking of aesthetic, have you tried that new perfume, ‘Midnight Bloom’? Sarah was wearing it yesterday. Midnight Bloom? No. Is it one of those ones that smells like everything and nothing at once? I’m quite attached to my Chanel No.5, thank you very much. A classic for a reason. Though it does rather cling, doesn’t it? People know I’ve been in the room long after I’ve left. Oh, it’s definitely powerful stuff. Sarah said it’s supposed to smell like night-blooming jasmine and something called 'ambergris'. Sounds rather exotic. It didn’t really suit her, though. She's a bit…brighter, you know? Needs something a little softer. She’s got that really clear, precise accent… it’s very…  London . London? What do you mean? Everyone sounds like they're from London these days. It's a creeping monoculture. Although, thinking of accents, I was on a video call with Hamish this morning. Still sounds like he’s just stepped off the train from Edinburgh. Proper rolling ‘r’s and everything. Oh, Hamish! I haven’t ‘spoken’ to him properly on Facebook in ages. Just the usual likes and comments on kitten videos. He always struck me as fiercely Scottish, even when we first met him at university.

…and honestly, the heat! I’d prepared for warm, of course, but Queensland in December is another thing entirely. It just…sits on you. Sticky heat. Quite unlike a pleasant English summer day. You didn’t find that, did you, Arthur? You spent a good deal of time there, I understand. Aye, Queensland. Right up in Cairns, mostly. And you're spot on, Margaret. It  is  a different heat. Like being wrapped in a warm, damp towel. But you get used to it, after a fashion. Though I must say, I always appreciated a good air-conditioned pub when I was there. And the flies! Don’t get me started on the flies. Flies are a constant, aren't they? I was only in Sydney, mind. A bit further south. Still warm, but manageable. Though the sun… even with factor 50, I looked like a lobster after a day at Bondi. Oh, Bondi! I didn’t venture quite that far. Mostly stayed around Brisbane. My daughter, Emily, she’d moved out there with her husband – he was doing some sort of consultancy work, all very hush-hush. Lots of suits. Speaking of which, did you notice how…how  relaxed  the business attire was? I’m used to seeing men in proper suits, even in warmer weather, back home. But over there, it was linen shirts and chinos. Looked like they were going for a picnic, not sealing million-dollar deals! That’s the Australian way, lass. Less fuss, more practicality. I found the same. They’re not so bothered about appearances. Though I do remember one young man, selling me some insurance – couldn’t have been more than twenty-five – who was wearing a very loud Hawaiian shirt. I thought, ‘Good heavens, you’re trying to convince me to invest my money, put a tie on!’ But he did the job, fair enough. It’s interesting, isn't it, how ingrained those expectations are? I was lecturing at a university there for a semester. The professors were similarly casual. I initially felt terribly underdressed in my usual tweed! It took me a week to realise nobody was judging. Tweed! Oh, you wouldn't get away with tweed in Brisbane. People would think you were mad! It's a world away from Almondsbury, let me tell you. Though, when I first left, I kept expecting to hear a Bristolian accent. Silly, I know.

…and honestly, the algorithm is  determined  to show me videos of people unboxing things. Unboxing! What is the appeal? It's just… cardboard. And plastic. And manufactured excitement. Oh, I know! It's bizarre, isn't it? My feed is full of skincare routines that cost more than my rent. It's completely unrealistic. Though, I have to admit, sometimes I get sucked in. It's a weird kind of passive entertainment. Passive is the word. It’s brain-rotting. I tried deleting the apps for a week, you know. A digital detox. It lasted… three days. I felt so disconnected. Which, paradoxically, made me want to reconnect  more . It's a vicious cycle. I completely understand. I tried limiting myself to half an hour a day. Failed miserably. It’s designed to be addictive, isn’t it? Like those slots machines. Little dopamine hits every time you get a ‘like’. Exactly! And the comparison! Oh, the comparison. Everyone's life looks so… curated. So  perfect . You forget that people only show you what they  want  you to see. It’s not real life. I saw Penelope’s latest holiday photos, all turquoise water and cocktails… she was complaining to Mum last week about a leaky roof and a dodgy washing machine. Oh, Penelope. Always the picture of glamour. Speaking of which, have you been watching anything good on TV lately? I've been trying to avoid it, honestly. It feels like another time suck. But my housemate is obsessed with that new historical drama, “The Serpent’s Crown.” He says it's brilliant. Historical dramas aren't really my thing. I did start watching “Happy Valley” again. Sarah Lancashire is just phenomenal, isn't she? So gritty and believable. Though, it is rather bleak. I need something a bit lighter after that. I’ve been listening to podcasts more. Oh, podcasts! Yes! What are you listening to? I'm currently hooked on "Maintenance Phase". It's about the history of wellness and weight loss and it’s just… fascinating. It completely deconstructs all those diet myths we've all grown up with. Ooh, that sounds interesting! I’m doing one called “You’re Wrong About”. They pick a person or event that’s been misunderstood or misremembered by the public and really dig into the details. They did a really good one on the DC sniper case. Quite disturbing, actually.

Right, so, swimming is definitely on for Saturday morning. Though someone was  very  insistent on spending the whole time pretending to be a mermaid again, weren't you, Lily? I  am  a very good mermaid, Mummy. I can hold my breath for ages! Not as long as a whale! Whales don’t need to breathe! That’s… debatable, Leo. Whales definitely need to breathe, just not in the same way we do. Anyway, after swimming, we need to quickly get ready because… remember what we promised ANON? Pippy! And Blue Peter! Can we take Pippy to the circus? Well, that’s the question, isn't it? I'm not sure the circus is the  best  place for a slightly over-enthusiastic, fluffy unicorn. It might get lost. Or trampled. Trampled by elephants! Possibly, yes. Though I think ANON’s circus is mostly acrobats and jugglers. Still, best to leave Pippy at home, I think. We're going to help ANON with something very important, remember? Getting a photograph for their Blue Peter badge! Oh! The one with all the sparkly bits? The very same. Apparently, the judges are really keen to see everything ANON’s been doing with the travelling circus. It’s a pretty big deal, having a Blue Peter badge. Do you remember when I told you about trying to get one when  I  was little? No. You were a baby! Very funny. I was not a baby! I was… considerably smaller. I sent in a drawing of a rather lopsided badger, but it wasn’t quite good enough. Was it a  really  lopsided badger? It was… artistically challenged. Anyway, we need to think about the photo. Maybe a nice one of ANON doing a trick? Or all of us with the circus van? I want to be the ringmaster! With a top hat! That would be brilliant, Leo! We'll see if we can find a top hat. Right, things are getting a bit complicated. This also reminds me, we need to check our passports are still valid. We might need them if ANON ever decides to take the circus on a worldwide tour. Do passports have sparkly bits? Not usually, sweetie. They mostly have stamps and pictures of you. Speaking of pictures, do you know how old ANON is? I keep forgetting! Old! Like… seventeen? No, not  quite  seventeen. They're actually only fourteen. A remarkably talented fourteen-year-old, honestly.

Right, so… that was awkward. Proper awkward. Awkward how? Don’t tell me your mum tried to set you up with old Mr. Henderson from down the street again. No, no, worse. Well, not  worse  exactly, just… different. It was Liam. Liam? As in, your boyfriend Liam? What did he  do ? Well, he didn’t…  do  anything, exactly. He just… mentioned something. And then I asked a follow-up question. A really, really nosy follow-up question. Oh dear. Go on. You’re killing me with suspense. And is tea strong enough for this story? Because I think I might need it. It’s as strong as I could make it. Okay, so we were, y’know… being intimate. And things… weren’t exactly going as planned. And he kind of mumbled something about being stressed with uni and it affecting things. Okay… that’s… relatable. Uni stress is a killer. Affecting things how? Affecting his… ability to, um, perform. He didn’t say it like  that , obviously. He was all vague, saying things weren’t “cooperating”. But I, being the brilliant conversationalist I am, just blurted out, “Oh, do you mean like… erectile dysfunction?”  You did not!  Oh my god, Chloe! I did! I completely did! And the look on his face! It was a mixture of mortification and… I don't know, maybe a tiny bit of relief that I’d actually  said  it? That is… spectacularly bad. But also, kind of brave of you, I guess? Most people would have just pretended not to hear. Brave? It was tactless! I just… I always feel like I have to fill the silence. Especially when things are a bit awkward already. It’s a terrible habit I picked up from my dad. He'd just yack on and on about anything to avoid quiet moments. I know the type. My grandad was the same. So, what happened then? Did he confirm it was…that? He hemmed and hawed for a bit, said it might just be a one-off, pressure, stuff like that. Then he looked  really  sad. Like I’d ruined something. Oh, Chloe. That’s rough. He probably just felt vulnerable. It’s not exactly easy to talk about stuff like that, y’know? Especially for lads. There's still so much pressure on them. I know, I know. I just felt awful afterwards. Like I’d interrogated him about his… plumbing.

Right, honestly, this cauliflower cheese is going to be  amazing  with the roast tomorrow. I’ve used a proper mature cheddar this time - but it’s still going to need a good dose of that 0 calorie syrup to make it properly… well, cheesy without the syns. Oh, good shout with the syrup. I always forget about that! Is it the golden syrup one you got? It’s the only one that doesn’t taste… chemically. Though, let’s be real,  all  0 calorie syrups taste a bit artificial, don’t they? They do, sadly. It’s a necessary evil. I was eyeing up a chocolate one earlier, but I figured that was edging a little too close to treat day territory. Speaking of which… Saturday. What are we thinking? Full-blown fakeaway? Pizza? Ooh, pizza sounds GOOD. But maybe something a bit… less regretful? I was thinking maybe burgers? We can do them really well, use the Quorn patties, loads of salad… Frylight instead of oil. We can even get those wholemeal buns from Sainsbury's – they’re surprisingly decent. They have the best Quorn range, don’t they? Better than Tesco, definitely. Definitely Sainsbury’s for Quorn. Though, morally, I feel like I should be buying more from the local shops. But convenience… and cost! This veg box delivery is saving my life, though. Honestly, the amount of veg we get for the price is incredible. It makes me feel less guilty about the syrup. That’s a good justification! And it forces us to actually  use  vegetables, which is always a win. Remember that time we got a massive box of parsnips and just… let them go off? Don't remind me! It was shameful. I think that’s when we realised a weekly delivery was better. Anyway, back to syns. I'm convinced my scales are lying to me. I was the same weight this morning as I was three days ago, even though I’ve been sticking to the plan. It’s infuriating! Scales are the enemy, honestly. They’re just designed to make us miserable. I read somewhere that they can fluctuate by a couple of pounds depending on hydration levels and…stuff. Don’t focus on the number. Focus on how your clothes feel. True. These jeans  are  feeling a bit looser. I just… I have that target in my head, you know? Trying to lose another stone before… well, before anything.

Right, so I’ve had a proper look at prices for the Greek islands. Santorini is…well, it’s beautiful, but  eye-wateringly  expensive. Even for a week. Santorini’s always been a bit of a banker for price, hasn't it? All that caldera view premium. What about Crete? You mentioned Crete last week. Crete is much more reasonable. And bigger. More to  do  if the weather turns a bit dodgy. I was looking at a little villa near Chania. It has a tiny plunge pool. A plunge pool sounds perfect. I’m definitely leaning towards Crete. Less…Instagram influencer traffic, too, I reckon. Remember that awful time in Barcelona? Felt like queuing for everything. Oh, god, Barcelona. Never again. Especially not during school holidays. It's just a jostle, isn't it? Alright, Crete it is then, provisionally? I’ll start looking at flights. What sort of dates were you thinking? I was hoping for…mid-September? Mid-September's good. After the school rush, but still warm enough for swimming. Though honestly, even a slightly chilly sea wouldn’t bother me after this summer. I’ve started dreaming of wearing a cardigan again. Tell me about it. I feel like I’ve lived in shorts and a t-shirt for three months straight. Speaking of clothes… I was thinking about finally getting that tattoo. Oh? Still pondering the floral sleeve? I thought you’d decided against it. Not the sleeve. That was a bit…ambitious. But I saw this artist online, she does really delicate botanical illustrations. I’m thinking a small sprig of lavender, maybe, on my wrist? Something understated. Lavender suits you. Bit more sensible than a full-on rose bush wrapping around your arm, anyway. What made you decide now? I don’t know. I just feel… restless. Like I need to mark myself, I suppose. Which sounds incredibly dramatic when I say it out loud. It's probably because Mr. Harrison at work is driving me up the wall again. He's decided  now  is the time to reorganise the filing system. After fifteen years! Harrison. Predictably infuriating. You need a holiday  and  that lavender tattoo just to recover from him. Honestly, the man thrives on minor administrative chaos. It’s true. He’s like a tiny, beige dictator. You wouldn’t believe the email he sent about the colour coding of folders. It was three paragraphs long.

Honestly, Margaret, this view from your holiday… it’s breathtaking. The colours are just… well, they're not quite Crickhowell, are they? But close. Very close. Did you send this to deliberately taunt me with sunshine? Possibly! A little bit of sun deprivation guilt, perhaps. It  was  lovely, truly. Though a bit crowded. And the price of a pint near the harbour… criminal, I tell you. Criminal. But yes, wanted you to see it. Remind you that somewhere, warmth exists. Warmth exists in a good book and a roaring fire, thank you very much. Although, I admit, a week in the Outer Hebrides sounds… restorative. Speaking of which, have you given any more thought to Alistair’s 70th? It’s looming, you know. I have. I’ve been sounding out a few people. Fiona suggested a small gathering at The Old Mill, just family and a close circle. She thinks trying to wrangle everyone for anything larger will end in disaster. And frankly, she’s probably right. What do you think? The Old Mill is a good shout. Cozy, and they do a decent set lunch. Though, knowing Alistair, he’ll want to hold court and deliver a ‘state of the nation’ address to anyone unfortunate enough to be within earshot. Exactly! And we’ll need to ensure there’s plenty of single malt on hand to facilitate that. I was thinking we could ask Edward to do a little something with the music. He’s been practising that dreadful jazz piano again. Dreadful is a strong word, David.  Unique  is perhaps more accurate. Though, yes, a touch of musical distraction might be helpful. What about a cake? Who’s doing the cake? That’s where I'm stuck. Shirley offered, bless her, but her last attempt at a Victoria sponge resembled something excavated from an archaeological dig. Perhaps we should just bite the bullet and get one from that bakery in town? The French one? Excellent plan. No need to risk culinary catastrophe. Although… Shirley’s heart is in the right place. Right, so Old Mill, music slightly off-key, professionally-made cake. We’re making progress. Now, what about this weekend? Any plans? I was hoping we could finally tackle the garden shed. It’s looking rather…prehistoric. Oh, not the shed. Anything but the shed! I promised Brenda I’d help her with something at her place. Some sort of tech issue.

Right, so, the plan is still on for drawing pictures for the families coming from Syria, yeah? Mrs. Davies at school said they’d really appreciate something to brighten up their new homes. Is it for  real  people, Mummy? People who don’t have houses? Sadly, yes, darling. Their houses weren’t safe anymore, so they had to leave everything behind and come here. It must be very scary. I’m drawing a chair! A super-fast racing chair! It’s got flames! Vrooom! That's… a very impressive chair, Leo. Perhaps we could draw some chairs  for  the families? Proper chairs, you know, the kind people sit on in their living rooms. But chairs are boring! Flames are much better. They can be, but maybe a nice comfy chair is something they'd  really  like. Remember when Grandma got her new armchair? How happy she was to curl up with a book? Grandma's one’s really squishy! And smelly of biscuits. It does have a certain… biscuit aroma. But the point is, a chair can be a good thing. What kind of chair should we draw, then? A big comfy armchair? Or maybe a smaller one? A sparkly one! With wings! Like a fairy chair! That… sounds lovely, but maybe something a bit more practical. Do you know what different kinds of chairs are called, Leo? Umm… chair? And… dining chair! We have those. And… Daddy’s office chair! It spins! Exactly! Different chairs for different jobs. So, what would a family need a chair  for ? For reading stories! And for watching telly! Perfect! So, we could draw a chair for reading, a chair for watching TV… What about the colours? What colours make you feel cosy and safe? Blue! Because that’s the colour of superheroes! Pink! And purple! And glitter! Everything sparkly! Okay, okay, we can definitely incorporate some sparkle. But maybe not  too  much. Now, I was thinking about school today. They’ve started talking about tests again. Tests are mean! I don’t like tests. I know, sweetheart. They can be a bit stressful. But they're just a way for the teachers to see what you're learning, and where you might need a little extra help. It's a bit like… drawing a picture of a chair to see if we understand what a chair  is . I understand chairs! You sit on them.

…and honestly, I’m just really worried about her. She's barely slept since Leo was born, apparently. Says he’s lovely, of course, but she's a complete mess. Sarah? Still? I thought things might have settled down a bit by now. It's been… what, three months? Three months and a day, if you must know. She texted me this morning, said she accidentally put salt in his bottle instead of sugar. Apparently, he  screamed  the house down. Oh, God. That’s… rough. She always was a bit of a worrier though, wasn’t she? Remember when she convinced herself that organic carrots were actively harmful? Oh,  please . Don't remind me. The debate at the farmer's market! Honestly, she was arguing with Old Man Hemmings for a good twenty minutes. But this feels different, doesn’t it? It’s not just neurotic worrying. She sounds genuinely… overwhelmed. It  is  different. Having a baby changes things. It’s a complete upheaval. I mean, you already know that, thinking about it. It's easy to give advice from the outside, but it's completely different being  in  it, sleep deprived and covered in… well, you know. Everything. Exactly. And Mark isn’t exactly helping, apparently. She said he’s been ‘managing’ the situation, which, as far as I can gather, means handing Leo to her and then disappearing into his study to “catch up on work.” Mark! Seriously? He always struck me as the more level-headed one. Thought he’d be more hands-on. That’s what I said to her! Well, not in those exact words. I didn’t want to come across as judgmental. I just… I suggested maybe they could talk about sharing the load a bit more evenly. She just sighed and said he’s “really stressed” about his new project. Honestly, that's infuriating. A new project doesn't give him a free pass to abandon ship. She needs support, not excuses. It makes me think of Helen and David, actually. They’re so good at it, aren’t they? Always bouncing off each other, sharing everything. They are. It’s almost sickeningly perfect sometimes. Though, you know Helen. She probably has a colour-coded spreadsheet for nappies and feeds. Probably. But even spreadsheets are better than what Sarah’s dealing with. Do you think we should just go round there? Just… pop in with some biscuits and see how she’s really doing?

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Just… green. And quiet. London feels like a constant thrumming headache these days. Did you see that article about the congestion charge going up  again ? Don’t even. It’s highway robbery, literally. Though, thinking about it, did you hear about old PC Davies getting a commendation? Apparently, he talked a bloke down from a rooftop just using… observational comedy. PC Davies? Observational comedy? Is this the same PC Davies who once tried to arrest a scarecrow because he thought it was a suspicious person? The very same! Apparently, the guy on the roof was a struggling stand-up. Davies started pointing out the flaws in his material, the predictable punchlines, the lack of stage presence… the guy just… deflated. Started laughing. Came down. It's all over the local paper. That is… astonishing. And utterly horrifying. It feels like a very specific brand of Norfolk policing. It’s almost… superstitious, isn’t it? Like, ‘if you can make someone laugh, you’ve disarmed them.’ Maybe! Old Norfolk is steeped in that sort of thing, isn’t it? All the rural traditions and… well, let's call them 'peculiarities'. My Nan used to insist on hanging Rowan branches over the door to ward off evil spirits. Even in London, she’d have a little twig tucked away somewhere. Oh, my Auntie Brenda was the same! Except hers was lavender. Said it kept the negativity away. It did smell nice, I’ll give her that. Though it didn't stop her complaining about the neighbours. Speaking of negativity, how are you feeling about the university’s push for more publicity? They want us to be ‘visible experts’ on everything now. It's exhausting, isn’t it? I got another email this morning, listing potential media outlets and ‘key messages’ for my research on… 18th-century agricultural practices. Who  wants  to hear me discuss turnips on BBC Radio 4? Exactly! They want us to be like… celebrity academics. It feels so performative. And completely misses the point of actually  doing  the research. I swear, half my time is spent writing press releases instead of papers. It’s all about league tables and student recruitment, isn’t it? They think a bit of media buzz will magically attract better applicants. I'm not convinced. Though, I did overhear Professor Armitage bragging about his recent TV appearance. Apparently, he spent the entire segment talking about his collection of vintage tractors.

Honestly, Dad, you wouldn't  believe  the state of my phone battery. It’s just… draining so fast now. I’m convinced it knows I have an essay due and is actively sabotaging me. Sabotaging, is it? Phones, honestly. All these fancy gadgets. Back in my day, a phone was for calling people. Not for… whatever it is you youngsters do with ‘em. Is it a new one then? You had a perfectly good one last time I saw you. It’s about three years old now, which apparently is ancient in phone years. I've been looking at getting a new one, but they’re ridiculously expensive. And then you have to transfer everything over… it's a whole  thing . A whole thing. Everything's a ‘whole thing’ these days. Reminds me of when we were trying to move that wardrobe of your Nan’s.  That  was a whole thing. Needed three blokes and a pulley system. Speaking of moving, have you given any thought to finding a place near the university next term? I have, but it’s so competitive! And expensive. I was thinking about maybe just staying here a bit longer if that’s alright? It saves a fortune, and I can actually save up for, you know, a phone that  doesn’t  hate me. Course, love. Stay as long as you need. Your mother and I are happy to have you. Though, the house is getting a bit… cluttered, isn't it? All your books and bits and bobs. And truthfully, I wouldn’t mind having the spare room back for all my… acquisitions. Acquisitions? You mean antiques? You’ve been spending a fortune at those car boot sales again, haven’t you? What’ve you got this time? Another chipped teapot? Now, hold on a minute! This isn't just  any  chipped teapot. This is a Victorian Minton, and it’s got a rather interesting maker's mark. I’ve been doing a bit of research. It could be worth a pretty penny. Though, don’t tell your mother. She thinks I waste my money. I won't. Although, she's not wrong, Dad. You did buy that ‘antique’ barometer that didn't actually work. It  looked  good! And I got a bargain. Speaking of bargains, saw a van for hire down at Henderson’s. Thought about maybe going down to the Great Dorset Steam Fair next weekend, if you’re free.

Honestly, it’s just infuriating. They’re really going ahead with it, aren’t they? The library…demolishing it for  another  bloody car park. The library? I thought that was just local gossip, stirred up by Old Man Hemmings. He gets going about things, you know. It’s not gossip, David. I saw the notice pinned up on the community board this morning. Official. Public consultation starts next week, but everyone knows what that means. It’s a formality. They’ve already decided. Crikey. That  is  bad. I used to spend hours in that library as a kid. Proper old building too, all dark wood and dusty corners. Remember the smell of the books? Of course I do! It's a beautiful building, and it’s part of the character of the High Street. It's not just a library, it’s… a landmark. And they want to replace it with concrete. Honestly, the council just wants everything to be shiny and new, doesn’t matter if it has any soul. They’re obsessed with ‘modernisation’. It’s all about attracting investment, apparently. Though I’m not sure what kind of investment needs a car park more than a library. Exactly! And it’s not like there  isn’t  parking. There’s that multi-storey just a five-minute walk away. They just want to maximise profit, I reckon. Let some developer build flats on the land eventually. It's the same story everywhere, isn't it? They say they’re preserving facades, but they’re just sticking a new shell around a gutted building. Like that old pub they 'restored' last year? More plastic than history. Ugh, don’t even remind me. It looks like a film set. All wrong. Speaking of things looking wrong… have you had a chance to look at those upholstery swatches I showed you? Still trying to decide on the chair for the living room. Oh, yes. I had a quick glance. A bit too much to take in all at once, to be honest. So many patterns. I know, it’s overwhelming. I think I’m leaning towards that muted teal one, but I'm worried it'll be too dark. And then there’s the linen, but will it stand up to the cat? You know how Winston likes to sharpen his claws... He does. That linen won’t stand a chance. Teal sounds nice, though.

Oh, this takes me back. Duran Duran. Absolute classics, weren’t they? Though I suspect you two weren’t even twinkles in your parents’ eyes when ‘Rio’ came out. Probably not, yeah! Mum plays a bit of 80s stuff, but it’s not really my thing. Too… synthesized, maybe? I’m more into, like, indie stuff. Wet Leg, that kind of vibe. I actually don’t mind a bit of the 80s, surprisingly. It’s got a certain…energy. But I'm definitely more a Phoebe Bridgers girl most of the time, if I'm honest. Bit melancholic, I know, but it suits editing, you know? Keeps the mood right. Melancholy and editing go hand in hand, don’t they? Always something that needs tweaking, something slightly off. It's just the nature of the beast. Though, I have to say, I’m a bit of a rock man myself. Still love a good guitar riff. See! A man of taste, David. Although, this  is  a good tune. Reminds me of university. Speaking of which… have you two actually started thinking about Christmas presents yet? It's creeping up on us. Oh god, no! I’m terrible for leaving it to the last minute. I usually end up panicking and buying gift cards. Sorry, Mum! No judgement here, darling. I’ve done the same more than once. Though, I was thinking about your hair, Chloe. You’re always talking about wanting those special conditioning treatments. Maybe I could get you a voucher for that fancy salon in Winchester? Oh, Mum, you shouldn’t! But… actually, that would be  amazing . I’ve been eyeing up their Olaplex treatment for ages. It’s so expensive though. I was thinking maybe something practical for you, David. Like, a new noise-cancelling headset? You were complaining about the office being a bit chaotic last week. That’s… incredibly thoughtful, actually. You remembered. They  are  dreadful in there. Constant chatter, phone ringing… a good headset would be a lifesaver. I was considering taking up woodworking again, now that the evenings are getting darker. Might need to invest in some decent tools. Woodworking? David, really? That’s… a departure. Well, I used to be quite good at it, back in Southport. My grandfather taught me. It’s just… relaxing, you know? Something tangible to  make  after a day of just shuffling papers and attending meetings. That sounds really cool, actually!

Right then, lad. You've been glued to that computer for hours. Still looking at cars, are ya? Don't tell me you've found another one that's "perfect." Actually, yeah! This one’s… different. It’s a Mini Cooper, but a proper old one. Like, a classic. Saw it on a site called ‘Bring a Trailer’. It needs a bit of work, but… imagine driving  that  to college! A classic Mini? Oh, bless your heart. You and your aesthetics. They're lovely, alright, don't get me wrong. Your Grandad had a green one back in the day. But “a bit of work” usually translates to “a money pit” with those old things. And where would you even  put  it, parked on the street here? I know, I know, it's not exactly practical. But it’s only £3,500! And I could probably get a space in the college car park if I pay extra. It’s just… it’s got character. All these new cars are so… boring. Boring, are they? Reliable, I'd call them. And safer. And that price doesn't include insurance, does it? That's where it’ll sting you, love. A classic Mini… even one needing work… they’re considered a bit of a risk by insurance companies. That’s what I was hoping to ask you about, actually. I did a quick quote online, and it came back… rather terrifying. Even with a black box. Terrifying, you say? Let me guess - four figures? It’ll be the age, mostly. Young drivers are high risk, plain and simple. And old cars… well, they don’t have all the safety features newer cars do. Airbags, ABS… the works. They assume you’re more likely to have an accident. It was… just over £1,800. For a year. With a black box that monitors everything I do. It feels a bit… Big Brother-ish. Oof. That  is  steep. Even for a young driver. Look, you need to understand how they calculate it all. It’s not just age and car type. They look at postcode, your driving history – which you haven't got much of yet, admittedly – your occupation… even what you plan to  use  the car for. Commuting to college is a big factor. So, what can I do? Should I just forget about the Mini and go for something… sensible? Like a boring hatchback?

…And then young O’Malley, bless his heart, sends an email at 8 pm on a Friday night asking for a full system diagnostic report for Monday. A  full  one. Like I haven't a life outside of servers and firewalls, you know? Sounds rough, Dad. Mr. Henderson just makes us write essays. Boring, but no emails at eight at night. Honestly, Sean, you let them walk all over you. You need to learn to just say no. Or, at least, ‘Not tonight, O’Malley. I have… important family time.’ Easy for you to say, love. You're not the one who'll have to deal with the fallout when the system goes down on Monday morning. They'll be lookin' at me, like  I  planned it. What  is  fallout, Dad? Like, nuclear stuff? Not quite, darling. It just means the consequences. Things going wrong because of something else. It’s more than consequences, it’s a right headache, so it is. I was reading an article about stress levels, actually. Apparently, they can test your cortisol levels with saliva. Just spit in a tube and send it off. Fancy that, eh? Spitting away your troubles. Ew! Gross. Well, it's a bit invasive. I suppose it's useful, but I prefer sticking to a long walk and a good cup of tea. Or maybe… remembering that time we all went to that equality vote rally. That felt important, didn't it? Such a powerful day. To think, not so long ago... Aye, it was somethin' alright. Everyone out, banners flyin', a real groundswell of support. Took a while, though, didn't it? All that debate. And people lookin' at you funny if you dared to suggest everyone deserves the same rights. Seems ridiculous now. What's ‘debate’ mean? Like arguing? It's a polite argument, sweetie. People discussing different sides of an issue. It's important, but it can be tiresome. Actually, now that I think about it, is this conversation being recorded? I swear I heard a little click earlier. Are we on, like,  Big Brother ? Sean! Don’t be ridiculous. You've been listening to too many podcasts. It’s just the central heating kicking in. Though, speaking of podcasts, have you heard that new one about true crime? It’s absolutely gripping. I don't trust those podcasts. They're all sensationalised. Still, you might be right. Now, you two.

Honestly, this traffic is mental. Feels like we’ve barely moved in twenty minutes. You’d think being this close to the moors would mean fewer people, but no. Everyone’s heading to somewhere with a view, are they? Aye, well, Bank Holiday weekend. Always the same. Remember when we could just  drive ? No thinking about it, just get in the car and go. Now it’s all apps and traffic updates. Though, it’s nice to get out, isn’t it? Even if it’s just looking at fields. Did you see that kestrel hovering near Belmont earlier? Beautiful. A what? A kest-rel? What’s that, like a really big pigeon? No, not quite. It’s a type of falcon. Smaller than a buzzard, hunts over fields. Very graceful birds. They look a bit like miniature hawks. You see a lot of them around here. It's funny, isn't it? We build these massive metal birds that fly, and people still get excited about the real ones. It is a bit ironic, isn’t it? Bit mad how something so flimsy can stay up in the air, though. Makes you wonder about aerodynamics, really. Speaking of getting somewhere, are we nearly at Grandma’s? I’m starving. Another twenty minutes, give or take. Depends on this traffic. She’s already prepping the roast, bless her. Asked me three times if I was bringing Yorkshire puddings. Yorkshire puds are the best bit! Can we go to the village shop when we get there? They sell those fizzy sweets I like. The one with the wonky cobbles? That place is ancient. Honestly, how those villages are built on top of hills, I’ll never know. It’s like whoever planned them just thought “Right, let’s make it  difficult .” They often evolved organically, you see. Before cars, the steepness wasn’t necessarily a problem. Defensible positions, closer to water sources… a lot of practical considerations. And they're rather charming, aren’t they? Much more character than these modern housing estates. Charming when you’re not trying to push a pram up them! You'd think after Brexit they'd have sorted out all the road maintenance, promised loads of funding for infrastructure... Oh, don't even  start  on Brexit. That's a whole can of worms. I still think we were better in the EU, honestly. Easier for everything, not just roads.

…It’s just, I keep thinking about it. This ‘chicken’ is… really good. Honestly, better than some actual chicken I’ve had. But it’s  weird , isn't it? Knowing it never, you know… clucked. Weird in a good way, though, right? It massively reduces suffering. I mean, that’s the whole point. It feels morally… cleaner. And it tastes pretty decent, which is a bonus. I was reading an article about the scalability of cultured meat production. Apparently, it's getting  much  cheaper. Cleaner is a good word. But is it actually, though? I mean, all that energy to grow it in a lab… it's not exactly zero impact on the environment. And the whole process feels… artificial. Like, where do you draw the line? It's not natural. Natural isn’t always good, is it? Loads of naturally occurring things will kill you. And think about the environmental impact of  traditional  farming. The land clearing, the methane emissions… it’s massive. This feels like a compromise. A halfway house. Plus, let's be real, the conditions in most abattoirs are horrific. It’s not a pretty picture. Exactly! Remember that documentary we watched, ‘Dominion’? I had to be vegetarian for a week afterwards. I still feel awful thinking about it. I’m trying to be better about checking where my food comes from, even the vegetarian stuff, but it’s a minefield. I get it. That doc was…intense. I’ve never been able to look at sausages the same way. Honestly, sometimes I think hunting, as awful as it sounds, is  less  cruel than factory farming. At least the animal has a chance to live a life, even a short one, in a natural environment. Abattoirs are just… systematic oppression. Woah, hold on. Hunting? You’re saying hunting is  less  cruel? Surely stalking something, terrifying it, then… shooting it? That sounds pretty awful to me. At least in an abattoir, it’s supposedly quick, efficient… even if the ‘supposedly’ part is debatable. Quick and efficient isn't the same as humane. It's just… less visibly distressing, maybe? Plus, with regulated hunting, there's a population control aspect to it. Whereas abattoirs are driven purely by profit. It’s a horrible equation. I'm not saying I  like  hunting, just… it feels more honest, somehow. Honest cruelty? Is that a thing? . It’s all awful, really. It makes you want to live on air and sunshine.

Right, I’m officially bored of scrolling. Nothing on telly. Absolute rubbish. Did you two see that deal on Amazon for the new Playstation game?  Elden Ring , yeah? It's a tenner off. A tenner? That’s… something. Though, a tenner’s a lot when you’ve not  had  a tenner in a fortnight, innit? Don't start, Dan. You said you were gonna look at jobs today. You could earn a tenner in an hour if you actually applied for something. Easy for  you  to say, Miss 'Going to Uni to be a fancy doctor'. I applied for that warehouse job last week, remember? Didn't even get a reply. It’s all automated these days, just robots saying no. Aye, it’s rubbish, that. I applied for a summer job at the pub, figured it'd be a sure thing, but haven't heard anything back. They probably got a hundred applications. Still, this game… it’s getting rave reviews. Imagine smashing it over Christmas, when we're all stuck indoors. Christmas is going to be  expensive  this year, though. Mum was going on about needing to start saving now. And Gran keeps hinting she wants that fancy foot spa thing. Gran always wants something fancy. Remember last year? The heated blanket with the massage function? Said it was for her circulation. I reckon she just liked the vibrating. She's a character, our Gran. Speaking of expensive, I need a new phone. This one’s on its last legs. Keeps freezing when I’m trying to stream stuff. It's embarrassing when I'm trying to show people clips from uni. Get one of those refurbished ones. You can get a decent one for half the price. I saw some on Music Magpie. Refurbished? Sounds dodgy to me. Probably full of… spy stuff. They’re listening to us all anyway, aren't they, through the phones? Come on, Dan, you watch too many conspiracy videos. It's just algorithms, not secret government agents. Still, Chloe’s right, refurbished could be a good shout. I'm skint enough as it is being a student. Honestly, uni is draining my bank account. I'm living on pot noodles and hope right now. It’s not all bad, is it? You’re learning stuff, meeting people… don’t you like your course? Yeah, the course is good. It’s just… the social side is pricey.

…and honestly, Gran  loved  the whole ‘research co-ordinator’ title. Made me sound terribly important, didn’t it? She kept asking if I was ‘solving mysteries with words’ which, I suppose, isn’t entirely inaccurate sometimes. Oh, bless her! She’s always had a flair for the dramatic interpretation of everything. Mine just asked if my job involved a lot of paperwork. Which, also… not entirely inaccurate. How was the drive down from Aylesbury, though? Dreadful on the A1, I imagine? Surprisingly smooth actually! Left early-ish, beat most of the traffic. Although, the service station near Huntingdon was  rammed . Felt like everyone in the Home Counties decided to come to Cambridge for the day. You drove up from Lincoln, right? That must have been… a shift. A proper shift. Left at half six this morning. Needed about three coffees just to stay awake on the A1. But it's nice to be back, isn’t it? Even if it's just for Alumni Day. It feels like ages since we wandered these corridors as stressed-out law students. Remember Professor Davies’ contract law lectures? I swear he deliberately spoke in monotone just to see who was paying attention. Don’t even  mention  contract law. Still have nightmares. No, but honestly, it’s good. It's weird seeing it all so… calm. We used to practically live in the library during exam season. What are you up to at the moment work-wise, besides surviving the Lincoln-Cambridge commute? Still with the firm? Still at the firm. Doing pretty much the same thing, truthfully. Admin, organizing, keeping everything running smoothly behind the scenes. It's…stable. Pays the bills. Though, to be honest, I’m starting to feel a bit restless. I was scrolling through travel blogs last night and suddenly got this urge to just… go. Go where? Don’t tell me you’re plotting an escape to Patagonia. Gran would have a fit. Not quite Patagonia. Though… it  does  sound appealing. No, I was looking at Italy. Specifically, Tuscany. I’ve always wanted to spend a month just wandering around, eating pasta, attempting to learn Italian. You know, the whole cliché. Oh, that sounds  amazing . You should absolutely do it! You deserve a proper break. I've been trying to convince my parents we should all go to Greece next summer. My auntie has a little place on Crete and keeps offering it to us.

Right, I am  completely  wrecked. That lecture on post-structuralism… honestly, I think my brain just melted a little. Rough day, then? Thought you were enjoying that module. You were proper buzzing about Derrida last week. Enjoying is… a strong word. I  appreciate  it, yeah? It's just…dense. Like trying to wrestle an octopus. And Professor Davies just drones on and on. I swear, he’s actively trying to induce sleep. He's a bit of a monotone merchant, I’ll give you that. Did you take notes, at least? You know you struggle to recall things if you don't. Oh, loads of notes. Mostly doodles of little octopuses being wrestled, to be fair. And massive question marks. It's just... it doesn’t  click , you know? All that deconstruction and questioning everything? It feels like a massive philosophical headache. It  is  a headache, love. It's supposed to be. It’s about challenging assumptions. But yeah, Davies isn’t the best at making it accessible. Maybe try reading some secondary sources? Find someone who explains it in plain English. I’ve got a few bits from my Masters, if you want. Ooh, that would be amazing, actually. Ta. God, I needed that. I’m just…stressed. And achy. All this sitting hunched over books is murder on my back. You are perpetually hunched. You need to sort that posture out. Remember what the physio said about keeping your shoulders back? Easier said than done when you’re battling the existential dread of postmodernism. Seriously though, I'm thinking of booking a massage. You know, one of those proper deep tissue ones. Now  that’s  a good idea. You deserve it. Been working yourself ragged. Where were you thinking of going? That place near the train station does good ones, doesn’t it? I was looking at ‘Serenity Now’ on Kirkgate. It's a bit pricier, but the reviews are amazing. People saying it's completely transformed their posture and banished all their tension. Sounds like heaven. Kirkgate, eh? That's a bit of a trek. But if the reviews are that good… you shouldn't scrimp on your wellbeing. Though, 'Serenity Now'… feels a bit ironic considering how you were five minutes ago. I know, right? The irony is not lost on me. Although, honestly, I'd take serenity in  any  form right now. Even if it involved a slightly overpriced massage.

…Honestly, this roast is lovely, love. Better than anything I’d attempt myself these days. Though I used to be quite the cook, you know. Before… well, before everything. Glad you think so, Dad. I tweaked Mum’s recipe a bit, a little more rosemary. It’s good to hear you say that, though. You  did  make a mean shepherd’s pie. Oh, absolutely. Remember that one Christmas, when you tried to make goose? That was… an experience. A smoky, slightly burnt experience. Don't remind me! The smoke alarm was going off for hours. Still, we all had a good laugh. Speaking of experiences… did you see what’s happening in Calais again? Absolutely dreadful. More boats, more people risking their lives. It's awful, isn't it? I was reading about it this morning. The conditions they're living in... it’s just heartbreaking. It feels so helpless, being here. I try to explain it to my class, the complexities of it all, but it’s hard for them to grasp. It is. And the rhetoric gets so heated. It’s easy to forget they’re people, just desperate for a safer life. They’re not statistics, they’re families. I had a Syrian refugee in my Year 7 class last year, brilliant boy. Took him ages to settle, the trauma he'd been through… It’s a complex situation, that’s for sure. Always has been. Used to be simpler, or at least  seemed  simpler, when I was a lad. Though, thinking back, maybe I was just less aware. More sheltered, growing up in Southend. Nothing much happened in Southend, to be honest. Except for the pier, obviously. Dad, you always end up talking about the pier! It’s become your defining characteristic. Well, it’s a magnificent pier! The longest pleasure pier in the world, you know. Anyway… back to more pressing matters. Have you two given any more thought to next summer? I was wondering if we could all maybe… go somewhere? Not a fancy holiday, mind you. Just… a week away, all together. We’ve talked about it, dear. It’s just… finances are a bit tight at the moment. School holidays are extortionate, aren't they? And with the price of everything going up… Mum’s right. Also, I’m planning on doing that summer school on inclusive teaching practices, which means a few weeks of extra work to save up for the course fees.

Honestly, David, this whole bathroom renovation is proving to be… a trial. A complete and utter trial. I thought, you know, having done a bit of DIY in my time – replacing a tap here, re-grouting there – that I could at least  manage  the project. Manage? Oh, Alistair, you optimistic soul. Bathrooms are the devil's own work. Always are. I went through this with Margaret five years ago. Still finding stray tiles under the sofa. Tredegar builders are… robust, let’s put it that way. Not exactly known for their finesse. Finesse is a word I haven’t encountered in connection with  any  tradesperson I’ve met so far. This plumber, bless his heart, seems convinced the original plumbing was designed by Escher. Says everything's at right angles, and utterly illogical. Escher! That’s brilliant! Mine just kept referring to everything as ‘a bit wonky’. 'A bit wonky’ covered a multitude of sins, believe me. Did he at least give you a quote before starting to re-imagine your pipework? He did. And then, naturally, it doubled once he started “investigating”. Said he found “unforeseen complications.” Isn’t that their favourite phrase? Like discovering a hidden civilisation behind the plasterboard. Standard. Absolutely standard. They all have that phrase tucked away. Reminds me of old Mr. Davies, used to do gardening for the university. Every hedge trimming was an “archaeological dig”. Unearthing things, he was. Mostly old biscuit wrappers, if I recall correctly. Sounds about right. I’m beginning to think I should have just left it alone. It was perfectly functional, if a little… beige. Now it’s a building site and a significant drain on my bank account. Beige is underrated, Alistair. Seriously. It’s the colour of peace. Though, speaking of colour, are you going bold with it? I know you've always liked a bit of… flair. I was thinking of a deep teal. Reminded me of a riad I stayed in in Marrakech a few years ago. Very calming. But the painter, young chap, seemed aghast. Said teal’s “not really selling” at the moment. Apparently, it’s all greige now. Greige. Don’t get me started on greige. It's the colour of despair. Margaret wanted greige for the hallway. I put my foot down. Absolutely not. We went for a lovely ochre. Reminded me of the hills around Tredegar in autumn. Ochre, that’s…a good colour.

…And I’m telling ya, this curry is  almost  as good as Mammy used to make. Almost. Still needs a good whack of chili powder, mind you.
