Though, maybe that's just me being Irish and liking to set me mouth on fire. It’s…spicy enough. It feels like it’s burning a little bit. Don't worry, darling. It  is  a bit warm. I told Liam not to go too mad with the Vindaloo paste, but he never listens. It’s a wonder he doesn't drink petrol with everything, the man. Now, now, it's a  subtle  heat, Sarah! A complex flavour profile. And I don't drink petrol, I appreciate a good stout. Though, now you mention it, young Finn here tried to eat a bit of the cooker the other day. Liam! Don’t encourage him! Honestly, that boy. Anything and everything goes in the mouth. Is he even feeling any pain when he tries these things? He just  chews . No sense of self-preservation, the lad. He was going after a screw, a  screw , Sarah. I swear he thinks he's some sort of miniature metal-eating superhero. “Strongest boy in the world!” he shouted after nearly swallowing it whole. Superpowers are cool. I wish I had one. Like, super speed, so I could finish all my homework in five seconds. Or invisibility, so I could sneak into the kitchen and get biscuits when Mum says no. Invisibility, eh? That’d be handy for emptying the night deposit box at the credit union. Don’t get any ideas, now! Only joking, obviously. But seriously, those things are a relic. Who even uses them anymore? People who don't want to be seen bringing large sums of cash in, Liam. It's a security thing. Speaking of things being secure... have you even  started  thinking about Finn's birthday? It's only a month away. A month already? Jaysus, time flies. I was thinking of that new park they're building down by the river? The one with the pirate ship? Oh, yeah! That one looks awesome. They're having a big event there next weekend, aren't they? Loads of bouncy castles and stuff. It is, but it’ll be  packed . And we'll have to keep a ridiculously close eye on Finn. He’s a wandering soul, that one. Last week he nearly ended up in Mrs. O’Malley’s greenhouse.

…and then young Timmy, bless 'im, he went as a ghost, right? But he’d put ‘is pajamas on  inside out . Said it made ‘im spookier. Proper little scamp, that one. Drove his mum round the bend, it did. Oh, they’re all the same at that age, aren’t they, Arthur? Little terrors. I remember little Leo, wanted to be a dinosaur, but insisted on wearing a bright pink tutu  with  it. Said it was a ‘sparkly dinosaur’. Couldn’t argue with that logic, could you? Sounds chaotic! My lot are a bit older now, thankfully past the dressing-up debates. Though, my daughter was very insistent on being a historically accurate Victorian schoolgirl one year. The bonnet nearly caused a riot at a friend’s party. Honestly, Halloween’s kinda… lame now. It was good when I was little, but everyone just wants to see how scary they can be. It’s all about the TikToks now, not the actual dressing up. TikToks? Is that one o’ them… computer things? Sounds a bit daft, if you ask me. A good ghost story, now  that’s  scary. Old Man Hemmings used to tell a tale about the marshes down near Costessey… a will-o’-the-wisp that led folks astray. Gave me nightmares for weeks, it did. Arthur, you and your stories. You’ve been telling that one since I was a girl! Still gives me the shivers though. It’s funny, isn’t it? How places hold onto stories. Harrow’s got its share, though more about highwaymen than ghosts, I think. My grandma used to talk about Dick Turpin hiding out in the fields near Wealdstone. It’s the landscape, I think. Some places just…feel like they  could  hold secrets. I took my class to Ironbridge Gorge last week, and you could almost  feel  the history seeping out of the stone. It's completely different to Birmingham, obviously, but even there, you get pockets of that feeling if you look for it. We went to Ironbridge last summer. It was alright. Bit boring, though. All old buildings and stuff. Give me Norwich any day. It’s got a vibe, you know? Plus, the shops are way better. Norwich is a fine city, Norwich is. Been goin’ there all me life. Though it’s changed somethin’ awful, mind. Used to be able to walk down Gentleman’s Walk without bein’ bowled over by tourists.

Honestly, this traffic is  mental . We’ve barely moved in the last twenty minutes. I thought leaving at 8am would beat the worst of it, clearly I was optimistic. Optimistic is a strong word, love. You're always optimistic. Remember when you thought you could get us to Glastonbury on the Friday morning and  walk  in? That was a logistical miscalculation, alright? And it was a different era of my life! Less…realistic. This is just frustrating. I wanted to check out the show ring before it got rammed. It’ll be alright, dear. The steam fair isn’t going anywhere. Besides, it gives us time to chat. How’s the flat hunt going, then, Chloe? Still no luck? Absolutely awful. Everything is either a shoebox for an extortionate price or needs a complete gutting. I saw one yesterday that was apparently ‘charming’ – it had damp, a wonky floor,  and  the landlord wanted six months’ rent upfront. Six months! They’re having a laugh, aren’t they? Back in my day… well, things were just different. You could get a perfectly decent council house, and if you needed help, the council  helped . Now it’s all about right to buy and private rentals and…well, it’s a mess. It is, isn't it? It's so hard for young people to get on the ladder. I'm lucky, I managed to get a mortgage back in the day, but even that was a struggle. And thinking about Mum... she’s starting to need more help, you know? How is she, actually? You said she’d been a bit unsteady on her feet? Yeah, she had a little wobble last week. Nothing major, thank goodness, but it scared her, and it scared me more. I’m starting to look at sheltered housing options, but…they’re all so expensive, or the waiting lists are ridiculous. She’d hate a full-on care home, obviously. Sheltered housing is a racket, if you ask me. They charge an arm and a leg for a bit of peace of mind. And half the time, the staff are overworked and underpaid. It’s just…another way for them to make money out of vulnerable people. It's awful. They really need to invest more in truly affordable options. And not just flats, places with proper support networks. Somewhere Mum would feel safe and independent. Exactly!

…and honestly, the state of the garden when we moved in was  shocking . Just weeds, mostly. And a patio covered in moss. It's slowly coming together, but it's a lot of work. That's why I was so excited when you said you were thinking about the allotment! It's a completely different scale of commitment, though, isn’t it? It is, isn't it? Terrifyingly so. I've always  wanted  one, you know? My nan had a huge garden and grew everything. Proper veg, flowers, the lot. I used to spend summers with her, just picking strawberries and getting covered in dirt. It feels like a nice connection to her, if that makes sense. But I’m realising now I have absolutely no idea where to start. Hence, needing to pick your brain – the expert! Oh, don't call me an expert! I just...persist. And make a lot of mistakes. But I’m happy to help. What allotment are you looking at? The ones near Tooting Bec? I drove past them the other day, they looked pretty busy. Yeah, Tooting Bec is the one. Apparently, there’s a waiting list, of course. I put my name down last week. They said it could be anywhere from six months to a year. But I thought, even if it’s a year, I should start planning now. I’ve been looking at those raised bed kits online… are they worth it? Or are they just a fancy way to spend money? Ooh, raised beds are tempting, aren't they? I have a couple. They're good for drainage, especially in London clay – which I assume is what you’ll be dealing with. And they save your back a bit. Though, they do dry out quicker, so you have to water more. Honestly, if you’re starting small, maybe just mark out a couple of beds directly on the plot and see how you go? It’s cheaper. You can always add raised beds later. That's a good point. Money  is  a consideration. I'm trying to be sensible. I was thinking… courgettes, definitely. And tomatoes. Everything in the supermarket tastes so… bland. I’d love to grow some proper flavourful tomatoes. Courgettes are easy! Maybe  too  easy. You’ll be giving them away to everyone you know. Tomatoes need a bit more care, you'll need to think about support – staking or cages.

…and then, honestly, Liam just  stared  at Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning marrow. Like it’d personally offended ‘im. It were proper awkward at the village fete, I tell ya. Did you even  go  to the fete, Anya? No, sadly not. Mum dragged me back to Cambridge for the weekend to ‘help’ with sorting through Grandad’s attic. Apparently, decades of stamp collecting is a national treasure. It mostly smelled of dust and regret, to be honest. A marrow staring contest sounds far more entertaining. Dust and regret, eh? Sounds about right for a family attic. Though a staring contest with a marrow is a special kind of suffering. Anyway, that’s not what I wanted to properly chat about. I’ve been doing a bit of thinking… about us, a bit. ‘Us’? Oh dear. This sounds serious. Don’t tell me you’ve decided Doncaster’s finally too…Doncaster for you and you're running off to join the circus? Nah, not the circus. Though that  would  be a story, wouldn’t it? No, it’s just…uni starts proper next month, yeah? And we're both going to be properly busy. I was just wondering… where does that leave us? I mean, we've been practically joined at the hip since year seven, and I don’t fancy losing that just 'cause we're at different places. I’ve been thinking the same thing, actually. It’s just… different, isn’t it? Everything’s been so easy up to now. Same school, same town, always bumping into each other. Now it’s going to be deliberate effort. Which, I mean, I  want  to make, but it feels… daunting. Especially with me being down south. Daunting’s the word. It’s not like we’re talking about a quick train ride anymore. Cambridge is…well, it’s Cambridge. Ages away. And everyone down there’s probably all posh and… and… Don't start with the stereotypes, Em. Not everyone drinks tea with their pinky out. Though, admittedly, there  are  a lot of rowing clubs. But seriously, it won't be all that different. There'll be students from all over. And we can visit each other, can't we? Aye, we can. It's just...money. Petrol's ridiculous, and train tickets are daylight robbery. I’m already worrying about affording books, let alone travelling to see you every other weekend.

Right, right, RIGHT! Nearly had 'im. Blasted goblin kept healing. Honestly, this Dungeon Master is taking the mickey. Sounds stressful, Liam. You’ve been at that campaign for, what, six hours straight now? You need to blink, lad. You’re starting to resemble a particularly grumpy owl. Six hours? That’s nothing. Remember that time you tried to solo ‘The Forgotten City’ back in first year, Liam? You didn’t surface for a full 48, fuelled solely by energy drinks and spite. That was a  different  situation, Raj. And it was 36 hours, thank you very much. And it was a matter of principle! The guide said it was possible! Principle and a severe caffeine addiction, more like. You looked like you were communicating with higher beings. Didn’t even register when my mum brought pizza. Alright, alright, you’ve all ganged up on me. It's just… this boss is genuinely unfair. And old man Hemlock keeps dropping cryptic riddles, not actual loot. It’s infuriating. What game even  is  it? You never tell us the names of these things. Is it another one of your obscure role-playing ones where you name your character something like ‘Borgrim Stonefist’ and spend three hours min-maxing their stats? It’s ‘Echoes of Aethelgard’. And Borgrim Stonefist was a perfectly respectable dwarf warrior! And yes, proper character build is vital! This one's a bit different though, it's got a really cool narrative, even if Hemlock is a pain. It's all based around these ancient Norse myths, but… twisted. Norse myths, you say? I read a fascinating article about the origins of Ragnarok… it’s surprisingly dark when you dig into the original texts. Less about epic battles and more about… well, the inevitable decay of everything. Sounds cheery. Right up Liam’s street, considering his gaming choices. Still, at least it's keeping you occupied. Uni’s been dead quiet this week. Anything exciting happening on your side of campus, Zara? Not much. The Student Union had that ‘Sustainable Fashion Swap’ thing yesterday. Went and dropped off a bunch of stuff I don't wear anymore. Picked up a pretty decent vintage jacket though, only cost me a fiver. Fiver? You lucky thing. Everything’s gone mental with prices these days. Trying to find a decent pair of jeans that don’t cost a week’s rent is a mission.

…And there’s Maureen. Honestly, haven't seen her in… goodness, must be nearly ten years now. We used to get into  such  trouble, didn’t we? Remember that time we tried to sneak into the Roxy? The Roxy in Elephant & Castle? No way! I’ve only heard stories about that place. Mum, you were a rebel! Rebel? Oh, pshaw. Just young and foolish. We wanted to see The Clash, but hadn’t got tickets. Thought we could just… blend in. Didn’t quite work. Bob the bouncer had other ideas. Gave us a right telling-off, he did. Bob the bouncer! Sounds terrifying. You never tell me these stories. It’s all “Don't do this, don’t do that” and “when  I  was your age…” Where's the scandalous Mum I suspect existed? Well, you wouldn't want to know  everything . Some things are best left buried, love. Besides, my rebellious days are long gone. Now I’m just an old woman who enjoys a cup of tea and a good film. Speaking of which, have you seen that new one, ‘Saltburn’? Everyone's talking about it. ‘Saltburn’? Oh, God, yeah. It's… a lot. I saw it with Chloe last week. A lot? That's a vague description, dear. Is it good? I heard it was quite shocking. Shocking is an understatement. It’s beautifully shot, the acting is fantastic, but… honestly, Mum, it’s  intense . Really disturbing in places. It’s one of those films that stays with you, you know? You’ll be thinking about it for days afterwards. Disturbing, eh? I’m not sure I fancy something disturbing. I’m more of a feel-good film sort of person these days. Though, I did enjoy ‘The Banshees of Inisherin’… that was wonderfully sad. Oh, 'Banshees' was brilliant! Colin Farrell was amazing. ‘Saltburn’ is… different. It's less about sadness and more about… examining privilege and obsession and just… pushing boundaries. Boundaries, eh? They’re good to have sometimes, I reckon. Don't want to go getting ideas above your station. Were there any nice outfits? I always appreciate a good costume drama. Nice outfits? Mum, it’s not really a costume drama. Although… the clothes  are  a thing. It’s very… decadent. Lots of very expensive, very impractical things. And a lot of… skin. Oh. Right. Well. Sounds a bit much for me then. I'd rather watch 'Call the Midwife', all comforting and clean.

…and honestly, the  audacity  of him to suggest Scrabble was a ‘strategic masterpiece’ when he clearly just threw tiles at the board hoping for the best. It was painful. Absolutely painful. Oh, bless him. Who was this Scrabble offender, anyway? Not… Dave, is it? Because if it’s Dave, I need to warn my mum. She still hasn’t forgiven him for the Monopoly incident of '18. No, no, thankfully not Dave. This was Ben from work. He's… enthusiastic. About everything. It was during that team building thing last week. Supposed to foster collaboration, mostly just fostered my inner rage. More tea, anyone? I’ve put the biscuits out. Digestives, obviously. Yes, please, lovely! Team building, eh? Sounds… thrilling. How’s the research going, by the way? Still wrestling with the nuances of Estuary English? It's…a process. Honestly, the more I listen, the more I realise how fluid everything is. People code-switch within  sentences  sometimes! It's fascinating, though, genuinely. Trying to pin down specific features is like nailing jelly to a wall, though. Interviewing people’s grandads is proving fruitful, though. They’re a wealth of linguistic history. It's amazing how much dialect slips back in when they’re talking about their childhood. That's brilliant! It sounds really interesting. I’m just stuck in a cycle of proofreading articles about celebrity handbag choices. Slightly less intellectually stimulating, shall we say. Although, Brenda in accounts is  obsessed  with a particular tote bag. It's genuinely concerning. Oh, Brenda. She’s a character. You know, you really deserve a spa day. You’re always working, always fixing everyone else’s formatting errors. Don’t even  start  with the spa idea. I saw an offer for one in Shoreditch, but then I started thinking about all the things I should be doing instead – clearing out my DVD collection, finally sorting through those magazines…It's a black hole, honestly. I’ve got issues from like, 2015. 2015?! That's archaeological. Listen, we  need  to go to a spa. Proper pampering. Facials, massages… No guilt. I’m booking it. Next Saturday? Saturday… I was supposed to meet Chloe for brunch. She’s been on another disastrous date. She’s currently convinced she’s found “the one”, then realises he collects miniature spoons. It’s a recurring theme. Miniature spoons?! Oh, Chloe. She’s a magnet for eccentricities. Tell you what, we can brunch  then  spa.

Right, so I’ve chucked a load of veg in this, it’s supposed to be a sort of…Italian-ish stew. Hopefully it'll be edible. You know how my mam always said I couldn’t boil an egg? Well, this is me proving her wrong, slowly but surely. Though, honestly, the washing machine's been more of a challenge this week. Italian-ish, eh? Sounds ambitious. And the washing machine? What’s it doing now, staging a full-blown rebellion? Last time I checked, it was making a noise like a strangled badger. Strangled badger is… remarkably accurate, actually. It’s stopped doing that  particular  noise, thankfully. Now it just…doesn’t spin. Properly. Everything comes out soaking. I’ve tried everything the internet told me to – resetting it, checking the drain, even that weird thing about balancing the load. Nothing. Have you checked the pump filter? That's usually the culprit. It's a nightmare to get to, though, isn’t it? All that fiddling about at the bottom. I remember Dad spent a whole afternoon wrestling with ours once, covered in… well, I don't want to think about what he was covered in. Honestly, I'm terrified to look. I’m half expecting to find a sock civilisation down there. I’ll have a go tomorrow. I'm just… knackered after work. Trying to manage that new research assistant is exhausting. He asks so many questions, bless him. It's good he’s engaged, but it’s relentless. That’s research for you. Constant questioning, constant doubt. It’s why I’m holed up in the library most days, avoiding actual human interaction. Though, I did have a rather heated debate with Professor Davies today about the methodology. He thinks my approach is “too radical.” "Too radical"? That sounds like something  he  would say. He's always been a bit stuck in his ways, hasn't he? Remember when he dismissed your paper on post-structuralism as "nonsense"? How could I forget? I nearly walked out. I think I just stared at him for a good minute, speechless. It’s just… frustrating. I’ve spent months on this. Building the framework, analyzing the data… You'll crack it. You always do. You're way too clever to let him grind you down. Speaking of clever… how’s your brother doing with the new baby? Has he lost all sleep yet?

…and honestly, the estate agent was pushing for offers  over  asking price. Over! In Hunsonby, of all places. It’s madness, isn’t it? Utter madness. You'd think being so far removed from…well, from  everything  down south, prices would be a bit more sensible. It is a bit surreal, isn’t it? I was looking at properties back near Birkenhead last month, just out of curiosity, and even  there  it’s gone absolutely bonkers. Small terraced houses going for… well, let's just say my entire freelance income wouldn’t touch it. It's the 'London effect,' plain and simple. Everything gets sucked south. Money, opportunity… sanity, probably. Property becomes an investment, not a home. And then it ripples out. Exactly! When I was younger, buying a house was about having somewhere to  live . Now it’s just a game for investors and people who’ve already got several. Remember when we were looking at that cottage near Penrith, David? Before we decided this was more manageable? They wanted a premium just for the 'Lake District postcode'. I do indeed. Highway robbery. Though, speaking of things being overpriced and misrepresented… did you both see that latest piece on the VW emissions scandal? Still rumbling on, isn't it? Oh, yeah. I skimmed an article. Something about further payouts? I thought they’d pretty much settled everything years ago. Settled? They’ve barely scratched the surface. Apparently, they were actively obstructing investigations even  after  the initial scandal broke. Dodgy software updates to mask the emissions, internal memos… the whole lot. It's staggering. A deliberate deception on a massive scale. Goodness me. You’d think a company like that would have better people managing their… ethics. It’s the same sort of thing, isn't it? Artificial inflation, creating a false value? Similar to the house prices, really. Except people's lungs are at risk instead of their bank accounts. That’s a pretty bleak parallel, Mary, but… not inaccurate. It’s all about appearances, isn't it? Making things  look  good on paper, while the reality’s completely different. And who suffers? The average person. Precisely. They were selling a ‘green’ image while simultaneously polluting the atmosphere. And they calculated that paying the fines was cheaper than actually fixing the issue. It's a chilling indictment of corporate greed. You know, my background was in development planning for the oil industry – and even  we  had ethical guidelines, albeit conveniently bendable ones at times.

…Honestly, Marjorie, I don't know  why  I bother sometimes. Trying to explain things to young Thomas is like talking to a brick wall. He gets all huffy if you so much as suggest he might be looking at things a bit…askew. Thomas always was a sensitive soul, Arthur. Takes after his mother, that one. Though, mind you, your approach isn’t always the gentlest, is it? Straight to the point, you are. Sometimes folks need a little softening up before you start pointing out their… deficiencies. Deficiencies is a bit strong, isn't it, George? He just doesn’t see things the same way. He's convinced these new houses going up on the old meadows are a good thing. Says it’s ‘progress’. Progress! It's ruining the countryside. Ruining it! Exactly! And I tried to tell him, I said, “Thomas, son, you remember when we used to walk Maisie the dog out there? Fields as far as the eye could see!” He just said something about needing housing for young families. As if  we  didn’t need a bit of peace and quiet. He's probably thinking about Sarah and little Emily. They’re struggling to find somewhere decent. Still, doesn't make those concrete boxes any prettier. Remember old Farmer Giles? He fought tooth and nail to keep that land. He did. A lovely man. And all for nothing. They just steamrolled right over him. It's the same everywhere, isn’t it? I read about it in the paper last week – they're planning another development near Harrow, where I grew up. Just swallowing up green space. It's a disgrace. And the thing is, nobody seems to be thinking about the infrastructure! The roads are already choked. The doctors can't cope. And what about the schools? They're overflowing as it is. They say they'll build a new school. They always say that. Takes years, it does. And by then, there’s another hundred houses needing a school. It's all a bit of a mess, really. Speaking of messes… Have you sorted that blasted computer out yet, Arthur? Don't even mention it. The thing is possessed. Keeps asking me for a ‘password’. What password? I don't  have  a password! It’s supposed to be simple, for looking at the gardening websites, not cracking codes at GCHQ. Oh, Arthur, you and technology.

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  loves  to hear himself talk about the Krebs cycle. Like, we get it, it’s important for respiration, but does he need to dedicate an entire lesson to memorising every single enzyme? It's brutal. Tell me about it! I swear, Biology is trying to actively kill my brain cells. I spent three hours last night trying to differentiate between mitosis and meiosis. Three hours! And I  still  get confused. You guys are complaining about Biology? Try Physics. Mr. Harrison actually  enjoyed  setting us a problem involving quantum entanglement and a theoretical spaceship. A  spaceship ! Where are we even supposed to get the context for that? Oh, come on, that sounds kinda cool actually. A bit extra, but cool. Although, yeah, Davies is… intense. Remember when he went on that twenty-minute tangent about the evolutionary advantage of hiccups? Oh god, yes! And then tried to demonstrate a hiccup. It just came out as a weird grunt. Mortifying. Speaking of evolution though, did you guys see that TikTok going around? The one about how humans are still evolving, and our wisdom teeth are basically disappearing because we don’t need to chew as much anymore? Yeah! My little sister showed me. It was going viral. Apparently, jaw size is shrinking too. They said something about soft food diets. Honestly, makes sense, doesn't it? We’re getting softer as a species. It's weird to think about, isn’t it? Like, everything we think of as ‘normal’ about our bodies is just…temporary. A snapshot in time based on what our ancestors needed. It’s evolution, innit? That’s what it  is . But it does make you think about what we’re selecting  for  now. Are we accidentally breeding out useful traits? Maybe we're breeding out the ability to cope with hardship? Everything's so easy now. But then again… I saw another TikTok, this one was about how online dating is changing mate selection. Apparently, people are more likely to choose partners based on perceived social status and looks now, because it’s all curated online. Oh god, no. Don’t get me started on dating apps. It's all just superficial. And the amount of ghosting! It's just…rude. Like, just say you’re not interested. It is weird, though, isn’t it? How gender roles come into play even on those apps.

Honestly, the whole thing with Mum’s infection has just been  stressful . They kept saying it wasn't anything to worry about, just a water infection, but she was so floppy, so unlike herself. She really went downhill quick, didn’t she? I popped round Tuesday and she was barely responding. I’ve seen her a bit brighter today, thank goodness. Is she still on those awful antibiotics? Awful doesn’t begin to cover it. They knock the stuffing right out of you, those things. And then the probiotics to  try  and fix the damage… it’s a never-ending cycle. I feel like I’m rattling with tablets these days. Rattling with tablets! You always were a little hypochondriac, Elsie. Though I must admit, Maureen, you're right. Those antibiotics are rough. Makes you feel worse than what you’ve got, sometimes. They said it was a complicated UTI, complicated because of her age and… well, everything. And then they were worried about pneumonia on top of it. It was a bit frightening, to be honest. They kept running tests. Poor love. It’s just… getting old isn't for the faint-hearted, is it? My Doris had a scare last year with her hip. Thought she'd broken it, turned out to be just inflammation, but the waiting, the worrying… It’s the waiting that gets you. Sitting in that hospital, surrounded by the sick, and all you can do is  wait . It feels so helpless. Hospitals. Don’t get me started. Last time I went, parking cost more than the appointment! And the food… You’d get more flavour from a cardboard box. Dad, you always complain about the hospital food. Though you’re not wrong, it’s never exactly gourmet. I was reading about acupuncture for pain management. Apparently, it can be really helpful for arthritis, you know, for Mum’s hands. Acupuncture? Oh, I don’t know about sticking needles in! Seems a bit… drastic. I tried that reflexology once, didn’t feel a thing. Waste of money, if you ask me. Oh, I’ve tried everything. Nothing really touches it, does it? It’s just something you live with. Though Mrs. Higgins down the road swears by cod liver oil. Says it’s kept her going all these years. Cod liver oil! That’s a remedy from the dark ages. I remember my mum making me choke it down as a boy.

Right, so, we were talking about… well, about some really difficult things, weren't we? About things that happened a long, long time ago. Things that weren’t fair. Like when Mum accidentally ate  my  biscuit? That wasn’t fair! That wasn't  quite  the same, sweetie. This was about…people being treated very badly, a very long time ago. It’s called slavery. Slavery? What’s that? Is it like when Leo makes me share his Lego? It’s… a bit like that, actually, because it's about someone taking something that isn't theirs. But much,  much  worse. Imagine someone deciding you didn’t belong to your mum and dad anymore, and they made you work for them, and wouldn’t let you choose what you did, or where you went. And they could be really mean to you. That’s horrible! Why would they do that? That’s a really good question. Sometimes it was because they were greedy and wanted free work. Sometimes they… thought they were better than other people, which is, you know, completely wrong. It happened a lot in America, a long time ago. People from Africa were brought over to America and forced to work as slaves. But… why didn't they just  leave ? Oh, Leo, if only it were that simple. They weren’t allowed to. They were kept prisoners. They faced terrible punishments if they tried to escape. It’s… a really complicated story, and a really sad one. It was a very cruel system. And even when slavery was  officially  stopped, it took a long time for people to be treated equally. So… it’s like when Jasper the cat tries to steal my toys and I can’t get them back? In a way, yes. It's about someone taking something they haven’t earned the right to take. But imagine that happening to  you , Amelia. Every single day. And not just toys, but your freedom, your family, your whole life. Did people fight it? Did heroes come and save them? Yes, they did. There were lots of brave people, both Black and white, who fought against slavery. Some of them helped slaves escape to freedom on a secret route called the Underground Railroad. It wasn't a real railroad, it was just a way to describe the network of people who helped. And then there was a terrible war… the American Civil War.

Honestly, David, I don’t know  how  you watch those true crime documentaries. They give me the creeps! I had to turn off that one about the antique dealers… far too unsettling. Oh, come on, Brenda. It's fascinating! The psychology of it all, the detective work… it’s like a puzzle. Besides, it’s better than another re-run of ‘Bargain Hunt’, isn’t it? Though I do admit, that bloke Tim Wonnacott was a loss. Speaking of puzzles, did you see that article about the woman who solved a cold case using genetic genealogy? It's incredible what they can do now. It’s like real-life detective work, but with algorithms. Algorithms. Everything's algorithms these days. Reminds me of that time I tried to explain online banking to old Mr. Hemmings next door… nearly gave him a heart attack. Thought I was a scammer, he did. Poor old Hemmings. He’s a good ‘un, though. Always offering me a biscuit, even if he does think the television’s spying on him. Saw him talking to his telly the other day. Said ‘Now then, you won't be telling tales on me, will ya?’ Oh, Arthur, you’re terrible! But he’s sweet, isn’t he? I popped round with a Victoria sponge yesterday, and he insisted on giving me one of his prize-winning marrows in return. It was enormous! Marrows the size of small children, that’s Hemmings all over. Speaking of gardens, how's your rosemary doing, Brenda? You were worried about the frost. It survived, surprisingly! A little battered, but it’s still going strong. Though the squirrels are having a field day with the bird feeder. I swear they’re plotting against me. They sit on the fence, taunting the cat! They’re little bandits, aren’t they? I saw one trying to get into a neighbour’s compost bin the other day – looked like he was attempting a full-body squeeze. Reminds me of when we had Buster, our spaniel. Absolute menace around the kitchen. Could sniff out a dropped crumb from a mile away. Spent half my life cleaning up after him. Ah, Buster! A good dog, that one. Proper cheeky, though. Used to steal sausages off the barbecue when you weren't lookin'. Nearly gave Margaret a fit! We were thinking of going to Cornwall this year. Haven’t been for ages.

Honestly, this dishwasher is a blessing, but it's  always  full. It's like a bottomless pit, isn't it? Right, who wants the job of putting away the cutlery? Not me. It’s pokey. I'm building a railway! It's going to go all the way to… to Hogwarts! Hogwarts, eh? Ambitious. Is George Stephenson helping you with that? Who’s George Stephenson? Is he a wizard? No, darling, not a wizard. He was a… a very clever engineer. A long,  long  time ago. Before electricity, even. He built some of the first proper railways. Think about it – trains weren't always like they are now, sleek and speedy. He figured out how to make them work, how to use steam to pull them. Steam? Like when Mummy makes hot chocolate? Sort of! But much, much bigger and hotter. He made the ‘Rocket’, which was one of the fastest trains of his day. He wanted to make travelling faster and easier for everyone. Faster than a broomstick? Well, probably not  faster  than a really good broomstick, but definitely faster than a horse and cart! He was trying to do something similar to what the people in Harry Potter were trying to do with the Knight Bus, only without the magic. The Knight Bus is purple! And it jumps! And it smells like old socks! Ron said so. That’s… a very accurate description according to Rowling, actually. But back to George Stephenson. He was incredibly important because he basically kickstarted the railway age. Imagine trying to get everywhere without trains! It would take forever. But Harry gets everywhere with Floo Powder! Yes, Harry does. Although, even  he  uses the train sometimes, doesn’t he? The Hogwarts Express. That's kind of like George Stephenson’s legacy, in a way – a magical train connecting people. Can we read about George Stephenson? After our Harry Potter chapter? We absolutely can. There are some lovely picture books about him at the library. He didn't have a magic wand, but he had a brilliant mind. Speaking of brilliant minds, have either of you finished your times tables practice? Not even close! I was too busy designing the Hogwarts Express route. It needs a loop-de-loop! A loop-de-loop? That sounds… hazardous. Maybe we can focus on the engineering aspect of  that  after the times tables. Honestly, linking George Stephenson to Hogwarts is brilliant, though.

Right, so listen to this. Apparently, Brenda's been absolutely  smashing  it on Words With Friends. Like, consistently three-hundred-and-something points a game. It's suspicious, innit? She’s never been one for, ya know, words. Brenda? Our Brenda? The one who thinks ‘quinoa’ is a type of exotic bird? No way. She’s cheating, Jamie. Absolutely cheating. Probably using one of those word-finder websites. She’d be terrible at hiding it, wouldn't she? She'd be braggin' about it to everyone. Remember when she tried to convince us she’d won the lottery but just hadn’t ‘cashed the ticket yet’? Yeah, that was a classic. Brenda’s a character. Reminds me of me Auntie Mavis. She convinced the whole family she'd become a qualified dolphin trainer. Turned out she’d just been watching a documentary. Exactly! It’s the brazenness of it all. Still, it’s good entertainment. Speaking of entertainment… anyone fancy a proper supper club night soon? I was thinking we could do a Moroccan theme. I’ve been finding some wicked recipes online. Oh, amazing! I'm in. I could contribute a tagine, maybe? Although, I did have a slight disaster last week trying to copy that Persian saffron rice… it ended up looking like radioactive orange mush. Oh, dear. Sounds…vibrant. I’m happy to handle the seating and general ambiance. Maybe light some proper candles. I was thinking of doing a themed one at the café, but then I remembered the fire regulations are a nightmare. Seriously, they want me to have a fire marshal on duty for anything beyond a tealight. Crikey. Bureaucracy, eh? It's the same back home. Trying to get a license to serve coffee outside…forget about it. Too many hoops to jump through. Makes you wonder why anyone bothers. Tell me about it. I'm still chasing up that issue with the landlord about the leaky ceiling in my flat. He keeps saying he'll "get to it," but it's been six weeks and I'm starting to think I need to actually contact a solicitor. It’s a proper headache. Ugh, landlords. Mine's alright, thankfully, just… a bit useless. He sent me a text the other day asking if I remembered to pay the council tax. Like, seriously? He has the bank statements! You need to know your rights, love.

Honestly, this week has been  manic . Year 10 are testing every boundary they can find. I swear, I spend more time breaking up arguments over who sat where than actually supervising their work. Oh, tell me about it. Though, thankfully, my battles are usually with the printer refusing to cooperate. It’s developed a distinct personality, and it’s a  grumpy  one. Did you manage to get away for half term, at least? We did, thankfully. Just a long weekend in Cornwall. Rain for most of it, naturally. That's Britain for you. But the kids loved building sandcastles in the drizzle, so all was not lost. How about you, Anya? Did you go anywhere exciting? Not particularly exciting, no. I went back to visit my mum in London. It's always good to see her, though flights back to Russia are…complicated right now, to say the least. She made pelmeni, though.  Lots  of pelmeni. I think I’m still full. Oh, pelmeni! That sounds lovely. I’ve only had it a couple of times, at a Russian restaurant in Cambridge. So comforting food, isn’t it? I’m usually more of a roast dinner sort of person, myself. Very British, I suppose. My daughter, Emily, is trying to get me into more…adventurous cooking. Adventurous? What does that entail? Is she trying to turn you into a sushi master? Worse, actually. She's vegan now. And thinks I should be too. She’s currently pushing for a lentil shepherd’s pie. I drew the line at the seaweed burgers, though. Oh dear! That sounds…challenging. My little brother went through a vegan phase. It lasted about a week. Said he missed cheese too much. Honestly, cheese is a national treasure. Exactly! It  is  a national treasure. Emily will come around, she always does. Though, I suspect I'll be eating a separate meal for foreseeable future. Speaking of children, how old is your little one now? I remember you mentioning a son. Dimitri is three. Three and a half, he's very specific about the 'half'. He's…a handful. Keeps me on my toes, that's for sure. And very demanding of Paw Patrol. Honestly, I think I know the theme tune better than my own name. Oh, Paw Patrol! My youngest went through that phase. It's permanently etched into my brain. They are  very  good at marketing to toddlers, aren’t they?

Right, so are we definitely going the right way? This roundabout’s a nightmare, init? I swear they change the road markings every week just to confuse people. Relax, love. I’ve used the satnav. We’re heading towards Mothercare, perfectly on route. Honestly, you’d think we were navigating the Amazon, the way you’re carrying on. Aye, she’s right, lass. You always worry too much. Though I will say, Preston’s roundabouts  are  a bit mental. Remember that time we ended up going round the same one three times trying to get to Auntie Brenda’s? Don’t remind me! That was embarrassing. I was like, fifteen, and convinced I knew where I was going. Oh, and Dad, you weren’t exactly helping, shouting directions that were completely wrong! He thought he was being helpful. It’s the thought that counts. Anyway, about Mothercare…did you make a list of everything we need? I’m terrified we’ll forget something crucial. Like, what if we forget the car seat?! I did, yeah. It’s on my phone. We need the car seat, obviously, a few outfits, blankets…and Mum, you said you wanted to look at those sleep pods? Aye, those look comfy. Better than what  I  had as a baby. Just a scratchy blanket and a prayer, more likely! Your Grandma didn’t believe in all this fancy stuff. "Builds 'em character!" she used to say. Well, times have changed, thankfully! Though I do remember being wrapped up in a rather terrifyingly floral blanket as a child. It smelled of mothballs. Oh god, that sounds awful! I’ve seen some proper cute blankets though, tiny little knitted ones. Maybe we should get a few, even if we don't  need  them. Go on then, spoil the little one! You only get one chance to smother them in soft things. Speaking of spoiling, did that survey come back on the house yet? The one the buyer sent over? It did. They picked up on the damp patch in the downstairs loo. It’s not a huge deal, but we’ll have to get it fixed before exchange. That's another thing to add to the list, isn't it? Building surveys are a pain. Actually, talking about fixing things...the kitchen needs a complete overhaul. I was thinking, after we move, maybe we could rip out those awful cabinets and get something more modern?

Honestly, this raid was a disaster. A  complete  disaster. Ooh, what's gone wrong now, love? Still battling dragons with your mates online? Sounds exhausting, that. It  is  exhausting, Mum! And it wasn’t the dragons, it was Gareth. Gareth kept running into the fire. Literally. Over and over. He blames lag, but I think he just...doesn’t think. We were supposed to be getting the Sunstone Amulet, and now it’s probably sitting at the bottom of a lava pit because of him. Gareth, eh? Isn't he the one who argues with the game's AI? I overheard you two the other night. You were explaining to him that the goblin  isn't  deliberately trying to annoy him. He thinks the AI is personally targeting him! It’s… a complex relationship. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if he understands cause and effect. It's like he doesn’t grasp the consequences of his actions. That sounds a bit… worrying, doesn’t it? All this internet gaming, it's not real life, is it? Though I suppose when you’re that age, it feels pretty real. I remember when your dad got addicted to that… what was it, Tetris? Drove me mad! Dad and Tetris is a story for another time. But you’re right, it can be a bit consuming. And Gareth… well, he’s always been a bit… different. He's really bright, but just doesn't always…  connect  the dots. It makes for entertaining gameplay, but frustrating raids. Entertaining for  you  maybe! I’m the one who has to explain to everyone why we failed. It feels like a really basic thing to understand - don’t run into the fire! It's literally glowing red! Perhaps it’s a bit of impulsivity? I was reading an article… it was in that magazine, the one with all the celebrity gossip… but it touched on behavioural psychology a little. Apparently, some people struggle with delaying gratification, and that can look like acting without thinking. It said it’s linked to dopamine levels. Mum, you read celebrity gossip magazines and  also  know about dopamine levels? That's… quite a range. Don't be cheeky. You learn things! Anyway, it got me thinking about how everyone's brain works differently. Your cousin, Amy, she's the one who plans everything six months in advance, isn't she? Opposite end of the spectrum.

Right, so copper conducts heat really well, that’s why so many pans are made of it. But it tarnishes, doesn't it? Gets all green and…well, a bit grim. Unlike stainless steel. This is steel! It’s  super  fast. It doesn’t get grim. Mine’s going to be made of diamond. Diamond's the best. Diamond’s a bit tricky to work with for a car, love. Unless it’s a  Minecraft  car. Speaking of which, what’s everyone been up to in Minecraft today? Any significant diamond finds? I found a whole load of emeralds! And I traded them for a really good enchanted pickaxe. Emeralds are good! Very valuable. Almost as valuable as netherite, isn’t it? Though getting netherite is… an adventure. Netherite is  way  better. You need to go to the Nether to get it. And fight piglins. They’re grumpy. Grumpy is an understatement. They’ll trade with you though, if you have gold. Which reminds me… talking about metals, have you two been taking your vitamins? The ones with the little iron in them? They taste yucky! Like metal. Well, that’s… accurate, actually. Iron does have a taste. Not a  pleasant  one. But it’s important for your blood. I swallowed mine with juice. Didn't taste it then. Good thinking! Clever boy. Now, back to materials. I was thinking about fabrics earlier, for the story I’m writing. You know, the one about Old Man Tiber and the lost city? What city? Is it made of gold? It’s made of… shimmering silk, actually. And guarded by creatures woven from moonlight. I was thinking silk because it’s so strong, despite being so delicate looking. And really expensive. Moonlight creatures sound scary. They  can  be. But Old Man Tiber, he’s not afraid of anything. He used to be a… a treasurer for a dragon. Actually, no, that’s ridiculous. He was a shepherds. A shepherd who discovered a map on the back of a sheep. A map on a  sheep ? Yes! It was a very clever sheep. It had been travelling the world, apparently, and collected all sorts of interesting things on its wool. The map was stitched into the fleece, using threads made of… spun gold! Did the sheep talk? This sheep… this was a particularly special sheep. It didn’t  talk  in words, exactly. It communicated through… bleats of ancient wisdom.

Honestly, this week’s been a right mess. Uni’s just… draining me. Feel like I’m constantly chasing my tail. Tell me about it. History lectures are turning into an endurance test. Professor Armitage just drones on and on. You’d think engaging with the Tudors could be a bit more… lively, wouldn't ya? Least we've got this, eh? Proper good to just switch off for a bit. Aye, proper. Needed this. It's just…everything feels a bit pointless sometimes, d’you know? What’s the point of knowing all about Henry VIII’s wives if I can’t even afford a decent guitar? There you go again, obsessed with guitars. You've said that every time we've been in here for the last month! What is it with you and wanting a new guitar? You’ve already got that lovely acoustic your grandad gave you. It's not  just  a guitar, is it? It's… an escape. Something I’m actually good at. And that one's alright, but it’s not… electric. I want to be able to play proper riffs, y’know? Like the stuff 'The Reytons' do. The Reytons are decent. Bit shouty for me sometimes, though. I prefer something with a bit more… melody. Like ‘The Amazons’. They’re class. Have you seen them live? Nah, not yet. Too skint. Speaking of class, did you see what Gary posted on Facebook? Oh, don’t even. That bloke is asking for trouble. What did he do  now ? You won’t believe it. He was liking… pictures. Really dodgy pictures. Like, seriously concerning pictures. I don't want to go into details. Seriously? Like…  that  kind of dodgy? Blimey. That’s… awful. Did anyone else see? Yeah, a few people commented, telling him to sort himself out. He deleted them all, quickly. But it's stuck in my head, y’know? It’s just… creepy. Makes me feel sick thinking about it. It  is  creepy. Absolutely disgusting. It’s just… hard to fathom how some people think. You have to report that, don't you? To the police or something? Even if it’s just a precaution. I don’t know. I feel like a grass, don’t I? And he  is  someone we’ve known since school. But… aye. You’re right. It’s not right, ignoring it. It just feels… wrong. God, it's horrible thinking about it.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of reading for the EPQ is killing me. Like, Mr. Davies just throws articles at you and expects you to synthesise them into…well, whatever he decides is a coherent argument. It's supposed to be independent research, but it feels incredibly directed. Tell me about it. Mine's on the history of grime music, which I’m actually interested in, but finding properly  academic  sources? Forget it. Everything’s a blog post or a YouTube documentary. Though, finding the documentaries  is  fun, I guess. Have you even started properly planning yours, Leo? You said it was about…sustainable architecture, right? Yeah, sustainable architecture. And I've got a plan, a decent outline, loads of notes…it's the  doing  that's the problem. It all feels so…large. It needs to be, like, seven thousand words. Seven  thousand . Seven thousand? Ouch. My EPQ is on the portrayal of women in Shakespearean comedies. It’s slightly less daunting, I think. Though dissecting all those patriarchal structures is draining. Speaking of draining, has anyone seen that new exhibition at the V&A? The one about Surrealist fashion? No way! Is it any good? I’ve been meaning to go. I saw some pictures online, it looked…weird. In a good way, hopefully. Apparently, it's amazing. Properly thought-provoking. My aunt went last week and she said it made her rethink everything she thought she knew about clothes. She’s really into fashion, so that’s saying something. The V&A feels miles away though. A trek even. I’d rather just stay local. What are you doing later, anyway, Jamie? Mum’s making that veggie shepherd’s pie, if you're interested. She’s been experimenting with lentils again. Ooh, veggie shepherd’s pie sounds good actually. You know, for years I thought vegetarians just…ate salad. My nan genuinely believed that. She’d offer me a plate of lettuce whenever I said I wasn’t eating meat. Oh, bless her! My grandad was the same. He thought vegetarianism was a personal attack on his roast dinners. It’s that whole generation, isn’t it? Very entrenched views. It's funny, he always talked about being properly poor when he was a kid, like really scraping by during the war, and now he's all about abundance and…meat. It's weird, thinking about poverty and food. My mum was talking about her childhood, growing up in Slough, and how they didn't really  have  choices.

Honestly, this place is daylight robbery. £120 a  week  for a room that’s basically a glorified cupboard? And the kitchen… look at it. It's always like this. A biohazard. Tell me about it. I swear, I spent the first week cleaning this kitchen and then someone just… unleashed chaos again. Though, to be fair, it’s usually Jamie. Jamie's a good lad, just… doesn’t quite grasp the concept of ‘cleaning as you go’. My mum would have a fit if she saw this. She'd be brandishing a Dettol wipe before you could blink. Mum would have a  proper  fit. She cleans the whole house, top to bottom, every Saturday morning. No exceptions. Even when she's got a cold. Sounds… intense. My nan's bad, but she mostly just rearranges things. Like, finds a rogue cushion and demands to know why it’s “living a life of sin” on the floor. That's brilliant! My grandma just complains about the price of everything. Everything. Went to visit her last weekend and tried to tell me a loaf of bread cost tuppence back in her day. Mine's the same. Always going on about how everything was cheaper in India. Which, I mean, it probably was. But she forgets she's living comfortably here now, you know? She keeps trying to get me to send her all my student loan. Says I don't need it, I'm getting a 'free' education. Oh, don’t even  start  me on the 'free education' thing. I had to take out a maintenance loan just to afford beans on toast. Seriously. Beans on toast are my staple diet. My mum keeps sending me little care packages with biscuits, but it doesn't exactly cover rent. I'm lucky, my dad helps out a bit. But I still have to work weekends at the pub to cover everything. It’s knackering. Especially after a long week of A-Levels. Oh, speaking of A-Levels… Did you hear what happened with Chloe at school? Apparently, she completely bombed her History exam. She was convinced she'd get an A , and now she’s talking about deferring a year. No way! Chloe? The one who color-coded all her notes and stayed back after every lesson? That’s rough. That’s terrible. History’s a killer. So much to remember. I struggled with the Tudors, personally.

…and honestly, Mrs. Higgins  insisted  little Timmy needed extra glitter on his snowman. Extra! Like, it was a hazard to navigation. He looked like he'd been caught in a snow globe explosion. Oh, bless her. She always did have a flair for the dramatic. A bit much sometimes, admittedly. Reminds me of your Auntie Maureen, actually. Remember her attempts at decorating the Christmas cake? One year it nearly collapsed under the weight of all the sugar flowers. Oh god, yes! And the fondant reindeer that looked more like… like mutated badgers? That was a Christmas to remember. Is Uncle David still grumbling about having to eat a slice despite its structural failings? He occasionally mentions it. Mostly just to wind us up. He secretly loved it, I think. He always did have a soft spot for Maureen’s…enthusiasm. Speaking of family, how’s your mum doing with all the Christmas preparations? Is she attempting another ambitious turkey this year? She insists. Every year she insists. She’s convinced she’s perfected the brine recipe. I’m half expecting Gordon Ramsay to burst through the door and stage an intervention. I’ve subtly suggested a smaller bird, maybe a goose, but she won’t hear of it. It wouldn’t be Christmas, apparently, without a turkey ‘fit for a king.’ She’s a force of nature, your mother. Still, the effort is lovely, isn't it? And it’s good to have traditions, even slightly stressful ones. Are you back to Torquay for the big day, then? Yep. Train down on the 23rd. I’m a bit worried about the weather, though. They're predicting some pretty nasty storms. Hopefully, it won’t mess up everyone’s travel plans. What about you and David? Staying put in Cardiff? We are, yes. David's back is playing up again, so a long journey wouldn't be wise. Besides, we’ve got Fiona and the girls coming down. They're bringing their new puppy, a little scamp called Winston. Apparently, he’s already chewed through half their Christmas decorations. Oh, no! That sounds like chaos! But adorable chaos, I suppose. How are the girls? Last I heard, Lucy was thinking about taking a gap year. She is. She's got her heart set on travelling around Southeast Asia. David's a bit anxious, naturally, but Fiona's being wonderfully supportive. She's helping Lucy plan everything, looking at volunteer opportunities, that sort of thing.

Right, so you’re  sure  this is the quickest route, Dad? It feels like we’ve been circling Kent for the last hour. Everything looks…different. Different? What do you mean, different? It's Kent, lad, it doesn't change much. Though… I suppose they’ve built a few more of those bloody warehouses. And that field where old man Hemmings kept his sheep? Gone. All houses. All of ‘em. Yeah, exactly! It’s… unsettling. Remember when this felt like countryside? Now it’s just one long industrial estate bleeding into housing developments. It's the speed cameras too, honestly. There’s one every five minutes. They're actively trying to take our licenses. They're doing a job, son. Keeping people safe. Although, I do agree, they're a bit enthusiastic. They’re relying on the revenue, that’s what it is. Speaking of jobs, how’s the teaching going? Still wrangling teenagers with their grammar? Still wrangling, yeah. It's good, though. Challenging, obviously. I’ve got a student from… well, originally from Syria. It’s been interesting helping him navigate the idioms, you know? Trying to explain why we say ‘break a leg’ when we mean good luck. It feels a bit…tone deaf when you think about it. That's a good one, isn’t it? Always struck me as a bit odd. It's a weird language, English is. Anyway, you were saying you were thinking about moving to Brighton? Is that still on the cards? Yeah, potentially. Found a few places I like. It’s just… a big step. Leaving London, proper. But I think I need a bit more… space. And less noise. London feels a bit suffocating lately. It’d put me closer to the coast, too. Brighton’s alright. A bit…alternative for my tastes. A lot of stag dos. Remember your Auntie Carol went down there once? Said it was full of people wearing nothing but Speedos. Oh god, Auntie Carol. Never a dull moment with her. Still, it’s a change. Have  you  been feeling alright, by the way? You seemed a bit…off when I first saw you. A bit pale. Just a bit of a bug, really. Got a bit of a tickle in my chest a few weeks back. Thought it might be… you know. But it passed. Doctor said it was probably just a virus. It’s just… getting old, I suppose.

Honestly, that was a  day . The students were… spirited today. Particularly during the seminar on post-structuralism. Someone insisted Derrida was just deliberately trying to be difficult. Oh, the joys of undergraduate philosophy. Sounds about right. Mine were fixated on whether Baudrillard predicted TikTok. I swear, sometimes I feel like I’m running a millennial advice hotline disguised as a sociology lecture. It’s exhausting, isn’t it? Trying to bridge the gap between, you know,  theorists  and… viral dance challenges. Did you manage to escape without needing a lie-down? Managed. Just. I had that meeting with the university PR team afterwards, trying to explain why my research on urban soundscapes isn’t inherently depressing. Apparently, ‘sonic pollution and alienation’ doesn’t scream ‘positive university image’. Oh, good grief. They just want everything rosy and optimistic, don’t they? Like the world is one giant campus picnic. I got a similar grilling last week when I suggested my work on Victorian mourning rituals was… relevant. Relevant! It  is ! People are obsessed with death and grief, even if they’re just experiencing it vicariously through period dramas. They just want soundbites. “Groundbreaking research leads to happier students!” or something equally ridiculous. Exactly! Anyway, enough about work. Distraction tactics are required. I did a bit of online shopping this morning, actually. Found a gorgeous vintage velvet jacket. It's a bit… much, perhaps? Oh, go on! Details. You and 'a bit much' are a winning combination. What colour? Deep emerald green. And it has these amazing gold buttons. It's from that little shop in Brighton, "Retrograde". Remember we went there on that weekend away? Vaguely… was that the one with the slightly aggressive owner and suspiciously cheap prices? The very one! It was a bargain, honestly. Although, I'm starting to worry about my spending. I seem to be accumulating clothes at an alarming rate. It's a coping mechanism, I think. A fluffy, fabric-based coping mechanism. I understand. Retail therapy is a legitimate field of study, if you ask me. Speaking of distractions, have you heard the new Dry Cleaning album? It's brilliant. That sort of detached, observational songwriting… it’s perfect for post-PR-meeting decompression. Dry Cleaning? No, I haven't. I've been stuck in a Joni Mitchell loop for a week. Feeling particularly melancholic, I suppose. Though, maybe I need something a bit less…soul-baring.

Right, onions are softening nicely. Honestly, this smells  much  better than it looked five minutes ago when it was just…chopped onion mountain. You say that every time. It always looks like a disaster zone at the start. But you pull it off. What  is  this wondrous creation tonight, anyway? Smells vaguely…Moroccan? Tagine. I found a recipe online. Lamb, apricots, almonds…it's supposed to be really cosy. Perfect for a drizzly Tuesday. Speaking of cosy, how’s the beanbag coming along? Still seemingly growing by the stitch? It’s…progressing. Slowly. I'm on the sixth ball of yarn. Six! I’m starting to think I should have just bought one. Though, honestly, the meditative quality of the knitting is rather good. It's just the sheer  volume  of wool that’s daunting. It’s taking over the living room. You always underestimate projects. Remember the birdhouse? You swore it would be a quick weekend job and it took a month. That was structurally complex! It needed proper joinery! This is just… giant knitting. Though, I did have a slight crisis with the stitch pattern earlier. Kept adding extra rows. It’s looking a bit… lumpy. Lumpy beanbags are perfectly acceptable. It adds character! Honestly, having something handmade will be wonderful. Much nicer than the mass-produced stuff. Though, speaking of things needing attention… have you had a chance to look at the bathroom? The bathroom? What about it? Is the grout crumbling again? I swear, that stuff disintegrates within months. No, no, the grout’s holding. It’s the shower curtain. It’s… a bit sad, isn’t it? That faded floral pattern is actively depressing me. Depressing you? It's a shower curtain, love. It keeps the water in. Function over form, that’s what I say. But it doesn’t have to be  actively  unpleasant form! I was browsing online earlier, and they have some really lovely ones. Simple, geometric patterns. Or even just a plain, calming colour. That awful beige thing just…exists. It doesn't  enhance  the bathroom experience. You’re planning a bathroom re-design based on a shower curtain? Not a re-design! Just a slight… elevation. And maybe new towels. The current ones are also a bit…tired. I was thinking navy blue? To go with a grey shower curtain? Navy blue towels? Sounds rather…regal. Are we turning the bathroom into a nautical theme now?

…and that Mrs. Higgins, bless her, she's put up fairy lights  already . Fairy lights in October! Feels a bit early, don't it? Though, mind you, a little cheer never hurt anyone, did it? Especially with the weather turnin’ like it is. Proper grey out there. She's always been a bit of a Christmas fanatic, Elsie Higgins. Remember last year? She had a snowman on her roof in November. A  snowman , Arthur. I do, I do! Nearly caused old Mr. Peterson a heart attack, thinkin’ it was the roof collapsin’ in the dark. Goodness me, the fuss. Still, she’s a good soul, Elsie. Always bringin’ round a tin of biscuits. Biscuits are always a good thing. Though, frankly, I'm more concerned about this energy price hike. They're threatening another increase. It’s just…relentless. Oh, don't start on that, David. It’ll give Arthur palpitations. He worries enough as it is. Honestly, you read these newspapers and you’d think the world was ending tomorrow. Now, now, Dorothy, let the man speak his mind. It  is  worryin’, though. Remember when a few quid could keep the house warm all winter? Now…well, it feels like we're just handin' over all our pensions. It’s not just the pensions, Arthur. It impacts everything. The cost of food is going up, transport… I had to increase the price of a repair job at the shop today. Old Mrs. Gable nearly choked on her tea when I told her. Said she’s on a fixed income, naturally. Always the same story, isn't it? The little people get squeezed. And what does the government do? Talk about tax cuts for the wealthy. It’s scandalous. Tax cuts…Hmph. They don’t understand what it’s like to have to count every penny, do they? I remember me father, workin’ down at the sugar beet factory. Hard work, that was. Never complained, though. Just got on with it. Said a man’s gotta provide. It’s a different world now, Arthur. There aren’t the same opportunities. Even reliable employment is scarce for some. My young mechanic, Liam, he’s got two jobs just to make ends meet. Two! And he’s a qualified tradesman. That's just awful. I used to worry about little Timmy when his mum went back to work after maternity leave. She was struggling to afford childcare  and  everything else.

Honestly, this article is ridiculous. “Ten ways to have a minimalist Christmas.” Honestly, who  wants  a minimalist Christmas? It's the one time of year you can go a bit overboard, isn't it? Overboard is putting it mildly, love. Remember your Auntie Brenda’s glitter explosion of 2018? We were finding sequins in the gravy for weeks. Oh god, yes! The glitter incident. That was…intense. I still find myself subconsciously checking my hair for rogue sparkles. Brenda does like to make a statement, doesn’t she? Though, I secretly loved it. It was  festive . And she makes a cracking Christmas pudding, that woman. She does, she really does. But minimalist? Honestly. It's all about the excess! And speaking of excess, have we finalised the food order for Christmas Day? I was thinking goose this year, a change from the usual turkey. Goose is ambitious, isn’t it? A bit…messy. But alright, if you’re set on it. Just promise you won’t attempt to carve it yourself. I still have flashbacks to the turkey debacle of ‘16. I was perfectly capable! It just…needed a little encouragement. And a bit of sawing. "Encouragement" and "sawing" are two very polite words for it, Mum. I think Dad was quietly relieved when I stepped in with the carving knife. It was a good team effort, though. And the dinner  was  lovely, even if it was a little…anatomically correct in its presentation. Right, well, let’s not dwell on past carving failures. Goose it is. We need to get that ordered soon, and all the trimmings. And what about presents? Have you all done your shopping? I've gotten most of mine, just a couple of bits left for your father, David. He’s so difficult to buy for. I’ve started. Got something for you, of course. And something…practical for young Emily. She keeps complaining about her backpack. She needs a new one. I'm still chipping away at it. It's harder than it looks! Everyone either has everything, or they hint at something ridiculously expensive. I'm trying to be mindful of the budget this year, though. Freelancing can be a bit…unpredictable. I've been looking at things for my niece and nephew, mostly art supplies. They're really into drawing at the moment. It’s lovely to see. It's getting expensive, though, isn’t it?

…and honestly, the driving here is something else, isn't it? I thought I was a fairly confident driver, navigating the narrow lanes back in Dorset, but this is… a different level of ‘assertive’. Assertive is putting it mildly, my dear. It's more like organised chaos. I’ve been coming here for nearly fifteen years now, wintering mostly, and you get used to it. Eventually. Though I still clench the jaw a bit when I’m a passenger. It's not the speed, it’s the  proximity . They seem to believe inches don’t exist. Exactly! And the seemingly random overtaking! I nearly had a heart attack yesterday coming back from Bellapais Abbey. A little scooter just  pulled out  in front of us, straight into oncoming traffic. Oh, the scooters. They’re a menace. No headlights, no helmets… it’s a wonder there aren’t more accidents. Thankfully, people are generally quite skilled at dodging. But you're right about Bellapais. Beautiful place, though, isn’t it? All that history… reminds me of bits of Italy, actually. Have you explored the ruins much? A little. It’s breathtaking, especially in the morning light. I took some students there last week. They’re all history students, thankfully, so they were properly appreciative. It’s a bit of a contrast to the curriculum back home, isn’t it? We're mostly bogged down in the Tudors at the moment. It's good to give them something a little…different. The Tudors! Goodness. Always the Tudors. I remember my own history lessons being saturated with Henry VIII and his wives. This place… this is where empires  really  happened. Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman… it layers and layers of it. You feel it, don't you? I do. It feels… weighty. I’ve been trying to get my head around the division, obviously. It’s difficult to understand the history without acknowledging the political situation. That's the tricky bit, isn’t it? It's a sensitive subject, naturally. Most people here are perfectly friendly, hospitable even. But it’s always there, simmering under the surface. You won't find many openly discussing it, especially not with someone they’ve just met. I suspected as much. I overheard a bit of a discussion in a restaurant the other night – couldn’t understand the language, obviously, but the tone was… heated. It made me feel a bit uncomfortable, to be honest.

Honestly, this air is just… oppressive today. It feels like you’re breathing through cotton wool. Did you see old Mrs. Li coughing fit to burst outside the faculty building? I did. It’s getting worse, isn’t it? The pollution index was ‘hazardous’ this morning. I swear it wasn't  that  bad when we first moved here five years ago. Though, to be fair, I was probably wearing rose-tinted glasses, excited about the food and the calligraphy classes. Rose-tinted glasses is putting it mildly! You were practically learning Mandarin overnight, determined to haggle for the best price on dumplings. Remember that unfortunate incident with the tea set? Don't remind me. I thought I was being all savvy, bargaining hard. Turns out I offended the vendor by offering what amounted to pocket change. He gave me  the look . You had to smooth things over with a ridiculously generous tip. Someone had to. Anyway, back to the air… It's worrying. I was reading an article about the long-term effects on lung development in children. Makes you really think about… well, everything. It does. And it’s ironic, isn’t it? We came here for a different pace of life, the ‘authentic’ experience, and now we’re constantly calculating whether it’s safe to go for a run or even just open the windows. Exactly! And then I feel guilty complaining, you know? There are so many people here who are genuinely struggling, and we’re just… academic expats worrying about a bit of smog. Don’t feel guilty. It’s legitimate to be concerned about your health. And it’s not ‘just a bit of smog’. It’s impacting everyone. Speaking of worrying, how did your meeting with Professor Zhang go? You looked rather… intense when you left the department. Oh, that. It was… a discussion. He’s resistant to the idea of incorporating more contemporary British literature into the syllabus. He keeps saying it’s not “relevant” to Chinese students. Not relevant? That’s ridiculous. It’s about expanding perspectives, isn't it? Showing them different literary traditions. What did you say? I tried to explain that literature transcends national boundaries. That Austen, Woolf, even Zadie Smith, deal with universal themes – love, loss, class, identity. He just kept talking about Confucius and the importance of upholding traditional values. It felt like talking to a brick wall.

Right, onions are nearly done. Honestly, this smells  amazing . Did you remember to get the thyme, love? It just makes the whole roast chicken thing, doesn't it? Thyme’s here, safe and sound. Though, I maintain it's a bit much effort for a Tuesday. We had roast chicken on Sunday! Are we turning into our parents? Don't be ridiculous. It’s comforting. Besides, Millie’s been going on about wanting it all week. Aren’t you, love? Mmmhmm. Comfort food is  necessary  after the week I’ve had. My client changed the entire brief  again  this afternoon. Honestly, it's like they don’t even know what they want. Typical. Still, pays the bills, eh? What was it this time? More ‘vibrant’ and ‘dynamic’? Worse. They want it to appear “authentically vintage” but also “cutting edge.” Apparently, those aren't mutually exclusive concepts. I showed it to Liam, and he just laughed. Oh, darling, that sounds awful. Some people just don’t understand copywriting. It’s an art, really. It’s… persuasive writing, dear. Let’s not get carried away. Speaking of art, did you see that documentary about Hockney last night? Absolutely fascinating. I meant to! I got halfway through  Great British Bake Off  and just couldn’t tear myself away. That Rahul… what a sweetie. Though, his biscuit constructions are a bit… ambitious. Oh, Rahul! He’s the absolute best. I’ve been rewatching old episodes on YouTube. It's purely for stress relief. Speaking of relief, I found a load of old photos on my phone. Remember that disastrous holiday to Cornwall when I was about ten?  Disastrous  is an understatement. The tent flooded. You were convinced a seagull stole your biscuit. And your mother… well, let's just say she wasn’t thrilled about the mud. Honestly, it was a comedy of errors. But we all laughed about it for years. Here, let me see… Oh, goodness me! Look at your hair! So much fringe! You looked like a little mushroom. Rude! But accurate. It was the 90s, okay? Everyone had a fringe down to their eyebrows. It’s just good to see those memories. Makes you realize how quickly time goes. I was looking at photos of you two when you first met the other day. You looked so young! Don’t remind me. I had questionable fashion choices. And you had  all  your hair.

…and honestly, the 11’s a nightmare now. Packed every five minutes, especially after four. You’d think with all the extra students coming back, they’d put on another bus, wouldn’t ya? But no. Still the same three rattling things. You're telling me. I tried getting it last week to go to Mill Road, and I ended up just walking. Took about forty minutes, which is slower than the bus  should  be, but quicker than waiting for the next one that wasn't already full. They’ve announced a new route though, haven’t they? The one down Trumpington Road? Supposed to relieve some of the pressure. Oh aye, I saw something about that. Does it go near the station? Because that’s where my mam gets off when she visits. She'd be lost without a decent bus route from there. I think it does, yeah. It loops around Addenbrooke’s and then heads back through Newnham. It's just, knowing Cambridge, it’ll probably be another overcrowded mess within a month. It's not like they're building new roads here, is it? Nah, they’re too busy building more student accommodation. Speaking of things overpriced and packed…I tried to go to the Cambridge University Press bookshop yesterday. Honestly, it was heaving! And everything is so expensive. I just wanted a nice notebook. A  notebook , mind. Ended up leaving empty-handed. That place is ridiculous. It's a tourist trap as much as anything else. You’re better off going to Waterstones, or even the little second-hand bookshops near the market. You can find proper gems there. Did you see that lad protesting outside the Divinity School yesterday? The one with the placard about tuition fees? Aye, I did. Bit of a shouty one, wasn’t he? Wonder what uni he's from. He was a student at Essex, apparently. Got a bit of a telling-off from a porter, but he wasn’t moving. It got quite a crowd. Made me think about uni actually. Remembering all the…enthusiasm. Enthusiasm and questionable life choices. You were a bit of a protester yourself back in the day, weren’t you? Though I seem to remember most of your protests involved demanding better coffee in the library. Hey, caffeine is a basic human right! But, yeah, I did get involved in a few things. Though it was different at Imperial.

…and honestly, the shepherd’s pie at The George was  nothing  like my mother made. Nothing. She used proper lamb, you see, and a sweet potato topping. This was all beef and…well, it tasted like it had been sitting under a warmer since Tuesday. Oh, Mum's shepherd’s pie is legendary. Anything will fall short of that, won’t it? Though, I think we’re being a  little  harsh on The George. It's a pub, not a Michelin-starred restaurant. True. It’s a nice spot for a quick lunch though. And honestly, I’m just glad to be out of the office. This week's been… intense. Three disciplinary hearings in one week. You wouldn’t believe the things people get up to. Oh dear. Always the drama, isn’t there? Though I suppose that’s what keeps you employed. It’s a world away from fractions and equations, I’ll tell you that. Though sometimes, dealing with teenagers felt surprisingly similar to dealing with…well, let’s just say ‘difficult employees’. You’re not wrong about that! Speaking of difficult… how was Liam on the phone last night? Still regaling you with tales of his latest coding triumph? Oh, he’s a treasure, that boy. He was explaining some new algorithm he's developed. Honestly, it went completely over my head, something about 'blockchain' and 'decentralized systems'. I just smiled and nodded and agreed that it sounded terribly clever. He's coming up next weekend, you know. Oh, brilliant! That’s lovely. He’s a good lad. Does he still talk about wanting to move up here permanently? He does. He says he prefers the quiet, the countryside. He’s grown so used to London, though. He worries about… well, boredom. He's a city boy at heart, I think. I keep telling him, there's plenty to do, it just requires a bit more  effort  to find it. He'd get used to it. It's definitely a different pace than London. It's good he has somewhere to come back to though, isn't it? Somewhere… grounding. How’s Sarah? Has she started looking at universities yet? That's the current battleground. She's dead set on art school in London. Absolutely determined. I'm trying to gently suggest she keep her options open, maybe something a bit more…practical. Though, what do I know?

Honestly, it's lovely just  being  here, isn’t it? Proper London. Though I still maintain Woolwich is a bit…rough around the edges. Remember when we first came down here with the kids? Little Leo was convinced the boats were going to crash into each other. He did, didn’t he? Bless him. He was terrified of anything bigger than a puddle back then. And you’re right, Woolwich has improved, but it still feels a world away from Greenwich. Look, you can almost see the Cutty Sark now. It’s a beautiful sight, though. Even on a grey day like this. Beautiful, yes. Though I always think of the sheer  effort  involved in building those things. And the people who sailed them… imagine being stuck on the water for months. No Spotify, no Netflix, just… the sea. And biscuits. Probably. Probably a lot of biscuits. And we complain about the commute! Speaking of which, I’m dreading the thought of getting the tube  and  the DLR to get back after this. Honestly, I sometimes think we should have just bitten the bullet and bought a car. Oh, don’t start that again. We’ve been over this a million times. A car in London? A money pit, a stress inducer, and a guarantee of never finding a parking space. No thank you. I’d rather walk, even if it takes twice as long. And it’s healthier. Besides, you hate driving. I don't  hate  driving. I just… find it utterly unremarkable. It’s just point A to point B. And frankly, sometimes I wish point B involved a beach in Spain, and not a cramped train carriage. We haven't had a proper family holiday in ages. I know, I know. It's been too long. Work’s been utterly mental for both of us. And saving for a deposit for a bigger place… it all adds up. Remember that ridiculous American recipe I was trying to follow last week?
