The one for the chocolate brownies? Vaguely. Something about… cups? Cups! Everything in American baking is measured in  cups . What even  is  a cup? It's not a standard measurement! It’s just… arbitrary! How am I supposed to accurately translate ‘one and a half cups of flour’ into grams? It’s a nightmare. I ended up just guessing and they were… edible. Thankfully. You and your precision.

Honestly, this rain is  relentless . It’s been chucking it down all morning. Feels like proper November weather, not mid-June. Tell me about it, love. Makes you wanna just curl up with a cuppa and a good book, doesn’t it? Though, trying to get anywhere is a nightmare. Had a right struggle getting Mrs. Henderson’s shopping delivered this morning. Nearly slipped on the pavement twice. Elsie’s lost Barnaby again. Honestly, that bear has more adventures than I do. She's convinced he’s gone swimming in the garden pond. Swimming? Elsie and her imagination! Remember when she thought the washing machine was a spaceship? Oh, I do! She was trying to pack Barnaby for the journey then, wasn't she? Bless her. She’s a little whirlwind, that one. She is. It's exhausting, but… worth it. This is the third time this week Barnaby's gone AWOL. I'm starting to think we need to invest in one of those ‘Build-a-Bear’ workshops. At least then she can make a proper, traceable bear. And maybe one that doesn’t attract mud quite so readily. Oh, ‘Build-a-Bear’! I went to one of those with Chloe when she was little. It's brilliant, but expensive! And then they’re attached to the thing  forever . Chloe’s still got her purple unicorn, even though she's practically a teenager now. It's the sentiment, innit? They keep those things for years. Like little reminders of when they were tiny. Speaking of tiny… how’s Leo doing with the potty training? Still a work in progress? Don’t even  ask . We had a minor incident this morning involving the rug, a full bladder, and a very vocal protest. I swear, he knows exactly when I’m just about to get something done. It's a power play, I'm convinced. Oh god, potty training. I vaguely remember that being… intense. Chloe was surprisingly easy, actually. She just  got  it. But her friend, little Alfie… his mum was practically camping out in the bathroom for a week! It’s different with every child, isn't it? You just have to keep at it. Honestly, sometimes I think my job is easier than being a full-time mum. Dealing with grumpy residents is one thing, but a toddler with a will of steel? That's something else. It is!

Right, so, Operation ‘Life Audit’ continues, I suppose. It feels a bit…formal, doesn’t it? Doing this on holiday. But we said we would. It does feel a little odd, doesn't it? Discussing five-year plans whilst surrounded by kookaburras. But honestly, James, we’ve been drifting a bit. And this house-sitting gig gives us the headspace. Less… London. Less 'everything all the time'. Drifting is a good word. I felt like I was just… reacting to things instead of  making  them happen. The tech startup’s doing okay, genuinely. But “okay” isn’t really the goal, is it? I was talking to Liam the other day – he’s seriously considering joining forces with Ben and Sarah on that eco-tourism venture in Costa Rica. Oh, really? Liam? I always thought he’d stick with the corporate world. That’s…bold. And smart, I think. They’d be a good team. A bit…intense, maybe, all four of them together, but good. Are you… envious? Not envious, exactly. More… prompted. It’s made me think about what I  really  want. The money’s good with the startup, yeah, but the daily grind… chasing funding, dealing with investors… it doesn’t fill the tank, you know? It doesn't hit the same spot as, say, working with my hands, being outside, something… tangible. I was rather hoping we could talk about that. I’ve been looking at some online courses – sustainable building, permaculture design… crazy, I know. Not crazy at all! You’ve always been brilliant at practical things. Remember the shed you built at Mum’s? It's still standing! And you always said you felt a bit stifled by the city. It’s a massive shift from coding, though. Would it be financially viable? That's what I'm a bit worried about. We’ve got the mortgage, and… well, you know… the potential for kids. That’s precisely why we’re doing this, isn’t it? To work that out. I’ve been running some numbers. If I scaled back the startup – maybe brought in a partner to handle the day-to-day – and supplemented it with some freelance consulting and, eventually, some hands-on work… it's possible. Not lavish, obviously, but comfortable. Enough to, you know, maybe think about starting a family without crippling ourselves with debt. Okay. That’s… encouraging. And genuinely, that sounds like it would suit you.

…and then he just  looked  at me, proper deadpan, and said “You think you’re a good driver ‘cause you can parallel park?” Like, what even  is  that? Sounds like Mark, to be fair. He’s a wind-up merchant, that one. Always has been. Remember when he convinced old Mrs. Higgins he’d won the lottery? Oh god, yes! She was offering to bake him a celebration cake for a week! He felt terrible eventually, didn’t he? But the initial reaction… priceless. It’s that Wigan accent, isn’t it? Sounds perpetually mischievous. No offence, Liam. None taken. It's a gift, lass. A gift. Though, honestly, sometimes  I  can't understand what I'm saying when I'm back home. Everything just blurs into a sort of Northern mush. You think? I go back to Warrington and me mum says I'm talking 'posh' now. Apparently, learning to explain audit reports has altered my dialect. You’re always exaggerating, Ben. You still sound proper Scouse when you're annoyed. Speaking of accents, have you heard Sarah trying to do a Yorkshire accent? It's… a choice. Hey! I'm right here! It’s a nuanced accent, alright? It's not just about shouting 'Ey up!' every other word. It's getting there, love. It’s getting there. Sarah’s committed, that’s what counts. It started with a Pokémon obsession, if I recall. Something about wanting to sound like a Gym Leader? Pokémon? Ah, that’s a rabbit hole I actively avoid. Too much remembering types and weaknesses. My brain’s full enough just tryin' to recall what I had for breakfast. You haven't changed, Liam. Still terrible with remembering things. Remember that camping trip last summer? You forgot the tent poles. Don’t remind me. We slept in the car. It wasn’t ideal. And it rained. Solid. I still maintain it was character building. Plus, we saw that badger. That made it worth it. Actually, talking about animals… my auntie keeps trying to convince me to get chickens. Says it’s ‘therapeutic’. Chickens? In Leeds? Where would you even keep them? On your balcony? That’s what I said! She said something about a coop. Honestly, she’s gone proper country since she retired. And she’s started smoking again. Oh, no. She’d finally given up, hadn't she? That’s a shame. It’s just…comfort, innit?

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘is ‘eart, ‘e goes and tries to dribble the football  inside  the house. Right through Mrs. Higgins’ best china display! Nearly gave the poor woman a turn, it did. Still makes me chuckle thinkin’ about it. Though, she weren’t amused at the time, mind. Oh, Arthur, you and your stories! Timmy was always a handful, wasn’t he? Though, it’s good to see him settled now, with little Maisie. Such a sweet girl. Speaking of sweet, this roast is lovely, dear. Did you make the gravy with that stock cube I got? The proper one, not the cheap stuff. It is delicious, honestly. Mum, your gravy is legendary. And Grandpa, that story is brilliant. It reminds me of some of the chaos we had during the university football intramurals. Absolutely wild. Wild is an understatement. I still have nightmares about Dave trying to play goalkeeper. He genuinely believed shouting ‘I’m here!’ was an effective tactic. Shouting at a football! Reminds me of the managers we ‘ad back in the day. All bark and no bite, mostly. Though, I suppose they tried. It weren’t like today, with all the fancy tactics and foreign players. Real football used to be… well,  real . It’s different now, definitely. More globalized, more commercialized. But there’s still some fantastic skill out there, isn't there? I was watching the Women’s World Cup highlights earlier. Some incredible goals. Oh yes, that Lionesses team. Lovely girls. So determined. It’s about time women were given the same opportunities, innit? It’s not fair, all that fuss over the men. Though, I do enjoy a good football match myself, when England's playing. Absolutely. And the level of coverage is improving. But it's a wider societal thing, isn’t it? About equal pay, equal representation… it all connects. Speaking of things that need fixing, did you see that new policy proposal… Now, no politics at the dinner table, please. I’ve ‘ad enough of that on the telly. It's all just yappin' and nothin' gets done. It's like watchin' a pack of dogs arguin' over a bone. Give me a good nature program any day. David Attenborough's a national treasure. Grandpa, you’re right. Let’s save the political debates for another time. Although it  is  impacting funding for universities, which is… concerning. Oh dear, that doesn't sound good.

…and honestly, the essay just felt… pointless. Like, genuinely. Three thousand words on the semiotics of garden gnomes? Who  cares ? It’s not even a module I particularly liked, I just needed the credits. Garden gnomes? Seriously? That sounds… uniquely Lancaster. I’m glad I’m doing History. At least  that  feels vaguely useful. Though even then, sometimes I question everything. You thinking about actually… dropping out then? You said ‘felt pointless’ with a tone. I don’t  know . It’s just… overwhelming, innit? It’s not even the work, it’s the whole… performance of it. Pretending to be interested, pretending to be grown up, pretending I have any clue what I want to  do  with my life. Back in Falmouth, I knew I wanted to be near the sea, maybe work with boats, something practical. Here… I just feel lost. Yeah, I get that. Being away from home does that to you, doesn't it? Makes you realise how much of your identity was tied up in where you  were  from. My Nan always says leaving Liverpool is like having your legs chopped off. Dramatic, but she’s got a point. It's a proper feeling, being ripped out of your context. Your Nan sounds brilliant. Mine just tells me to “buck up and finish what I started.” Very Cornish of her. No nuance, just… grit. It wouldn't kill her to ask how I  am , though. It's always the course, the grades. Mine’s the same. It's all about "a good education" and "not wasting opportunities". They don't understand that sometimes the opportunity  is  wasting time on something that isn’t right for you. Speaking of wasting time… look at your shoes! What about them? They’ve seen things. Adventures. They’ve seen a field. And brought half of it back with you. Honestly, you’re tracking mud everywhere! Did you even try to wipe them? No. I was contemplating the existential dread of garden gnome semiotics, alright? Shoe-cleaning wasn't a priority. Besides, they look… lived in. Lived in and actively contaminating my rug. You’re just like you were when we were kids, remember? Always covered in dirt, building dens. I remember that time you tried to build a raft to go across the boating lake in Newquay. Oh god, don't remind me. It was a  terrible  raft. Made of driftwood and stolen bin bags.

…and honestly, the amount of passive-aggressive post-it notes Brenda leaves on the shared fridge is  astounding . Like, seriously, who needs a detailed diagram of how to load the dishwasher? It’s not rocket science! Oh, Brenda sounds… delightful. It’s always the seemingly harmless ones, isn’t it? The quiet, efficient types who are secretly judging your life choices via appliance usage. Exactly! And she’s the head of accounts! The power… it’s terrifying. Anyway, enough about office politics. It’s so good to actually  see  you, properly. It feels like ages. Last time was that disastrous Christmas party, wasn't it? Where Dave tried to serenade everyone with a karaoke version of Bohemian Rhapsody? Don't remind me! My ears are still recovering. And yes, a solid six months, at least? Life just…happens, doesn't it? Work’s been a bit chaotic, honestly. Pearson are pushing this huge new marketing campaign for their online learning platforms. All very ‘future of education’ and ‘personalised learning journeys’… buzzwords galore. Oh god, sounds exhausting. I'm glad I escaped the corporate world, relatively speaking. Project co-ordinating is stressful enough without having to pretend you’re revolutionising anything. What are you actually  doing  practically? Mostly spreadsheets and trying to herd cats – getting different teams to agree on a colour scheme for a banner ad feels like a major achievement some days. And a lot of data analysis. They’re obsessed with A/B testing everything. I think they even A/B tested the font size on an internal memo last week. Seriously? That's...commitment. Or madness. Either way. Have you been seeing anyone lately? Last I heard you were tentatively dating that architect, what was his name… Ben? Ben. Right. Ben was… a mistake. Very handsome, very into brutalist architecture, very little interest in, well,  me . We went to that new modern art gallery, and he spent the entire time lecturing me about the concrete composition of the building. It was less a date and more an architectural thesis defense. Oh, ouch. That does sound…singular. Singular is a kind word. Back to being single and enjoying my own company, basically. How about you? Any romantic entanglements I should know about? Still friends with Liam? Liam and I are firmly in the ‘just friends’ zone. It's surprisingly peaceful. And no, no one particularly noteworthy on the dating front.

Right, now then. Three quid forty-nine for a pack of…fairy lights? Honestly, you wouldn't think fairy lights were so expensive these days. What’cha buying, Mum? More Christmas stuff already? It's only November. Not  just  Christmas stuff, love. Though, yes, a bit festive. It's for Mrs. Higgins. Her garden got a bit…blown about in the winds last week, poor soul. She was admiring mine at the village fete, so I thought I’d get her some to cheer her up. It's all on eBay, mind. Best prices, usually. eBay? Don't you usually go for Amazon? It's quicker, isn't it? And the delivery's faster. Amazon’s alright, don't get me wrong. But it's often a bit pricier, and sometimes you’re paying for the convenience more than the actual item. eBay's got proper bargains if you're willing to have a bit of a rummage. It’s like a car boot sale, but online. A car boot sale? Sounds stressful. Remember that time Dad bought that…thing…on eBay? The one that was supposed to be a vintage radio but turned out to be a broken biscuit tin with a speaker stuck on it? Oh, don’t remind me! Your father and his "bargains." He thought he'd found a steal. Lesson learned, though. You’ve got to check the seller's feedback, that’s the golden rule with eBay. And read the description  carefully . This seller’s got a 98% positive rating, and they're a local business, too – Malton Garden Supplies. 98% is pretty good. So, what's the difference between buying from a business on eBay and just buying from Amazon directly? Well, with Amazon, you're dealing with Amazon. They handle everything – the shipping, the returns, the customer service… it’s all streamlined. On eBay, you're buying  from someone . It could be a business like this, or it could be a fella clearing out his attic. So there’s slightly more risk. But you can often negotiate prices on eBay – you wouldn't be doing that with Amazon. Negotiate? Like…offer them less money? Aye, sometimes. Especially if it's a longer listing and they haven't had any bids or interest. It's not always successful, mind. You have to be polite about it, of course. Just send a message saying something like, "Would you consider £3 instead?"

Honestly, this coffee's not quite right, is it? A bit…weak. Used to be able to stand a spoon up in a cup of coffee down the pub, you know. Proper stuff. Oh, Dad, you always say that. It’s perfectly good coffee, honestly. I made it exactly how you usually like it - one sugar, dash of milk. Maybe your tastebuds are just getting…refined with age? Refined? Don’t be daft, love. It’s just… things aren’t  made  like they used to be. Everything’s watered down. The coffee, the telly programmes, even the people! Oh, here we go. The "everything was better in the old days" lecture. It's not a lecture! It's an  observation . Remember Mrs. Higgins from next door? Used to bake the most wonderful Victoria sponge. You just don't get baking like that anymore. All pre-packaged rubbish. True, Mrs. Higgins was a legend. But people bake now, Dad. They just… share it on Instagram rather than bringing it round the garden fence. Besides, you loved her sponge because she’d always slip you an extra large slice when Mum wasn’t looking. Well, a man’s gotta have his pleasures, doesn't he? Speaking of pleasures… how's work going? Still slaving away at that… production controlling place? It's not  slaving , Dad! It's actually pretty good. Challenging. We’re launching a new product line next month – eco-friendly packaging for a big supermarket chain. It’s been a lot of late nights, but it’s rewarding. Eco-friendly, eh? Another one of those things. Costs a fortune, I imagine. Everything’s getting so expensive. Did you see the price of petrol this week? Robbery, I tell you. Pure robbery. It is pricey, yeah. Although, with working in Cambridge now, I’ve started cycling to work most days. It’s good for the environment  and  my wallet. Cycling? In  Cambridge ? You're a brave girl. Those students haven’t got a clue. They just appear out of nowhere, heads down, glued to their phones. Nearly ran me over last week, trying to cross Mill Road. You and Mill Road! It’s a hazard zone, I agree. But you love a good grumble about Mill Road. Have you been to that new Italian place, "Bella Notte"? Apparently, it’s amazing. Italian? Hmph. Used to be a proper chippy there, you know.

Right, so we're actually doing this then? Christmas  at  your place, Liv? Feels a bit…radical, innit? Usually we rotate. Radical? Jamie, it's a house! And a kitchen, importantly. You know my flat’s tiny. Plus, Mum and Dad are staying with Auntie Carol this year, so it's either here or squeezed onto her sofa with a miniature poodle trying to steal your Quality Street. Quality Street is a  battleground , let me tell you. Last year, my Nan nearly took a swing at Uncle Barry for going for the toffee deluxe. Crikey. Sounds…intense. Christmas with families, eh? Different gravy. Back home, it was always beach barbecues and avoiding sunburn. Beach barbecues  sound  idyllic, actually. Beats arguing over Brussels sprouts. Speaking of which, are you doing the full Christmas dinner, Liv? Because if so, I'm bringing reinforcements – mainly in the form of strategically deployed stuffing. Of course I'm doing a full dinner! I’m a baker, Jamie, organizational skills are built in. Turkey, all the trimmings, Yorkshire puds… the whole shebang. Though I  am  thinking of doing a gingerbread house this year, a proper one, like something out of a film. Ooh, yes! A gingerbread house competition would be brilliant! I'm fairly competitive when baked goods are involved. Don't underestimate me. I could contribute pavlova, maybe? Bit of Aussie flair to the spread. Though, fair warning, it’s proper sweet. Pavlova sounds amazing, mate. Seriously. So, logistics. Getting back to Birmingham on Boxing Day. Awful isn’t it? All the roads packed and I swear everyone decides to learn to drive  on  Boxing Day. It’s a nightmare. Absolute nightmare. Last year it took me six hours to get back from London. Six! And I saw something…disturbing. Disturbing how? Don't tell me you saw another one of those roadkill deer. You were going on about that for weeks last time. Worse. It  was  a deer, but… it wasn't just lying there. There were foxes, like, a whole gang of them, just… at it. Circle of life and all that, I suppose, but it was a bit much for a post-Christmas dinner haze. Oh, that’s… grim. Foxes are getting bolder around here, too. I left the back door open for five minutes the other day while I was taking the bins out, and one just strolled in like he owned the place.

Right, Cambridge is looking… Cambridge-y. Still can't believe how flat it is around here. Birmingham’s got hills, you know? Proper hills. Makes a difference. You and your hills, Liam. You’d think you were scaling Everest the way you talk about the Five Ways. And honestly, this is flat for a  reason . Good for cycling. You’d be huffing and puffing on a bike uphill all the time. Speaking of huffing and puffing… this little car of yours is doing alright, Liam? Sounds a bit… strained going up even slight inclines. Nah, she’s fine, she's fine. Old Bessie’s got a bit of character. Just needs a bit of… encouragement. Plus, she's seen me through a lot. University, dodgy dates, even that time I tried to build a robot that would make me tea. Oh god, the tea-making robot. That was a disaster. Remember the short circuit and the smoke alarm? Your landlord was  not  impressed. Don’t remind me! Still, it was a learning experience. And Bessie didn’t even flinch. She’s a trooper. Although, I’m starting to think maybe I should’ve taken Ben’s offer of a lift in his… what is it, a hybrid Volvo thing? Ben and his eco-credentials. It's a perfectly good car, but it does feel a bit…clinical. Like everything’s been filtered. No soul. Bessie has  soul . Plus, I like the smell of… well, old car. It’s a comforting smell, strangely. You two are properly sentimental about vehicles, aren’t you? It's a bit weird. I just see them as means to an end. Get me from A to B, ideally with air conditioning. Speaking of which, Liam, are we stopping for coffee soon? My brain is starting to feel a bit fuzzy. Yeah, definitely. There's a decent little cafe I know just off Market Square. Good coffee, plus they do proper bacon butties. We can sort out the logistics for tomorrow too. Are we still aiming to leave by nine? Nine's good. I need to pack the last of my board game stuff, plus I haven’t even started thinking about what clothes to take. Sarah's parents’ place is… rustic. I suspect wellies might be a good shout. Wellies are  always  a good shout in the English countryside. You never know what you’re going to stumble into.

Honestly, I still can't believe Mr. Davies gave us homework  over  half term. A whole physics problem set? What is he even thinking? It's supposed to be a break! Tell me about it, man. I was planning on finally getting round to finishing that new album by Section 8, but now I'm stuck calculating…what was it? The trajectory of a projectile fired at an angle? Seriously? It's not like we're all gonna be artillery specialists. You two are moaning again? It's not  that  bad. It’s just applying some of the stuff we learned about vectors, yeah? I actually quite enjoyed that part of the lesson. Not the bit about air resistance though, that gets messy fast. Easy for you to say, Ash. You're basically a walking calculator. I swear you dream in equations. I'm more of a lyrical kinda guy, you know? Speaking of which, have you guys heard that new track from Nova Skies? "Static Bloom"? Nova Skies? Nah, not really my vibe. Too…atmospheric, innit? I need something with a bit more bass, something you can  feel . Section 8 are wicked, proper grimey. They sample a lot of old jungle stuff which is cool. It’s a bit underground, but it’s proper good. I think I've heard of Nova Skies, they did the soundtrack for that short film, "Echo Chamber," right? It was pretty decent, very layered sound. It did fit the film really well, all moody and dystopian. Yeah, that's them! "Static Bloom" is completely different though. It’s got that driving synth beat, and the lyrics are about…well, I think it's about feeling disconnected, you know? Like everyone’s glued to their phones. It’s a bit meta, actually. Disconnected? Mate, I  am  disconnected from my homework. That’s a feeling I understand perfectly. Seriously though, try Section 8. They got this one track, "Concrete Jungle", it's a banger. Proper London sound. Reminds me of walking through Shoreditch on a Saturday night. Full of energy. Shoreditch…that’s a bit far for me. Slough doesn't exactly have a thriving underground music scene. We're more of a Wetherspoons and indie covers band kind of town. Harsh, Ash. There must be something going on there. Not much. Last exciting thing that happened was old Mr. Henderson's cat got stuck in a tree.

…and honestly, the whole Balanceability thing has been brilliant for Leo. He was  so  wobbly on his bike before, practically horizontal! Now he’s zipping about with confidence, even attempting little ramps in the park. It was scary before. I used to run alongside him holding the seat. You did, sweetie. You were a star helper. And you, Archie? How was your session? It was good! I didn't fall over  once ! Mr. Harrison said I’m getting the hang of looking where I want to go, not at my feet. That’s fantastic, Archie! That's the key. It's like everything, isn’t it? Looking ahead. It's what I tell my Year 5s all the time, especially with their assessments coming up. They get so bogged down worrying about what they  might  get wrong that they forget to actually  do  the work. What are assessments? Are they like tests? They're a bit like tests, yes. But they're not always about getting everything right. They’re about showing what you've learned. Remember how proud you were when you finally managed to tie your shoelaces, even though it took loads of tries? That was showing me what you'd learned! I can tie mine now too! Without looking! See! That’s amazing! You just needed to keep practicing, that's all. It's the same with everything. Speaking of everything…Did I tell you Sarah’s finally started the renovations on her new house? Sarah? The one with the fluffy cat? The very same! She sent me pictures. They’re ripping the kitchen out. It’s going to be massive. And…get this…she's putting in a swimming pool! A swimming pool?! Will it be a big one? Can we go swimming there? Apparently it’s quite big, and she’s even planning a little manmade waterfall. Sounds rather fancy, doesn’t it? But she said she's being really careful about safety. Water is scary. You can’t breathe under the water. You're right, darling. Water  can  be scary. That's why we always have to be careful, especially around swimming pools. No diving in, ever, unless it is specifically designed for diving, okay? It's so dangerous. I had a conversation with some of the kids at school today about that actually. One of them told me his cousin jumped into a shallow lake and…well, it wasn’t a happy story.

…and honestly, I felt right daft, didn't I? Trying to follow that Zumba class online. It were all flashing lights and bouncy instructors and I just ended up looking like a confused octopus. Oh, Lucy! You and exercise, it's a long and storied battle, isn't it? I swear, you find new and inventive ways to avoid it. Aye, well, it’s not  avoiding  it. It's… strategically postponing it. There’s a difference. Plus, the gym’s closed for refurbishment, remember? And running in Cambridge is just… people. Everywhere. Dodging tourists and students is a workout in itself. Back home in Doncaster, you could run for miles without seeing a soul. Just sheep. True. Cambridge does have a density problem. Though, I actually quite like the Botanic Gardens for a walk. Less opportunity to be mown down by a rogue punt. Speaking of which, how  is  the Botanic Gardens going with the conference next month? Still on for the horticultural society? It is, thankfully. Bit of a nightmare coordinating plant deliveries and making sure there’s enough space for all their exhibits. Old Professor Armitage is a lovely fella, but he has  very  specific demands about the feng shui of the herbaceous border. Apparently, the lavender needs to be facing northeast for optimal floral energy. Floral energy? Right. Sounds… taxing. You’re a saint. Honestly, coordinating events is something I could never do. I need everything to be… predictable. Which is why I love production control. Boxes arrive, things get made, things get shipped. Simple. Simple for  you , maybe. I’d be lost in a factory. Too many moving parts. Anyhoo, enough about my work stress. How’s things with Ben? You were looking a bit… preoccupied last time we spoke. It’s… complicated. Which, let’s be honest, is usually the story with Ben. We had a bit of a row last weekend. Actually, a silly row. It was about whether pineapple belongs on pizza. Pineapple on pizza?! That’s what you’re arguing about? Seriously? I know! It sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud. But it escalated. He's so firm in his anti-pineapple stance. Said it was a culinary crime against humanity. I just think it adds a bit of sweetness. It's a texture thing! And then he went on a whole rant about the decline of Western civilisation. Oh, bless him.

Aye, that’s better than nowt, that is. Proper good pizza, this. Did yer mam get the pepperoni just how you like it, lad? Yeah, she did. Loads of it too. Best pizza in Newcastle, honest. Though, Mr. Henderson reckons Sal’s is better. Mr. Henderson would reckon black’s white if you told him it were! He's always gone on about Sal’s. Can’t taste the difference myself. Though, he  does  have a fancy palate, that one. Always going on about 'notes' and 'textures'. Aye, Henderson’s a bit of a food snob, isn’t he? Remember when he nearly had a fit when I put brown sauce on me chips at the pub? Said it “masked the subtle flavour of the potato.” Subtle flavour! They were chips! I heard! He told me all about it at school. Said you looked like you were committing a crime against gastronomy. Gastronomy! Honestly. It’s chips and sauce, not a Michelin star meal. Speaking of Henderson, did you hear about his new haircut? No! What's it like? Oh, it’s… something. He went for one of them really short ones, all shaved at the sides. He looks like a little… a little mushroom. A mushroom?! No! You’re pullin’ me leg! I am not! Honestly, he walked past me in town yesterday and I nearly choked on me tea. He was wearing one of them flat caps too, trying to hide it, but it didn't help. Looked even more daft. Maybe he's trying to look younger? Younger? He looks like he's tryin' to look like a soldier on parade! I had a trim meself last week, mind. Just a tidy up, needed gettin' rid of the bits round me ears. You always get a good cut, Arthur. You’ve been going to Mrs. Higgins for… how long now? Thirty years? She knows exactly what you like. Aye, since I were a lad, practically. She keeps me lookin’ respectable, y’know? Can’t be havin' a scruffy haulier drivin’ around the country. Speaking of drivin', did that log finally slide out of the fireplace, love? Been meaning to ask. It did, eventually. After I gave it a proper shove. Nearly took me with it! It was wedged in there proper tight. Thankfully, your nephew, bless him, was around to pull me back. It was nothing, Gran. You’d have been alright, you're tougher than you look.

Right, milk first for me, always. Though, honestly, I’m starting to think my entire life is just a series of strong opinions weakly held. Like,  milk first ? Why? It’s completely arbitrary. You’ve been reading too much philosophy for work, love. It’s seeping into the tea-making. Milk first is perfectly sensible. It protects the china. My nan swore by it. Protects the china? Since when have we cared about protecting the china? It’s all mismatched charity shop stuff anyway. Besides, you’re more of a builder than a protector of delicate things. Remember that 'DIY' shelving unit? That  was  ambitious. And okay, structurally unsound. But I learnt from it! Anyway, what sparked this existential tea crisis? Just thinking about pubs, actually. Back home. Old Man’s. You wouldn’t  believe  the clientele sometimes. All shouting about football or… root vegetables. Root vegetables? Honestly! Old Arthur, he’s convinced parsnips are the key to eternal life. He lectures anyone who’ll listen. It’s a whole thing. And you get Doreen, always going on about the price of Maris Pipers. They’re obsessed. It's a world away from these fancy Cambridge gastropubs. Gastropubs are overrated. It's all foams and micro-herbs and ten quid for a pint. Give me a proper, sticky-floored pub any day. Though, I’d probably avoid the parsnip debate. Exactly! It’s… a vibe. A very specific, slightly unsettling vibe. Though, thinking about it, I saw a picture of Gordon Ramsay in a pub in Sunderland last week. Apparently, he’s a secret fan of proper chips. Gordon Ramsay? In Sunderland? No way. That’s definitely a staged pap shot. He'd probably be horrified by the grease levels. He's all about precision and presentation now. Remember when he was just  shouting  at people? Good times. I do! That was peak TV. Though, he's mellowed slightly. He's got all those kids now, hasn't he? Still looks terrifying, though. Like someone could offer him a badly cooked scallop and he’d launch into a full-scale tirade. Probably. Speaking of things that need precision... I’m attempting a butternut squash risotto tonight. It’s for Professor Davies - he's doing a tasting panel for my research, trying to convince him my work is actually worth funding. Oh, right, the all-important funding meeting. Butternut squash risotto? Ambitious.

Right, okay, I officially concede this round. "Synonym for ecstatic"... honestly, Rhys? You’re a menace. It was  delighted , wasn’t it? Not “over the moon and back and doing a jig!”      Well, if I’m going to be penalised for enthusiasm, I’d rather be penalised for enthusiasm! You’ve got to paint a picture, Sarah. It’s  Articulate , not…  Precise Definitions .      He’s got a point, you know. You were taking far too long. The timer’s there for a reason. You were waffling about happy feelings for a good forty seconds.      Waffling? I was building suspense! And you, Dafydd, were barely looking at the card! You were too busy observing  my  waffling!      Now, now. Let’s not get competitive. It’s just a bit of fun. Though, I will say, Rhys’s descriptions are… expansive. Remember last time, with ‘ambulance’? It was a twenty-minute saga about the sound of the siren and the urgency of a life saved.      It  was  a compelling narrative! Besides, it got everyone guessing. That’s the point!      It’s lovely to see you all getting so into it. It's been ages since we’ve all been together like this, just relaxing. Even if it is filled with vocal gymnastics from some of us.      Relaxing? I’m simultaneously stressed, amused, and slightly offended by my inability to convey simple synonyms! Okay, new game. New card for me, and Rhys, zip it. Let’s see… ‘Obsolete’. Easy.      Oh, go on, give it a go. I’ll be a supportive audience. Mostly.      Right. Okay… something that doesn't exist anymore… gone… finished… antique! No, that's not it... vintage? Hmm… archaic… dusty… out of fashion!      You’re getting warmer. You’re circling it. Think older. Much older.      Like something from a museum?      Yes! Museum piece! Antiquated! Oh! Oh, I’ve got it! “Typewriter!” Yes! Typewriter!      You got it. Fair play. But you nearly lost it with ‘dusty’. That could have been anything.      A typewriter! My grandmother had a beautiful old one. She used to make all her letters on it. The sound of the keys was so satisfying.      They were incredible machines, weren’t they? So tactile. It's funny, I used one once for an art project, years ago. Found one in a junk shop in Cardiff.      Cardiff? You were in Cardiff? When was that?      Oh, ages ago. Before I moved back to England properly.

Honestly, Rhys, you’re ruthless! Another point to the Welsh contingent. It’s becoming a massacre. Just employing a little strategic thinking, Sarah. You South Africans are too busy relying on… flair. It’s charming, but not particularly effective in a game of Rummy. He’s got a point, Sarah. You play like you’re conducting an orchestra. All flourish, no actual sequence. Oh, very funny, you two. Ganging up on the exile, are we? Just because I grew up under Table Mountain doesn’t mean I don’t know how to play a simple card game. And for the record, I  do  have a sequence! It’s just… a very subtle one. Subtle is not a word I’d associate with you, love. Remember that lime green dress you wore to Uncle Bryn’s funeral?  That  was subtle. Oh, Mum, please. That was fifteen years ago! And it was a vibrant celebration of his life! He loved colour. He also said it looked like a highlighter pen had exploded. But he said it with affection. Speaking of affection, Dai, you're awfully quiet. Still stewing about losing at Monopoly last night? Monopoly’s just… unfair. It’s all luck of the dice and then the rich get richer. This is at least  slightly  skill-based. Though Rhys is rather bending the rules of fair play, wouldn’t you say? He’s definitely a card shark. I swear he’s counting them. I resent that! I am a master strategist, honed by years of competitive… well, competitive Rummy with my mother. It’s a tough training ground. He learned from the best, you know. I’ve been playing Rummy since before he was born. It's how I survived those long winters in Cardiff. A good card game and a strong cuppa. Essential. It’s nice to get away though, isn’t it? Hereford is lovely. Such a change from London. Though I do miss a decent flat white. The coffee here is… hearty. Hearty is a polite way of putting it. It tastes like someone brewed it with gravel. I thought you enjoyed it, Dai? You had three cups this morning. I was being polite! My upbringing dictates I must always be polite to anyone offering me sustenance. Especially when it’s brewed by your mother, who will relentlessly guilt trip me if I refuse. Nonsense, darling. I just want you to be comfortable.

Honestly, this uni application process is  stressful . I’ve spent the last three hours staring at my personal statement, and it still reads like a robot wrote it. "Passionate about the intricacies of cellular biology…blah, blah, blah." It doesn’t sound like  me  at all! You’re telling me! I remember that feeling. It’s awful trying to condense your entire being into 47 lines. Did you get any feedback from your teachers yet? Mine were… helpful, in a very ‘you need to rewrite the whole thing’ sort of way. Oh, the classic teacher feedback. “Show, don’t tell!” They love that one. I'm trying to steer clear of all the science stuff, to be honest. Accounting just feels… safer. Less existential dread about, you know,  the future . Safer? You think spreadsheets are safer than understanding how life works? You'll be wishing you’d paid more attention in biology when you’re auditing a pharmaceutical company! Emily: Okay, Mr. Navy Seal. It’s a career choice, not a personality test. Besides, I’m pretty good with numbers. It’s just… less pressure than, say, discovering a cure for cancer. Speaking of pressure, my nan is already asking about Christmas presents. And the dreaded "What are your plans?" question. I swear, she thinks I’ve got a five-year plan mapped out already. I’m still deciding what I want for tea tonight! Chloe: Tell me about it. My mum’s been dropping hints about needing help with decorating. Like I don’t have enough on my plate! Though, I did manage to convince her I absolutely  need  a new graphics tablet for my art A-Level. Fingers crossed. Sarah: You’ve got to be firm. I've been working at the care home since I finished sixth form, and frankly, it's exhausting. It’s rewarding, definitely, but the hours are long and it’s emotionally draining. Nana keeps suggesting I do a nursing degree, but I just... can’t face more studying right now. Liam: It’s good you’re doing something you find fulfilling, though. Even if it is tiring. My training was brutal, don't get me wrong, but it’s given me such a sense of purpose. Plus, the pay isn't bad. Emily: Is it really as intense as they show on TV? All the running and shouting and…looking very serious? Liam: It has its moments.

Oh, honestly, this is lovely, love. You really do make a good shepherd’s pie, don’t you, dear? Though, I still reckon my mum’s was the best. She used a secret ingredient… a tiny bit of Worcestershire sauce. Changed everything. Thanks, Gran! I’m glad you’re enjoying it. Worcestershire sauce, huh? I’ll have to try that next time. It’s a bit of a family heirloom recipe now, isn’t it? Mum always said the same about  her  mum. Did you see that cheetah go for the gazelle? Brilliant! Absolutely brilliant. Faster than a cyclist going downhill, I reckon. Oh, leave the poor animals alone, Arthur. Honestly, you and your animal programmes. Always getting excitable. Though, a cyclist going downhill…that  is  something. Makes me nervous just thinking about it. Especially those young lads whizzing around Cambridge. No respect for pedestrians, I tell you! It's not  all  cyclists, Gran. Some are really careful. I cycle to work most days, remember? And Cambridge is pretty good for cycle lanes, generally. Though I do agree, some of them do take risks. Well,  you  may be careful, love. You’ve always been a sensible girl. But I saw one nearly knock Old Man Hemmings into the canal just last week! Said he didn't hear the bell. Honestly! He’s nearly deaf, the poor thing. I told him he shouldn't be walking so close to Mill Road, it's just too dangerous. Mill Road’s always been a nightmare, hasn’t it? Used to cycle down there myself, years ago when I still bothered with a bike. More trouble than it's worth, I always thought. Give me four wheels any day. You can just…  go . Now  there's  a sensible man. Though, driving in Cambridge is a nightmare these days too. All those one-way systems and bus lanes…you need a degree just to understand it! And the parking! Don’t even get me started on the parking. It's a bit better if you know where to look. There’s that park and ride, which is really good, and I’ve found a couple of side streets, but yeah, it can be stressful. I'm thinking of getting an electric scooter actually, for shorter trips. Less hassle than the bike, especially in the rain. An electric scooter? Goodness me. Sounds a bit precarious. Aren’t they a bit… fast?

…and honestly, the sherry trifle they had at the reception was  remarkably  good. Though, perhaps I was just pleased to be out of the office for a bit. It's been a proper slog coordinating all the language data for the new dialect project.      Oh, tell me about it! I've been buried under logistics for Alumni Day. Just getting everyone’s dietary requirements sorted felt like a research project in itself. Sherry trifle though… that  does  sound good. I missed that bit, I was stuck troubleshooting the AV for Professor Davies’ talk.      Davies and his technology, eh? Always a gamble. Good man, though. Knows his Roman Law. You two are… relatively new faces, aren’t you? I’m Arthur Penhaligon, lectured here for… well, far too long to admit.      I’m Eloise, Eloise Harding. I’m the Language Research Coordinator. And this is Clara.      Hi, Arthur. Clara Bennett. I'm the Research Administrator. It’s lovely to meet you. This building is absolutely stunning, though. I haven’t been back since I graduated.      Stunning, yes. And full of ghosts, if you believe in such things. Mostly the ghosts of students lamenting missed deadlines, I suspect. So, language research, Eloise? What sort of linguistic mysteries are you unraveling these days?      Mostly regional dialect variation, actually. We're building a large corpus of spoken data. I’ve got a team working on everything from subtle vowel shifts in Norfolk to… well, trying to decipher what some people are saying in parts of Cornwall is a project in itself! It's fascinating, though. I was actually in Spain last year, doing some preliminary work on Basque.      Oh, Basque! That’s amazing. It's such a linguistic isolate, isn’t it? I tried to learn a bit of Spanish when I was travelling, but it felt like I was barely scratching the surface.      It  is  incredible. The origins are still debated, but it’s unlike anything else in Europe. The people were lovely, though. Very proud of their culture. I was in San Sebastián – have you been?      San Sebastián? Beautiful city. Spent a week there once, many years ago. Trying to convince myself I was a Hemingway character. Didn’t quite pull it off, I’m afraid. Too fond of a comfortable hotel. But the pintxos… remarkable. Tell me, Eloise, you mentioned regional variation. Does that extend to dialectal differences within Spain? I recall a student once doing a rather spirited report on variations in Andalusian Spanish.

…Honestly, it feels so weird being back here. It hasn’t changed a bit, has it? Still smells faintly of Mum’s potpourri and…polished wood? Oh, God, you’re right about the potpourri. It's a constant. She thinks it disguises the smell of…well, everything. And don’t pretend you don’t secretly like it. It  is  Mum. It's comforting, isn’t it? Like stepping back in time. Two years is far too long. It felt like forever since I last saw you both. How’s the teaching going, Liam? Still trying to instil proper grammar into the masses? It's…a battle. A constant, uphill battle. You wouldn't believe the things students think are acceptable now. Like, using "literally" to mean figuratively. Drives me absolutely mad. Though, I did have a student last term who was convinced Shakespeare was just a really good rapper. Oh, bless him. Sounds about right for this generation. You know, I was just thinking about all the ridiculous things  we  got up to at school. Remember that time David Higgins tried to sell glow-in-the-dark worms in the playground? Oh my  God , yes! And Mrs. Peterson confiscated them and made him write lines! “I will not attempt to profit from invertebrate bioluminescence.” It was legendary. That's a good one. It’s amazing the things you forget. Speaking of forgetting things, Mum was going on about Aunt Carol the other day. Apparently she’s started filling out forms for everything, just to “keep her brain active.” Oh, Carol. That’s…Carol. Probably filling out forms for a discount on prune juice as we speak. She's always been a bit of a worrier. She always said she wanted a big family, didn't she? Remember how she and Uncle Peter talked about adoption for years? They did. They were really good about it, too. Open and honest. It was always a case of 'if it's meant to be'. It's a shame it didn't work out for them, but they had such a full life otherwise. It is. It makes you think, y’know? About… well, about everything. I was scrolling through Facebook the other day - don't judge - and saw Sarah Thompson just announced she's expecting again. Third one. It’s… a lot. Sarah always wanted a big family. She always said she wanted a football team. It must be exhausting.

Honestly, this coffee machine is the bane of my life. It makes a noise like a strangled badger every time it brews, and half the time it just spits out lukewarm water. You’d think for the money your brother spent on it… Dad really did go overboard, didn’t he? He always has to have the ‘best’ of everything. It’s probably one of those ‘smart’ machines that needs an engineering degree to operate. Overboard is an understatement. He could have bought a perfectly good kettle and a French press for a tenth of the price. And achieved a superior cup of coffee, I might add. Speaking of spending money… have we actually gotten quotes for the storage unit yet, Helen? For all the stuff we’re… re-homing from the house? I started looking, Michael. It's… depressing. The prices are ridiculous. And the further you get from here, the cheaper it gets, naturally. But then you're looking at endless drives. I found one in Penrith, reasonable monthly rate, but they charge extra for insurance and… access at different times. It's a minefield. Penrith’s not  that  bad. Still, if you’re talking about long-term storage, the cost mounts up. Maybe we should be ruthless. Really, really ruthless. Do we  need  all those boxes of Christmas decorations? And are we seriously keeping Uncle Patrick’s collection of porcelain thimbles? Your father insisted the thimbles were ‘family heirlooms’. He’s rather sentimental about things. And those Christmas decorations contain memories, darling. They remind me of… well, of when things were simpler. Sentiment is a luxury we can no longer afford, Helen. We’ve got to be pragmatic. The house is sold, we’ve a new, smaller place to furnish, and frankly, we're not rolling in it. Speaking of things changing… did you see what Keir Starmer said about reversing the tax cuts? Oh, here we go. Politics at breakfast. Honestly, Dad, can't we just enjoy a peaceful cuppa? Peaceful? When the country is being run into the ground? It’s a civic duty to be informed, you know. This whole thing with Starmer… it's interesting. He's trying to position himself as the sensible alternative, but it feels… lacking. Where's the vision? Where's the fire? Vision and fire? From a Labour leader? You’re asking a lot, Michael. It’s been decades since we’ve had a Labour leader with any real… bite.

…and honestly, Mum, the Christmas market was  packed . Like sardines. You could barely move for people clutching mulled wine and questionable knitted reindeer. I did manage to get some lovely beeswax candles though, for the living room. Oh, dear. Sounds a bit much, doesn’t it? They really do start earlier and earlier every year, don't they? It used to be Advent, a quiet build-up. Now it’s practically November First and everyone’s got a tree up. I’m still hoping we can have a proper, calm Christmas at yours this year. Absolutely. That’s the plan. Though calm with Uncle Barry around… is a big ask. He already asked me,  last week , if I'd started practicing my carol singing. Honestly, the man lives for Christmas. He does, doesn't he? Bless him. He just wants everyone to be happy. Did you ask him about his hip replacement consultation? He was a bit cagey when I spoke to him. I did, briefly. He said it’s all booked for January. He’s trying to power through Christmas first, apparently. Thinks it’ll be his last truly 'mobile' Christmas before he gets it done. Dramatic, as always. Oh, that's good, good he's finally going for it. He's been putting it off for ages, that man. Stubborn as a mule. Speaking of stubborn, how’s Liam taking all the Christmas planning? Last year he seemed… less than enthused. It’s a work in progress. He’s good at the practical stuff, you know, putting up the lights, wrestling with the tree. But the  feeling  of it all… he doesn’t really get it. He says it’s all consumerism, and stresses about the cost. Which is fair, I suppose, things are…tight. They are for everyone, love. But Christmas isn't  just  about the presents, is it? It’s about being together. And I think Liam’s just a bit… stressed with work. How's the teaching going, by the way? Still enjoying it? It’s… okay. It pays the bills. Though I'm seriously starting to think about doing that online TEFL course I saw advertised. The one that qualifies you to teach business English. Actually, I was looking at it last night. It’s quite expensive, but the potential earning is so much better. Oh, that sounds sensible. You've always been a good teacher, you have a knack for explaining things.

…and honestly, I’m convinced Dave’s started snoring  louder . It’s like a foghorn, I swear. Last night, I actually nudged him and he didn’t even stir. Just… continued on, full pelt. Aye, he's always been a snorer, hasn’t he? Remember that camping trip to the Lake District? Old Man Hemmings threatened to report us to the park rangers. Said it sounded like a wounded bear. Oh, God, I’d forgotten about that! Hemmings was a grumpy sod anyway. Probably just looking for an excuse. But Dave  does  have a particularly impressive snore. It’s a talent, really. A terrible, sleep-disrupting talent. My flatmate, Chloe, snores, but it’s this…weird, high-pitched whistle. It's less 'bear' and more 'tea kettle about to explode’. It's unsettling. I've had to start wearing earplugs. Earplugs are a lifesaver. Though, I just end up twisting them around all night and waking myself up anyway. Still better than the alternative, I suppose. Speaking of waking up…did anyone manage to get those bloomers from Waterfields yesterday? They had that special offer on, didn’t they? Ooh, good shout! I completely forgot! No, I didn’t. I was running late for that meeting with Mr. Harrison. He's obsessed with spreadsheets. Honestly, it’s like he’s in his element when he’s just staring at numbers all day. Did you, Liam? Nah, I was stuck finishing off my application for that…well, it doesn’t matter. Didn’t get ‘em. I was hoping to snag a couple of those Eccles cakes too, they always sell out fast. Ruth mentioned she went early doors and got the last pack. Ruth is always strategic with her Waterfields visits. She knows the prime time to go. I went in for a loaf of their bloomer last week, and they’d already sold out of Richmond sausages! Richmond! Can you believe it? It's a travesty. Richmond sausages  are  a staple, aren’t they? A proper weekend breakfast isn’t a weekend breakfast without them. They’re miles better than anything else you can get. Agreed. My nan used to always have them cooking when we went round. Good times. Although, she always insisted on serving them with a tiny, embroidered handkerchief under each plate, just in case of drips. Oh, your nan and her handkerchiefs! She carried one everywhere, didn't she?

…and honestly, the whole thing was just  chaos . Like, beautiful chaos, but chaos nonetheless. Old Man Hemmings decided mid-bake-off that his Victoria sponge needed lavender. Lavender! It tasted like soap. Lavender, you say? Sounds like Hemmings, alright. Always one for a… unique flourish. Did young Emily win with her lemon drizzle again? She’s a proper baker, that girl. No! Surprisingly, it was Mrs. Patel. Her chocolate Guinness cake. Apparently, she’s been perfecting it for years. It was… intense. Rich. I only managed half a slice. Though, I did have seconds of Emily’s, just to balance things out, you know? Guinness in a cake, eh? Never would’ve thought. Still, good on Mrs. Patel. She deserves it, always a lovely woman. So, the village fete was a success then, despite Hemmings’ floral ambitions? Oh, absolutely. Loads of people turned out. It was baking, face painting, a ridiculously competitive tug-of-war… the usual. It was just nice to be  outside  for a change. This past week at work has been… draining. Tell me about it. Seems everyone wants everything yesterday these days. How's the Miller project coming along? Still chasing your tail? You have no idea. They decided,  last Friday , that they needed a complete overhaul of the data analysis section. A complete overhaul! After I’d already finished the initial report. So, I spent all weekend wrestling with spreadsheets and pivot tables. I swear, I dreamt in Excel. Sounds like Sarah is asking a lot of you, doesn’t she? She’s a bright spark, that one, but she does push people. You’re too good at saying ‘yes,’ you know that? I know, I know. I just… I want to prove myself. It's a good project, genuinely. And I do like the team, mostly. But I'm starting to wonder if “Project Co-ordinator” is just a fancy term for “professional fire-fighter.” You’ll get there, love. It takes time to find your feet. Remember when I started out with the farm? Thought I knew everything. Old Man Abernathy quickly put a stop to  that  notion. He had me mucking out stalls for a month before he even let me near the accounts. Oh, stop it. That sounds… character building. Though, I think I’d rather stick to spreadsheets than stalls, thank you very much. It’s all honest work. Speaking of work, I had a right palaver with young Thomas today.

…and honestly, the kids were  brilliant  that lesson. Absolutely brilliant. They were attempting to describe their weekend using only past continuous. Chaos, naturally, but glorious chaos. It's just… the marking is relentless. Honestly, I spend more time marking than actually  teaching  sometimes. Tell me about it! My Year 5s did descriptions of imaginary creatures yesterday. Twenty-five glitter-covered, vaguely dinosaur-shaped monstrosities, and twenty-five accompanying essays full of adjectives I didn’t know existed. My eyes are still recovering. How’s the French going, though? Still enjoying it? It is, actually. It's the escape, isn’t it? From the past continuous and the glitter. I'm doing the DELF B2 prep course online, which is…challenging. The listening comprehension is the killer. They speak so fast! And with so many idioms. It’s completely different from the textbook French. Oh, I remember grappling with that. I tried to pick up Spanish a few years back, proper conversational stuff, thinking ‘oh, I’ll be able to finally understand my mother-in-law’s family!’ Utter disaster. So many regional variations, and they just spoke too quickly for my brain to process. I got to the point where I could order a beer and ask where the toilet was, and then gave up. That’s a good baseline, though, isn't it? Practical skills. No point learning to discuss existentialism if you can’t locate the loo. It’s amazing how much confidence it gives you, even knowing just a little bit of a language. Makes you feel… less insular, I suppose. Definitely. And it forces you to  listen  properly. Something we don’t do enough of, I think, even in our own language. Speaking of things that force you to listen… how’s everything going with you and Mark? Any news on the baby front? It’s… slow. We went for another appointment last week. Everything’s ‘normal,’ apparently. Which is good, but also means no closer to a little one running around. Mark's starting to get… anxious. He's always wanted a big family. I’m trying to be realistic, you know? We've been trying for over a year now. Oh, honey, I’m so sorry. That must be really tough. Don’t feel like you need to put on a brave face with me. It's completely understandable that you're both feeling it.

Now that’s a right proper nest, innit? Massive thing. Bet there’s a whole family o’ blue tits in there. Though, I saw a great spotted woodpecker ‘avin’ a go at it yesterday. Proper territorial dispute, it were. Woodpeckers are cheeky beggars, they are. No respect for established homes. Remember Old Man Hemmings’ shed? Pecked holes right through it, he said. Drove him mad. Oh, don't remind me of Hemmings. Always complaining. Though, the woodpecker  was  a bit of a nuisance. Speaking of nuisances, have you two tried the cake? I made it this morning. Bit of raspberry jam in the middle, just how Arthur likes it. Gawd, that’s good, Doreen. Properly good. You’ve outdone yourself. Much better than that shop-bought stuff Elsie brought round last week. Tasted like cardboard, it did. Lovely. Truly lovely. Though, I shouldn’t, should I? With… you know. Don't you worry your head about that, Reg. A little bit of cake won't hurt. Doctor said moderation, not elimination. Besides, it's good for the soul! Exactly. It's a bit of joy, isn't it? Though, I did use a little less sugar than usual, Reg. Just in case. I was reading something about diabetes and how important it is to watch the refined sugar. It’s frightening, really, how many people are getting it these days. Everyone's getting something these days, Doreen. It’s this modern life, I tell you. Too much stress, too much processed food. When  we  were lads, we ate what we grew, ran about all day… Didn’t have time to get sick! Ran about? You were always more interested in building things with your Meccano, Arthur. And getting covered in grease. Well, someone had to be the engineer of the operation! Speaking of building, you remember young Timmy, Doreen? From next door? He used to love watching me fix things in the garden. Asked me if I could build him a puppet theatre. Oh, yes! A lovely boy. He had such an imagination. And he was fascinated by your tools. I  still  have some of those old puppets he made. The ones with the button eyes. They’re in the attic, somewhere. Puppets? Goodness me. That takes me back. My sister used to have a Punch and Judy set. Scared the life out of me, it did. Look at ‘em go!

Oh, this looks lovely. Everything smells of lemon and garlic. I think I’ll have the  sheftali  – those little grilled meatballs. Have you decided, Arthur? Honestly, I’m a bit overwhelmed. So much choice! I might just go for the mixed grill. Can’t go wrong with that, can you? Though I do wish they’d list the ingredients a bit clearer. My stomach isn't what it used to be, you know. You and me both! It’s funny, isn’t it? When you get to our age, eating becomes… a more considered activity. Not just fuel, but a potential minefield! Reminds me of Auntie Mabel, always fretting about gluten before anyone even  knew  what gluten was. Mabel was a character. Always convinced she was allergic to something new. Though, thinking about allergies, young Timmy back home – my granddaughter’s friend – developed a terrible reaction to peanuts. Scared the life out of everyone. Little mite swelled up like a balloon. Oh dear. Poor thing. It’s frightening how common those things are becoming. Makes you wonder what we’re all breathing in these days. Speaking of things back home… how’s Maggie doing? Still battling with… well, you know. It’s… difficult. The treatment is taking its toll. She’s trying to be brave, she really is. But the fatigue is awful. She used to be so vibrant, always gardening, always on the go. Now she spends most of the day in bed. I’ve had to get one of those amplified phones for her, you know. She said she couldn’t hear a thing I was saying sometimes, even with me shouting! Oh, Arthur, I’m so sorry to hear that. She’s a wonderful woman. It's hard watching someone you love…fade. Have you…have you considered talking to her about… well, about making arrangements? I know it's a dreadful thing to suggest. We’ve had a little chat. Nothing concrete. She’s adamant she’s going to beat this. And I want to support that, of course I do. But being practical… it’s important, isn't it? Losing Mum was… well, it was a shock, even though she'd been unwell for a while. Didn't prepare us at all. It rarely does, does it? My father… it was so sudden. Heart attack. One minute he was pruning the roses, the next… gone. It leaves a hole, doesn’t it?

Honestly, Mum, this is exactly what I needed. Escaping London for a weekend, even if it  is  back to the parental unit, is a lifesaver. Work’s been… intense. Intense how, love? Still all those spreadsheets and chasing people for updates? You always were a meticulous one, just like your father. Meticulous is a polite way of saying I'm the only one who cares if things are actually  on time . It’s a new project, launching a new marketing campaign for that sustainable clothing company. It  should  be exciting, it’s a great cause, but the client keeps changing their mind. It's like herding cats, honestly. Sounds about right. Clients. Always wanting the moon on a stick and expecting it yesterday. Reminds me of old man Hemmings, used to want me to deliver potatoes to his doorstep at six in the morning, rain or shine. Sounds delightful. Not quite the high-powered world of ethical fashion, though. But seriously, this project is draining. I think I’m starting to dream in Gantt charts. Well, you need to take some time for yourself. Are you still going to that pottery class? That seemed to relax you. I was! But I had to drop it. No time. It’s a casualty of the ‘urgent’ everything at work. I might try and find something else later in the year. Though honestly, I’m tempted to just spend all my free time eating biscuits. Now  that’s  a plan I can get behind. Your mother makes a cracking biscuit, you know. Though, she insists on putting too much cinnamon in them. Don’t you start, Arthur. They are perfectly spiced. And speaking of spiced… did you remember to book a table at The King’s Head for Saturday? I know you wanted to watch the rugby with Derek. Ah, yes, the rugby. Completely slipped my mind! Blasted memory. I'll do it right now. England’s got a chance this year, I reckon. Though, honestly, the scrum-halves aren't what they used to be. Honestly, rugby just looks like a mass of bodies tackling each other to me. No offence. No offence taken. It's a strategy, a beautiful, brutal strategy. You wouldn't understand. It's a man's game, mostly. Oh, Arthur. Don’t be so old-fashioned. Anyway, have you thought any more about Grandma’s birthday next month?

…and honestly, I still can’t believe she fell for it. Like,  completely  fell for it. A bloke pretending to be a professional rugby player with a yacht? Honestly, love, you’d think people’d have a bit more sense. Ay, but it’s easy to get caught up, innit? When someone’s layin’ it on thick, tellin’ ye what ye wanna hear. Especially online. It’s all curated, isn't it? Not like meeting someone down the pub where you can actually  see  if they’re a knobhead. I think it's the loneliness, though, isn’t it? Like, people are desperate for connection, especially if they’re a bit… vulnerable. Makes ‘em easier to manipulate. I read an article about it – proper sad cases. They lose everything. Aye, sad it is. This lass, Sarah, she sent him… well, I won't say how much, but it was enough to pay a deposit on a little house, apparently. Her mum’s absolutely fuming. She’s always said she’s too trusting. A deposit?! Blimey. Proper taken for a ride, she has. Did she at least do a reverse image search and that? Come on, it’s 2024! You gotta check that sort of thing. It takes two minutes. She did, eventually. After months of chatting, apparently. He sent her a picture of himself “on tour” with the team, and that’s when her friend was like, “Hold on a minute, that’s a stock photo of some fella from America!” Oh, that’s awful. It’s like watching a train wreck in slow motion, y’know? You just want to shout at the telly, “Don’t do it! He’s clearly a liar!” It's like a real-life episode of… well, you know. Don’t even  say  it. Jeremy Kyle? Ugh. Don't remind me. My Nan was  obsessed  with Jeremy Kyle. Wouldn't miss it for the world. It was awful. All that shouting and confrontation, and the lie detector… horrific. Nan's are weird, alright? Mine loved bingo and Coronation Street. Proper stereotype, she was. But Jeremy Kyle  was  compelling, though, wasn’t it? In a really messed-up way. Compelling in the same way car crashes are compelling. You don’t want to look, but you can’t help yourself. And it felt so… exploitative. It definitely was. And now they’ve taken it off air, it’s just… migrated to TikTok, hasn't it?

…Honestly, Nan, this is brilliant. Proper cheese and pickle. You always make the best. Reminds me of being a kid, honestly. Oh, hush you. It's just a bit of bread and cheese. Though, you  were  a fussy eater. Remember all the battles over vegetables? You’d only eat green beans, and even then, only if they were perfectly straight. Don’t remind me! Mum never let me forget that. Though, I think I've broadened my horizons since then. Speaking of horizons… Paris is looking  very  tempting. I'm thinking of trying to get a placement over there for next year. Paris! Oh, darling, that’s lovely. You’d adore it. It's so different to London, you know? More…considered, perhaps. Though the traffic is just as dreadful. Have you been before? Nah, never. Always wanted to though. Part of the reason I started taking French again, actually. Still rusty as anything, mind. My German's better, weirdly. Oh, your German  is  good. You picked that up so quickly, didn’t you? Always surprising me, rattling off phrases. It’s funny, isn’t it? How languages stick. I practically  lived  in German for years, growing up. My mother insisted, even though we were in Italy. She said it was vital. A proper education. Italy, though! That’s gotta be amazing. You were born in Vienna, right? Then moved to Italy? Sounds…complicated. Complicated is rather an understatement. My father was a musician, a violinist, and Vienna was a hub, you see. Wonderful city, though I mostly remember the cold. After the war… well, Italy offered a new start. A bit more sunshine, thankfully. We moved to Florence. My childhood was a blur of art and opera and trying to understand why my mother was always correcting my Italian pronunciation. That  does  sound amazing. I’m stuck here, grinding through Classics essays. It's…interesting. But sometimes I feel like I’m reading about dust and ruins when I should be, you know,  doing  things. Classics are important, darling. They teach you how to think. Though I can understand the need to experience things, too. That's why I always travelled. Even when money was tight. Actually, talking of things… have you managed to fix that ridiculous computer yet? You were wrestling with it all morning. Don't even  mention  it. It’s possessed, I swear. I tried reinstalling the graphics drivers, and now it just keeps freezing.

Honestly, Dad, you were  flying  back there. I thought we were going to end up in a ditch somewhere near… well, I don’t even know where we were! Somewhere beige. Beige is a perfectly good colour, darling. And I wasn’t flying, I was making good time. Holiday traffic, you know. Gotta be assertive. Though, admittedly, that van driver did look a bit startled. Assertive is one word for it, George. Terrifying is another. Honestly, I nearly swallowed my tongue. You’ve still got that lead foot, haven’t you? It’s a perfectly functioning foot! And besides, I used to drive for a living, remember? Though admittedly, that was before all these roundabouts… they’re the devil’s work, those. It’s just… I’m trying to revise in the back, you know, for my dissertation? And being thrown around like a rag doll isn’t exactly conducive to critical analysis of post-structuralist feminism. Oh, don't start on that again, love. Sounds exhausting just  listening  to you talk about it. What  is  it even about? It's... complicated. Basically, how language constructs gender. It's fascinating, actually, when you get into it. Although, trying to explain it to anyone who hasn’t spent the last three years immersed in Michel Foucault is… challenging. Michel who-now? Sounds like a French pastry chef. See, this is why I stuck to building. Bricks and mortar, that's understandable. Speaking of which, I keep meaning to ask, have you sorted that damp patch in the downstairs loo, Carol? Not yet, George. I’ve had two days off this week with a migraine, so everything’s backed up. Mrs. Peterson needed her medication, then old Mr. Davies decided he needed a full bed change at 7am… It’s relentless. Oh, Mum, that sounds awful. You work so hard. It’s alright, dear. Keeps me busy. Though honestly, some of the families… it’s heartbreaking. And the paperwork! I swear, I spend half my shift filling out forms. Paperwork. Don't get me started. I had to pay the solicitor again this week. Another hundred quid gone, just for him to send a letter saying he was still waiting on information. Criminal, I tell you. Absolutely criminal. Still with that probate stuff then? Isn't it dragging on? Dragging? It’s trying to grow roots! Apparently, Cousin Mildred’s second husband’s illegitimate daughter has a claim.

Lovely cuppa, eh, Margaret? Just what a body needs on a day like this. Feels right chilly, even with the fire on. It is nice, Arthur. Though I think you put a bit too much milk in again. It's practically beige. Beige is a perfectly respectable colour! And I like a creamy tea. Reminds me of me nan, she used to make it just the same. Thick enough to stand a spoon up in, she did. Your nan could get away with murder. She had that way about her. Remember when she convinced the butcher to give us extra sausages 'cause it was young Timmy's birthday? Even though it wasn’t? Oh, I do! Old Mr. Henderson, bless his soul, didn’t stand a chance. She had a gift, that woman. A real gift for getting what she wanted. Though, I reckon I get me charm from her side o’ the family. Charm? Arthur, you haven’t charmed a soul in years. Unless you count the postman, and that was just because you offered him a biscuit. He  looked  like he appreciated a biscuit, didn't he? A hard life, delivering letters in all weathers. Still, talking of Timmy… how’s he getting on with that new job? Last I heard, he was training to be… what was it? Some sort of computer man? A software developer, dear. And he’s doing brilliantly, apparently. He called last week, all excited about a project he’s working on. Something to do with… well, honestly, it went right over my head. Something about algorithms and cloud storage. Algorithms and cloud storage… sounds like something from a science fiction film. Fancy that. All them fancy things now. When I left school, the height of technology was a Bakelite telephone. And you were perfectly happy with it! You never were one for embracing the new. Remember when I tried to get you to use a microwave? You swore it would ruin the flavour of everything. It  does  ruin the flavour! Everything tastes… sterile, somehow. Give me a proper oven any day. A good roast, cooked slowly. That’s the ticket. Speaking of which, are we having lamb on Sunday? I was thinking chicken. Easier on the pocket, and the butcher had a lovely selection. Plus, I found that new recipe with the lemon and rosemary… Chicken’s alright, I suppose. Though lamb has more… substance.

Mmm, this is lovely, this is proper nice, actually. You’ve outdone yourself with the dauphinoise, love. Cheers, pet. Just a Jamie Oliver recipe, to be fair. Nothing too taxing. Glad you like it. Been a long day wrestling with data, needed a bit of comfort cooking. How was your day? Still battling with the ethics committee? Oh, don't even  start  me. Honestly, they want me to rewrite half the participant information sheet. Apparently, the wording around potential psychological distress is “not sufficiently sensitive.” Like, I’m not  trying  to cause distress, am I? It's a study about attitudes to public transport, not a horror film! Bureaucracy, eh? The bane of every researcher’s existence. They mean well, I suppose. Just covering themselves. Though I did have Professor Davies corner me today asking about my methodology, and honestly, I felt like a right idiot. Like he was just waiting for me to trip up. Oh, Davies? He's a nightmare. Always has been. Remember when he tried to tell Ben off for having a Metallica poster in his office during undergrad? Said it wasn’t “intellectually stimulating decor.” Oh god, yes! Ben was fuming! He nearly challenged him to a guitar duel. Honestly, the man… Anyway, speaking of Ben, have you heard from him lately? It feels like ages. Not properly, no. Just a quick message on Facebook last week. He's busy gigging, apparently. He sent a link to a video of them playing in Leeds. Sounded good, though it’s not really my thing, is it? Too much… thrashing about. To be fair, his band  is  a bit intense. But he's good. Really good. He always had that energy, y’know? Remember when he tried to learn the bagpipes? That was a short-lived experiment. Short-lived is an understatement! The neighbours nearly called the police. It sounded like a dying moose. Although, I did think it was quite brave of him. Trying to embrace his heritage and all that. Brave… or completely bonkers. Either way! This weather's been mental, hasn't it? Proper up and down. One minute sunshine, the next it’s chucking it down. It’s making getting on with the garden a nightmare. Tell me about it. I finally got the tomatoes planted last week, and then we had that torrential downpour. They’re looking a bit bedraggled, bless ‘em. I was hoping for a bumper crop this year, proper Sunderland tomatoes.

…and honestly, the look on Mr. Henderson’s face when I told him I was leaving was  priceless . He genuinely thought I'd be stuck there forever, managing spreadsheets and pretending to care about quarterly reports. Henderson, huh? The one who always wore that awful mustard cardigan? Serves him right. You were massively overqualified. Research management is a step down after your Masters, isn’t it? Even  I  know that. Well, it was a job, wasn't it? Needed to pay the rent. And the student loan interest is… well, it’s a monster, honestly. I’m still paying it off, years later. It feels like I’m donating to the government indefinitely. Tell me about it. Mine’s… substantial. Although, to be fair, I keep extending it by going  back  to being a student. It’s a vicious cycle. Still, at least PhD funding covers most things. Relatively. It's definitely better than the alternative. Better than drowning in debt and soul-crushing admin? Definitely. I’m just… restless, you know? I need something that actually  uses  my brain. Which is why I'm applying for these research roles now, even if the pay isn’t amazing. You’ll get something good. You always do. You're brilliant. Remember that time you completely tore apart Dr. Albright’s argument in your undergrad dissertation? She practically had steam coming out of her ears. Oh, don’t remind me! She marked me down for “aggressive analysis”, apparently. But honestly, it was a flawed argument! It just… irked me. It still irks me if I think about it too much. It’s that Sunderland stubbornness kicking in, I suppose. Sunderland stubbornness is a national treasure. It’s what separates you from… well, everyone else. Speaking of irritations, have you seen the university's new proposal for tuition fees? They’re hiking them  again . No! Seriously? That’s… outrageous. How are people supposed to afford this? It’s just pricing an entire generation out of higher education. I feel incredibly lucky I got in when I did, even with the debt. It feels like it was the last reasonably accessible window. Exactly. It’s supposed to be about merit, about opportunity. But it’s increasingly about who can afford to jump through the hoops. It's just... deeply unfair. It's making me question the whole system, even as I’m benefiting from it, to a degree.

Right, so this is… okay. It’s a bit  much , isn’t it? All these glittery unicorns. Little Leo would last about five seconds with this before it was covered in jam. It  is  rather…extravagant. Though Leo does seem to have a talent for finding jam, no matter where it is. Remember when he smeared it all over your grandad’s newspaper? How could I forget? Grandad wasn’t pleased. Though he pretended to be. We were thinking something a bit simpler, weren't we? Something…Bristol. Bristol? Lovely city. Though a bit…flat, if you ask me. Nothing like the hills of Glasgow. Though I suppose for a story, flat's fine. What sort of Bristol story? Well, I was thinking, maybe something about the docks? Or maybe the Suspension Bridge. Something kids would recognise and…care about? I had this idea about a little seagull who loses his favourite bottle cap. Oh, that’s sweet! A little lost treasure. Maybe it’s a bottle cap from his dad’s favourite fizzy drink? That gives it a bit of emotional weight. Yeah! Good idea, Mum. And the seagull could ask all the different people around the docks if they've seen it. The boat captains, the fishmongers… You know, that reminds me of a story my own grandfather used to tell me. He was a dockworker in Glasgow, back in the day. Not seagulls, obviously, but lost items were  always  a big deal. People cherished the smallest things. It’s funny, isn’t it? How things change…and don’t change. Everything always circles back, doesn’t it?
