She's saying they’re utterly swamped, but haven’t got the staff to cope. Complicated? Oh, Doreen, you always were one for smoothing things over. It's always been the same. Back when I was working, designing roads and all, you could  see  where your taxes were going. New bypasses, properly maintained infrastructure…now? It’s all cobwebs and excuses. Speaking of roads, have you seen the price of houses creeping up again? Trying to help my grandson, Liam, get on the ladder. Impossible! Impossible is right. Young people have no chance. My granddaughter, Chloe, she’s been saving for years, working two jobs, and still can’t afford a deposit around here. Used to be you could buy a perfectly decent little semi for a few thousand. Now they’re asking for a king’s ransom. I remember when we bought our place in Costessey… didn’t even  need  a mortgage! That's before everything changed, wasn’t it? My Harold and I, we bought our first house in Harrow in the early seventies. Small, but it was ours. I wonder if Liam’s considered looking further afield? Somewhere a bit…remote? I saw a lovely little cottage advertised in Cumbria. Proper countryside, very peaceful. Cumbria? That’s miles away! He works in Norwich, Doreen. Besides, he’d need a Sat Nav just to find the garden gate. Honestly, some of these modern gadgets… I swear my old paper maps were more reliable.

That was a grand bit of roasted chicken, Mary. Honestly, you outdo yourself every time. Ah, shush now, Liam. It's just a chicken. Though, I  did  find a new recipe for the roasting potatoes… a little rosemary and garlic, does the trick. These potatoes are amazing! Can I have another one? Go ahead, Ollie. Help yourself. Though, maybe slow down a bit, you’re eating like you haven't seen food in a week. Mmm! Potatos! Goo! He’s a happy little man, isn't he? Though 'goo' doesn't exactly sound like a glowing review, does it? No, but the enthusiasm is there. Right, Ollie, about your laptop… still acting the maggot? Yeah, it keeps freezing. I was trying to finish that history project, the one on the Tudors, and it just… stops. Then I lose everything! It’s really annoying. I had a look at it earlier. Seems like the graphics card is starting to give up the ghost. I ran a diagnostic, and it's throwing up errors. Oh dear. Is it fixable, Liam? Or are we talking about needing to buy a new one? Ollie needs it for school, you know. Well, I can try to re-seat the card, see if that helps. It's a long shot, mind you. It’s an older machine. The bigger problem is, it's just  outside  the warranty. By two months. Two months! Seriously? That's rubbish! I know, isn’t it? I checked the receipt, and we bought it in August of last year. Warranty was a year. Now, I could try contacting the company, explain the situation… but they're usually fairly rigid about these things. It's worth a shot, Liam. You're good at talking to people. You can be very persuasive when you want to be. I can try, but don't get your hopes up. If it  is  the graphics card, a replacement will be fairly expensive. We’ll have to weigh that up against getting him a basic new one. Could I maybe save up some of my pocket money? That’s a good lad, Ollie. That’s a very kind offer. But we’ll figure something out. Don't you worry about that now. Speaking of figuring things out, what about Saturday? Is the rugby training still on? Aye, it is. The coach sent out a text this morning. They're having a bit of a session at Muskerry RFC, preparing for the away match next week.

Right, who wants another slice? Honestly, this Margherita is disappearing  fast . It’s a good job I made two. Me! Me! A big one, please, Mummy! With loads of cheese. Can I have the crusty bit? The really,  really  crusty bit? Of course you can, darling. Both of you. Honestly, you two are like little locusts when pizza’s involved. Did you tell Grandma about the handstand you finally managed, Leo? I did! She said I was a ‘strong little badger’! But it’s hard. My head gets all… wobbly. I can  almost  do a handstand! I can hold it for… one… two… …seconds. That’s fantastic, Rosie! Practice makes perfect. Though maybe  after  the pizza, eh? We don’t want any pizza-related incidents. Speaking of which, whose birthday party are we thinking about outfits for tomorrow? Auntie Carol sent a message asking. Flora’s! And I want to wear the sparkly dress! The  really  sparkly one! But I want to wear my dinosaur jumper! It roars! The dinosaur jumper is excellent, Leo. Perhaps we can compromise? Maybe the dinosaur jumper  with  something sparkly? We need to think about what to tell Flora as well. She’s been a bit quiet lately. I think she’s feeling a bit left out because she hasn't been invited to as many things. She just needs a friend! Maybe we can be her friend? I  am  her friend! We build Lego at school. You absolutely are, sweetheart. And being a good friend means noticing when someone’s feeling a bit sad and making an effort to talk to them. It’s about… communication, isn’t it? It's not just about  saying  things, but  listening  too. It's hard, even for grown-ups. Listening is boring! Sometimes, yes. But it’s also how you find out what people are thinking and feeling. Now, quick maths test. If I have three slices of pizza left and Leo eats one, and Rosie eats two, how many slices will I have left? Zero! No! One! Because… three take away one is two, and two take away two is one! Brilliant, Rosie! Absolutely right. You’re both getting so good at your numbers. Right, another topic change before my brain explodes with pizza and arithmetic. I was thinking this weekend, instead of going to the park, we could  make  a fairy garden. A fairy garden?! With little houses?!

Honestly, this is proper good. I weren’t expecting Croatian food to be…well, this good. It’s miles better than that place back home, 'The Olive Branch', pretends to be. Remember that, Mum? All style, no substance. Oh, don't get me started on ‘The Olive Branch’. More olive  branching  out with prices than actual decent grub. This is lovely, isn’t it? Really fresh. And the wine…proper Croatian Malvasia. Not like that watered-down stuff they sell in Tesco. This pizza is AMAZING. Loads of cheese. Can I have another slice? Certainly, lad. It’s a beautiful spot, isn't it? Istria is genuinely surprising. I expected somewhere…touristy. But it's got a real charm. Reminds me a bit of the Amalfi Coast, though a bit less…frenetic. It’s so laid-back here. Even the weather's showing off. Back in Bolton, it’d be chucking it down right now. Proper grey skies and needing three coats. Aye, you're right about that. We were lucky escaping the rain. Though, I did pack five waterproof jackets just in case, knowing our luck. Remember that trip to Whitby when it rained for a  week  straight? Whitby was cool, though! We saw that massive whale skeleton in the museum! And I got a pirate hat. You did indeed, young man. A rather fetching pirate hat. Sarah, you were saying about wanting to explore Rovinj tomorrow? Yeah, I was reading about it. It apparently has these cobbled streets and a really stunning church on a hill. I’d like to take some photos. I’ve been trying to get better with the camera since uni. It’s just…finding the time, and the inspiration. Everything in Bolton looks grey, even  with  a filter. Rovinj’s lovely. I’ve been before, with your Auntie Brenda. She practically lived there one summer. Kept going on about the local art scene. You'll love it, love. Can we go swimming tomorrow? The pool at the hotel is massive! I was doing bomb dives earlier. Careful now, Ethan! No bombing when people are actually swimming. Speaking of pools, this hotel is significantly better than the last one we stayed in in…where was it? Tenerife? That one had a pool that smelled faintly of chlorine  and  sadness. Oh, don’t remind me! Honestly, it was like swimming in disinfectant. And the floors were permanently sticky.

Right good soup, Eileen. Always is, innit? Though, I do say, a bit more pepper wouldn’t go amiss next time. Feels a bit… bland, doesn’t it? Not like your mother used to make, bless 'er. She'd have had a whole shaker in, I reckon. Oh, Harold, you and your pepper. You say that  every  time. And my Mother’s soup was always a bit watery, let's be honest. It's good as it is, dear. Anyway, did you get that letter sorted? The one from… what was it, Legal & General? Ugh. That blasted thing. Still not sorted, Eileen. Still denyin' it all. PPI, they called it. Payment Protection Insurance. Never even  wanted  the bleedin’ stuff. They shoved it on me when I took out that loan for… well, a lot of years ago now. They reckon I’m owed money. But they reckon I owe  them  money too, for 'admin fees'. It's a right pickle, it is. PPI is a nightmare, Harold. Absolute daylight robbery. I had a chap from a claims company ring me last week. Said the same thing – they could get me money back, but there were “handling charges”. I told him where to put his handling charges. You tell ‘em, David. They prey on people, those companies. It's all a racket. Though, truthfully, I did use one. Got a decent return, paid the fee, and considered it money well spent to avoid the hassle. Hassle’s all it is! Endless letters, endless phone calls. They sent a bloke round, you know. Actually  to the door . Said he needed to ‘discuss my account.’ I told him I was ‘discussing my lunch’ and shut the door on ‘im. Can’t believe they still do that, knockin' on doors like debt collectors in a film. Good for you, Harold! Though, honestly, you shouldn’t have answered it at all. It's probably a scam. We saw that article in  The Lady  about all the new scams targeting pensioners. Dreadful, it is. I read that too. Something about fake TV licensing letters. Preying on people’s fears. Speaking of TV, has anyone seen that new series on the Abbey? The one about the restoration? It's quite fascinating. Not yet, but Carol’s been raving about it. Says it’s beautifully filmed. She’s already planning a trip to visit when it's open again.

Right, that’s another day done. Honestly, Mr. Henderson this time… thought he could argue the CCTV footage. The cheek! Aye, they all think they're clever, don't they, love? Been seein' it for twenty years. You teachin' them manners in school doesn't seem to stick when they're face-to-face with a fine or worse. It really doesn’t. It’s frustrating, actually. You try to instill a sense of responsibility, of understanding consequences… and then someone like Henderson thinks he's a legal genius. What about you? Busy day in Court 3? Fairly. Young lad, shoplifting. First offence. Mum was in bits. Always gets to me, those young ones. Makes you wonder what’s gone wrong, doesn't it? Not like it was when  I  was growing up. You knew where you stood then. It's hard, isn't it? I mean, I'm teaching teenagers now, and the pressures they face are just… different. So much social media, constant comparison. It feels like the stakes are higher for them. Social media... don't even get me started. My granddaughter's always on it. Says it's how she keeps up with her friends. Seems like a lot of bother to me. Though, she did send me a picture of a seal in Scotland the other day. Lovely thing. Oh, that’s sweet! I keep meaning to visit Scotland again. It’s been years. I went as a child, to my aunt’s in Inverness. I remember it being…wild. And cold! Wild and cold is a good way to put it. Insch, where I’m from, is a bit milder than Inverness, but still, you need a good coat. You a big traveller normally, then? I used to be, before… well, before things got expensive. And teaching doesn't exactly pay a fortune, does it? I'd love to go back to Italy, I spent a year there after university teaching English. That was  amazing . But weekends are usually spent marking essays and trying to keep the house vaguely tidy! Ah, money... always a problem. Gets tighter and tighter, doesn't it? They’re talkin' about raisin’ National Insurance again. What’s a body supposed to do? They say the younger generation can't afford houses. I don’t know how  anyone  can afford anything these days. It's terrifying, honestly. I’m trying to save for a deposit, but it feels like an impossible task.

…and then the little bear just  had  to have a picnic, didn’t he, Poppy? Even though it was raining! But bears don’t  have  picnics when it’s raining, Mummy! They’re sensible. They stay in their caves. My bear  does ! He wears a little hat and a raincoat! And he has sandwiches! Well, this bear is a very adventurous bear, Leo. He thinks rain is… sparkly! Speaking of sparkly, you two seem awfully happy building today. What makes you both happy? Building! And… when Nana sends us stickers. And chocolate. Definitely chocolate. Dinosaurs! And roaring!  ROAR ! And when you read me the dinosaur book, Mummy! Those all sound lovely. It's the little things, isn’t it? Do you know, sometimes people think happiness comes from having lots and lots of  things ? Like, loads and loads of money. Loads and loads? Like… a swimming pool of money? Well, maybe not quite a swimming pool! But a very,  very  big amount. Enough to buy everything you could ever want. Could I buy a real dinosaur? Sadly, I don't think even all the money in the world could buy us a real dinosaur, sweetie. They lived a very, very long time ago. But… what if you  did  have lots of money, Poppy? What would you do with it? I’d buy a pony! A fluffy white pony with a pink mane. And a stable, a really big one. And… and… I’d buy everyone in my class presents! That's very thoughtful of you. And Leo? What about you? I… um… I’d buy a hundred dinosaurs! And a robot dinosaur! And a dinosaur castle! And… and… I’d buy you a new chair, Mummy, because yours is a bit wobbly. Oh, Leo. That’s incredibly sweet. You're such a kind boy. See, you two already  have  loads of things that make you happy, and you want to share that happiness with others. That’s much more important than a swimming pool of money, don't you think? But wouldn't it be fun to  jump  in a swimming pool of money? It sounds… messy! And probably not very comfortable. It’s nice to  think  about, though, isn’t it? But having money doesn’t automatically make you happy. I know people who have lots of money, and they're often very busy and stressed. They don’t have time to build towers with bears or roar like dinosaurs.

…and honestly, the whole thing just feels…pointless. Like, memorising the dates of every single battle in the Wars of the Roses? What’s the actual  use  of that? It’s not like I’m going to be a historian. Relax, Alfie. Mr. Davies just likes a challenge. Besides, understanding history gives you context. You know, helps you understand  why  things are the way they are. Though I agree, the level of detail is a bit…intense. Still, better than Physics. Honestly, electromagnetic induction? My brain just melts. Context? I need context for choosing a career, not knowing who Henry VIII’s sixth wife was. Speaking of which, have you thought any more about what you want to  do ? Everyone’s going on about Uni applications and gap years, and I’m just… blank. A little. I was reading this article online about investment, actually. It got me thinking. Apparently, there’s a real opportunity in green tech right now. Like, developing new battery tech or more efficient solar panels. Investment? You? Since when are you suddenly a financial whiz? Last week you were trying to work out how much a packet of Monster Munch cost per crisp. Hey, I’m a meticulous cost analyst! But seriously, the article was about the booming market in China. Apparently, they’re investing  huge  amounts in renewable energy. It's not just about saving the planet, it's about economic growth. They’re basically patenting everything. China, huh? Always seems to be at the forefront of… everything these days. It’s a bit intimidating, isn’t it? They’re building cities faster than we can fix potholes. And the tech… all those AI breakthroughs. Exactly! Which is why I was thinking. What if someone invented something genuinely groundbreaking, something  new ? Like, forgetting AI for a second, what about a really efficient water purification system? Or a way to generate energy from… I don’t know, ocean currents? You could patent it, get investors, and boom – you’re set. Patent it? That sounds… complicated. And expensive. And what if someone steals your idea? It is, but there are people who specialise in that. Patent lawyers and all that. And there are ways to protect your intellectual property. It's not easy, but the rewards could be massive. Apparently, the guy who invented the self-sealing fuel tank for aeroplanes made a fortune. Saved loads of lives too, obviously.

Honestly, I still can’t believe we actually made it. Remember last year, all the talk about ‘maybe next year’? And then work just…exploded for both of us. Exploded is putting it mildly. You were practically living on coffee and red-pen corrections, and I was juggling three projects at once. It felt impossible. But here we are. Bansko of all places! Though, I have to admit, I was picturing something a little… fancier. This hotel is…rustic. Rustic is a polite word for ‘slightly dated’, isn’t it? But the skiing is brilliant, and it was such a steal. Besides, we're not here for the décor, are we? We're here to fall over gracefully in the snow, drink too much vin chaud and generally escape. How are your knees holding up, by the way? You were worried about them before we came. They're… protesting. A bit. I did that green run yesterday, the Shiligarnika one, and they were okay. But even that felt tougher than I remembered. I think I’m losing muscle tone. All those years of office work, you know? I’m definitely avoiding the black runs. Unless you're planning on dragging me down one. Absolutely not! I'm perfectly happy sticking to the reds with you. Though, I did eye up the Pirin one yesterday. It looked fantastic. Pristine snow. But no, you and your knees are my priority. We're supposed to be relaxing, remember? Speaking of priorities… have you heard anything from Mum and Dad? They were supposed to call yesterday. Oh, yes! I spoke to Mum this morning. She and Dad are having a lovely time in Cornwall. Apparently, Dad’s finally mastered the art of making scones, and Mum is thoroughly enjoying critiquing them. Said she was sending pictures, but I haven't seen them yet. She also asked after us – incessantly. Wanted to know if we were being sensible, if we were wearing enough layers, if we were drinking enough water…you know Mum. Oh, absolutely. She worries about us like we’re still ten years old! She’s convinced Bulgaria is full of bears and pickpockets. She is! She’s watched way too many travel documentaries. And she kept going on about Auntie Brenda's hip replacement. Brenda's hip is irrelevant to our skiing trip, Mum! I tried to explain that, but… well, you know how it goes.

Oh dear. Honestly, Arthur, I do apologise. I thought I had a clear line for the sideburn…but it seems I’ve taken a little  more  than anticipated. Hmm. Bit nippy, Margaret, bit nippy. But nothing a good comb-over can’t solve. More importantly…back to the strings. Cable ties. Are you  sure  about the cable ties? It feels…a bit Heath Robinson, doesn’t it? Heath Robinson? Now, Arthur, that’s insulting! It’s ingenious! Think about it - readily available, cheap as chips, and surprisingly strong. We're talking a temporary fix, remember? Until people see the value in a proper re-stringing service. And they  will  see the value. So many broken rackets just languishing in sheds. I suppose. It's just...the aesthetic. A pristine badminton racket, then a bright orange cable tie holding the frame together. It doesn't scream ‘professional restoration’. More ‘desperate measure’. What about the dimensions of the ties, though? Do we need different sizes for different rackets? A child’s racket will need a significantly smaller tie than mine, won’t it? Excellent point! We’ll need a range. I was thinking three sizes, predominantly. Small, medium, large. We can buy them in bulk online. I did a preliminary search – a thousand for under a tenner. Profit margins, Arthur, profit margins! Always thinking of the profit, aren’t you? Though, to be fair, that  is  a good price. But what about weight distribution? Won’t the cable tie add a noticeable imbalance to the racket? Badminton’s all about balance, you know. Years of coaching, you see. It's ingrained. A minor imbalance, surely? We can position them strategically. Near existing grommets, perhaps, to minimize disruption. We'll need to experiment. Speaking of experimenting… I was thinking about the word ‘fleet’. ‘Fleet’? What on earth are you talking about now? For the business! “Fleet Fix” or “Racket Fleet Repair”. It suggests a whole  collection  of rackets being brought back to life! It's memorable! Margaret, seriously? "Fleet"? It sounds like we're fixing boats, not badminton rackets. Besides, it implies we're dealing with a large volume. We’ve currently got  two  rackets to practice on. My old one and Mrs. Higgins' from next door. Well, it's aspirational, isn’t it? We need to think big! This could be huge, Arthur! We could offer it at primary schools, secondary schools… imagine the PE teachers being grateful.

Now, that one there… your Auntie Mabel did that, didn’t she, dear? Always had a knack with the colours, Mabel did. Though I never understood all that modern art nonsense, myself. Give me a nice landscape any day. Something you can  recognise . She did, Arthur. That’s the one she did of the Broads, just after she moved to Wroxham. It  is  lovely, isn’t it? Though, you’re right, you've never been one for abstract things. You like to know what you're looking at. It’s interesting, isn’t it, how much personal connection we have to art? It’s rarely just about the aesthetic. With Mabel's painting, you remember  her , the place, the time… it’s a memory trigger as much as anything. Absolutely. And that’s what makes discussing art so rich, I think. It’s rarely objective. I was talking to my students about Rothko this week, and the response was… varied, to say the least. Some found it profoundly moving, others just saw coloured rectangles. Rothko? Sounds German. Is that one of them ones where you need a fancy explanation to tell you it’s good? They’re all the same to me, those. Just splodges. I remember going to a gallery in London, years ago, with your mother, and… honestly, it was a waste of a perfectly good afternoon. Oh, Arthur, you were never impressed with the ‘high art’ scene. You wanted Constable, Turner… something you could point to and say, “That’s a tree! That’s a boat!” But isn’t that part of the point, though? That modern art often tries to move  away  from representation? It’s about exploring colour, form, emotion… bypassing the need for a literal depiction. Rothko, for example, was really interested in creating a kind of immersive emotional experience. He was deeply impacted by the Second World War, actually. A lot of his work is thought to be a response to the trauma he felt. He wanted to express feelings that were beyond words. Trauma? Good heavens. Art should be cheering, not reminding you of terrible things! That's what a good floral painting’s for. Keeps you happy. Reminds you of summer. He’s a simple man, you know. Needs his cheerfulness. I understand. But it's fascinating how those different approaches coexist. You don’t need to  understand  the theory behind abstract expressionism to have a reaction to it.

Honestly, I just… I can’t  with  Chloe anymore. She messaged me asking for notes…  again . Like, hello? We had the lecture, you were  there . Is it really my responsibility to hand-feed her a degree? Oh, Chloe. The eternal student. What did you say? I just said I was really busy. Which is true, obviously. This project at work is properly kicking my arse. Mr. Henderson decided  this  week, the week before Christmas, was the perfect time to completely restructure the entire report format. Ugh, classic Henderson move. He enjoys chaos, I swear. Is it all just cosmetic, or is there actual new information you need to find? A bit of both. The new format wants a full risk assessment for  every  single task. Every. Single. One. It’s ludicrous. And he wants it… visually appealing. Like, what does that even  mean  for a risk assessment? Little cartoon hazard symbols? Oh god, please don’t tell me he suggested that. Honestly, the things people come up with. I had a patient today who was convinced the hospital food was communicating with him. He said the peas were plotting against him. Right. That's… a different level of chaos. At least Henderson just wants pretty spreadsheets. Still, I'm officially procrastinating by complaining to you. I should be wrestling with pivot tables. Procrastination is a valid Friday night activity. Speaking of valid activities… this kitchen. It’s…an experience. When was the last time we actually  cleaned  in here? Don’t even. I’ve been ‘meaning to’ all week. It started with just a few dishes, then it escalated. It’s like a biohazard zone now. And honestly, looking at it just…demotivates me. It's a vicious cycle. It  is  pretty grim. Though, honestly, some of it is just…the inherent messiness of living. Like, crumbs are just a fact of life, aren’t they? No! Crumbs are a symbol of societal decay! Okay, maybe I'm being dramatic. But seriously, if I look closely enough at that counter, I’m pretty sure I can see new lifeforms evolving. Okay, okay, you’ve made your point. We should probably tackle it tomorrow. Or…Sunday? Sunday. Definitely Sunday. I need a buffer day to mentally prepare for a deep clean. We could put on that awful 90s playlist and just…attack. The one with all the one-hit wonders? Deal. Though, can we talk about the English language for a sec?

Honestly, this day has just…vanished. One minute it was 7am and I was battling the coffee machine, the next it's nearly nine and I've fielded three "urgent" requests from Mr. Davies, all of which could have waited an hour. You know, the man genuinely thinks email is a form of instant messaging. Sounds like a typical Tuesday with the Boss. Are you at least managing to avoid Brenda from accounts wanting help with her printer  again ? She’s a lovely woman, but technologically… challenged. Miraculously, yes. I think she’s finally taken a course or something. Although, I did overhear her trying to explain to someone that the cloud was literally a fluffy white thing in the sky. It’s exhausting. Honestly, sometimes I think I need a PA to  be  my PA. Now  that  would be efficient. You’d end up with a PA’s PA, and so on, ad infinitum. A bureaucracy of assistants! You deserve a medal, you do. Speaking of needing things… I’m down to my last cigarette. Oh, don’t even start. We had this conversation last week. And the week before. It's awful for you, and frankly, the smell is getting to me. We’re supposed to be enjoying our retirement, not slowly choking each other. It’s not that simple, is it? It's a habit, a…comfort. It’s the five minutes of peace I get when I step outside. And look, I know it’s bad, I’m not denying that. But honestly, compared to the amount of wine you consume some evenings, it feels a bit…hypocritical. That’s different! Wine is…civilized. A nice glass of Pinot Grigio with dinner. It's relaxing. It’s not puffing away on something that's actively trying to kill you. Civilized? Last Friday you were attempting to teach the cat to dance while reciting poetry after your third glass. I hardly call that  civilized.  It was entertaining, admittedly… Okay, fair point. I can get a bit…enthusiastic. But still, there's a difference! It’s about moderation, isn't it? Is it though? Is it really about moderation, or is it about what society deems acceptable vices? Look, I was reading something the other day about how some cultures openly embrace smoking, even encourage it as a social ritual, while others demonize it completely. It got me thinking about what we actually consider ‘normal’.

Right, who wants peas with their fish fingers? Honestly, after today, I feel like  I  need a farm visit, just to recover from taking you two. Peas! Yes, please! And can I have ketchup? Lots and lots of ketchup! Did you see the piglets, Mummy? They were SO pink! They smelled funny. And one tried to bite my wellies. They do have a certain… aroma, don't they? And yes, piglets are known for exploring with their mouths. They weren’t trying to  bite  your wellies, sweetheart, just investigating. Honestly, you were remarkably brave considering. Did you tell your teacher about it at school today? No. Miss Davies would just say ‘use your words, Leo.’ I  did  use my words! I said ‘get away, piggy!’ Well, that's perfectly good use of words, Leo. And a very sensible thing to say to a piglet. How was school otherwise? Anything interesting happen? I drew a picture of a cow! A really, really good cow. With purple spots! Miss Bell said it was ‘imaginative’. That sounds lovely, Daisy. Miss Bell always appreciates your imaginative artwork. She told me you’ve been very good at sharing this week. I  tried  to share my sparkly pen with Sophie, but she already had one. Well, trying is the important thing, darling. And Sophie’s lucky she has a sparkly pen too! Leo, how about you? Any sparkly pen incidents? I got a gold star. For… for being quiet during story time. Oh? That's good, Leo. Was it a particularly long story? It was about a dragon. And he roared really loud. And I didn’t shout ‘ROAR!’ back. Even though I wanted to. That  is  commendable restraint. Sometimes being quiet is a superpower. It sounds like you both had a busy day. Did you enjoy the tractor ride at the farm? It was wobbly! And the hay smelled tickly. I wanted to drive it. I think that might have been a bit beyond our insurance policy, darling. Although, you both looked very important sitting on the hay bales. It was nice to see you enjoying yourselves. It’s just… keeping track of you two in a field full of animals is  exhausting . It felt like a full-time job just making sure you didn’t end up covered head-to-toe in mud. But mud is fun! It  is  fun, I’ll grant you that.

Right, milk first for me, always. Though Gran always said tea made  properly  is tea made after the milk’s gone in. She was a woman of strong opinions, our Gran. And strong knitting. Honestly, the Aran jumpers she churned out… you could moor a boat with them. Moor a boat, aye. She was prolific, wasn’t she? And stubborn. Milk last, she used to declare, or it wouldn’t brew right. I think it was just a control thing. Birmingham Grandmothers are the same, mark my words. Though mine was more into crocheting doilies. A whole house full of them. Doilies! Oh, the horror. Knitting's just…better. More  substantial . Anyway, speaking of substantial, have you seen what Harry Styles is wearing now? Honestly, the floral suit at the BRITs…it was like a garden exploded. Did I miss this? Let me guess, feathers involved? He’s committed to the look, I’ll give him that. Though sometimes I wonder if it’s all a performance, you know? Like he’s deliberately trying to wind people up. Probably. He’s clever, that one. I’m just…confused. It’s a long way from the One Direction days. Remember when everyone was obsessed? It's mad how quickly things change. It feels like only yesterday we were arguing about whether Zayn was going to ruin the band. Oh god, don't remind me. Heated debates in the student union. Speaking of things changing quickly…the Olympics are looming, aren’t they? Have you seen the training schedules? It’s intense. A bit. To be honest, I’m more interested in the art installations they’re doing around the city for the cultural festival. I saw a preview of this massive sculpture they’re putting up near the Scott Polar Research Institute. It's made entirely of recycled plastic. Apparently, it’s supposed to look like a wave. That sounds…ambitious. Is it going to be any good, or one of those things that’s conceptually brilliant but aesthetically… questionable? Cambridge gets a lot of that, doesn’t it? Very ‘thinking person’s art’. You’re not wrong. It depends on your tolerance for pretension, I suppose. I’m hoping it’ll be good. It's nice to see them trying to do something environmentally conscious. It's just…everything feels so fraught right now, doesn’t it? So much going on.

…and honestly, Arthur, the National Maritime Museum is just  gorgeous . Did I tell you they’ve redone the galleries about the East India Company? It's not just about the ships y'know, it's about the people, the trade, everything. Though, mind you, it does gloss over some of the… less pleasant bits, doesn’t it? Still, worth a visit. Maritime, eh? Not really my cup of tea, love. Too many ropes and… well, water. Give me something solid, like the Victoria and Albert. Now  there’s  a museum. All that furniture, those tapestries… proper craftsmanship. We went years ago, didn't we? When the kids were little. Ages ago, Arthur. Before they were even thinking about university. And the V&A  is  lovely, I’ll grant you that. But I was thinking something a bit different this time. We’ve done the V&A, we’ve done the British Museum… I was hoping for a bit of a change. Perhaps something a little… interactive? Interactive? What’s that supposed to mean? Museums are for looking, not for fiddling. Last time we went somewhere ‘interactive’ young Timmy nearly broke a Roman pot. Nearly gave me a heart attack, he did. Oh, stop exaggerating. He was six! And it wasn't a Roman pot, it was a replica! I meant somewhere like the Science Museum, or even… have you ever been to one of those IMAX cinemas? I hear they have a new documentary about space, with 3D. IMAX? 3D? Good Lord, Doreen. All that flashing about. Gives me a headache just thinking about it. Remember that one we saw, years back, the dinosaur one? I felt seasick for the rest of the day. And getting  to  these places… that's my biggest worry. London transport is a nightmare. Oh, don’t start on the transport, Arthur. We’ll manage. I’ve got the Oyster cards topped up, and I’ve checked the tube lines. Mostly alright, apparently. Though there is engineering work on the District line, so we might have to use the buses for a bit. Buses! Wonderful. Stuck in traffic for hours. And all sorts on those buses. Last time I was on a London bus, a bloke was singing opera at the top of his voice. Scared the life out of a little girl. Well, it certainly sounds like a memorable journey! Look, don’t be such a grump. We haven’t been into London properly in months.

…and honestly, the heating in these apartments is a bit… optimistic, isn’t it? Even with this, I’m still layering. Feels a bit like December in London, actually. Which, speaking of, has got me thinking about Christmas. Absolutely mental that it's next month already. Optimistic is a polite way to put it. It’s more like a gentle suggestion of warmth. And you're right about Christmas. It sneaks up on you. Especially out here. Doesn’t  feel  like Christmas, does it? No biting wind, no grey skies… it’s all a bit…tropical. Exactly! It's hard to get into the spirit when you're thinking about suncream instead of scarves. I was trying to explain a proper Christmas to one of my students the other day – the whole roaring fire, mulled wine, family chaos thing – and they just looked at me like I was describing a historical re-enactment. I can imagine. They're probably picturing a very different kind of festive season. So, what are your plans then? Going home? I’m thinking about it. Flights are… well, you know. Astronomical. And the thought of the airport queues… it's tempting to just stay put. I was thinking maybe we could do a little something here? A Christmas dinner? We could invite a few of the other lecturers, the ones who are also stuck here. That's a brilliant idea, actually! A little slice of home. I’m in. I’m not necessarily rushing to brave Manchester’s winter - my mother will have already cooked enough for the entire borough, I imagine. And frankly, escaping the annual ‘are you seeing anyone?’ interrogation is a bonus. Oh, I know that one well. Mine’s moved on to detailed life planning, listing potential grandchildren by name. It's exhausting. Right, so dinner… Who should we invite? Sarah from the linguistics department, definitely. She’s been missing proper gravy since she arrived. Absolutely Sarah. And what about old man Hemmings from history? He’s always up for a good moan, and a good Christmas pudding. Though he does have a habit of correcting everyone’s historical inaccuracies  during  dinner. Oh god, Hemmings. Okay, but we strategically seat him next to someone who enjoys a debate. Maybe David from engineering? They could argue about the structural integrity of the Titanic all night. Perfect! Suffering through a detailed analysis of maritime disasters is a Christmas tradition I can get behind.

Right, I’m officially logging off for the night. My brain is fried. Honestly, scrolling through Twitter all day is a recipe for existential dread. Tell me about it. I deleted the app again. Found myself arguing with someone about… sourdough hydration levels. Like, seriously? Who has time for that? Though, it  is  strangely addictive. Sourdough hydration levels? Oh, bless you. My drama today involved a bloke who complained his latte wasn’t hot enough, then proceeded to microwave it  in the café . No way! Did you say anything? What could I say? I just stared. Honestly, some people. It’s always the quiet ones, innit? The ones who look like they wouldn't hurt a fly, then pull something like  that . Reminds me of this review we got last week – “Charming café, lovely atmosphere, but the barista clearly hates her job.” Like, how?! I was practically skipping around all morning. Ugh, reviews. Don’t even get me started. I swear, people think they’re Gordon Ramsay when they haven’t even baked a cookie. I had one saying my lemon drizzle was “too lemony”. Too lemony! It’s a  lemon drizzle ! Honestly, the audacity. It's the internet, right? Gives everyone a platform to be…unpleasant. I saw someone on a restaurant review site complaining the portion sizes weren’t big enough at a tasting menu. A  tasting  menu! It's exhausting, isn’t it? Running a small business. You put your heart and soul into things, then someone decides to tear it all down with a few tapped-out sentences. Speaking of running a business, have you two given any more thought to the whole Margate thing? Margate? You mean…a café down there? I've been daydreaming about it constantly, actually. It would be amazing. Escape London prices, a bit of sea air… and honestly, the design scene down there is really blossoming. I saw some incredible interiors when we went last month. Yeah, it did look really cool. I was more thinking about a little bookshop, maybe with a small coffee bar attached? The rent’s still cheaper than anything central here. But…starting a new business is terrifying. Terrifying but exciting! I mean, look at me. I scrapped together enough to open this place, and it’s the best thing I ever did. Sure, there are days I want to scream into a pillow, but then a customer tells me they love the vibe, or the coffee, or whatever, and it makes it all worthwhile.

Honestly, this is lovely. Just what I needed after marking those practice exams all afternoon. The Year 10s are… enthusiastic, let’s say. But not always  accurate  in their enthusiasm. Is ‘enthusiastic’ good, Miss Davies? Like, when I’m enthusiastic about drawing? It is good, Lily-Rose! Especially when you’re enthusiastic about drawing. It means you’re excited and putting your all into it. With the exams… well, sometimes they get enthusiastic about the  wrong  answers! Sounds about right. They all think they know everything, until you actually  ask  them something. Did you give them the one on the migratory patterns of swallows? They always mess that one up. Oisin, darling, please. No throwing the peas. We’ve discussed this. It’s not a game. Children and peas, a classic struggle. Honestly, it’s amazing how much drama can revolve around a tiny green vegetable. Speaking of which, anyone fancy some garden raspberries for dessert? I picked a few this morning, they’re absolutely glorious. Raspberries! Yes, please! Can I have loads and loads? I'm good with raspberries, actually. Though, if we're talking dessert, is there any chance of chocolate ice cream later? I had a particularly brutal PE lesson today and deserve a reward. Perhaps, Leo.  Perhaps . If Oisin doesn’t empty the fridge looking for snacks first. He’s been on a mission for chocolate all day. He even tried to barter a gerbil chew toy for a biscuit this morning! A gerbil chew toy? That’s a new one! How’s Barnaby and Pipkin doing, anyway? Are they still racing around their wheel like tiny furry maniacs? They are. Absolutely manic. They’ve dug tunnels… everywhere. I swear, half the bedding ends up outside the cage. I found some under the sofa yesterday. It's a constant battle! Gerbils are pretty cool. My nan had two when she was a kid. She told me stories about how she used to try and teach them tricks. Didn’t really work, apparently. They were more interested in stuffing their faces. Can we get a gerbil, Mummy? Please? I promise to clean their cage! We’ll see, darling. Maybe. It’s a lot of responsibility. We need to think about it. Right now, let’s just try and get some dinner eaten, okay? Oisin, please,  no  playing with the broccoli. Back to the exams… I’m starting to wonder if I should have included a section on bird eggs.

…and honestly, the avocados were rock solid. Rock. Solid. You could’ve built a small fortress with them. It’s just getting so frustrating, isn’t it? Spending good money and getting…well, not good money’s worth. Tell me about it, love. I went for oranges last week. They were all mouldy inside, wrapped up all pretty in their skins. It’s a right con, it is. They want your money, they don’t care if you can actually  use  the stuff. Back in my day, you knew where you stood with the greengrocer. Old Mr. Hemmings, he’d practically guarantee everything. If a tomato wasn’t right, you took it back and he’d give you another, no questions asked. None of this supermarket nonsense. Exactly, Gran! It's all about volume now, isn't it? No personal touch. Speaking of which, I was thinking…you’ve been looking a bit tired lately. Are you managing alright with everything? Oh, I'm fine, dear. Just a bit…slow these days. The legs aren’t what they were, you know. And Mrs. Higgins next door, bless her, she’s been poorly. I’ve been popping in with a bit of soup now and again. You're a saint, you are, Mum. Always looking after everyone. I wouldn’t know what she’d do without you. I popped round yesterday, she was looking really peaky. That’s lovely of you, Mum. It’s just…I worry. Are you taking on too much? I could pop over more often, help with shopping or…anything? Now, don't fuss. I appreciate the thought, I really do, but I’m not helpless yet. Though, a little help with the garden wouldn’t go amiss…that bindweed is getting out of control. I can have a go at that bindweed, Mum. I'm not doing much on a Tuesday. It’s just…well, work’s been quiet. They've cut back hours at the school. Oh no, I’m sorry to hear that, love. That’s awful. Is it enough to manage on? We'll manage, we always do. It's just…tight. Still, it gives me more time to potter about. I was thinking I need to get my eyebrows done. They're a right mess, aren't they? They look fine to me! But if it makes you feel better…You know, I was thinking of getting my hair cut.

Honestly, this is lovely. Just… a quiet five minutes. He’s been a little bundle of energy all morning, hasn't he? Nearly launched himself off the changing table twice. He’s discovering gravity, Mum. It’s a crucial stage. And yes, a  very  energetic little man. He's definitely getting stronger, which means the weaning is going to be… interesting. Interesting is one word for it. Chaotic, messy, and possibly involving a full outfit change for both of you feels a bit closer to the mark. How did the sweet potato go yesterday? You looked a little frazzled when I called. Let’s just say it wasn't a graceful introduction to solid food. It ended up everywhere. Hair, face, the high chair, the dog… even a little bit on the ceiling, I swear. He mostly just  looked  at it, then pushed it away with a very determined 'no'. Oh, bless him! They're so single-minded, aren’t they? My sister had the same with little Thomas and the butternut squash. Pure rebellion. You’ll get there. Maybe try something a bit… less orange? I was thinking of apple and cinnamon today. Perhaps a gentler flavour. And definitely a bigger bib. Honestly, I'm starting to consider investing in a splash suit for me! That’s a good idea! You should. It won't be the first time a mother's had to armour up for feeding time. Speaking of needing armour… did you manage to get hold of Auntie Carol about Sunday? She was driving me mad asking if we were still on for lunch. I did, just this morning. Yes, we’re still on. She was relieved. Apparently, she'd already planned three different desserts, just in case. You know how she is. Oh, Carol and her desserts. It’s a superpower, really. I’m trying to subtly hint that we don’t need a full roast  and  a pie  and  a trifle, but she doesn't take hints. I suspect nothing can deter a Carol dessert plan. She's impenetrable. Are Uncle David and the cousins coming too? David is, but Emily’s got a school trip on Saturday, and Mark’s got that football tournament. It’s a shame, but it'll be nice even if it's just a smaller gathering. It’s been ages since we’ve all been together. It has. It would be good to catch up with everyone.

Honestly, it’s just… different, isn’t it? Coming from London, even just for a weekend, you forget how  flat  everything is there. It’s all straight lines and buildings. Here… it's gentle. Even these little rises feel like hills. “Hills” is generous. Norfolk’s idea of a hill is a slightly enthusiastic bump. But you’re right, it’s a completely different landscape. It gets under your skin, doesn’t it? I mean, I grew up with it, but even  I  notice it more when I’ve been back in the city for a while. Everything feels… rushed there. Here, it just… breathes. Exactly! Rushed is the perfect word. Everything feels so  contained  in London. Like you're constantly hemmed in. And the light! It’s different here. Brighter, somehow. Even on a cloudy day. It’s the space, I think. The light has room to move. And there’s less pollution, naturally. You can actually  see  things. Remember that view from the pub garden in Burnham Market last time? You could see for miles. Oh, Burnham Market is lovely! A bit too…polished now, perhaps? It’s getting quite swanky. Still, that view  was  incredible. And the way the fields just stretched out… It's the vastness, isn’t it? Compared to those little pocket parks in London. It is. And the villages. They all have such character. Little Walsingham, for example. That priory ruins… it feels like stepping back in time. Did you read about the supposed Holy House there? The one that was brought over from Walsingham itself? Vaguely. Something about a shrine and pilgrims? My medieval history knowledge is a bit rusty, I confess. I'm more of a 19th-century literary type, you know. Though, I did look into the history of Norwich a bit before we came. Incredible how it was such a major wool trading centre. Shaping everything. Oh, it totally was. The wealth from the wool trade built a lot of what you see in Norwich still. That cathedral, the Merchant's Hall… all down to sheep, essentially. And the surrounding villages were all part of that system. Each with its specialism. Some for breeding, some for weaving… That’s fascinating. You always know the historical context to everything. I’m embarrassingly bad at remembering dates and details. I get the general  feeling  of a place, I think. That’s why I love walking.

Right, that was a proper brew, wasn’t it? Needed that after wrestling with those XML tags all day. Honestly, sometimes I think the corpus is actively  trying  to break me. Sounds thrilling. Corpus administration, the glamour job of the 21st century. Seriously though, you sounded stressed on the phone. Is it still that bad with the new data ingestion pipeline? It’s… a process. Old Professor Davies, bless him, designed the thing back when computers were the size of rooms. And now everyone’s wanting to shove massive datasets through it. It's like trying to force a whale through a garden hose. Classic Davies. Always thinking big, practicality not always his forte. Speaking of big…did you hear what Liam's up to now? Liam? No, what’s the latest escapade? Last I heard he was trying to make artisanal dog biscuits. Worse. Well, not  worse , just… different. He’s become a ‘life coach’. Apparently he's got a website and everything, all motivational quotes and pictures of him looking meaningfully at sunrises. You are kidding! Liam? The Liam who once spent a week convinced he was a pigeon? The very same. He’s offering ‘unlocking your potential’ packages. I nearly choked on my tea when Mum told me. Apparently, he's charging a fair bit too. Oh, that’s brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. I need to see this website. Does it involve a lot of crystals and positive affirmations? I shudder to think. Honestly, he’s always been a bit… directionless, hasn’t he? But this feels like a whole new level of directionlessness packaged as expertise. Aye, he’s always been a bit lost. Remember that time he tried to learn the trombone? That lasted all of three weeks. And the noise… the neighbours threatened to call the police. Oh god, the trombone. I'd blocked that out. Anyway, enough about Liam’s questionable life choices. Did you manage to see that new action film,  Nexus Protocol ? Everyone at work was raving about it. I tried to, but craved something a bit less… blow-upy. Ended up watching that French New Wave thing you recommended.  Breathless , was it?  À bout de souffle . Good choice! It's a bit slow-paced, but visually incredible. So, what did you think? Really liked it, actually. Different. Very… existential. Although, I did keep expecting someone to pull out a gun. My action movie brain was struggling to adjust.

Oh, this is  exactly  what I needed. London feels… oppressive, doesn’t it? Even after all these years. Just concrete and noise. You can actually  hear  the countryside here. Absolutely. It’s the lack of constant demands on your attention, I think. London’s brilliant, but it never lets you switch off. Did you spot that field of oilseed rape back there? Beautiful, isn't it? That vibrant yellow. It was stunning. Though it always feels a bit… well, economically fraught, doesn't it? All that reliance on a single cash crop. One bad season and… You’re thinking about the subsidy arguments? Yeah, it’s a tricky one. My uncle’s got a smallholding near Cambridge, he’s constantly moaning about it. Says it’s increasingly difficult to make a decent living even  with  the farm payments. It's a precarious existence, really. Different world to lecturing about post-structuralism, isn’t it? Worlds apart. Though, in a strange way, both are built on a foundation of… dependence. We depend on funding councils, they depend on government policy. It’s all interconnected. Speaking of dependence, did you see Professor Davies’ latest paper? The one about language acquisition and early childhood exposure? I skimmed it. Bit dense, even for me. He’s getting increasingly fixated on the critical period hypothesis, isn’t he? I’m still a bit skeptical. I think the neurological plasticity is underestimated. Plus, you get these incredible polyglots who pick up languages as adults. Busts the whole theory, really. True. But he’s got the data to back it up, which is frustrating. He’s a pain sometimes, Davies. Always has to be right. Reminds me of… well, never mind. Reminds you of someone? Do tell. Don’t leave me hanging. Oh, just a particularly stubborn student I had last year. Kept arguing with me about Derrida. It was exhausting. Anyway, look! Those are cowslips. Remember when we were kids and we’d make chains of them? Vaguely. You were much better at it than I was. I always managed to snap them. Probably why I ended up pursuing less delicate academic pursuits. Still, they’re lovely. Honestly, this whole area is just covered in wildflowers. It feels almost… deliberately curated. It is, in a way. The farming practices around here are quite good for wildlife. They’ve got stewardship schemes running, encouraging them to leave field margins wild.

…and honestly, the parking situation ‘round there is a nightmare. Absolute nightmare. I was thinking maybe we could get the train if we go to that new Italian place in Newcastle next weekend? Saved hassle, yeah? Hmm, the train's not bad, I suppose. But it feels a bit…limiting, doesn’t it? Like, if we want to nip somewhere else afterwards, or even just explore a bit, we're stuck relying on buses. Which, let’s be honest, in Newcastle aren’t exactly renowned for their punctuality. Aye, true enough. But even driving… finding a space near that restaurant is going to be a mission. Remember when we tried to go to that tapas place in Ouseburn? We circled for half an hour! I nearly lost the will to live. Oh god, don't remind me. That was… a strategic error. Maybe we just book a taxi to and from? Expensive, but less stressful. Speaking of stressful, how’s work been? Still drowning in linguistic data? You have  no  idea. This new project is… intense. I'm indexing this massive corpus of spoken language, and half of it is people talking about football. Honestly, I'm starting to dream in offsides and VAR decisions. It’s endless. Football, huh? I'm guessing you're not exactly a massive fan? Nah, not really. I can’t stand it. All that shouting and… the emotion! It’s baffling. My dad tries to get me into Sunderland games, but I just politely decline. It's a whole culture I don't understand. What about you? Still glued to every Arsenal match? Pretty much. It’s a familial obligation, really. My dad and grandad are huge fans, so it’s been passed down. Though, I have to say, this season's been… unpredictable. Still, better than watching Leeds, I suppose. Oh, don't even get me started on Leeds. My friend Sarah's boyfriend is a die-hard Leeds supporter. It’s… challenging. Anyway, back to more important matters – have you seen the Angel lately? I drove past it the other day, and it looked particularly imposing in the mist. Not for ages, actually. It's one of those things you forget is there until you actually see it looming over the A1. Honestly, it's a bit of a masterpiece, isn't it? Though, I always wonder what people think when they first see it.

Honestly, this whole Rebekah Vardy thing is just… exhausting, isn’t it? I mean, the details! It's like something out of a really bad soap opera. Though, I suppose that's why everyone's so hooked. Exhausting is a good word for it, love. I tried to follow it a bit, but all the legal jargon just went straight over my ‘ead. Seems a lot of fuss over a few Instagram posts. My Nan always said, never put anything in writing you wouldn’t want shouted from the rooftops. Seems like good advice still. Oh, that woman! Always thought she was a bit… much. Too much make-up, too much showing off. Though, mind you, the papers do love a scandal. Sells more copies, doesn't it? Used to be, it was just the Royal Family getting all the attention. Exactly! And it's not just the details, it’s  how  long it's gone on. Remember when it first started bubbling up? Feels like ages ago. It's taken over the news cycle entirely. It makes you wonder what other dramas are going on we  don’t  hear about with celebrities. Proper distraction, innit? From everything else that's going on. Petrol prices, bills going up… better to watch someone else's mess, I suppose. Speaking of distractions, have you seen the geese are back in force down by the river? Oh, yes! I saw a huge flock heading north this morning as I was driving to a client meeting. It’s amazing, isn’t it? That instinct to just  go . Thousands of miles, guided by… what? It’s incredible. My dad was a keen birdwatcher, he'd spend hours with his binoculars. He could identify birds just from their calls. Your dad was a quiet one, wasn’t he? Always had his nose in a book or peering through those things. Wonderful man. The geese… they’re a sign of the times, they are. Always have been. Reminds me of my Arthur, bless him. He used to work down at the sugar factory, and the geese would follow the tractors during harvest. Always hoping for a dropped beet. Same down our end. Old Man Hemmings had a little orchard, and they’d descend on his fallen apples. Nuisance, he called ‘em, but he secretly liked having the company. They’re clever birds, geese. They know where the food is.

Oh, this is  exactly  what I needed. Honestly, school dinners these days… they’re… an experience. Not always a good one. Though little Timmy did tell me his shepherd’s pie tasted “like sunshine” which was rather sweet. “Like sunshine”? Oh, children. Bless them. I’m glad you’re enjoying it. I tried to make a fancy quiche this morning, and it ended up looking…deflated. Like a sad, eggy pancake. Oh no! Quiche is deceptively difficult. It’s all about the blind bake, isn't it? I attempted one once for a staff potluck. Let’s just say it was… structurally unsound. Everyone was very polite. Very polite covering thinly veiled horror, you mean? I know the feeling. It's the pressure, isn’t it? Trying to be a Domestic Goddess while simultaneously marking 30 essays. It’s exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, how did the interview go? You were so nervous about it last week. Ugh. Don't even. It was… okay. A complete and utter mess, stylishly disguised as "okay." The head of department was  very  enthusiastic about their new ‘innovative learning programme’ which, as far as I can tell, involves a lot of brightly coloured beanbags and children learning through ‘experience.’ Beanbags? Seriously? Is that actually a pedagogical approach now? Apparently! And singing. A lot of singing. They wanted me to demonstrate how I’d incorporate song into a lesson on the subjunctive mood. I nearly choked on my own tongue. I just… rambled about verb conjugations. And then I think I mentioned Geoffrey Chaucer at some point. It was not a good look, I suspect. Oh, no. That sounds… intense. Chaucer is a bit much for a beanbag-based subjunctive lesson, I think. But honestly, some of these schools are obsessed with trends. It feels like they prioritize buzzwords over actual teaching sometimes. Exactly! And the woman interviewing me kept referring to the children as “little learners.”  Little learners . It makes me feel ancient! Oh, I hate that. Everything's 'learning' now. I was talking to Sarah the other day - you remember her, from the history department? - and she’s in the trenches with this new ‘learning journey’ they’ve implemented. Apparently, it's just walking around the school grounds looking at trees. You’re joking! No. I wish I were. It's something to do with 'connecting with nature' and 'holistic understanding'. Honestly, I'm starting to think I prefer marking essays.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I had to clear this morning was  criminal . Like, who needs fifteen different updates on the same bloody bolt order? It's a bolt! Fifteen? Seriously? Sounds like someone's overcompensating for…something. Maybe they’re terrified someone will realise they don't actually know what's going on with the bolts. Probably. It's the kind of environment where admitting you don’t know something is a capital offense. It's wearing me down, actually. I thought going for the production controller role would be…more? More strategic, less…bolt policing. I get that. I mean, I’m basically a professional calendar-tetris-er at the moment. Scheduling meetings, making sure everyone has the right biscuits for their tea… It's not exactly changing the world, is it? Though, Mrs. Hawthorne was  very  grateful for the ginger snaps yesterday. Bless Mrs. Hawthorne. She’s a legend. But seriously, we’re both postgraduates, right? We spent years and a fortune on degrees. Are we destined to manage biscuits and bolts for the rest of our lives? Woah, existential crisis alert! That’s a bit bleak, isn’t it? I mean, I always thought… I don’t know, something with research, maybe? But the funding's just… impossible to get. Everyone wants experience, and you can’t  get  experience without a job, and you can’t get a research job without experience. It’s a vicious cycle. Exactly! It feels like everyone's perpetually stuck on level one. Remember when we used to talk about travelling the world, writing novels, starting our own businesses? Oh god, don’t remind me. I had a whole Pinterest board dedicated to nomadic van life. Solar panels, tiny kitchens, the works. Now, the most adventurous thing I do is try a new flavour of instant coffee. I was going to be a documentary filmmaker! All gritty realism and uncovering hidden truths. Now I'm uncovering discrepancies in supplier invoices. It's… a downgrade. I’ve started looking at online courses, actually. Data science. Apparently, it’s where the money is. Data science? Really? That's… surprisingly sensible of you. I always pictured you leading a rebellion against the man, not…analysing spreadsheets. The rebellion got expensive. Rent's not cheap, even in Cambridge. Plus, I'm starting to think 'sensible' isn’t a dirty word. It might actually be the key to a slightly less stressful existence.

…and honestly, I’m starting to think Liam’s just  saying  he’s busy to avoid me. Like, every time I suggest doing something, it’s ‘work’, ‘family stuff’, or ‘helping a mate’. It's a right cheek, innit? Ooh, that's rough, Jess. Are you sure? Maybe he genuinely is swamped. Uni lads and all that. Swamped for the last three weekends running? Swamped to the point where he can’t even manage a text back for more than six hours? Nah. Something’s up. I just  feel  it. It sounds a bit dodgy, yeah. Though, boys are just… baffling creatures, aren't they? I mean, remember Ben and the whole ‘lost phone’ saga? Turned out he was just chatting up Chloe from the library. Oh god,  Ben . Don't even get me started. He was a walking disaster. Worse than a broken washing machine! At least Liam seems… marginally less of a mess. Though, you are right to be suspicious, Jess. Trust your gut. See! Glad someone's on my side. It’s just… I really liked him. I thought things were going well. We had a proper laugh last time we went to that gig in Sheffield. He even offered to carry my bag! A  massive  gesture for Liam, believe me. A bag carry is serious boyfriend material, absolutely. Though Cambridge boys are slightly better at basic courtesy, I will say. Not by much, admittedly. Oh, here we go with the Cambridge superiority complex. We're in France, love, not a competition for the most polite blokes. Anyway, Jess, what are you gonna  do  about Liam? Are you gonna confront him? That’s what I’m wrestling with. Part of me wants to just march over there and demand an explanation. But then I’m worried I’ll come across all…clingy. And he’ll just lie. He's good at that, the little scoundrel. Confrontation is always good. Even if it’s just to get it off your chest. You deserve to know where you stand. Plus, if he  is  doing something dodgy, you’ll find out sooner rather than later. I went through a similar thing with… well, never mind. Suffice to say, ignoring it makes it ten times worse. Definitely. It’s better to rip the plaster off quickly. Though, maybe a casual 'Hey, just checking everything's alright, haven’t heard from you much' text first?

…Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is  exactly  what I needed after that day. Absolute chaos with Mrs. Henderson’s manuscript. Apparently, ‘affect’ and ‘effect’ are interchangeable in her world. Mmmph, it  is  good, Mum. Best shepherd’s pie ever. Though, I think I prefer yours with sweetcorn in, not peas. He’s a sweetcorn devotee, this one. Reminds me of my cousin, always demanding sweetcorn with everything. You know, it’s funny the things you remember… speaking of remembering, did anyone manage to get a photo of Ethan scoring that goal today? I did! Loads! I got the one where his stick’s practically horizontal and his face is all… determined. It’s going straight onto my Insta. Hashtag ‘hockeyhero’. Oh, good, because your father was attempting a video, but all it captured was the back of Mr. Davies’ head and a lot of shouting. He’s still convinced the referee was biased. A classic Dad reaction. They all are, aren’t they? But seriously, Ethan, that was a brilliant goal. You weaved through practically the whole team. He’s getting really good, isn’t he? Almost as good as Leo… though Leo’s still the captain for a reason. Hey! Now, now, boys. No need for rivalry at the dinner table. You’re both fantastic players. Different strengths, that’s all. Speaking of Leo, did he finally manage to sort out his trip to see his grandparents in Scotland? He was sounding so frustrated last week. I think so. His mum mentioned something about a train ticket being booked. It’s proving difficult with everything going on with the rail strikes, isn’t it? We were talking about potentially going to visit my sister in South Korea next year. But honestly, the flight prices are… astronomical. Oh, they are. We were briefly toying with the idea of a week in Italy – just a bit of sun and pasta. But the cost of everything… It’s easier to stay put, really. Fradley’s not so bad. Italy sounds amazing! Can we go to Rome? I’ve seen pictures of the Colosseum and it’s huge. Yeah, and all the pizza! Maybe someday, lads. Maybe someday. We'd need to start saving now! It's just... with the business, things are a bit up and down. One month, it’s a frantic rush of assignments, next it's… quieter. Still, can't complain.

Honestly, this is just… incredible. I mean, I've  seen  pictures, obviously, but nothing prepares you for the sheer scale of these trees. It feels like being on another planet. Right? Completely. I was trying to get a good photo, but it's impossible. Everything looks so… miniature next to them. My phone just can’t capture it. It's a bit humbling, isn't it? Makes you feel pretty small. Humbling is the word. Reminds me a bit of Dad, actually. Not in the tree-like way, obviously… more in the way he always put things into perspective. Remember that time I was completely devastated about failing my mock A-levels, and he took me to the beach and just pointed out how vast the ocean was? Oh god, yes! And said something about my algebra being statistically insignificant in the grand scheme of things? He was brilliant at that. Brutally honest, but brilliant. How  is  he, by the way? I haven’t spoken to him properly since Christmas. He's… Dad. He's pottering. Apparently, he’s taken up birdwatching. Can you imagine? Dad, with binoculars! Mum sends pictures. He’s already identified, and apparently named, every bird in a five-mile radius of Pembury. He calls one of the robins ‘Reginald’. Reginald! That's perfect. He hasn’t changed a bit. It's amazing how he finds something to obsess over. Remember when it was model railways? The whole spare room was taken up! And the neighbours complained about the noise! Good times. Mum deserved a medal for putting up with it all, honestly. Speaking of Mum, she’s driving Aunt Carol mad, apparently. Aunt Carol decided she was going to ‘declutter’ Mum’s spare room, and Mum’s taken it as a personal affront. Oh,  no . That's… predictable. Aunt Carol and her ‘helpful’ decluttering. She did the same to Gran, remember? Ended up ‘reorganising’ all her photo albums into completely random order. Gran was furious for weeks. Exactly! It's not about the stuff itself, it's the principle of the thing. She's convinced Carol is trying to tell her she’s a hoarder. Honestly, the family drama never ends, does it? Even when we're three thousand miles away, it follows us. Never. It’s… comforting, in a way? Knowing that even whilst we're having an amazing adventure, everything is still ticking over back home, with all its usual chaos.

Now, that Kiev was…alright. Not a patch on the ones my mother used to make, mind you. She’d always sneak a bit of extra garlic in. Nearly gassed the whole kitchen some nights, she did. It was good! Better than school dinners, anyway. Though, Mr. Henderson did try to pass off some sort of…grey chicken thing last week. I reckon it was reconstituted. Reconstituted? You've been watching too much cooking TV, love. Though, you’re right, school dinners aren't exactly renowned for their culinary excellence. Honestly, I’m just glad someone’s cooking something that isn’t beige for once. Beige is a plague on the nation, I tell ya. Speaking of plagues… did you see the rugby yesterday? Absolutely brutal. That penalty decision in the last five minutes… scandalous! I was roaring at the telly like a banshee. Yeah, it was a bit dodgy. Dad was going mad! He nearly threw his biscuit at the screen. Don’t you  dare  throw biscuits at the television, John! Especially not digestives. They leave crumbs everywhere. Honestly, the state of this living room after a rugby match... Now, now, Maureen, a man’s gotta express himself. Though I admit, the biscuit nearly missed the telly and went straight into young Master Finley's building blocks. That wasn’t ideal. It was a good shot, though. Finley will be finding crumbs in those blocks for months! Speaking of finding things, are we still on for Granny next weekend? I was thinking Saturday. Saturday’s grand. I’ll give her a ring this evening, just to let her know we're coming. She'll be expecting it, the old bird. Always asking when we're popping over. Though, be warned, she’s been on a bit of a ‘backchat’ streak lately. Backchat? What does she mean? Oh, just… questioning my life choices. Suggesting I should be spending more time gardening, less time staring at a computer screen. The usual Granny stuff. She reckons IT managers just sit around all day playing with ‘Wallies’. Oh, she's a character. Though, John, she has a point about the gardening. The roses are looking a bit neglected. I'll get to them! Eventually. There’s this new cloud storage thing I’ve been wrestling with at work. Trying to migrate everything from Dropbox to Flickr, it’s a disaster. You wouldn't believe the permissions issues.

Honestly, I think I’ve developed a problem. A  serious  problem. Let me guess. It involves floral patterns, delicate handles, and a disproportionate amount of time spent refreshing eBay? You know me too well. It’s the Shelley cups, David. They’re just… calling to me. I saw one this afternoon, a Dainty Blue, and it was  almost  mine. Almost. Someone snipped me at the last second. Right. The perils of online vintage auctions. Is it actually worth getting this upset over a…cup? It’s not  just  a cup! It’s history, it’s artistry! And it’s a beautiful, beautiful thing. Plus, I’m building a collection. A very discerning collection, I might add. I’m thinking of dedicating the whole display cabinet. The one we use for the good china that only sees the light of day at Christmas? You’re replacing the Royal Albert with Shelley? Brave move. Well, perhaps not  replacing . More… augmenting. Expanding the aesthetic. Anyway, it’s a distraction, isn’t it? From, you know… everything. From the impending doom of my leaving do? Or the general chaos of life? Both, mostly. Speaking of your leaving do, are you sure about The Black Swan? It's lovely, but rather…formal. That’s what Brenda insisted on. Apparently, my admin team considers it ‘fitting’ to send me off with a three-course meal and a slightly forced speech from old Mr. Henderson. Sounds…pleasant. Though, knowing Henderson, it'll be less a speech and more a rambling anecdote about the time the photocopier broke down in '98. Exactly my fear. I suggested the pub, a few pints and some chips, but apparently, 'that wouldn’t be respectful'. Honestly, sometimes… Bureaucracy. It’ll be the death of us all. Still, we’ll be there. And we'll make the best of it. I'll stage an intervention if Henderson gets too carried away with the photocopier. You’re a lifesaver. I'm genuinely dreading it. I’ve been there fifteen years. It’s…strange to think it’s ending. I know, love. It is. But exciting too, surely? All that free time for pottery classes, or finally finishing that book you started… or expanding  my  cup collection, perhaps? Don’t push your luck. Speaking of exciting things, did you hear about the community market starting up on Saturday in the village hall? Old Mrs. Higgins is running a stall selling her jams.

…And then she just  assumed  I’d understand all this tax stuff. Like, I’m studying English Lit, not accountancy, love. It’s just…a different world. Welcome to the glamorous life of self-employment, lass. Honestly, it’s more paperwork than actual work sometimes. You’re doing brilliantly with your degree though, Chloe. Don’t let a bit of tax stress you out. It’ll all make sense eventually…or you’ll hire someone who makes it make sense. Which is what I do. Sounds rough, Chloe. My old man used to say taxmen are like vampires – they only come out when you've got something worth taking. Now, now, Ben! Don't be filling the young 'un's head with notions. They're not  that  bad. Though, I’ll admit, HMRC does have a knack for finding things. Especially if… well, if you're not entirely straightforward with them. Not straightforward? What do you mean, Mr. Davies? He just means, Chloe, that it’s really important to keep impeccable records. Like,  everything . Receipts, invoices, bank statements…everything. Especially now with online banking, it’s so easy to fall behind. That’s putting it mildly, Sarah. I know a guy…lost a rather substantial fine because he ‘forgot’ to declare some income. Said it was a genuine mistake. HMRC wasn’t buying it. Aye, fines are nasty. Remember old man Henderson down the pub? Got caught fiddling his VAT. Nearly lost the place. Fiddling his VAT? Sounds… dodgy. It was. He was trying to claim expenses that weren’t really expenses. It’s a slippery slope, that is. You start playing with the system, it quickly escalates. It can even get into…other areas. I had a client a few years back, a builder, who was running cash through his business. Didn’t look good. Very quickly, things moved from ‘questionable accounting’ to ‘potential money laundering’. Money laundering?! Seriously? Here in France? It happens everywhere, Chloe. Especially with cash-based businesses. Easy to hide things. Though, honestly, the banks are getting pretty good at flagging suspicious activity. You deposit a large sum of unexplained cash, they’re going to ask questions. My cousin works at a bank. He says they have whole teams dedicated to just looking for that sort of thing. Good. They should. It’s a rotten business, and it funds worse things. Still… it’s tempting for some.

Honestly, this weather is just  exhausting , isn’t it? One minute it's bright sunshine, the next it's threatening to pour. You can’t even plan a sensible walk without packing for all four seasons. Tell me about it. I was out canvassing for the hospice this morning, trying to get people to sign up for the sponsored walk, and got absolutely soaked. Had to abandon ship and find a little cafe. People weren't exactly queuing up to pledge sponsorship while raindrops were bouncing off their noses, I can tell you. Oh, no! That’s awful, Dad. You must be freezing. Did you manage to salvage anything from the morning, at least? A few promises, thankfully. Mostly from people who felt sorry for me looking like a drowned rat, I suspect. But every little helps, doesn't it? How’s the teaching going, love? Any horrors to report from the front lines of Year Three? It’s… eventful. We had a glitter incident this week. Everywhere. And little Leo tried to convince everyone that he was a dinosaur. Sweet, but disruptive. They're starting to grasp the concept of phonics, which is a win. It's just keeping up with the marking, honestly. It sounds hectic! My shop was surprisingly quiet today, which was a nice change. Though ‘quiet’ usually means I end up re-organising the entire stockroom. It’s never-ending. I’m thinking of asking for a pay rise, actually. I’ve been there nearly two years now, and I practically run the place. You absolutely should, darling. Don’t undervalue yourself. You’re brilliant at what you do, and you’re always so dedicated. When's your birthday again? We need to start planning something. It’s the 18th of next month. I was thinking… nothing too big? Maybe just a meal out with you all? A meal out sounds lovely. We could go to that Italian place in Tamworth. You always liked it there, didn’t you, Sarah? Oh, yes, that’s a good shout. I remember when we took the kids there after your school play, Emily. You were such a little star. Mum, please don’t bring up my tragically awful attempt at playing the Little Mermaid. I was mortified for years! Nonsense, you were adorable! Anyway, have you both booked onto a new sign language class? I was looking at one that starts next week at the community centre.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is just  immense . We’re looking at dialectal shifts across three generations, all based on transcribed interviews. It’s fascinating, but my head feels like it's going to explode sometimes. Oh, God, I know that feeling. Luckily, my current workload is mostly proofreading, which is… less existential. Though even spotting the tenth instance of ‘affect’ versus ‘effect’ in one manuscript can feel a bit soul-crushing. How’s the Cambridge project going overall, then? You never really said much about  what  you’re researching. It's focused on the evolution of Estuary English, actually. Not the classic sort, but the way it’s branching out – traveling further inland, merging with other regional variations. We're particularly interested in how social media is accelerating those changes. It’s a bit meta, really, using digital data to track the impact of, well, digital data. That's brilliant! It’s funny, isn’t it? We’re constantly talking about 'proper' English, but language is just constantly  moving . I'm wading through a manuscript at the moment - historical fiction - and the author is trying so hard to mimic 18th-century prose, it's...stilted, to say the least. Authenticity is so hard to achieve. Sometimes it’s better to just  suggest  the period. Totally. I was reading a piece the other day about language policing and how much of it is linked to class anxiety. Like, people getting upset about split infinitives as a way of asserting their ‘educated’ status. It felt a bit… sad, honestly. Oh, absolutely. My nan is  obsessed  with correcting people’s grammar. It’s less about language itself and more about… well, asserting a certain order, I think. She genuinely believes misplaced apostrophes are a sign of societal decay. That’s brilliant! It's the same with pronunciation. My mum gets very twitchy about ‘h-dropping’ even though I grew up surrounded by it in Aylesbury. It’s ingrained, isn't it? That feeling that  your  way of speaking is the ‘correct’ one. It's interesting coming from Malaysia, actually. I grew up speaking English, but it was very different from what I encountered here, even though it’s supposed to be the same language. ‘Manglish’ as we call it, is… a glorious mess of influences. People here sometimes look at me funny when I use certain phrases. Oh, I get that. I think growing up with Swedish and Spanish in the mix definitely made me more aware of how fluid language can be.
