Right, so I’ve been lookin’ at these visa requirements again for Mongolia. Proper headache, this is. They want a  letter of invitation  from someone  in  Mongolia. Like, who d'ya just…  find  someone in Mongolia, eh? It’s not like there’s a Mongolian Penpal directory. Tell me about it! I was reading the same thing. It’s completely bonkers. I was thinking maybe we could try and contact one of those tour companies over there? See if they'd be willing to write one for us, knowing it’s for a charity thing? Might cost a few quid, but it’s gotta be easier than cold-calling random Mongolian businesses. Not a bad shout, actually. A tour company… yeah, that’s worth a look. I'll have a rummage online tonight. You been any luck with the donations front? We’re still a fair way off the £5000 target, aren't we? Slowly but surely. I put a post on Facebook, got a few bits and bobs. Mum’s been badgering her bridge club, apparently. Says Marjorie’s husband used to be a mechanic and is “very supportive of young lads doing daft things for good causes”. Bless ‘em. But we need to start thinkin’ bigger, lad. Aye, we do. I was thinkin’ we could stick an ad on Gumtree, maybe? “Two lads, Mongolia Rally, help us raise money for [Charity Name]!” Bit desperate, I know, but it's worth a try. Free advertising, innit? Gumtree’s a good shout! And we could put up flyers around campus. The Students’ Union might let us do a stall during lunchtime, maybe with the car there? That’d get people talking. The car… speaking of which, we need to get those passport photos sorted. I swear, every time I try and take a decent photo of myself, I look like I've just been mugged. I know the feeling! I look permanently stressed. I was going to go to that photo booth down by the market. It’s a tenner for six, isn’t it? Properly rips you off, but it's quick and easy. Saves us messin’ about with tryin’ to get the lighting right and my mam shoutin’ instructions. A tenner? Robbery! I’ve got that new printer, remember? The one I got for uni? It can do photos. We could try and do ‘em ourselves. It'll take ages to adjust the settings and probably look awful, but it’ll save us a fiver each.

Right, so you  actually  went to the A&E last night? Honestly, Liv, you’re a menace. A beautiful, chaotic menace, but still. I  told  you, it was properly bad! I thought it was broken. Properly. And they kept me there for ages. Honestly, the waiting room was full of… well, everything. Old men with coughs, lads who’d clearly had a bit too much, a woman who was convinced she’d swallowed a button battery… It was a vibe. A vibe? Sounds… stressful. You okay now, Liv? They x-rayed it, didn’t they? Just a bad sprain, right? Yeah, yeah, just a sprain. They said I’ve done a bit of damage to the ligaments, but no break. They just strapped me up like a mummy and told me to take paracetamol. Honestly, the most helpful part was the vending machine. I needed chocolate. Desperately. See? This is what happens when you try to recreate parkour moves in the Sugarhouse. I told you it was a bad idea to climb on the booth! It  looked  easier than it was. And Leo was egging me on! Honestly, boys are the worst influence. Speaking of boys… you seen Ben today? He promised to help me with that essay on post-structuralism. I'm drowning in Derrida, honestly. No, haven’t seen him. Probably glued to a computer screen somewhere dissecting code. He’s such a tech head. Though, I did hear him on the phone yesterday sounding… flustered. Something about needing to ‘explain things’ to someone? Ooh, drama. Maybe he’s finally realised Chloe’s a bit of a handful. She's always going on about 'manifesting' and crystal healing. It's exhausting just  listening  to her. Honestly, I just want a normal conversation sometimes. Like, about… I don't know, the weather? Or whether the library queue is going to be insane tomorrow. Tell me about it. Uni life is wild. The other day someone was trying to sell me air purifying plants in the lecture hall. Air purifying plants, during a philosophy lecture! Right, I need more tea. And maybe something to actually  eat . That vending machine chocolate barely counts. Anyone want anything? A biscuit would be lovely, actually. Thanks, Liv. It’s just…everything feels a bit much at the moment. The essay, trying to figure out which seminars to actually attend... You’re not the only one, love.

…and then your Auntie Brenda, bless her heart, decided the buffet needed  more  pickled onions. More! Like there weren’t enough already threatening to overpower everything else. Honestly, you’d think she’d run a pickled onion farm in her youth, the way she goes on. Haha, yeah. Gran was giving her side-eye the whole time. Gran knows a good buffet doesn’t  need  that much vinegar. Your Gran’s a woman of refined tastes, that's true. She was saying afterwards, quite pointedly, that the smoked salmon was a much better addition. Though, between you and me, I think she just wanted an excuse to boast about sourcing it from that fancy deli in Helmsley. She  always  does that. “Oh, this salmon? Well, you simply  can’t  get anything like it anywhere else.” It's a running joke. Did Uncle David actually manage not to spill red wine on anything this year? That’s the real milestone. Surprisingly, no! He was on strict instructions from your mother, and I think the fear of her wrath kept him relatively steady. Though, I did see him eyeing your cousin Emily’s cream dress with a rather… calculating look. I intervened just in time, mind you. Classic Uncle David. Emily would’ve been  fuming . So, was the party a success then, overall? Apart from the pickled onion situation? Oh, absolutely. It was lovely. Seeing everyone together, celebrating forty years…it goes so quickly, doesn't it? Your father did a brilliant job with the slideshow, too. All those old photos…you were such a little rascal! Remember that phase with the dinosaur obsession? Don't remind me. I made everyone roar at me for, like, a whole year. And I insisted on wearing that inflatable T-Rex costume everywhere. Even to your wedding, apparently. Mum keeps bringing it up. It's endearing. And your dad has the photos to prove it. It was lovely to see your Great-Aunt Margaret too; she doesn’t get out much these days. She was asking all about your A-Levels. Ugh, don’t get me started. She kept asking if I’d applied to Oxford. Like, no pressure or anything. She already thinks I’m going to be a doctor. She just wants the best for you, love. She’s from a generation where university was... different. It was expected, and certain universities were  the  places to be.

Honestly, Dad, this water bottle is  useless . It leaks every time I tilt it, and honestly, it tastes like plastic now. I swear, I’m going to just buy a proper one when we get to Cornwall. Maybe from Holland & Barrett, they always have good ones. Holland & Barrett for a water bottle, eh? Bit fancy, isn’t it? Your mother would have a field day. She still thinks they sell potions in there. Anyway, that bottle was perfectly good last week. You probably just didn't tighten the lid properly. You're forever losing pens too, mind. I bet you've got about ten rolling around in your bag, all uncapped. No, I haven’t! And it's not just the lid, it's… the  plastic . It lets the taste seep in. Speaking of which, are we stopping soon for lunch? I’m starving. I had that tiny breakfast, remember? All because I was trying to be quick. Aye, we'll stop near Exeter, should be around half one. There's a decent services there, proper sandwiches. Not like those motorway ones that taste of nothing. Though, I’m starting to think maybe I should’ve packed a picnic. Your mum was worried about my stomach, said this long journey might flare things up again. Your IBS? Oh, right. Are you okay? You haven't mentioned it much lately. Keeping on top of it, mostly. Trying to avoid too much stress, which is hard with the house move still hanging over us. Honestly, I’m glad we’re getting away. All that packing and sorting… it’s exhausting. Though, unpacking will be worse. I swear, half our possessions will end up in a charity shop just to avoid the effort. You said you’d put my furniture exactly how I wanted it in the new room. You  promised . I did, I did. And I will. Though, don't expect me to assemble it all myself. Your brother's coming down next week, he can do the heavy lifting. It’s a silly thing, moving house after all these years. Never thought we'd leave Bolton. It's just...everything felt a bit  stuck . Stuck like a chocolate biscuit in a mug of tea? That’s what Gran used to say when she was unhappy. Aye, something like that. Your Gran was a character. Remember that time she tried to convince us that Bramhall Hall was haunted by a medieval knight?

Honestly, this is lovely. Just… lovely. A proper sit down. It feels like weeks since we’ve all managed this. Weeks is an understatement, Carol. Life just  happens , doesn’t it? One minute you’re planning a relax, the next you’re firefighting at work, then the boiler decides to pack in… the usual. Oh, don’t I know it, David. Though my firefighting these days consists mostly of convincing the garden gnome thief that it’s really not worth the effort. Honestly, the cheek of it! A gnome thief? Is that a new low, even for…well, for everything these days? I had a chap trying to flog me ‘slightly used’ scaffolding poles last week. Slightly used as in, half-rusted through. Goodness me, Gareth! You’re always having adventures. You’d think being self-employed would give you more peace, but it sounds like it just invites a different kind of chaos. Chaos is my middle name, love. Keeps things interesting. Though sometimes I do yearn for a nice, predictable nine-to-five. Just for a week. A week of not chasing invoices and arguing about timber prices. You wouldn’t last a week, Gareth. You'd be scaling the office building within the first hour, probably trying to build a birdhouse on the roof. Don't put it past me. I've got itchy feet, I do. Speaking of feet, are we having another go at that jigsaw puzzle later? The one with the ridiculous number of green fields? Only if you promise not to ‘improve’ it by rearranging pieces to make ‘a more aesthetically pleasing landscape,’ as you put it last time. It took me an hour to sort it out! That was… a moment. It’s lovely seeing you all relaxed, though. It reminds me of when the kids were little, all of us crammed round the table, arguing about Monopoly. Ah, Monopoly… the game that ruins friendships and families. I still maintain I was robbed blind by young Emily that one Christmas. She's a ruthless negotiator, that one. She gets it from her mother, David. Don’t pretend you’re innocent in all this. You were always willing to bankrupt a sibling for Park Lane. That's not true! I was merely… strategically focused. Though Emily  did  have a knack for landing on my properties at the worst possible moment. How is she, by the way?

Right, operation Mother's Day is a go! Though honestly, your Grandma deserves a month of celebrations, not just one day. Can we  make  Grandma a cake? A really, really sparkly one? With sprinkles! And I’ll decorate it! With… uh… dinosaurs! Grandma loves dinosaurs, right? She does appreciate a good dinosaur, yes. A sparkly cake sounds lovely, Rosie. And Leo, maybe we can save the dinosaur decorating for  after  the cake is iced, alright? Don't want a prehistoric sticky situation. What's ‘prehistoric’? Oh, it means… very, very old. Like, dinosaur old. Before people even existed, almost. Woah. So like, Grandma was a baby when dinosaurs were still around? No, darling, definitely not! That's a bit of a silly thought, isn’t it? It's just an expression. You know, like when I say 'it’s raining cats and dogs’? It doesn’t  actually  mean cats and dogs are falling from the sky. But… that would be cool. Imagine a fluffy cat landing on your head! It wouldn't be very cool for the cat, I suspect. It's just an idiom. A funny way of saying it’s raining very hard. What’s an ‘idiom’? Is it like a secret code? That’s a good way to think about it! It's a phrase where the words don't mean exactly what they say. Like, if I told someone to “break a leg” before a play, I wouldn’t actually want them to hurt themselves! It means ‘good luck’. Break a leg…good luck… hmm. That's confusing. They can be! We'll work on them. Right, back to Mother’s Day. I was thinking, after the cake, maybe we can all go for a little walk in the woods? It's supposed to be quite nice tomorrow. Forest School! Can we go to Forest School? Can we build a den? Not  Forest School  exactly, love. Just a walk. But we can definitely try and find a good spot to gather branches and build a little den. If we're allowed to, of course. We don't want to disrupt anything. Oh! And can we collect leaves? Grandma loves pretty leaves. Especially the red and orange ones. She puts them in a scrapbook. That’s a lovely idea, Rosie. We can absolutely collect some leaves. Just remember to leave plenty for the trees, okay? They need them to stay warm in the winter.

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Just knowing she  knew  something wasn’t right for months, but put it down to just ‘getting old’. Mum always was stubborn. Wouldn’t bother the doctor for anything less than a broken limb. It is awful. That’s exactly what Dad did with his heart. Kept saying it was indigestion. By the time they found anything, it was… well, you know. It’s like they feel a burden, asking for help. As if admitting weakness is a crime. Exactly! And it’s not like she didn’t have symptoms. She kept saying she was just tired, but she was  always  tired. More tired than usual, even for Mum. And then the weight loss… I kept saying to Richard, “Something’s not right, Richard, look at her.” He just said she was being sensible, watching her figure. Men! Oh, don’t even get me started. They’re brilliant at fixing things, apparently, but completely oblivious to… everything else. Still, it’s easy to say that now, isn't it? Hard when you're in the thick of it. Were they able to pinpoint what stage it was when they finally diagnosed it? Stage three pancreatic cancer. Stage three. Can you believe it? She’d lost so much weight by then. And the pain… she tried to hide it, bless her, but I could see it in her eyes. It's terrifying how quickly it’s all happened. Just six weeks from diagnosis to… well, you know. Six weeks. Oh, Sarah. That’s… brutal. Pancreatic cancer is so vicious. My Auntie Maureen had that, years ago. It was a terrible, quick decline. It shreds you, doesn’t it? Watching someone you love just… fade. It does. It really does. And then there's Ben. He’s taking it… well, he's trying to be strong, for the kids mostly. But I saw him yesterday, and he just looked utterly lost. He's always been so grounded, so pragmatic. Seeing him like that… it broke my heart. Ben’s a good lad. He always was. I remember him and Tom getting into mischief at primary school. Absolute terrors, the pair of them. Though Tom was always the instigator if I recall. How are the kids coping? Little Emily is so sensitive. Emily's… fragile. She's being incredibly brave, but she's withdrawn. Not saying much.

Right, brain officially fried. That deconstruction of Chomsky's Universal Grammar was…intense. Honestly, sometimes I think  I  need a linguistics class just to understand the stuff I'm teaching. You say that every time, Liam. And then you go and flawlessly explain it to a room full of baffled undergraduates. Though, to be fair, it IS a lot. Did Old Man Hemmings drone on for the full hour again? Worse. He got sidetracked on the history of Proto-Indo-European for…at least twenty minutes. Twenty! They were glazing over. I swear Amelia nearly fell asleep into her notes. It's a good job I can fill in some of the gaps. It’s just… frustrating when the timetable's so packed, there’s no real room for proper discussion. Tell me about it. My Medieval Lit seminar felt like a speed-run through Chaucer. They just want to tick boxes, don’t they? Speaking of timetables, have you sorted out when you're teaching that intensive Korean class next semester? Not yet. They want me to do mornings, which is… problematic. All my research time is mornings. And I  need  to make progress on the phonological study. It's hanging over me, honestly. Trying to convince the department that ‘interesting’ is a valid reason to continue research is proving difficult. Oh, the joys of academia. It's always 'publish or perish', isn't it? Have you at least thought about the content for the Korean class? You were saying last week you wanted to focus more on real-world conversational stuff rather than just grammar. Exactly! Everyone just wants to learn how to say ‘Hello, my name is…’ and order bibimbap. I want them to be able to navigate a K-Pop concert or understand a political debate! It's about cultural nuance as much as the language itself. Apparently, the gendered language is… complicated. I need to brush up on the politeness levels. The whole ‘age hierarchy’ thing is fascinating but daunting to explain. From what I've read, it’s  really  complicated. Everything is about respect and seniority. Apparently, men and women use completely different speech styles depending on who they’re talking to. It sounds exhausting. It is! It’s a social minefield. But that's what makes it so interesting. Anyway, enough linguistics doom and gloom. This smells amazing. What culinary masterpiece are you conjuring up?

Right, okay, serious question. Does anyone else think this pizza tastes…sad? Like it  knows  it was a Tuesday night deal? Nah, it's pizza. It's never sad. You’re just projecting your module assessment stress onto a perfectly innocent pepperoni. You were moaning about that bloody Lagrangian mechanics all morning. I’m with Liv. It’s fine. Bit greasy, maybe. Anyone want another slice before I claim the last two? I actually need the carbs. Been attempting to decipher Dr. Davies' lecture notes on quantum…it's a disaster. I’ll pass, cheers. I’m still full from that weird protein bar I had before. Tasted like chalk and regret. Anyway, speaking of disasters, has anyone seen the state of the garden after the floods last week? Honestly, looked like a swimming pool out there. Oh god, don’t remind me. I was genuinely worried the Sugarhouse was going to be underwater. Imagine the chaos! Though, admittedly, a waterlogged dance floor might add a certain…vibe. You and your Sugarhouse obsession. It’s just sticky floors and questionable music. Though, I will admit, last time was surprisingly decent. Did you see Ben trying to do that complicated dance move? Nearly took out old Mrs. Higgins. Oh my god, yes! He looked like a malfunctioning robot. Did anyone actually manage to get a decent photo? I was too busy trying not to spill my drink. I got a blurry video. It's gold. Speaking of embarrassing moments, remember that time in primary school when… oh, actually, no. Never mind. Too mortifying. Ooh, spill! We  live  for mortifying stories in this house. Come on! Yeah, we’ve all got skeletons in the closet. Mine involves a questionable perm and a very unfortunate sportswear top. It was one of those shiny football kits. Foot joy, I think. Oh, those were the worst! I had one with, like, sparkly panels. I thought it was amazing at the time. Right? It was all about the brands. Anyway, I was thinking, we should definitely go camping again this summer. Not like that disaster in the Lake District where it rained for three days straight. Somewhere…African? Africa?! That's…ambitious. But amazing. Imagine the photos! Though I'd need to get all my vaccinations, and then there’s the whole malaria thing… It'd be brilliant! Do you remember Sarah talking about volunteering in Kenya? Maybe we could look into something like that.

Right, that was a proper brew, wasn’t it? Best petrol station coffee this side of the A19. Seriously. You and your petrol station coffee. You'd think, with a Corpus Administrator, you’d only drink ethically sourced, single-origin, hand-ground… the works. Aye, well, ethics don't fill a hole when you've been staring at linguistic data for eight hours. It's a quick fix, and it does the job. Besides, it reminds me of home. Mam used to get a coffee from that Esso on the A1018 every Saturday. Ah, nostalgia hitting hard? You haven't mentioned Sunderland in a while. Usually it’s every other sentence, involving something being ‘canny’ or someone being ‘proper mint.’ Don’t take the mickey. I just... it's different down here, isn’t it? Everything feels… polished. Like everyone’s pretending. Back home, you just  are . No one cares if your hair’s a mess or you've still got pyjama bottoms on if you pop to the shops. Fair enough. Harpenden is… let’s say, ‘aspirational’ in its tidiness. Though I'm fairly sure half the village is secretly running on caffeine and dry shampoo just like the rest of us. So, this fieldwork… are you actually enjoying tramping around all those villages, meticulously documenting how people say 'bath'? It’s… interesting. Honestly, the variations are  fascinating . I thought it would be pretty straightforward, North versus South, you know? But it’s not. Even within Hertfordshire, there’s such a range. Old man Higgins in Little Puddleton – pronounced ‘Puddl’n’, naturally – he says ‘barth’ like he’s gargling gravel. 'Barth'? That sounds… intense. And you're recording all this? Of course! It’s gold dust. Properly gold dust. We're building a huge corpus, documenting regional pronunciations. It's… it’s surprisingly political, actually. People get  very  invested in how their accent is perceived. I can imagine. Especially when people try to standardize things. My nan was forever correcting my pronunciation. Said I sounded like I was putting on airs. Honestly, I probably was, trying to sound less… Hertfordshire. See! It's everywhere. It’s not just a ‘Northern thing’ being looked down on. It’s about social capital, isn’t it? The way you speak marks you out. And then  we , as linguists, go around picking it apart. Feels a bit weird sometimes. It’s observation, not dissection. And it’s important work, really.

Ooh, that’s a good brew, love. Though it don’t half do nowt for this shoulder, does it? Feels like someone’s been takin’ a hammer to it all mornin’. There, there, Arthur. You did too much in the garden yesterday, I told you. Digging up them potatoes weren’t worth it. Especially with the weather turnin’ like it has. It  did  come down properly, didn't it? I got absolutely soaked walking from the car to the lecture hall this morning. Thought my shoes would be squelching all day. Thankfully, they dried out a bit. Yeah, saw a few people running for cover. Classic British summer, really. One minute sunshine, the next it’s biblical. Did well to get a dry afternoon for the football yesterday though. Football, eh? Norwich got trounced again, didn’t they? Saw the highlights. Dreadful stuff. Honestly, you'd think they’d learn. Still, keeps the young 'uns entertained, I suppose. They did, poor dears. Little Leo was absolutely gutted. Said they need a new goalkeeper, and a whole new defence! He’s got a proper head for the game, that boy. He gets that from you, Mum. You were always the tactical one when watching with Grandad. Dad just shouted at the telly. Your grandad was a passionate man. More passionate about Norwich than anything, I reckon. Speaking of shouting at the telly… Arthur, are you sure you shouldn’t see a doctor about that shoulder? You’ve been moaning about it for weeks. Doctor? Waste o’ time, if you ask me. They’ll just poke and prod and tell me it’s 'wear and tear'. What do you expect at my age? It's just…age. And they try and push pills on you. I don't hold with all that. It’s worth getting it checked, Arthur. Just to rule anything serious out. They might be able to suggest some physio or something. Physio? Sounds expensive. And uncomfortable! I remember old Mr. Peterson down the road had physio for his hip. Said it was worse than the original problem! Things have moved on a bit since Mr. Peterson, Grandad. They have much more targeted treatments now. I know someone who had really good results with acupuncture, even. Acupuncture? Goodness me. Sounds a bit…prickly. I think a hot compress is more your speed, Arthur. Have you tried a hot compress? Tried everything, Ethel.

…and honestly, the seating plan is giving me actual heart palpitations. Aunt Carol  insists  on being near the buffet, and Uncle Barry will actively cause a scene if he’s not within shouting distance of the bar. It’s like herding cats, I swear. Oh god, wedding seating. The bane of every bride’s existence. Seriously. You think you've got it sorted, then someone mentions a decades-old grudge and suddenly everything's chaos. Did you ask your mum for help? She’s a seating plan wizard. Yeah, your mum's amazing at that sort of thing. Mine… well, she just suggested putting all the ‘fun’ people together. Which, knowing my family, translates to a potential brawl by the cake table. Oh dear. Fun is definitely a subjective term in family dynamics. How many are you expecting in total, anyway, Liv? Around eighty, I think. Which feels HUGE. And half of them I haven’t seen in years! It’s a lovely feeling, but also…intimidating. I feel like I need to prepare little ‘remind me who this is’ notes. Eighty is a good number! It’s a proper party. Don’t stress too much about remembering everyone. People are just happy to be there, mostly. Though, you  should  have a little cheat sheet for the dodgy uncles. So, how’s planning going otherwise? All still on schedule? You’re not getting cold feet, are you? No! No cold feet. Just… overwhelmed. Everything’s mostly booked, dress is fitted, caterers are confirmed… it’s the little details that are eating me. And Ben keeps changing his mind about the first dance song! Honestly, it’s gone from Ed Sheeran to something by The Smiths to… I don’t even know what it is now. Men! Seriously. They’re so fickle. Remember when Liam tried to convince everyone he was a DJ for a week? Oh god, don't remind me. The ‘DJ Liam’ phase. The absolute  horror  of that playlist. It was mostly just really loud drum and bass. He thought he was the next Carl Cox, didn't he? Bless him. Speaking of boys… how’s Tom? Still talking about moving to Bristol? Ugh,  still . He's obsessed. Says it’s for ‘career prospects’, but I'm pretty sure he just wants to be near that vegan bakery he saw on Instagram. Honestly, it’s getting ridiculous. I'm trying to be supportive, but it feels like he’s already mentally moved out.

…Honestly, this new telly, eh? All these smart bits and bobs. I asked young Tim to set it up for me, and he just… waved his hands and spoke in a language I din’t understand. Said somethin’ about ‘streaming’ and ‘apps’. Sounds like a plague to me. Oh, Arthur, you and technology! It’s always the same with you. Remember when you refused to use a mobile phone? Said it’d be the end of civilized conversation. Well, wasn’t I right, to a degree? Nobody  talks  anymore, they just…thumb things. Still, a proper chat over a cuppa like this is better than any of that nonsense. Though, I do miss hearin' from young Elsie. She only sends them picture messages now, little smilies and all. Don't feel the same as a proper letter. Afternoon, you two! Sorry I’m a bit late, Year 11 were…spirited today. Biscuits, anyone? They’re ginger nuts – Mrs. Patel brought them in, absolute lifesaver. Oh, lovely, thank you, David. Just what I needed. And yes, Elsie's a texting fiend now, isn’t she? Though she did send me a rather nice photo of the new foal yesterday. A foal, you say? At Old Man Hemmings’ place? That’s the one. A beautiful little chestnut thing. Apparently, she's named it Buttercup. Elsie’s proper smitten. She spent the whole weekend mucking out stables. Buttercup, eh? Good name. Reminds me of Bess, my sister’s mare. She loved that horse more than anything. Old Bess was a proper character, she was. Once kicked down the garden gate when the vicar came visiting. Scared him half to death! That's a good story! Elsie’s always had a way with animals. It's lovely she’s got that outlet, being out with the horses. Keeps her busy, anyway. Speaking of busy, how are you keeping, Arthur? Still working on those jigsaws? Slow goin’, slow goin’. Got one of them landscapes, thousands of little pieces. Drives me mad, it does. You think you’ve got a bit sorted, then realise you've got three sky pieces where a tree should be. You need a bit of distraction, Arthur. Perhaps a game of Scrabble? We haven’t played in ages. Scrabble! You always win, Margaret. You and your fancy words. I just happen to have a good vocabulary, Arthur. It's years of reading! Besides, it's just a bit of fun.

…and honestly, young Thomas was convinced ‘literally’  always  meant 'figuratively' last week. It took a good fifteen minutes to untangle that one. Teenagers, honestly. They pick things up from…well, everywhere, don’t they? Ah, teenagers. A law unto themselves, always have been. My granddaughter, Chloe, she was the same. Full of these… Americanisms, she called them. "Awesome" for everything. Drove her Nan mad, it did. Though, to be fair, your job  is  to correct them, isn’t it? You’re a language teacher. Must be exhausting keeping up with all the slang. It is! It’s constantly evolving, which is the fascinating part, I suppose. But keeping track of what's 'in' and what’s just…wrong is a full-time job on top of the actual teaching. It’s not just slang, either, it’s the grammar eroding, the nuance getting lost. Though, I will admit, some of it's rather creative. Creative, you say? Sounds like a polite word for muddled to me! Back in my day, you knew where you stood with the Queen’s English. Proper sentences, proper punctuation. None of this… abbreviated nonsense. Though, I suppose language changes. Always does. My father, he used to complain about the younger generation shortening words even  then . It's true. It's a natural process. I try to explain that to the students. It’s not about being ‘right’ or ‘wrong’, it’s about appropriate context. Using slang in an essay isn’t going to win you any marks, but with friends, it’s perfectly fine. It’s about code-switching, really. Code-switching? Fancy name for talking different to different people, isn't it? We just called it common sense. Although, I wouldn’t have dared use slang with my boss, that’s for sure! Speaking of work…retirement suits me, you know. Absolutely suits me. No more board meetings, no more spreadsheets. Just…peace and quiet. And the garden, of course. I can imagine. It must be lovely to have that freedom. I do enjoy my job, mostly. It’s rewarding when you see a student finally ‘get’ something, but the marking… oh, the marking! It’s a never-ending pile. What have you been up to in the garden then? Anything exciting blossoming? Roses, mostly. Got a new variety this year, a deep crimson one. Nearly black, it is. Takes a lot of attention, roses do, but worth it when they’re in full bloom.

Honestly, Valentine’s Day is just… a load of pressure, innit? Like, everyone’s posting these perfectly curated couple things online and you just feel rubbish if you’re not doing anything ‘grand’. Tell me about it! My timeline was  flooded  with roses and fancy dinners. I spent mine watching documentary about sloths with my nan. Much more my vibe, to be fair. Did you…do anything? Don’t tell me you went full-on romantic. Nah, thank god, no. My brother and his girlfriend went to that new Italian place in Shoreditch - the one everyone's raving about. Apparently the queue was round the block. I stayed in and ordered a takeaway. Proper comfort food. Pad Thai, loads of it. Ooh, good shout. Pad Thai  is  a mood. Better than overpriced pasta any day. Though, I did see pictures of the tiramisu at that place… tempting. Still, better to avoid the crowds, yeah? Especially when you're just trying to chill. Exactly! It's all performative anyway, isn't it? Like, proving something to Instagram more than each other. Speaking of which, I tried to go to the cinema on Saturday. Absolute nightmare. Oh no, what happened? Attempted to see that new superhero film everyone's banging on about? Worse! Tried to see  Past Lives . Heard it was amazing. Sold out. Completely packed. Ended up wandering around Westfield for hours, avoiding all the Valentine’s displays. It was depressing. Seriously, heart-shaped everything. Even the crisps were heart-shaped! Heart-shaped crisps?! That  is  pushing it. Westfield on Valentine’s weekend…brave. It's always rammed full of people desperately searching for last-minute gifts. I went with my mum on Sunday to pick up a birthday present for my cousin, and honestly, it felt like navigating a warzone. It was like that! And the sheer  volume  of people trying on clothes… it was chaotic. I did manage to find some decent boots on sale though. Sixty quid! Can’t complain. That’s a steal! You're good at finding bargains. I have the worst luck. I saw this jacket I  loved … but by the time I’d decided if I wanted it, they'd sold out of my size. Actually, talking of luck… you wouldn't believe the week I've had with coursework. Oh no, what's going on? You seemed really stressed in the library yesterday. Everything alright?

Honestly, the spice level is  just  right. You went for the Laksa, yeah? Smells amazing. How is it? It’s good, really good. A bit coconutty, which is what I needed, I think. Needed something…comforting. God, this week has been a mess. And watching the news… honestly, it just gets heavier and heavier. Did you see that report on the new immigration bill? Vaguely. I was drowning in cladding regulations all day, so anything not directly relating to fire safety went a bit over my head. Though I saw something scrolling on Twitter about it. Something about…increased scrutiny? Increased scrutiny is a lovely way of putting it. It’s basically designed to make it impossible for people to claim asylum. And the rhetoric around it! Calling them ‘economic migrants’… as if just  existing  and seeking safety is a crime against the economy. It's infuriating. It  is . It always feels so… deliberately dehumanising. My nan used to talk about coming over from Ireland, the sheer prejudice she faced. You’d think we’d have learned something. But it feels like we’re just going backwards. And it’s not even about logic, is it? It’s about… scapegoating. Exactly! And the irony is, a lot of that rhetoric is subtly, or not so subtly, coded. It’s rarely  explicitly  racist, but… you know? It’s thinly veiled. My cousin, Aisha, was telling me how her flatmate had someone cross the street to avoid walking past her the other day. Broad daylight, in Ealing. Oh, that’s awful. Honestly. What is  wrong  with people? It’s exhausting being constantly aware of that stuff, isn’t it? It bleeds into everything, even work. Tell me about it. I was pitching a piece on the housing crisis to a new editor, and he basically told me it was ‘too politically charged.’ Said focusing on the social impact of landlords buying up everything was ‘taking sides.’ Like, what?! Whose side are you supposed to be on when people can’t afford to  live ? Ugh. The housing situation… don’t even get me started. I’m finally starting to look seriously, now that I've got a bit of a bonus at work, but it's completely bonkers. Everything’s either a shoebox for a ridiculous price, or needs a full renovation and you’re basically buying a project. Right? My friend, Liam, is openly talking about moving to Portugal.

Honestly, this is lovely. Just…peaceful. Five minutes of a proper lunch without someone launching mashed carrot at my head. It  is  nice. Though, judging by Leo’s current nap length, the peace won't last. He's usually up for another round of chaos within the hour. Don’t remind me. It’s the nursery thoughts that are occupying my brain now. I spoke to Mrs. Davies again this morning. And…? Still feeling anxious about it? You’ve been going over this for weeks, Mum. He’ll be  fine . Honestly, he's such a sociable little thing. He loves being around people. I  know  he is, darling. It’s just… letting someone else be his primary caregiver for those hours. It feels so strange. I mean, I’ve been with him every single second of his life, practically. And they’re starting the weaning properly there, you know? Proper finger food, and introducing more textures… I feel like I'm missing a milestone. They'll keep you fully updated, won’t they? And you’ve already done so well with the initial purees. Remember the face he made with the sweet potato? Like he’d been personally offended. Oh, God, yes. Pure outrage. But this is different. They’ll be doing things  their  way. I've printed out a little sheet with everything he likes and dislikes, his routine, the whole shebang. I feel like I’m sending my instructions for raising a small human along with him. You’re a good mum, you’ll be fine. And honestly, a few hours a day will do you the world of good. You’ve been running on fumes since he was born. Speaking of which, how’s the return to work shaping up? Have they confirmed your hours? They have. Three days a week, which is… manageable, I think. Though juggling everything is going to be a nightmare. I'm already dreading the school run chaos, plus nursery drop-offs and pick-ups. It’s a logistical puzzle. You’ll get into a rhythm. You always do. And Dad will help, won't he? He’ll try. He’s… enthusiastic, let's say. But he's not naturally gifted in the baby-wrangling department. He's much better at spreadsheets. True. Maybe he can spreadsheet the nursery routine for you? ‘Time Slot 1: Diaper Change – Probability of Messiness: 75%’. Don’t even start.

Honestly, this day has been…a lot. I still feel a bit shaky after that chat with the police. Still on about that, love? They just wanted a statement. Said it was standard procedure after what happened at the shop, didn’t they? No need to get yourself worked up. More gravy? It's not  just  a statement, Dave. It's reliving it, you know? Having to explain, again, about the shouting and the… the look on his face. It brings it all back. And they kept asking about details… things I hadn’t even consciously registered at the time. Was it the bloke who’s been hanging around the store a lot lately? The one who makes everyone feel a bit uneasy? Yeah, it was. Apparently, he’s been causing trouble at a few places in town. They’ve finally got a lead on him, thankfully. You did the right thing, Sarah, reporting it. I  hope  I did. I just keep second-guessing myself. Did I mention everything? Did I sound convincing? They made me sign something…felt awfully formal. You were perfectly convincing, dear. You’re a very articulate woman. They were just doing their job, and you did yours. Now, eat your dinner. You've barely touched it. You need your strength. Speaking of stressful things…has anyone looked at their EE bill this month? Mine’s ridiculous! Nearly seventy quid. I barely even use my data. Seriously? Mine’s gone up too. I thought it was just me. I’m on the same plan as you, Chloe. It’s daylight robbery. I’ve tried ringing them, but you’re stuck in a queue for an hour. I need to sort it, but I just haven’t had the energy. Being store manager is draining enough as it is. Trying to find staff who actually  want  to work is a nightmare. Tell me about it. Remember when finding a good PA was like finding gold dust? Now it feels like everyone just wants to be an ‘influencer’ or a ‘content creator’. Back in my day, people were grateful for a steady job. Though, to be fair, fund raising isn’t exactly known for its glamour. Honestly, Sarah, your worries about the police statement are far more important than a phone bill. Did they say when they might get back to you? Not specifically. They said they’d be in touch if they needed anything further.

…So, honestly, the wedding was  lovely . Proper lovely. Your Auntie Maureen nearly took out Uncle Geoff with a rogue bouquet toss, though. Nearly a disaster. Oh, Maureen. Always a hazard in a confined space. Glad it was good though, really good. It’s just… surreal seeing you all settled down, you know? Last time I properly saw you, we were both trying to avoid Mr. Henderson’s history lectures. Don't remind me. The man could make the Punic Wars sound like a shopping list. Speaking of history, though, I’ve been getting properly into Roman stuff again. Watched a documentary on Hadrian’s Wall last night. It’s just… incredible what they achieved, isn’t it? Romans, eh? Always figured they were a bit…showy. All that marble and conquering. I prefer something a bit grittier, like… Spartacus. Now  that  was a story. The show, I mean. Though probably not historically accurate. Oh, the show was…a bit much. All the slow motion and gratuitous violence. But it did get me thinking. So many of those figures – Spartacus, Crixus, Gannicus – died young, didn't they? Brutal, short lives. Makes you appreciate…well, making it past 30, I suppose. Tell me about it. Old Man Hemmings, down at the allotments, he was talking about his brother. Died young, he did. Had a bit of a reckless streak. Always chasing something. Reminded me a bit of…well, never mind. No, go on. Who did it remind you of? Just… a musician we both knew back in Luton. Jamie Carter. Proper guitar hero, everyone said. Died of a…a bad reaction, aged 24. A waste, really. He could've been massive. Awful. It’s a terrible thing, that feeling of potential unrealised. Right, enough depressing talk. This tea's good, though. What kind is it? Earl Grey. Thought that was your thing. I brought a bag of cardamom with me, if you fancy a bit in your next cuppa. It's pretty good. I’ve been experimenting with herbs and spices lately, trying to dry some for winter. Cardamom! Brilliant! You’re a wizard. I’ve been meaning to get a proper mortar and pestle. I’m still bashing stuff up with a rolling pin, which feels…uncivilised. Rolling pin, eh? Sounds like you. I got a good one from a market in Hitchin. Proper granite one. Makes all the difference. You can really get a good grind going.

…and then Mr. Harrison  actually  said my metaphor was “a bit of a stretch.” A  bit  of a stretch! I compared the protagonist’s internal struggle to a tangled ball of wool! It’s practically poetic, innit? Oh, Elsie, you and your metaphors. He probably just wanted to wind you up. He does that, doesn’t he? Especially with you, ‘cause you always come up with the… creative ones. It's not creative, it’s  insightful ! Honestly, English is just… frustrating sometimes. Like, what does he  want ? Straightforward descriptions? Where's the fun in that? Did you finish the practice test? I'm still panicking about Friday. I did, yeah. Managed to get through it. It wasn't  horrible . Mostly just questions about… symbolism, wasn't it? All that ‘what does the colour blue  represent ’ stuff? Ugh, don’t even! Mrs. Davies loves that. It’s always ‘the oppressive weight of societal expectations’ being blue, or ‘the suffocating sadness of lost love’. Honestly, it’s a colour! Sometimes it just  is  a colour! You’re terrible. But I think you'd do alright. You always write really well, even if your interpretations are...unique. I'm more worried about the unseen poetry. I always forget what all the poets even  said . Me too! I’m trying to memorise quotes, but my brain just keeps turning them into song lyrics. It's a disaster. At least Art is going well. I actually like that project on perspective. Oh, yeah? I'm struggling with mine. Keep messing up the vanishing points. Everything looks… wonky. Miss Peterson keeps telling me to use a ruler. Like I haven't  tried  that! She’s convinced we all suddenly forgot how to draw straight lines. She does have a habit of stating the obvious, doesn't she? But perspective is tricky. Maybe we could look at each other's work later? I could try to explain how I’m doing it, and you can tell me why mine looks like it's about to fall off the page. That would be brilliant, actually. Thank you. I'm definitely feeling a bit lost. French is also being a nightmare, though. Madame Dubois is on a mission to make us all miserable. Oh, don't even get me started on French! I can never remember the genders of the nouns. It’s either ‘le’ or ‘la’ and it feels like a complete lottery every time!

Aye, look at that drizzle. Proper Darlington weather, this is. Honestly, you'd think it was November, not… well, whatever day it is. Feels like ages since I’ve seen a proper sunny day. It’s Wednesday, Miss. And it's not  that  bad. It's just… wet. Mum says it’s good for the garden. Sorry I'm late, love. The bus was a nightmare. Packed with school kids, all shouting about… I don’t even know what. Something about Fortnite, I think. Honestly, the noise! No bother, love. Just glad you made it. I was just lamenting the weather with young Liam here. And he's glued to that phone, as usual. I wasn't  glued ! I was checking the football scores. Newcastle just drew. Again. Oh, dear. Still chasing that glory, are they? My Arthur used to be obsessed with football. Used to drag me to all the Hull games. Rain or shine. Though, I swear he mostly went for the pies. They’re good pies, mind you. Though nothing beats a proper steak pie from a Darlington bakery. Now  that’s  a culinary experience. Remember old man Hemmings? Best pies in the whole county. Oh, Hemmings! Now you’re talking. They did a mean sausage roll too. It's a shame his son didn’t keep it going. It all went a bit… chain bakery, didn’t it? All plastic packaging and tasteless fillings. Branding gone wrong, that is. Exactly! It lost its soul. It's the same with everything now, isn't it? Everything’s got to be… a ‘brand’. Remember when things just  were ? No fuss. No marketing. Just quality. Miss, you sound like Grandad. He's always going on about "the good old days." Well, there were a few good things about them! Though I’m not saying everything was perfect. Teaching back then was… different. Less paperwork, thankfully. But also, less support, less understanding of… well, everything, really. You’re right about the support. It was a lonely profession sometimes, back then. And the discipline! Goodness me. I remember young David Wilkinson – a terror, he was. Used to hide snails in my desk drawer! Snails?! Gross! He did! A right little rascal. But a bright lad, actually. Went on to university. Funny how things turn out. Speaking of which, how are your exams going, Liam? Are you stressing about them? They’re alright, I guess.

Honestly, Mum, you need to eat more of the chicken and less potato. You're barely touched it. Oh, I’m just not that hungry, love. Honestly. This roast is lovely, though, truly. Just… filling. And these sprouts are surprisingly good, considering. Filling? You could eat for England, Doris. Always have. Remember that time at Brighton? You polished off a whole bucket of doughnuts yourself. That was  one  bucket, Arthur, and we’d been walking for miles! And they were freshly made! It's different when you're active. Dad’s just teasing, Mum. He remembers everything. It's a gift. Though, it  is  true, you’ve always had a good appetite. It's genetic, surely? Grandma Betty could put away food like nobody’s business. It’s a complex thing, though, isn't it? Genetics definitely play a part, but lifestyle is huge. The obesity crisis is… well, it's frightening. So much processed food, so little activity. We’re practically engineered to gain weight now. Engineered? Rubbish. People just don’t walk anymore. Everyone’s glued to their phones, driving everywhere. When I was a lad, we walked miles to school, rain or shine. Built character, it did. And you didn’t get fat! Though, admittedly, driving is easier. Speaking of which, I finally got that new exhaust sorted on Mrs. Henderson’s Fiesta. Absolute nightmare getting the parts, though. Supply chain issues, they’re saying. That sounds awful, Dad. Must be frustrating when you can't get what you need to do a good job. It’s impacting everything, isn't it? Even research for my lectures. Trying to get hold of specific studies is becoming a real headache. It is. I had a student emailing me this morning, panicking about access to journals. Universities are cancelling subscriptions left and right. It’s… not ideal for academic progress. All this talk of progress… it doesn’t seem to make people happier, does it? More stressed, if anything. I was reading something the other day… about how religion used to provide a framework for people, a sense of community. Now… well, everyone’s off on their own little path. That's an interesting point, Mum. Though I think the 'framework' can be restrictive for some. My students are far more open to different ideologies, different ways of thinking. It's a good thing, I think, to question everything. It just feels very… isolating sometimes.

Honestly, this Moodle integration is driving me  round  the bend. I spent three hours last night trying to get the Turnitin plagiarism checker to talk to the assignment block, and it just…didn't. Kept throwing up error 500s. Error 500s, the bane of every lecturer's existence. Let me guess, you checked the logs, and they were about as helpful as a chocolate teapot? You know me too well. Utterly useless. Just a string of dates and times that offer absolutely no clue as to  why  it’s failing. I ended up emailing IT support again. They promised to look at it “within five working days”. Five! By then the deadline will have passed. Ouch. Standard, sadly. What course is this for? The second year History of Science, right? Yep. The essay on Faraday and Maxwell. It’s a big one. And I really wanted them to submit through Turnitin, just to get them used to the process for their dissertation next year. It feels… irresponsible to let them potentially plagiarise without at least having a check in place. I get it. It’s a pain, but it’s a necessary evil these days. Though honestly, the students are getting increasingly savvy. They know how to reword things. Turnitin only catches the blatant stuff. True. Still, it’s a deterrent. Have you had any issues with Moodle lately? You’re the clever one with the coding knowledge, maybe you can shed some light. I’m starting to suspect it’s something with the Moodle version itself. Not coding knowledge, just… a grudging familiarity born of necessity. To be honest, I’ve been mostly leaving Moodle alone for the past week. I've been focusing on rebuilding the introductory Python module for the first years. Trying to make it a bit more engaging, less… dry. Oh, that's good! How’s that going? Is it still just lists and loops? I remember when I first started teaching that module, everyone seemed to switch off about halfway through the ‘if/else’ statements. Trying to avoid that exact fate. I'm building in some mini-projects, actually. Like, they have to write a program that simulates a simple text-based adventure game. Nothing fancy, just choose-your-own-adventure style. That sounds much better! Practical application is key, isn’t it? They learn so much more when they’re actually  doing  something. I keep meaning to do that with my stuff, but I always get bogged down in the content itself.

Honestly, you look dreadful. Still battling the jetlag then? You’ve been staring into space for a good five minutes, just…existing. Existing is a good word for it. It feels less like living and more like a prolonged, vaguely unsettling dream. And honestly, the baby movements aren’t helping with the disorientation. It’s like there’s a tiny astronaut doing somersaults inside me, totally unaffected by time zones. Poor love. It’ll pass. Though I suspect the astronaut will continue its training for at least the next six months. Did you manage any sleep on the flight back? Pathetic attempts. Mostly consisted of trying to find a comfortable position while a toddler decided my armrest was a climbing frame. Then feeling guilty about being annoyed with a toddler. It's a vicious cycle. How was your meeting with the department head? Did you manage to convince Professor Davies that a combined history and archaeology module isn't a logistical nightmare? It was…a discussion. A lengthy discussion involving a lot of charts and Professor Davies muttering about ‘scope creep’. I think I planted the seed, at least. I highlighted the natural synergy, the benefit to student understanding of context… the usual lecturer spiel. Honestly, I'm not sure he was listening past ‘archaeology’. He's very traditional. Sounds about right. He’s still posting on the department noticeboard about the importance of proper footnotes, isn't he? In calligraphy, no less. You know him so well. Anyway, enough about work. We need to actually  do  something fun this weekend. Remember we booked tickets for ‘A Midsummer Night's Dream’ at the Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre? Oh, right! Yes. That's… good. Very good. Is it still on? I'm clearly losing track of reality. Very much still on. Saturday evening. We should probably think about logistics. Who's doing baby-sitting? Your mum offered, but she's got that bridge tournament… Oh, blast. You're right. She mentioned something about a 'significant prize pot'. Probably best not to disrupt the fierce competition of elderly bridge players. What about Sarah and Ben? They owe us one after we looked after Leo for that whole weekend when they went to Scotland. Good thinking. I’ll text Sarah. If they’re free, we could maybe grab a quick bite with them beforehand? There’s that new tapas place near the theatre everyone’s been raving about.

…and honestly, the whole thing with Omar’s sister’s visa is a right mess. She applied  ages  ago, you know? Said she just wanted to come and visit for a few weeks, see her brother, maybe do a bit of sightseeing. Thought it’d be straightforward. Aye, dealing with the Home Office… straightforward isn't a word I’d associate with them, is it? My cousin, Hakar, went through something similar just last year. Wanted to bring his wife over from Dohuk. Endless forms, bank statements, proving they weren’t going to overstay… it’s designed to wear people down, I think. What's the hold-up with Omar's sister? Apparently, they’ve flagged her as a ‘potential overstayer’. Can you  believe  it? She’s a pharmacist back in Algeria, a respected professional. She showed them proof of employment, property ownership… everything. They just keep asking for more and more. Omar’s beside himself. He reckons it’s just…well, you know. Seeing as she’s from a Muslim country. Sadly, that wouldn’t surprise me even a little. The rhetoric these days… it bleeds into policy, doesn't it? It's frustrating, especially when you see people jumping through hoops, and still being treated with suspicion. It’s different for some, isn’t it? Like, my brother, he can get a visa to practically anywhere, because he’s got a British passport and works for an oil company. It’s the politics of oil, plain and simple. Exactly! The double standards are infuriating. And it's not just Algeria. I was speaking to Wolfgang - you remember Wolfgang, did his PhD with me at Leeds? – he's working in Libya now, consulting on educational reforms. He’s saying the situation there is… complex, to put it mildly. The influence of Wahabi groups, the competition for control over the oil fields. It's all a tangled web. Libya… it’s always been a difficult place. After Gaddafi, everyone thought there'd be a fresh start, but it just seems to have fragmented into chaos. And yeah, the Wahabi influence is a big problem. It’s spreading through a lot of places, feeding off the instability. It’s not the Islam I grew up with, that's for sure. The culture in Kurdistan is much more tolerant, more integrated, you know? It's good to hear that. I worry about the younger generation, though.

Oh, that was  lovely , Agnes. Honestly, the lamb was perfect. Just falling apart. Though, I think I might be permanently ruined for anything  but  roast lamb now. Absolutely. You outdid yourself, Agnes. Really. And the gravy… I’ve been trying to replicate your gravy for years, but it's just not the same. What’s your secret? Is it… a pinch of nutmeg? Nutmeg is a good guess, David. But it’s patience, dear boy. And a really good stock. You can't rush good gravy. Though I suspect a generous splash of red wine helps too. It does! And speaking of generous splashes, anyone for another glass of red? I opened a new bottle. It's a Rioja, I think. Though honestly, after a day of transcribing legal jargon, all reds taste pretty similar to me. Yes, please! A small one. It's funny you mention the legal jargon, Sarah. Reminds me of all the paperwork I had to wade through this week. Apparently, the landlord’s decided to ‘modernise’ the kitchen in the flat. Which, knowing him, means slapping a coat of paint on the cabinets and calling it a day. Honestly, the man… Landlords. A necessary evil, I suppose. Though I always thought owning your own home was the only way to truly settle. We were fortunate, your father and I, we bought our house in the 60s, and it served us well for decades. Not like these rentals now. Easy for you to say, Agnes! Houses were affordable then. Try saving a deposit these days, especially around London. It's a joke. We’re stuck renting indefinitely, I think. Though, we’ve been lucky with our flat, all things considered. No immediate threats of 'modernisation' yet. Speaking of lucky… I was showing Mum the brochure for that cruise we talked about. The Mediterranean one. She got terribly excited. Started planning her outfits already. Oh, fantastic! That's lovely. I hope you two enjoy it. You deserve a proper break. Are you still feeling those twinges in your back, David? Maybe the sea air will do you good. They’re manageable, thankfully. Been trying to do those core workouts you recommended, Sarah. They’re… challenging. Let’s just say I’m not exactly a fitness fanatic yet. Workouts are all well and good, dear, but a brisk walk with a good dog is much more enjoyable. Remember Hamish?

…and then, honestly, me mam just  launched  into a whole thing about how I need to "apply meself" when I've sent out, like, fifty applications this month. Fifty! Does she think they multiply when I'm not lookin'? She's just worried, Liam. You've been at it a while now. Though, fifty is a good effort, I suppose. What kind of jobs were they, though? Were they stuff you actually  want  to do? Stuff I'm qualified to do! That's the point. All this fancy degree and nowt for it. Mostly admin stuff, a few assistant manager things, even saw one for a call centre…thought "nah, even desperate isn’t  that  desperate". Call centres are the worst. My cousin did one for about a week. Said she aged ten years. Here, anyone fancy a biscuit? So, Liam, what about that graduate scheme at the council? Did you ever hear back? Nah. Radio silence. It’s like I’ve been personally blacklisted by the entire working population of Cumbria. Don't be daft. It’s just… competitive. And it's early days yet. University careers advisor was always banging on about how it takes time, remember? Even  you  complained about her back then. I know, I know. It's just… depressing, innit? Everyone else seems to be sorted. Sarah’s loving her placement year, you’re smashing your A-Levels, Alex is…well, Alex is being Alex and apparently running some cafe in Keswick. He’s thriving, actually. Making proper money. Though, knowing Alex, half of it’s going on vintage cameras and obscure vinyl. He  did  send me a picture of a really cool old Leica. It was gorgeous. Although slightly out of my price range. Speaking of money… how are you finding living with your dad, by the way? Is he driving you up the wall? I can imagine having to explain your job hunt to him every five minutes. Honestly? It's… a situation. He means well, he really does. But he keeps leaving newspaper articles on me bed about lads me age who are already 'making a name for themselves'. One was about a farmer who turned his land into a glamping site! A  glamping site , Rosie! Your dad is a character. At least he’s trying to be supportive, in his own way. Supportive by making me feel like a failure? Thanks very much, Dad.

Right, okay. So, the year threes need to  actually  make something for their food tech lesson next week, not just… talk about biscuits. I was thinking fairy cakes. Simple enough, right? And we can talk about weighing, measuring, what happens when you heat things… Can  I  help decorate? With sprinkles? Lots and lots of sprinkles? Of course you can, Poppy. You’re the sprinkle master. But you have to promise not to eat all the sprinkles before the cakes are even baked. I want to help too! Can I stir? I’m really good at stirring! Roar! You are a very good stir-er, Leo. But fairy cakes need a gentle hand. Maybe you can be in charge of quality control – making sure we don't put too many sprinkles on. A very important job. Quality control is  my  job! No,  mine ! I’m a dinosaur, I have a sensitive palate! Okay, okay. We’ll work it out. Maybe you can alternate. Now, I was thinking, should we do vanilla, or chocolate? Chocolate! Definitely chocolate. With pink frosting! With dinosaur sprinkles! Do they  have  dinosaur sprinkles? I don’t think so, sadly. Although… I did see a rather interesting baking section in Morrisons last week. I was looking for that book Mrs. Peterson recommended – “The Boy Who Grew Dragons.” Have you guys read that one? No! Is it about actual dragons? It is! A boy finds a dragon egg, and it hatches, and…well, you’ll have to read it to find out. It was on a shelf right next to a whole display of baking things. They had everything! Edible glitter, shaped sprinkles… it was madness. I nearly bought a mould for making penguin-shaped cookies. Penguins! That’s even better than dinosaurs! Easy there. Now, about the lesson… I’m trying to explain how things change when you bake them. Like, a liquid becoming solid. It’s tricky with seven-year-olds to get across. They just want to eat the finished product. Because it’s yummy! Exactly. But understanding  why  it’s yummy is important too. It's like… a bit like Tomodachi Life. What? How? Well, think about it. You start with just little Mii characters, right? And then they fall in love, they have babies… things change! They’re not the same as when you started. Baking is a bit like that. You start with flour and eggs, and then,  poof , you get a cake.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. A proper pub garden, not one of those chain places trying to look ‘rustic’. And a decent cider, not that fizzy stuff they try to pass off in Cambridge. You're a Norfolk purist through and through, aren’t you, El? Though I have to admit, this is a good shout. Much better than battling the crowds in town. And you  were  complaining about marking essays all week. A change of scenery is definitely warranted. Complaining is a mild word, Ben. They were… soul-destroying. One student genuinely argued that the entire Roman Empire was a social media construct invented by emperors to control the narrative. Right. Facebook wasn’t exactly around in 44 BC, was it? You’d think not. It’s like their brains have been re-wired. Everything’s a meme, everything’s a ‘take’. It’s exhausting. Anyway, speaking of rewiring… have you seen old man Hemmings has finally given in and bought one of those electric cars? Hemmings? Old man Hemmings who still maintains his Morris Minor? Seriously? I know! Apparently, his grandson convinced him. He was showing it off in the village shop. Said it was ‘the future’. Though he also said he misses the sound of a proper engine. Well, he would, wouldn’t he? I still think they’re a bit… soulless. All that silent gliding. Give me the rumble of a good V8 any day. Although, I will concede they’re probably more sensible. Especially with petrol prices the way they are. Sensible isn’t a word I’d usually associate with you, Ben. Remember that bright red sports car you insisted on buying five years ago? “It’s an investment!” you said. Okay, that was… perhaps not my most financially shrewd decision. It was fun though. Until it decided it didn't like wet roads. And the insurance was frankly astronomical. But still, a proper car experience. These electric ones… it’s just a glorified golf buggy, isn't it? That's a bit harsh! They’re getting better. And you can’t deny the environmental benefits. It's just… I don't know. They feel so… disconnected. Like you’re playing a video game. Disconnected is a good word. Everything feels disconnected these days. Look at Facebook, for example. Do you actually  know  what’s genuine anymore? It's all curated highlight reels.

Honestly, this is… a choice. Your little sister really makes you watch  everything , doesn’t she? She insists. Says it's a "cultural experience." Apparently, all ten-year-olds need to understand the intricacies of sentient food falling from the sky. Plus, she knows I can't say no to those puppy-dog eyes. How was work today, by the way? Still battling the hordes for discounted bath bombs? Don't even  start  with the bath bombs. It’s like Black Friday every single day in there. Old ladies elbowing each other, kids screaming… I swear, I aged five years just restocking the lavender ones. And Mr. Henderson nearly had a fit because I accidentally put the rose-scented ones next to the vanilla. Apparently, that's a cardinal sin in the world of budget toiletries. Oh, Mr. Henderson. He's… a character. Still on about the correct way to fold hand towels, is he? Always. It’s a sacred art, apparently. Honestly, sometimes I think he misses being in the army. Speaking of characters, this film’s inventor bloke is a bit… intense, isn't he? Always tinkering, obsessed with flying. Bit of a control freak, maybe? Flint Lockwood? Yeah, I suppose. But that's kind of the point, isn’t it? He just wants to  make  something, even if it's ridiculous. I remember when I first saw this, I just thought it was funny that everything was food. Didn’t really pick up on any deeper stuff. See, I'm overthinking it, as usual. But doesn't it seem like a metaphor for... I don't know, unchecked ambition? Like, he creates this amazing thing, but then it spirals out of control and threatens everyone? It's a kids' film, I know, I know. But still. Okay, you’re officially analyzing a children’s movie like it's Shakespeare. Slow down. Can you hand me the remote? I want to see if there’s a volume button that  doesn’t  make it deafeningly loud or mysteriously silent. Oh, this thing. Honestly, it's a conspiracy. They design these things to be impossible to operate. Here. Honestly, it’s like they expect us to have a degree in astrophysics to adjust the sound. Found it! Thanks. You know, thinking about ambition… It’s interesting how we’re all pressured to have these huge life plans now, aren’t we?

…and honestly, seeing the state of things now, after all these years… it’s a bit depressing, isn’t it? Back then, with New Labour, there was a  feeling  of… possibility. Even if it didn’t entirely deliver, you know? Depressing's a good word for it, Professor. Absolutely depressing. Possibility? Aye, well, Blair was good at  selling  possibility. Slickest thing you ever saw. But deliver? That’s where it fell apart, wasn’t it? All style over substance, like a lot of modern footie teams. Fancy passing, no end product. A very apt analogy, actually. The passing triangles of New Labour… beautifully constructed, but often leading nowhere. Though, I think it’s unfair to say  nothing  was achieved. The investment in schools and the NHS… small steps, perhaps, but steps nonetheless. NHS is on its knees, Professor. You’ve been over here in Finland long enough to see how things  should  be done. Proper funding, proper care. Back home, it's just waiting lists and overworked staff. And the schools? They’re churning out kids who can’t even write a proper sentence, let alone think for themselves. Blame the curriculum changes, they say. I blame a lack of respect, a lack of… grit. Grit… interesting. It's a peculiarly British concept, isn’t it? That stiff upper lip. My students here, even the British ones, seem… different. Less inclined to just ‘muddle through’ as we used to. They want answers, they want things explained. That’s what comes of being mollycoddled. Everyone gets a trophy, everyone's a winner. Doesn’t prepare you for the real world, does it? Now,  football … that still prepares you for the real world. Brutal, competitive, doesn't matter if you've got a fancy upbringing. You've got to graft. Speaking of which, did you see the Liverpool match at the weekend? I did! A comfortable win against… was it Brighton? Klopp has really turned things around. Though I confess, I’m not as passionately dedicated as many. I follow the Bundesliga more closely these days. A bit less… frenetic, perhaps. Comfortable win? Comfortable?! They were two-nil down after half-time, Professor! Two-nil! It was a proper nail-biter. Salah finally found his feet again, thankfully. That Egyptian lad is world class when he's on form, but he goes missing sometimes, doesn’t he? Like the government. You never quite know where they’ve wandered off to.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data in the BNC is just… overwhelming. I've been trying to isolate instances of ‘right’ as a discourse marker, and it’s like wading through treacle. Every other sentence seems to have it! It’s making my head spin. Oh, tell me about it. Editing feels like that sometimes, except instead of ‘right’ it’s excessive commas. People just  love  a comma. Did you see Sarah posted pictures from her trip to the Maldives? It looked absolutely blissful. No, I haven’t been on social media much this weekend. Needed a bit of a detox, if I’m honest. It’s all just… curated happiness, isn't it? Though the Maldives  does  sound nice. A proper escape. Better than, say, another weekend spent deciphering dialects. Curated happiness is the only happiness most people show these days, isn’t it? It’s horrifying, really. Though a picture of turquoise water is never a bad thing. Are you two talking travel? Sort of. Sarah’s in the Maldives. I'm just… wistfully scrolling. And Lila’s complaining about linguistic data. Complaining is a strong word. I’m merely articulating the… challenges. Honestly, I’m starting to wonder if I made the right choice, taking this job. It’s fascinating, don't get me wrong, but the workload… And it’s all so solitary. You’re good at it, though. And it's important work. Preserving language is… well, it's more important than most people realise. Are you still seeing that bloke from LinkedIn? The one who works in… tech, was it? Oh, Mark. Yeah, we went for a drink last week. He was going on about blockchain again. It went straight over my head. He’s… nice, I guess. A bit obsessed with optimizing everything, even leisure time. He kept trying to suggest apps to “enhance” my weekend. Oh dear god. Sounds exhausting. Honestly, I’d rather just  be  bored. Speaking of exhausting, I'm trying to convince my mum to come visit. She’s been going on about London for ages. Oh, that’s lovely! She’d love it here in East London. Loads of little cafes, vintage shops… much cooler than Abergavenny, no offence. None taken! She loves a good vintage shop. The problem is… she’s  terrified  of flying. Absolutely petrified. It's been a whole saga trying to reassure her. Oh, that’s rough.

Right, so I'm thinking red wine reduction for the lamb. You reckon? It feels… festive. Though, festive feels a bit much considering it’s still only November, innit? Festive is good. We need a bit of cheering up, don’t we? And a red wine reduction sounds lovely, darling. Just… try not to cry while chopping onions, will you? You’ll taint the sauce with sadness. It's not sadness, it's the onion. Honestly. And it’s a  very  potent onion. Speaking of potent…did I tell you about Leo’s new tattoo? Oh, no. Not another one. What is it this time? A philosophical quote in Elvish? Worse. A tiny avocado. On his ankle. He said it represents his “growth as a person”. Oh, Leo. That boy is… something else. Honestly, he'll be covered head to toe in fruit and vegetables by Christmas.    Hellooooo! Am I interrupting a culinary masterpiece… and a roasting of poor Leo? Esme! Come in, darling, you're perfectly timed. We’re just getting dinner going. Lamb, red wine reduction thanks to Ethan's ambitious onion chopping. Sounds divine. Crikey, my day. Absolute madness at the office. The interns… bless them, they’re trying, but Sarah managed to send a rejection letter to our biggest author. With a smiley face. Oh.  Ouch . That’s…suboptimal. Oh dear. You’re remarkably calm considering. It’s a nightmare scenario isn’t it? How did you even fix it? A lot of grovelling and a very frantic phone call explaining it was an ‘automated response error’ which felt…unconvincing. He seemed vaguely amused, thankfully. Anyway, enough work drama. What are your plans for Christmas? Have you started thinking about it yet? We were talking about it actually. I was suggesting we try and get away for a few days, maybe a cottage somewhere. Get properly cosy. Mum's already threatening a twelve-course roast and a full-blown pantomime performance. Oh, your mother. Always a force of nature. A cottage sounds lovely, actually. I was thinking of just having a quiet one this year. The house renovation is  still  ongoing, and frankly, the thought of hosting fills me with dread. They’ve discovered dry rot in the dining room. Dry rot! It’s like something out of a gothic novel. Oh, no! Seriously? That sounds…expensive. And stressful. I'm honestly impressed you’re managing to stay sane.

Honestly, this risotto is being  difficult . I swear, Birmingham water just doesn’t behave the same way as Hitchin water. It needs… something. More stock, maybe? Hitchin water having special risotto-making properties, is it? You’re telling me your childhood village is the key to perfect creamy rice? Don't be ridiculous! It’s just… I used to make this  all  the time at my flat there, and it always came out beautifully. Maybe it’s the rice. Did I get the Arborio right this time? I always get confused between that and Carnaroli. You definitely got Arborio. I checked when I was at the shops. You were distracted talking about that new spin class you tried. How was that, by the way? Still feeling like you’ve been hit by a bus? Oh, don’t even. Hit by a  lorry , more like. I thought I was reasonably fit, you know, a bit of walking, the occasional jog… but those instructors! They're animals. And everyone else in the class seemed to be actual professional cyclists in disguise. I’m going to stick to Pilates for a bit, I think. Less…impact. Sensible. Pilates is good. I’ve been meaning to get back to it. Work’s just been…a lot. We're doing a big feature on the impact of long-covid on the workforce, and honestly, it's heartbreaking talking to some of these people. It feels a bit grim, editing all day about people’s long-term health struggles. Oh, that sounds awful, actually. Really draining. You journalists always take on the heavy stuff, don’t you? Are you looking after yourself? You've been looking a bit pale lately. I’m fine! Just…London life. Lack of sunlight, too much coffee. The usual. Though, I did attempt to cook a proper roast dinner last week and it was a total disaster. The Yorkshire puddings were flatter than pancakes. Oh dear. A culinary catastrophe! You know, you should come over more often and let me feed you proper food. You rely too much on Pret a Manger, I suspect. You're not wrong there. It’s just so  easy . But this smells amazing, even if it is being temperamental. What are you thinking of serving with it? I was thinking a simple green salad, with a lemon vinaigrette. Unless you’d prefer something else? I could quickly roast some asparagus.

Honestly, I needed that walk. The students today were…spirited. A lot of questions about Baudrillard, which is good, I suppose, but all at once. Like being cross-examined. Baudrillard always does that to them. It’s like he  wants  to be misunderstood. Were they at least engaging with the simulation argument, or were they mostly fixated on hyperreality being Disneyland? A bit of both, actually. One student kept trying to apply it to TikTok. Said it’s the ultimate proof of a simulated reality. I nearly lost it. I mean, it  could  be, but…TikTok? It feels a bit reductive, doesn’t it? It absolutely does. Though, you have to admit, there’s something to be said for the endlessly curated self. Feels pretty simulated. How did you steer them back on track? Pointed out the difference between representation and simulation, and then threatened a pop quiz on  Simulacra and Simulation . Usually does the trick. How was your afternoon? Did Old Man Hemmings finally grasp the concept of postcolonial literature? Slowly. Very slowly. He’s convinced Chinua Achebe is secretly a Marxist. Which isn’t entirely  wrong , I suppose, but... it’s a leap. He kept talking about class struggle in  Things Fall Apart . It’s exhausting sometimes, isn't it? Trying to get them to see beyond the surface. It is. It really is. It makes you question the whole point sometimes. Are we actually imparting knowledge, or just… shuffling ideas around in their heads? We’re planting seeds. That’s all we can do. Some will grow, some won’t. Like gardening. Speaking of which, remember old Mrs. Higgins from Norwich? She always had the most incredible roses. And the worst toenails. Oh my god, Mrs. Higgins! Don’t even get me started. Those nails were legendary. Like miniature armour plating. She’d proudly show them off, too! "Good strong nails, dear," she’d say. "Never could understand all this fuss about pedicures." Exactly! And she’d give you a pot of jam and lecture you about the importance of hard work, all in the same breath. It’s funny the things you remember. It feels like a lifetime ago, being back in Norwich. It does. It’s… strange, isn’t it? To feel so far away and yet so connected to those silly little memories. Have you spoken to Ben recently? I haven’t heard from him in ages.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of him to just walk off stage like that! It was the final of ‘Britain’s Got Talent’, for goodness sake! Simon Cowell looked absolutely gobsmacked. You’re still on about that magician, then? Honestly, Sarah, you get so invested in these things. It’s just telly. Probably a publicity stunt, anyway. A publicity stunt? Maybe. But it felt… disrespectful. All those people auditioned, and he just… bailed. Plus, my students were  obsessed  with him. I had to explain to a class of fifteen-year-olds why someone might do something like that. It was a linguistic nightmare, dealing with all the ‘why’s’ and ‘but’s’. Fifteen-year-olds. Right. They'll find something else to obsess over tomorrow. Remember the Tamagotchi craze? That was a proper societal meltdown. Makes a magician walking off stage seem pretty tame. True, true. Though, you have to admit, the Tamagotchi  was  strangely compelling. It was a miniature responsibility! Anyway, enough about reality TV. How’s work? Still battling the corporate dragons? You have no idea. We’re trying to push through a new marketing campaign and half the board think it’s ‘too edgy’. Apparently, showing people enjoying themselves is now a risk. Honestly, it's exhausting. They want ‘safe’, they want ‘predictable’. Oh, the joys of middle management. I think my job’s stressful enough trying to explain the subjunctive to teenagers! What’s the campaign about, anyway? It's for the new line of fitness trackers, ironically enough. We wanted to show people using them in real life - hiking, cycling, dancing, all that.
