Not just sterile shots of the device itself. They’re worried it’ll alienate the… let’s call them ‘less active’ demographic. Less active? That’s… incredibly tactful. It sounds like a good campaign, though. More relatable. It's about aspiration, isn't it? Showing people what they  could  be doing. That’s exactly what I said! But apparently, aspiration is ‘aggressive marketing’ these days. It's all very… circular reasoning. We’re spending a fortune on consultants to tell us things we already know. Speaking of fortunes, how's your brother, David? Still going strong with the organic farm? He is! Actually, he’s expanded. He’s got a small shop in St Albans now, selling all his produce. He’s completely dedicated to it, bless him. It’s very… ‘off-grid’ living.

Dad, honestly, are you  sure  this is the right way? We’ve been on the M5 for ages. It all looks…grey. Just grey roads and grey fields. It’s depressing. Now, now, Elsie. Don’t be dramatic. It’s England in summer, what did you expect, the Caribbean? And yes, I’m fairly sure. Satnav's doing alright, though I do trust my instincts a bit more. Besides, grey's a perfectly respectable colour. Think of a stormy sea, or a…a really sophisticated pigeon. A sophisticated pigeon? What even  is  that? And it’s not just grey, it’s… fifty shades of grey, and none of them are nice. Remember that film,  Jamaica Inn ? That was all moody grey and brooding moors. It looked properly miserable. Ah,  Jamaica Inn . Daphne du Maurier, good shout. Proper spooky that was. Filmed around here somewhere, I think. Though I reckon they probably bumped up the grey on purpose for effect. You know, like in the  Wizard of Oz  when they switched to technicolour? Before that, it was all sepia toned, wasn't it? Made Kansas look even more drab than it probably was. Yeah, I remember learning about that in Media Studies. They wanted to emphasise how amazing Oz was going to be. It's clever, isn't it? Using colour like that. It's a bit like Sherlock Holmes, though. All dark and foggy, and everything’s described in shades of brown and grey. It adds to the mystery. Good point, lass. Holmes and his London smog. Although Conan Doyle was a master of  description , wasn’t he? He could make you feel the chill right through your bones. It’s funny, isn’t it? How different writers use language to create a mood. Lewis Carroll was all about nonsense and wordplay, completely different vibe. Totally!  Alice in Wonderland  is just…bonkers. Speaking of bonkers, remember Gran telling us those old fairy tales? The ones with the really scary bits? Like, the original versions weren't all Disney-fied. Oh, don’t get me started on Gran and her fairy tales. She had a story for every occasion, and they always ended with someone getting their comeuppance. Proper grim! It’s probably why you’re so skeptical, you know. Always looking for the catch. Maybe. Hey, are we nearly there yet? I'm starting to feel car sick. Not long now, love.

…and honestly, Grandad, the price of a cinema ticket now? Ten quid for a student?! It's daylight robbery. Remember when it was… what, two bob back in your day? Two bob and sixpence, lass. And you got a bag of sweets with it! Proper sweets, not this rubbish they sell now. And the Odeon in Altrincham… Aye, that was a palace. We used to queue for hours to see a Dick Powell film. It’s inflation, though, isn't it? Everything goes up. Rent in London is insane. I was looking at places for a mate, and a tiny flat is like, two thousand a month. You could buy a house in Somerset for that! Don't even  start  on rent, Liam. I'm lucky my mam lets me stay at hers still while I save, but even up in Sunderland it's climbing. Though, admittedly, it’s not London prices. Still, two grand for a  flat ? Blimey. Sunderland, is it? Never been. Is it much different from Manchester? Used to be all shipyards, weren't there? Aye, used to be. It's changed a bit, though. A lot of the shipyards are gone, sadly. We’ve got a nice seafront now, trying to build up tourism. It's a bit… bleak sometimes, but it's home. Much cheaper than down south, that's for sure. What about you, Grandad? Timperley... that's near Manchester, right? Right near. Very posh area, even then. My father worked hard to get us a house there. Before that, we were proper working class, you know? Lived in a terrace house, shared a bathroom with next door. But he was a clever man, my dad. Worked for the railways, then BT when it all changed. He saw things, mind. Saw the war. World War Two, right? You were a young lad then? Did you get evacuated? Evacuated to Wales. Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch. Couldn’t pronounce it then, can’t pronounce it now! Awful time. Homesick as anything. The farmer's wife was kind, but it wasn't home. Watched the bombs fall from a distance on the newsreels, you see. Felt helpless. That sounds awful, Grandad. I can't imagine… I was reading about the Blitz in primary school, and the stories are just… heartbreaking. We did a project on Anderson shelters. Anderson shelters… aye, we had one in the garden. Damp and cold. We spent a lot of nights down there, listening for the sirens.

Right, Mum, where are we with the ‘Operation Move-Dad’s-Stuff’ list? Feels like we’ve been at it for hours already. And this tea is  exactly  how I remember it. Proper builder’s brew. Oh, don’t rush me, Daniel. It’s not like your father hasn’t accumulated a lifetime of…  things . I’ve got ‘shed tools’ here, but that’s a whole category in itself. There’s the rusty spanners, the… are those actual antlers?! And then there’s the ‘sentimental’ pile. Which is mostly old biscuit tins. Antlers?! Seriously? What did Dad  do  with antlers? Okay, okay, sentimental pile first. We can tackle the shed later. It’s like an archaeological dig in there. How’s your back holding up, by the way? You were complaining yesterday. It’s alright, dear. A little twinge, nothing a hot bath and a bit of Deep Heat can’t fix. Though honestly, lifting boxes full of his model railway accessories is asking for trouble. He really did have  everything . Remember when he tried to build that miniature village? It took over the entire dining room. How could I forget? I was forbidden from going anywhere near it after I accidentally sent a little porcelain villager flying with my toy car. He was  not  pleased. Speaking of not pleased, have you spoken to Aunt Carol about the wedding? She still hasn't RSVP'd. No. I left her a message two days ago. Honestly, that woman. She always has to make a production out of everything. Probably gauging how much fuss we’re making before deciding if it's worth her time. She always did favour your Uncle George. Don’t start, Mum. It's our day. And she  promised  she'd try and make it. It would mean a lot to both of us. I just... I want everything to be perfect. It feels a bit ridiculous sounding it out loud, doesn't it? No, darling, it's not ridiculous. It’s your wedding! You want everything nice. And Carol... well, she's Carol. Look, try again tomorrow. And if she hems and haws, tell her straight. You’re a grown man now, you can handle a bit of passive aggression. Though frankly, I'm tempted to call her myself. I think I will. Also, jet lag is  real . I flew back from Thailand just yesterday, and I feel like I’ve been run over by a weaver fish – seriously weird creatures, the way they build these elaborate sandcastles.

“Honestly, look at that one. It’s… it’s practically alien, isn’t it? How can something so delicate survive? It’s a wonder.” “Evolution, pet. Millions of years of perfecting the art of not being eaten. Though I’m more impressed with how  you  manage to keep practically everything alive in this flat. It’s a jungle in here, honestly.” “It’s not  that  bad. And they’re therapeutic! Plus, my grandma always said a home isn’t a home without a bit of greenery. She had prize-winning begonias, you know. Used to spend all day fussing over them.” “Begonias, eh? Sounds…intense. My grandma was more of a biscuit and daytime TV kinda woman. Speaking of intense, have you seen Sarah’s new hair? She went full-on 80s crimped, like, yesterday. It’s… a choice.” “No! Seriously? Sarah? That’s… bold. She always did have a flair for the dramatic. Remember that purple phase she went through in uni? It clashed horribly with everything." “Oh god, don't remind me. It was a visual assault. Still better than some of the things I saw during fresher’s week, though. Anyway, it made me think about when  you  changed your hair last. It's been ages since you've done anything different. You're stuck in a rut of sensible ponytails.” “Hey! There’s nothing wrong with a sensible ponytail. It’s practical. I’ve got a job, remember? I don’t have time to be messing about with curling irons and hairspray. Besides, I need to be taken seriously at work. Can't exactly be a Research Manager with rainbow hair." "True, true. Though I bet you could pull off anything. Though, honestly, work’s been a bit of a nightmare lately. Did you see that article about the NHS waiting lists? It’s appalling. My aunt's been waiting six months for a hip replacement. Six months!” “It is awful. It's just consistently underfunded. And then they wonder why everyone’s stressed and overworked. It's a system on its knees, and they're more worried about restructuring than actually helping people.” “Exactly! And it’s all linked, isn’t it? Fewer nurses, longer waiting times, more pressure on social care… it's a vicious cycle. It makes you wonder what future generations are going to be facing. Speaking of future generations, did you hear about the latest A-Level reforms?

Right, honestly, I'm  trying  to quit. Properly this time. It's just… stressful, innit? Essays piling up, Mum nagging about getting a proper job over the summer, and then there's Liam being… Liam. Liam being… vaguely infuriating, as always? You're much better off without the drama, honestly. And good on you for trying to quit. It's proper hard, I know. I went through it with the ciggies last year. Switched to nicotine patches, felt like a walking adhesive bandage for a month. Patches are grim. I tried those. Ended up just feeling perpetually nauseous. Vaping’s probably a bit gentler, yeah? Though, still not ideal. Speaking of stressful, uni applications are actually sending me into a spiral. I have NO idea what I want to do. Tell me about it. I’ve narrowed it down to… possibly something to do with history? Maybe archaeology? But then I think about the job market and think, ‘Right, you’ll be serving lattes for the rest of your days’. My dad practically had a heart attack when I said ‘archaeology’. He's all, "A proper degree! Get a proper degree!" Sounds like my grandad. "Get a trade, lass! Something  useful !" Like being a plumber is somehow more intellectually stimulating than, I dunno, studying feminist literature. Which, by the way, is what’s currently taking up 90% of my brain space. We were having a right ding-dong in the seminar today about intersectionality. Ooh, sounds intense. I’m doing a bit of sociology, so I get the debates. It's exhausting, though, isn't it? Constantly unpacking things. Though honestly, after the week I've had dealing with some of the boys in my flat… intersectionality feels  vital . They just don’t  get  it. It's always "but what about men’s issues?" It's like, mate, we're talking about systemic oppression here, not a slightly bruised ego. It’s the entitlement, innit? The sheer, unshakeable entitlement. It's exhausting. Actually, I was reading this academic paper the other day – about the economic impact of patriarchy – and it was genuinely shocking. The amount of wealth that's been systematically diverted away from women… Don't even get me started. I was trying to explain to my uncle why the gender pay gap isn’t just about ‘women choosing lower-paying jobs’. He gave me this whole spiel about biology and… honestly, I just switched off.

…and honestly, the whole weekend just felt  exhausting . Like, I was actively calculating how quickly I could make polite excuses and leave each conversation. It wasn’t even anything  she  did, specifically. It was just… everything. The constant one-upping, the relentless positivity, the need to dominate every story. Oh god, I know that feeling. It's like being trapped in a sparkly, relentlessly upbeat vortex. Is this about Sarah? You mentioned you saw her last weekend. It is. And it’s been building for a while, hasn’t it? It’s not like we’ve had a massive falling out. There's no drama. Just… a slow drift into realising I actively  dread  spending time with her. And the guilt! That's the worst part. Because she seems so genuinely fond of me. The guilt is brutal. Especially when it’s someone you’ve known for ages. I had something similar with Ben, from uni. We were thick as thieves, but then he got really into multi-level marketing, you know? And then  everything  became a pitch. Every single conversation. “Oh, you’re stressed? Have you considered the life-changing benefits of…?” Ugh. Oh no. That’s… special levels of draining. Sarah isn’t trying to sell me anything, thankfully. It’s just… her entire life is this performative perfection. And it makes me feel awful about my own messy reality. Right? It's the comparison thing, isn't it? You start to feel inadequate even though you know it's all a façade. So what are you thinking of doing? Just letting it fade naturally? Because that’s what I did with Ben. Just… less enthusiastic replies to texts, conveniently being busy. It took  years . Years! That’s what I’m worried about. I don’t want years of politely declining invites and slowly disappearing. That feels… cowardly, somehow. And potentially more hurtful in the long run. Part of me wants to just be honest. But I'm terrified of hurting her feelings. She’s one of those people who will genuinely be devastated. Honestly? Honesty is hard, but a slow fade feels worse. It’s like you're silently judging them, rather than just saying, "Actually, this friendship isn’t working for me anymore." It’s probably easier said than done, though. What would you even  say ? That's the million-dollar question. I was thinking something along the lines of, “I’ve been doing a lot of thinking lately, and I’m realising I need to focus on… well, a few things in my own life.

… Honestly, Mum, the reading list for this term is  brutal . Like, three novels a week, plus critical essays on each one. It’s less literature and more… endurance training. Oh, darling, university always was a bit of a pressure cooker, wasn’t it? Though when  I  was at university, it was mostly about debating and avoiding lectures. Not quite the same workload, I suspect. What are you reading, anyway? Anything… stimulating? Stimulating? It’s mostly Victorian stuff. Dickens, Brontë… a bit of George Eliot. It’s good, obviously, it’s  classics , but I’m craving something a bit lighter. I started that Philip K. Dick you recommended, though. "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?", right? Oh, excellent! That's a good palate cleanser after all that earnestness. He was a fascinating man, Philip K. Dick. So much paranoia woven into the science fiction. Did you know he was convinced the FBI was following him? Yeah, I read a bit about him. Pretty wild. It makes the book feel… different, knowing that. More unsettling. How’s the painting going? Still working on the coastal scene? Oh, the Hastings piece is  almost  finished, actually. I'm really pleased with how the light is falling on the water. It’s… elusive, that light. I’ve been experimenting with layering the blues and greys. It's a bit reminiscent of Turner, I suppose, though I would never dare compare. I’m thinking of entering it into the local art society exhibition. You absolutely should! You always downplay your work, Mum. It’s brilliant. Remember that portrait you did of Great Aunt Mabel? Still hanging in Uncle Arthur’s dining room, apparently. He carries on about it every Christmas. Oh, Mabel. She was a character and a half. Always insisted on wearing that ridiculous feathered hat. Arthur’s just polite. He wouldn’t know a good painting if it bit him on the nose! Speaking of family… have you heard anything more from Leo? He hasn’t called in ages. I texted him a couple of days ago. He's still in Barcelona, apparently. Said he’s totally immersed in the Gaudi architecture. Says it's… transformative. The usual Leo hyperbole, but he sounds happy. He's thinking about extending his trip, maybe even trying to find some freelance graphic design work over there. Barcelona… That's lovely. I always wanted to go back. Vienna was wonderful, of course, my birthplace, but Barcelona always held a special allure.

Oh, this is lovely. Just… lovely. The Polish countryside is really doing it for me today. Though I do feel a bit guilty being the passenger after you drove all that way yesterday. Perhaps I should have insisted on a shift. Don't be silly, Aunt Carol. You’ve been navigating, haven't you? And generally keeping me awake with fascinating historical tidbits about… well, everything. Besides, I don’t mind. It’s actually quite relaxing, after the chaos of teaching all week. Are you  sure  you're alright though? You’ve been a bit quiet since we stopped for that pierogi. Just digesting, dear. Those pierogi were…substantial. Maybe a bad time to eat before considering a gym session, though, eh? I'm already regretting that extra one. Perhaps a gentle walk around Tarnow would have been a better idea. A walk  instead  of the gym? That's a first! You and your fitness regime. Honestly, you’d think you were training for the Olympics. And yes, pierogi pre-gym… not ideal. I had a protein bar, sensible me. Sensible, always sensible, aren’t you, Liv? It’s just…I feel like I need to  do  something. Sitting around doing nothing makes me feel… useless. Especially after… well, you know. It's a habit formed after years of…nothingness, really. I know, Aunt Carol. I understand. But you're not useless. You give wonderful TEFL lessons, even if it's just a few hours a week. And you’re a brilliant navigator! Truly. I’d be completely lost without your knowledge of obscure Polish villages. Oh, please. It’s Google Maps mostly. Though I did recognise a few place names from a documentary I watched. It's embarrassing, isn't it? Knowing more about a country I’ve barely visited than some people who live here. It feels… very English, somehow. That need to catalog and understand everything. Very English? How so? I don't know. It’s just… a sort of colonial hangover, I suppose. That urge to classify and control. We're always analyzing, aren't we? Judging. Observing. It can be quite stifling, even for ourselves. And it probably comes across terribly in my teaching, now I think about it. Am I just imposing an English worldview on all my students? Now you’re overthinking it. You’re a good teacher, Aunt Carol. They appreciate your dedication.

…and honestly, Mrs. Higgins nearly had a fit when I brought 'em all in for the pottery class. "Too rustic, Margaret, too…  earthy ," she said. As if throwing a pot on a wheel should be about porcelain perfection! Honestly, some people. Still, these are lovely aren't they? Proper weight to ‘em. Not like those flimsy things you get at the shops. Aye, they are good mugs. Good and solid. Remind me of your Grandfather’s. He had a favourite, always demanded that one for his brew. Said it kept it warmer longer. Though he’d drink anything, bless him, even lukewarm tea if that was all there was. You’re right, he would. He wasn't one for fuss. Though I remember him grumbling something about the milk always being too cold. It's funny the things you recall. This weather's not helping, is it? Still damp. Supposed to brighten up, but I’ll believe it when I see it. It’s been drizzling on and off all week. Makes the slugs happy, anyway. They’re having a field day with the hostas. They are a nuisance, those slugs. I used to scatter eggshells around, when I were gardening. Old wives’ tale, maybe, but seemed to keep ‘em at bay a bit. Though I wouldn't fancy tripping over ‘em. Speaking of things crawling…I saw a spider the size of my hand in the bathroom this morning! Oh, don’t! Don’t even say it. I hate spiders. Absolutely loathe them. I had one drop on my head in the greenhouse last week. Nearly screamed the place down. Geoff had to come and dispatch it for me. Geoff’s a good lad. Always willing to help. Did you manage to get all the sweet peas planted? I noticed you were pottering about with them the other day. Most of them, yes. A few seeds didn't take, the greedy birds got to them, I suspect. They're enjoying the sunflower hearts I put out, though. Though that robin's getting a bit brazen now, perches right on the shed roof, staring me down. It probably thinks I’m running a bird cafe. They’re clever things, birds. They know a good thing when they see it. Makes a change from young Timmy next door, always kicking a ball against my fence. Drives me round the bend, he does.

Honestly, a week until Cornwall and I  still  haven’t managed to pack. It’s a disaster. A week is ages, darling. Plenty of time. You always leave it to the last minute, don’t you, Lily? It's a family tradition, I think. It's not a  tradition , Mum! It’s…procrastination born of overwhelming excitement and the sheer number of bikinis I need to decide between. Bikinis in Cornwall? You’ll be needing a wetsuit more like. It’s hardly the Med, you know. Dad! Don’t ruin my vibes. I'm picturing sunny days on the beach, ice cream, maybe even learning to surf. Surf lessons are a good idea, actually. Your Uncle David was a dab hand at surfing back in his youth. He’d probably be up for giving you a go. We should give him a ring while we're down there. It’s been ages since we’ve seen him and Auntie Carol. Oh, yeah! Uncle David is hilarious. Remember that time he tried to teach Grandma to paddleboard and she nearly ended up in France? Nearly! She clung onto that board like a limpet. Gave David a right telling-off too, didn't she? Said he’d promised her a relaxing holiday, not an aquatic assault course. She does love a good moan when things don’t go to plan, your Grandma. But she secretly loved it. She was showing pictures of it to everyone at bingo for weeks! Speaking of plans, have you thought about what you want to  do  in Cornwall, Lily, besides building sandcastles and avoiding the cold water? Well, I was looking at the Eden Project online. It looks…really cool. All those massive biomes. And there’s a little town called Padstow, apparently it's famous for its seafood. We could get proper fish and chips! Padstow’s nice, a bit touristy though. We could go to Port Isaac, that’s where they filmed Doc Martin. Lovely little harbour. Ooh, yes! That’s a good shout, Arthur. We’ve always meant to go. Lily, would you like that? Doc Martin’s quite popular with your generation, isn’t it? I’ve seen a few episodes! It’s okay. But honestly, I’m more excited about potentially meeting some people our age. I’ve been chatting to this girl online, Chloe, and her family are renting a cottage near Newquay.

Honestly, Heath Ledger in  10 Things I Hate About You … just  unfair . He was way too charming for Patrick Verona. Like, a bad boy with a heart of gold is one thing, but that whole paintball scene? Swoon. You’re still going on about Heath Ledger? We finished the film like, two hours ago! And yeah, okay, the paintball scene was good. But Julia Stiles was brilliant, you have to admit. Kat Stratford is iconic. Oh, she was! Don't get me wrong, I loved Kat. But Heath... he just had this…  vibe . Anyway. Distraction tactics. I’m trying to avoid thinking about Mr. Davies’ history homework. It's due on Friday, and I haven’t even started the research on the suffragette movement. Ugh,  Davies . He’s the worst. He just expects us to  know  everything already. My nan was actually involved in some protests back in the day, she had loads of stories. Maybe I could get some first-hand info for mine? Really? That's amazing! That would be so much better than trawling through dusty old websites. Honestly, I just get overwhelmed trying to find reliable sources. Everything feels so biased. I know, right? It’s like, who  do  you trust? Nan always said the newspapers back then weren’t exactly fair to them either. She used to talk about getting arrested and everything. It sounds scary, thinking about it now. Wow. I’d love to hear more about that sometime. Maybe we could work on our homework together? Misery loves company and all that. Plus, two heads are better than one - especially when one of those heads has a protesting grandmother! Definitely! We could do it tomorrow after school? And then maybe we can finally start planning what we’re actually going to  do  in London? Mum said she's tentatively booked the train tickets for the Easter holidays, but we need to make a list of things we want to see. Ooh, yes! London! I’ve been making a secret Pinterest board for months. We  have  to go to a proper theatre show. And that new exhibition at the Tate Modern – the one with the surrealist paintings? Yes to both! Though a theatre show will be expensive… maybe we can look for discounted tickets? Or a matinee performance? And we definitely need to factor in time for shopping on Oxford Street, even if it’s just window shopping.

Now, this Facebook…you say everyone’s on it? Even young Timothy next door, the one who used to collect bottle caps? Everyone, Arthur. Honestly. Even  I  have a profile, though I mostly just look at pictures of grandchildren. And cats. Mostly cats. It’s just…how people stay connected now, Grandad. It’s where people share things, news, photos… build communities. It’s how I keep up with old university friends. It can be a bit of an echo chamber, though. Everyone just reinforcing what they already believe. You get algorithms feeding you stuff… Algorithms? Is that like…a complicated clockwork thing? Sounds right unpleasant. I still prefer a good postcard. You know where you are with a postcard. A proper stamp and everything. Oh, postcards were lovely, weren't they? Remember when we used to get them from your sister in Bournemouth, Arthur? Always pictures of the pier. Aye, Beatrice loved her piers. Said the sea air was good for her rheumatism. Though I always suspected she just liked the amusements. Now, speaking of things I don’t understand… this ‘OCD’ you were talking about, Sarah. Is that a new illness? Sounds dreadfully modern. It’s not new, Grandad, but understanding of it is better now. It stands for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. It’s essentially…intrusive thoughts that cause a lot of anxiety and then compulsive behaviours to try and manage the anxiety. It's more than just being tidy, though that’s a common misconception. It can be really debilitating. I had a student last year who struggled badly with it. Couldn't leave the house without checking the cooker was off five times. Five times! Good gracious. Sounds exhausting. We used to have a neighbour, old Mr. Hemmings, who’d always have to…well, tap the gatepost three times before coming into the garden. I just thought he was a bit…peculiar. Probably was, Arthur. But maybe it gave him some comfort. It’s funny, isn’t it, what people latch onto? Reminds me of when little Emily got chicken pox. She didn't itch terribly, but she  had  to have me read her that same bear story, “Paddington and the Marmalade Sandwich”, every single hour. Drove me round the bend, it did. It’s a coping mechanism, isn’t it? Finding something that feels safe and predictable when things feel chaotic. It’s interesting how those things manifest.

Right, who wants gravy with their roast? Honestly, this smells amazing even  I  say so. Though, after a day on the ward, anything smells amazing.      Ooh, definitely gravy. Yorkshire puddings  need  gravy. And maybe a bit extra on my roasties, please, Sarah. You know me.      Yorkshire puddings are a national treasure, Chloe. Don't skimp on the gravy. Though, truthfully, I'm just happy to be here. A Sunday roast at home beats anywhere.      Definitely. It’s nice to just…be. No deadlines, no client calls, just family and good food. So, Dad , how was your week? Still wrestling with that shed build?      Wrestling is a good word for it, love. That wood doesn’t want to be where I want it to be. It’s possessed, I tell ya! And your mother here keeps offering advice I didn’t ask for.      Oh, don’t start, you two. Someone has to use their common sense around here. Besides, I’m just trying to prevent structural collapse. Remember what happened to Old Man Hemmings’ shed?      Hemmings’ shed? That thing was held together with hope and rusty nails. A good gust of wind was all it took. Sarah, is that rosemary in the potatoes? Smells delicious.      You have a good nose, Liam. It is. Reminds me of that holiday we took to Germany, doesn’t it? All that rosemary and garlic.      Germany… now there's a thought. We haven’t been back since… what was it, ’98? When the kids were little?      I remember that! We tried to teach me a bit of German before we went, but I could only say ‘Ich bin ein Berliner’ and look confused. It didn't go down well when I tried asking for chips.      Classic Chloe. Anything’s a chip opportunity for you.      You know, their accents are fascinating, aren’t they? Especially the way they roll their ‘r’s. I tried to mimic it once, ended up sounding like I was gargling with gravel.      Oh, Geoff, you  always  try the accents. You were terrible at the Italian one on our honeymoon! Drove poor Antonio, the waiter, mad.      I always thought the Bavarian accent sounded a bit like… well, a slightly posh version of how some of the older lads from Faversham used to talk. That sort of drawn-out vowel sound.      You’re right, there  is  a similarity. It’s funny how regional accents can creep into everything, even perceptions of foreign languages.

…and honestly, the sound at that festival was atrocious. Like, genuinely awful. You could barely hear Leo’s vocals over the bass. Which, admittedly,  is  a pretty powerful bass, but still! It was a shame, I’ve been wanting to see them live for ages. Right? I heard similar things. Luckily, the recording of their set that floated around online wasn’t too bad. Still doesn’t compare to, you know,  being  there. Did you at least get to catch anyone else decent? Yeah, ‘The Static Waves’ were surprisingly good. I'd only really heard one of their tracks before, but they completely smashed it. The drummer was phenomenal - really intricate fills, loads of energy. Proper technical. Reminded me a bit of that guy, Ben, from uni – you remember him? Total stick wizard. Ben… the one who ended up joining that prog-rock band? Yeah, vaguely. Always seemed a bit too intense for his own good, if I’m honest. Good drummer though, can’t deny that. So, ‘The Static Waves’, you say? I'll have to check them out. I need some new stuff to listen to while I’m prepping veg. It’s all a bit… samey in the kitchen these days. Everyone’s on the same playlists. Definitely give them a listen. They’re a bit indie-rock, but with a bit of a post-punk edge. Anyway, enough about my weekend of questionable sound engineering. How’s work been? Still slinging amazing food at The Salty Crab? Still slinging. It's…busy. Summer season, you know? Tourists flocking in like seagulls. Honestly, I’m starting to dream in chips and tartar sauce. The Head Chef, Mr. Henderson, is putting me under a bit of pressure to come up with a new special, though. Something seasonal. Oh, right. He always did have high standards, Henderson. Remember when he sent back your soufflé during your trial shift? Brutal. Don't remind me! I nearly walked out then and there. But I needed the job. Still… it’s good experience, I guess. It's definitely keeping me on my toes. I was thinking maybe something with sea bass and samphire? It’s all locally sourced. That sounds… actually really good. You’re way more creative than you give yourself credit for. I struggle to come up with exciting things to eat, let alone  make  them. Speaking of needing experience, have you thought any more about that internship at the restaurant in London?

Honestly, Liam, this place is  always  busy. You’d think for being tucked away like this, it wouldn't be such a scrum. And the music...it's like trying to have a conversation in a tin can. Mmm? Yeah, it’s a bit loud, Mam. But the coffee’s good, isn’t it? And at least it's warm in here. It was brass monkeys out there. Good coffee doesn't compensate for shouting across a table, love. I was trying to tell you about Mrs. Henderson. She rang this morning, practically in tears. Apparently, young Ethan’s failed his maths mock. The pressure these kids are under, it's awful. Oh, aye. Ethan's a bit of a worrier, isn't he? Still, plenty of time before the real thing. Did you tell him to just go over the basics again? Of course. I did. I also suggested his mam and dad maybe ease off a little. They're driving him into the ground. Now, speaking of driving… we need to sort out the transport for this weekend. Are you still wanting to go to Durham with Gran and Grandad? Definitely. It’ll be good to see the Cathedral again. And maybe get some decent trainers. Mine are falling apart. Remember that shop we went to last time, near the market place? The one run by that bloke who always tries to upsell you? Lord. Right, I’ll add trainers to the list. Speaking of lists… shopping list. I need to get bread, milk, eggs. And don't forget your sleeping bag for the summer holiday. Have you even thought about that yet? Er… vaguely? Is it the one with the dinosaurs on? Yes, Liam, it’s the one with the dinosaurs on. You’ve had it for three years. And it needs airing. Gran's offered to let us borrow one of the spare beds, but I think you’d rather have your sleeping bag, wouldn't you? It’s more adventurous. I suppose. It’s easier to build a fort with a sleeping bag. You and your forts. Always scheming. Did you hear about old Mr. Peterson? Apparently, he’s started a little business, making those scented candles. No way! Mr. Peterson? The one who used to complain about the noise from the domino drives at the community centre? The very same. Goes to show, doesn't it?

…and honestly, the recording quality is still dodgy. I’ve tried three different microphones, and I'm  still  getting that weird background hum. It’s driving me mad! It’s for my phonetics project, trying to get a really clear sample of West Midlands vowels. Yours, specifically. You and your vowels, Ben. Honestly, you were obsessed even  at  uni. Still trying to dissect how I say “bath”, are you? It’s just…how we say it. Never thought about it. It’s more than just “bath,” Tom! It’s the whole vowel shift. It’s fascinating! And I need a good, unadulterated sample. Everyone I’ve asked in Brighton’s either put on a performance, or has lived here too long and their accent’s softened. You’ve been back in Brum relatively recently, haven't you? Yeah, Christmas. Mum’s been…well, she’s thrilled, actually. Big news. Oh? Do tell! You've got that look. Something good, I presume? Good is an understatement. Sarah’s pregnant. Due in August. No way! Tom, that’s brilliant! Congratulations! I had no idea…Wow. That’s huge. How are you both feeling? Overwhelmed, mostly. Excited, definitely. Terrified is in there too, lurking. She’s been…not exactly  sick  sick, but having a rough time with the nausea. It’s been a lot. I'm trying to be supportive, doing all the cooking and cleaning... which is a shock to my system, to be honest. I’m used to ordering Deliveroo. You’ll be brilliant. You always were a good sort. Though, cooking and cleaning? That's a serious shift from late-night coding sessions at Uni. Speaking of which, remember that awful flat we shared with Dave? The one above the chip shop? Don’t remind me. The smell of frying oil permeated  everything . And Dave's constant…experiments. I still have nightmares about the time he tried to make his own beer. Oh god! The explosion! That was a week of airing out the entire building. We were lucky the landlord didn’t evict us. This place is vastly superior, thankfully. Less aroma of potato and dodgy home brewing. Actually, talking of landlords… the post is a nightmare here. I'm constantly getting things delivered for the previous tenant. It's the bane of moving, isn't it? I had the same problem. Have you tried writing "Not At This Address" on them and sending them back?

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Even knowing it was what she  wanted . Saying ‘yes’ to assisted dying felt…like giving up on her, even though she was the one desperately fighting for control  through  it. It does, doesn’t it? That’s a whole other layer of grief, isn't it? The ‘should I have…’, ‘could I have…’ It’s exhausting just thinking about it. How are your kids coping? They were so close to Gran. Honestly? A mess. Tom’s burying himself in university work – all A’s, apparently, but barely eats. And Lily… Lily’s the quiet one, always has been. She’s just withdrawn completely. Won’t really talk about it, just stares at her phone for hours. I keep trying to gently ask if she wants to see someone, you know, a counsellor at school, but she just shrugs. It's good you’re offering, though. Even if she doesn't take it up now, knowing it's  there  is important. My Ben was like that when his grandpa went. Wouldn't say a word, just… shut down. Took him nearly a year to really start processing it. Teenagers are strange creatures with grief. They don’t do it ‘right’, whatever ‘right’ even is. Right? Everyone keeps saying "there's no right way to grieve", which is true, but it doesn't make it  easier . And it’s not just Mum, is it? Auntie Carol’s diagnosis… it feels like one blow after another. I know. It feels… relentless. Breast cancer again, is it? She’s a fighter, Carol, but… it’s different when it comes back, isn’t it? It loses that initial ‘we’ll beat this’ optimism. Exactly. And she’s trying to be so strong for the kids, particularly little Emily. It’s heartbreaking. She's still going to work full-time, trying to maintain some sort of normalcy. I tried to tell her she needed to prioritise herself, even just take a few weeks off, but she wouldn’t hear of it. Said she needs the distraction. Sounds exactly like Carol. Stubborn as a mule! She always had to be in control. It reminds me a bit of what your mum was like towards the end, actually, that need to dictate how things went. It's a coping mechanism, I think. Trying to hold onto something when everything else is crumbling.

…and honestly, Mrs. Davies just doesn't  get  it. She keeps saying Year 10 is all about ‘solidifying foundations’ but it feels like relentless practice papers. No room to breathe, you know? Tell me about it. History is just dates. Dates, dates, dates. It’s so boring. Well, history  is  important, lad. Knowing where we’ve come from… it shapes where we’re going. Though I agree, rote learning isn’t the most engaging method. It’s alright if you like wars and kings. I’m more into coding. That's actually useful. Coding  is  useful, Liam. Very useful. Though, dates help you understand  why  those wars happened, don't they? It's all connected. Anyway, how was tennis practice, Alex? Did Coach Mark give you a hard time today? He was on about my serve again. Said I’m ‘too tentative’. Whatever that means. Tentative means you’re not committing, son. You’re holding back. He wants to see you really  hit  it, with confidence. Like a proper forehand in the football. You need to put your weight behind it. Your father’s good at analogies, isn’t he? Though, I still think a tennis serve is a very different beast than a football kick. It’s all about technique, the wrist… Tennis is alright, but football is where it’s at. We won 4-1 today. I scored two. Show off. It’s just facts! Good for you, Finn. Speaking of things 'where it's at,' I was reading an article earlier about the… well, the whole referendum business again. Seems like everyone is still passionately divided. Don't get me started. It's a mess. It feels like the country is still trying to figure out which direction it wants to go in. And the young people are the ones who will have to live with the consequences the longest. What referendum? The Brexit one? Yes, dear. The one about leaving Europe. It happened a few years ago, but the effects are still being felt. It's complicated. Complicated is an understatement. It's affected everything from trade to travel. It's something you two will be studying in school, I imagine. More dates to learn! Actually, it’s made me think a bit more about… well, Alex, you’re starting to think about what you want to do after school, aren't you? Have you given any more thought to apprenticeships?

Honestly, this is  lovely . Proper countryside whizzing by. Much nicer than staring at spreadsheets all day, eh? And miles better than the M1. Definitely. Though, spreadsheets are paying for this little trip, aren't they? Lancaster, of all places. You’ve really roped me into this uni visit with your cousin, Liv. Roped? Don’t be dramatic! Liv’s really excited to show us around. And it'll be good for you, getting a feel for things. You are thinking about a Masters, right? This could be a sneaky reconnaissance mission. Sneaky is a good word. I’m still…undecided. It feels a bit soon after finishing my undergrad. Plus, the dissertation nearly broke me. I swear, for a month after submitting I just stared at walls. Thinking about writing  another  long piece of academic work feels…daunting. What about you? Still riding high on your postgrad glory? Don’t remind me! Honestly, the data analysis nearly did  me  in. But it’s done now, which is the main thing. And yes, I’m loving the work, though. It’s fascinating, really. I’m heading up a small project at the moment looking at dialect levelling in younger generations. It's… complicated. Dialect levelling? Is that like… everyone sounding the same? Kind of. It’s the idea that regional accents are becoming less distinct, especially amongst younger people who move around more and are exposed to different accents. I’m focusing on the East Midlands. My supervisor's keen on it. It’s a bit depressing, actually, when you think about it. Losing those little linguistic fingerprints. That is a bit sad, isn’t it? My Gran always used to say you could tell where someone was from just by how they spoke. She was from near the coast in Lincolnshire, proper flat vowels. She always used to go cockle picking as a kid. Oh yeah? Lincolnshire coast? I've only been once. We went to Skegness when I was little. Awful. Filled with arcades and…beige. Skegness is...an experience. She used to talk about the cockle disaster, though. That was horrible, wasn’t it? All those people, lost at sea. It really impacted the community. Gosh, I remember hearing about that. So tragic. Did it affect her directly? Not personally, but she knew people whose husbands and sons were out there. It changed things, she said. It made people very cautious.

…and then Liam just  insisted  on trying to do a backflip off the picnic table. Honestly, bless ‘im, he’s got the enthusiasm of a puppy, but the coordination of a… well, a very uncoordinated puppy. No way! Liam? That's brilliant. Did he land it? Or did he end up needing an A&E trip? Oh, it was a spectacular failure. Spectacular. He ended up tangled in the bunting Mrs. Higgins had put up for the village fete. She was  fuming . Apparently, it was hand-stitched. Oh, poor Mrs. Higgins, she takes her bunting very seriously. Speaking of fuming, have you heard from Chloe about the gig on Saturday? She said she was trying to get tickets for that new band, ‘Static Bloom’. Aye, she messaged me earlier. Said she managed to snag us some, thankfully. She's proper dedicated, our Chloe. Remember when she queued for  hours  in the rain for those Arctic Monkeys tickets, back when they were still playing The Leadmill? How could I forget? We all thought she was mad. Frostbite and all. Still, worth it, wasn’t it? They were class. Static Bloom are… different though, aren't they? More… indie-synth-pop, is it? Not really our usual. Yeah, a bit of a departure. But Chloe’s been banging on about ‘em for weeks. Said they're amazing live. Plus, it’s a good excuse to get out. I’m starting to feel like I’m turning into a hermit with all this revision. History essays are slowly sucking the life outta me. Tell me about it. Mine's all coding, all the time. I swear, I dream in binary. Honestly, sometimes I just want to chuck the laptop in the River Don and become a shepherd. A Doncaster shepherd? Now  that’s  a career change. Although, you'd probably end up coding a robotic sheepdog. Don't put ideas in my head! No, you're right. I’d build an app to optimise sheep shearing. It's inevitable. So, apart from Liam’s acrobatic mishaps and your historical woes, what’s been happening? Have you been doing any sketching lately? Not as much as I'd like, sadly. Been too busy drowning in books. Did a quick little charcoal study of Old Bess the other day, though. You know, the pub? The one down by the market. Old Bess? Nice! You always get the light just right on those sketches.

Right, okay. Disaster strikes again. Another two epidemic cards popped up. Honestly, this feels less like a cooperative game and more like actively trying to  lose  at saving humanity.      Tell me about it! You’d think, with six of us, we’d be able to contain this thing. But no, it’s spreading like wildfire. Honestly, I'm starting to suspect Bryn here is secretly a disease agent. He’s  too  calm about it all.      Oi! That's rich coming from the man who seemingly has a personal vendetta against eradicating the blue disease. You've hoarded those cure cards like they're gold!      Well, someone has to! You’re too busy jetting around the world, building research stations in places nobody needs them. Honestly, Sydney as a priority? Bryn!      It's a strategic move, Rhys. Diversification of research. Spread the risk.      Right. Strategic. Or you just like seeing Rhys get flustered.      Oh, you two. Always at it. Honestly, it's like watching a particularly competitive chess match. Though, I think the game is winning. We’re down to three cubes in Paris, and the black disease is creeping into Moscow.      Now, now, Eira, don't be so pessimistic. We've recovered from worse. Remember that time, during our last Pandemic session, when Sarah accidentally triggered  three  epidemics in a row?      Oh, don’t remind me. That was… a dark day for humankind, simulated or otherwise. I was still pretty new to the game then. I thought 'event cards' were just…positive things. Lesson learned.      You thought an event card could  give  you a cure? Bless you, Sarah. You're a good teacher, but a terrible Pandemic player.      Hey! I've improved since then! I’m strategically… allocating resources now. Mostly to preventing Rhys getting to the blue cure first.      It's not about  getting  to the cure first! It's about saving the world! Though, admittedly, bragging rights are a nice bonus. Speaking of, does anyone have a city card for Atlanta? I desperately need to move my researcher.      I might. Let me check. Hmmm… no, sorry. Bangkok, Cairo, Chicago… plenty of exotic locales, but no Atlanta.      I’ve got one! But… I need it for a direct flight to San Francisco. We really need to get a research station out there. The yellow disease is exploding.      It's a tough call, Eira. But San Francisco is definitely a hot spot.

Right, so, Mother’s Day is looming. And after that…well, after that it's  your  birthday, isn’t it, Lily-Rose? Mmm-hmm! I’m gonna be seven! Seven is a  big  number. Bigger than six! Six  is  pretty big. I’m six. You are indeed a very important six-year-old, Leo. And Lily-Rose, seven  is  a big number. We need to start thinking about what kind of party you want. Do you want a princess party? A superhero party? A…CBeebies party? Ooh, a CBeebies party! Can we have…can we have the Numtums come? And maybe Andy from Andy’s Adventures? He knows  all  the animals! I want Bing! Bing is funny. He gets really cross sometimes, but then Flop makes him better. Well, getting the Numtums and Andy to a party in Comberton might prove tricky, darlings. But we can certainly decorate with CBeebies characters! Remember that panto they did last year? The one with all the presenters? Oh! The one with Mr Tumble and JoJo and YolanDa? It was SO funny! Mr Tumble kept losing his Spotty Bag! And JoJo was a really good prince! He wasn’t scared of the dragon! He wasn’t, was he? That panto was a bit of a lifesaver during December. Kept us all entertained. Speaking of entertaining, have you seen the new series on CBeebies, ‘Bluey’? It's Australian, apparently. Bluey? No. Is it good? Does Bluey have a magic wand? No magic wand, but she’s a very adventurous little Blue Heeler puppy. It’s about family life and playing games. It’s actually quite sweet, even for me! Though, honestly, sometimes I think all children's programmes just blur into one. All bright colours and relentlessly positive messaging. Oh no! My tower! Oh dear! Never mind, Leo. Accidents happen. We can build another one. So, back to the birthday… Lily-Rose, you were saying seven is a  big  number. What makes it big? Because when you’re seven, you’re almost eight! And when you’re eight, you’re almost a teenager! Grandma says teenagers wear makeup and listen to loud music. Well, your Grandma does like to exaggerate. You’ve got a good few years before you’re remotely interested in loud music or makeup, I think. But it’s good to have goals! We should probably think about what you want for your birthday too.

…Honestly, I still can’t believe you’re actually considering moving to  Hereford . Of all places. It’s…rural. Even for you, considering your childhood. Rural is precisely the point, Liam. You know I grew up surrounded by fields. It’s… calming. London’s starting to feel like a pressure cooker. And the house prices are insane. I saw a tiny flat in Clapham the other day that cost more than your entire flat, and it didn’t even have a garden. She’s not wrong about the prices, Liam. It’s gotten ridiculous. I'm starting to look at places further out myself, though not  quite  as far out as Hereford. Maybe something in St Albans. Commutable, still has some life… St Albans is just…expensive commuter-land. And Hereford? What will you  do  all day? Write articles about prize-winning pumpkins? Very funny. There's a surprising amount of local government activity, actually. And the  Hereford Times  is looking for a local affairs reporter. It’s not exactly frontline war correspondence, but it’s a start. Besides, I can work remotely for some of my other clients. That’s sensible, Amy. Don’t give up the freelance work entirely. It’s a lifesaver. Though, honestly, finding reliable broadband in the countryside is a whole other battle. Speaking of battles, how's the dating scene been? Still wading through a swamp of ‘gym selfies and vague professions’? I swear, that app is designed to induce existential despair. Don’t even  mention  it. I think I’ve mastered the art of the polite ghost. It’s less messy than actual rejection, for both parties. Though, I did have one promising conversation with a…beekeeper. A beekeeper?! That’s…different. Are you allergic to bees? That's a crucial first question. I asked! Thankfully, no. He seemed…nice. A bit… intensely passionate about honey. He sent me a seventeen-paragraph email detailing the different pollen counts. It was a bit much. Seventeen paragraphs about pollen? Right. That's a hard pass. Look, you need someone who understands the nuanced agonies of a good engineering problem, not the intricacies of apiculture. You're suggesting Amy needs a fellow intellectual, Liam? That narrows the field considerably. You know she enjoys a man who can talk about something other than stress and strain analysis. Fair point. I am a bit…focused. But seriously, escaping London doesn’t magically solve relationship problems.

Sarah     Denise     Chloe        …and honestly, my Nan used to make the  worst  Battenberg. It was always dry as a biscuit. But she insisted it was ‘traditional’. Said I wouldn't understand ‘proper baking’. Honestly, it tasted like sawdust and marzipan had a fight.      Oh, Nans and their ‘traditional’ recipes! Mine was obsessed with trifle. Layers and layers of sherry-soaked sponge, and always,  always  too much custard. It was less a dessert and more a structural engineering project.      Mine just made rock cakes. Literally, you could break a tooth on them. But you ate them anyway, out of politeness. Did anyone else get those little plastic toys inside Christmas crackers that were utterly useless? I always coveted the little plastic trumpets… but they’d break within five minutes.      Oh, the trumpets! Yes! And the paper hats. Always too small. I remember getting a tiny plastic comb once. A comb! What was I meant to do with  that ?      I was all about the little puzzles. The ones you had to try and assemble, but the pieces never quite fitted. It was infuriating. Speaking of infuriating, did you two ever try to learn French at school? Because I  clearly  did not.      Oh god, yes. Madame Dubois was terrifying. She had a ruler and wasn't afraid to use it. I remember being permanently confused by the genders of everything.  La  table,  le  chaise… it made no sense!      I was better at it, I think. I had a pen pal in France for a bit. A boy called Jean-Pierre. We mostly just exchanged pictures of our cats and… questionable teen fashion choices. But it helped with the speaking, I suppose. It's funny, though, isn't it? How much of what we learn at school just…vanishes?      It’s a sieve, isn’t it? I can barely string a sentence together in any language other than Lincolnshire English, and even  that’s  changing. I was talking to my nephew the other day, he's at university in London now, and I barely understood half the slang he was using. He was going on about being “peng” and "bare"... I just nodded and smiled.      Oh, the London lot and their slang! It's another language entirely. It's fascinating though, isn't it, how dialects change even within relatively small areas? My gran used to use phrases I’ve never heard anywhere else. Specifically related to the farm, I think.

…and then the seagull  actually  tried to steal Dad’s sandwich right off his plate! It was audacious, honestly. He barely even flinched, just glared at it. Classic Dad. He'd probably argue with a seagull about rightful ownership of a ham and cheese. So, was the whole caravan park as… lively as that first encounter? Lively is one word for it, love. Chaotic is another. Honestly, I haven’t seen that many floral shirts since the 80s. And the bingo… oh, the bingo. It was  fierce . Fierce is an understatement, pet. Old Mrs. Higgins nearly took out Brenda with her dabber. Brenda was complaining for a good hour afterwards. Said she’d seen action in the war less stressful. Oh my god! You’re making it sound like a proper scene. Was the weather at least decent? That’s all I really care about, honestly. Did you get some sun? The weather was… changeable. Started off lovely, sunny, a nice breeze. Then it rained for a full day. Absolutely  poured . We were stuck in the caravan playing cards. Your father nearly cheated at Rummy again. He  always  tries to cheat at Rummy. It’s a family tradition at this point. Did you manage to get down to the beach much, though? You mentioned wanting to collect shells. We did, on the good days. The beach was lovely, really. Long stretch of sand. Though mostly populated by children building sandcastles and those aforementioned floral shirts. I did manage to find a couple of decent shells, actually. Got them here somewhere. Ah, here we are. Not spectacular, but… a reminder. Those are nice! Really pretty swirls. You always find the best ones, Mum. Remember when we were kids and we’d spend all day on the beach building ridiculous sandcastles? How could I forget? Your father insisted on building a fully functional – or attempting to - replica of the Tower of London. It lasted about five minutes before the tide came in. That sounds about right. He's always been overly ambitious with sandcastles. Did you do any of the touristy stuff? Like visit the local town or anything? We went to Whitby, that was nice. Very picturesque. Lots of steps though, which nearly killed me. And the fish and chips were… underwhelming. Overcooked, I'd say. I’ve had better down in Sale, honestly. That's a bold claim, Dad! Whitby fish and chips are supposed to be legendary.

Right, this coffee is  essential . Didn’t sleep a wink, honestly. Old Mrs. Higgins’ boiler decided to throw a tantrum last night. Emergency call-out. Oh, no. Not again? That woman seems to specialise in boiler emergencies, doesn't she? Honestly, you’d think she deliberately… Don’t even start. She’s got a whole network of local handymen on speed dial, just waiting for the next crisis. It’s a lifestyle choice, I reckon. Speaking of crises, did you see what that… what's-her-name, the actress, did last night? At the awards show? No, thankfully. I was elbow-deep in cold water and furious metal. Which actress? Don't tell me it’s another wardrobe malfunction. Worse. Apparently, she dedicated her award to her… aura reader. And then proceeded to explain how the aura reader told her she was destined for greatness. No way! An aura reader? Seriously? The lengths people go to… It’s all over Twitter, naturally. Headlines like “Is Aura Reading the New Acting Coach?” Sounds about right. Sometimes I think people just  make  things up for attention. Now, focusing on things that are actually real – anyone fancy trying that new ramen place that opened up near the station? I finally looked at the menu online, and it looks decent. Oh, I’ve seen that! It's supposed to be amazing. I’m in. Though, potentially, also terrifyingly spicy. I’m a bit of a wimp when it comes to chilli. Count me in too. I’m doing a piece on new restaurants in the city, actually. Could be good content. Though, I need to finish interviewing that tech entrepreneur first. He’s convinced he's going to solve the housing crisis with… wait for it… vertical farming in repurposed shipping containers. Vertical farming? In shipping containers? That's… ambitious. Sounds like something straight out of a sci-fi film. Is it even practical? That’s what I’m trying to find out. He’s very confident, let’s put it that way. Spouting numbers about yields and sustainability. I suspect there’s a hefty funding round involved. It's surprisingly hard to get a straight answer out of people when money is involved. So true. People will say anything to secure investment. Speaking of money, I’m seriously considering taking on some extra tutoring to boost my savings. The price of flights to Italy this summer is ridiculous!

…and honestly, the satnav just decided I was going to drive  through  Mrs. Higgins’ garden. Like, actively routing me through her prize-winning roses. I had to override it three times! No way! You and technology, eh, Chloe? You always have these stories. I swear, Google Maps is usually spot on for me, though. Unless I’m trying to get anywhere near Dad’s, then it thinks the roads just…vanish. Aye, Google Maps is alright. Though, I still reckon a good old-fashioned map is best. You can  see  everything, know where you are. These things just tell you what to do, no understanding of the actual landscape. You lads are young, always relyin’ on these gadgets. Back in my day, we navigated by the stars and a decent compass! Though even I have to admit, the wife uses a satnav, and saves me a good argument about which way to go to Skegness. Skegness? Oh god, are we finally talking about going with Mum and Dad this year? I was hoping this meal was a strategic delaying tactic. She’s been hinting at it for weeks. Says Dad’s been particularly down lately and a trip to the seaside would cheer him up. He does seem a bit…off, doesn't he? More quiet than usual. Though he’s always been a bit of a grump, to be fair. He misses work, that's what it is. Being retired doesn’t suit everyone, you know? Used to havin’ a purpose, a structure. It's like taking a ship out of dry dock and just lettin’ it drift. Speaking of purpose… how’s the project going, Liam? The one in Saudi? You were saying it was a bit of a nightmare last time we spoke. It's… interesting. It’s definitely not what I signed up for. The cultural differences are…significant. And the bureaucracy! You wouldn't believe the paperwork just to get a simple meeting arranged. Saudi Arabia, eh? Bit hot for me. Give me a damp November day in Peterborough any time. I had a stint there meself, years ago. Different world entirely. Remember to respect their customs, son, and don’t even  think  about drinkin’ in public. Learned that one the hard way. Oh wow, Reg, you were  in  Saudi? Doing what? Different job then, of course. Royal Navy. We were helpin’ with training their coastal patrol forces.

Honestly, Astrid, this is exactly what I needed. Just…green. And quiet. Though ‘quiet’ is relative with you two around, isn’t it? Oh, you know us, Hamish. Can't help but fill a silence. Though, I have to say, Stockholm’s botanical gardens are exceptionally good at absorbing sound. It’s remarkable. Have you seen the Victorians’ glasshouses? They're doing a fascinating thing with humidity control to recreate tropical environments. They are. I was reading about the system – apparently, the principles are surprisingly simple, just incredibly precise. It reminded me of trying to get the orchid to bloom back home. You need the  exact  right conditions, or it just…sulks. Sulks is a good word for it. Mine just decided it preferred death. Which, frankly, feels a bit dramatic for a plant. Speaking of dramatic, how are you managing, Beatrice? Still battling the sniffles? You sounded dreadful on the phone last week. Oh, it was a beast, honestly. A proper head-cold. I tried everything. Vitamin C, zinc, lemon and ginger…the whole shebang. I practically lived on hot toddies. It’s finally clearing, though thankfully, before half-term. Can’t face a classroom full of ten-year-olds with a hacking cough. You're a braver woman than I am, teaching primary school during flu season. It's a biohazard! It really is. You lot are national heroes, honestly. Though, honestly, hot toddies sound appealing  regardless  of a cold. I’ve been feeling…off, myself. Just a general lack of oomph. I keep thinking it's the jet lag finally catching up, but it’s been a week now. Jet lag can linger. Are you sleeping alright? You were working right up to the last minute before you left Wellington, weren’t you? Burning the candle at both ends, as usual. Probably. That new venture is all-consuming. Trying to get the funding sorted is… exhausting. Though sleep's not the problem, strangely enough. I'm sleeping  too  much. And then feeling utterly drained when I’m awake. Have you had a check-up, Hamish? Just to rule things out? Don't be silly and think you’re invincible. You’re not getting any younger, you know. Don't remind me. I know, I know. It’s just… doctors. I always feel like I’m wasting their time. And the waiting rooms…ugh. Nonsense. It's prudent. And there are some very good GPs here in Sweden, actually.

Honestly, Siri just  cannot  cope with my accent. I asked it to set a timer for five minutes and it thought I said "fish fins"! It’s ridiculous. Dad, you don’t have this problem, do you? Your voice is… well, very BBC English. BBC English? That’s a bit much, darling. It’s just… clear. People understand me. You lot all mumble these days. All this estuary English. Sounds like you’re swallowing half the words. Oh, leave her alone, George. Estuary English is perfectly fine. It's natural. And it's not  just  young people, either. It’s changed things, hasn’t it? Even I sound different to how I did as a girl growing up in Harlow. Yeah, it’s just how people talk now innit? Like, I can switch it on if I need to for a job interview, but… why bother otherwise? Saves effort. It’s not about effort, Liam! It's about being understood by technology! And sometimes, by people who aren’t used to hearing it. Remember that professor at Uni who kept asking me to repeat myself? He was convinced I had a speech impediment. Speaking of things being misunderstood… how are things with Mark? Still… frosty? Don’t. Please. He did send a rather grumpy text about Poppy having too much screen time yesterday, didn’t he? I saw it pop up on your phone when you were in the kitchen. Right, well that's none of your business, is it? He's just… difficult. He’s convinced Poppy’s becoming addicted to Minecraft. Says it’s rotting her brain. Minecraft's wicked, though! You can build anything. I spent hours on that when I was a kid, back at Gran’s. Remember her house? Absolute chaos, it was. Full of clutter and cats. Your grandmother was a character, that’s for sure. Never a dull moment. Though I remember her mattress was something else. Felt like sleeping on a bag of rocks. Actually, speaking of mattresses, I've been looking at getting a new one. This one’s ancient. My back is killing me. You definitely need a new one, love. You’ve been saying that for months! I work with people with back problems all the time, it’s horrible to see. You need proper support. Have you thought about a memory foam one? They’re alright, but they get proper warm, don't they?

Honestly, Leo, you’d think grating cheese would be a universally understood skill at your age. It’s not  rocket science . Are you trying to take your knuckles with it again? It's…harder than it looks. And it keeps slipping. Mum, it’s really slippery cheese. There you go. See? Angle it slightly, firm pressure,  away  from you. Not towards. We don’t need a trip to A&E because of a block of cheddar. Okay, okay. Sorted. Are we still doing Baked Alaska for Halloween? That's ambitious. Ambitious, yes. But you promised to help with the meringue. And it’ll be  spectacular . Remember Mrs. Higgins’ face last year when we did the spiderweb cake? That was worth all the effort. She nearly screamed. It was good. Will we have lots of people at the party? We’re hoping for a good turnout. I’ve put posters up at school, and I’m sending out invites tonight. I’m trying to get a few of the older kids to help with supervising, you know, keeping an eye on the little ones. It’s a nightmare recruiting responsible teenagers these days. They all want to be DJs or influencers. Finn said he’d help. He’s good at making spooky sound effects. That’s lovely. Finn’s a good lad. Honestly, though, trying to get anyone to volunteer for anything is a struggle. It wasn’t like this when  I  was your age. We were always being roped into something. Remember Old Man Hemmings needing help with his garden every summer? Mr. Hemmings? The one with the really big roses and the even bigger dog? I remember you being terrified of Buster! Terrified is an understatement! He was a beast. But Hemmings was a good sort, always had a sweet for us. It’s funny, the things that stick in your memory. It feels like yesterday I was chasing you around this very dining room, trying to get you to eat your broccoli. Broccoli is evil. Still. Actually, talking about memories… Dad was showing me some old photos the other day. Of you when you were a kid. You had  really  bad hair. My hair was  not  bad! It was…stylish for the seventies! And your father says that just to wind me up. He was the one with the questionable fashion choices. Bright orange flares, remember those? He said they were ‘groundbreaking.’

…Aye, this is proper good toast, mind. Not like that pale stuff they try to pass off down south. You’ve still got a knack for it, Eluned. Oh, hush now, Bronwyn. It’s just bread, toasted. Though I am pleased you approve. I did buy that proper butter, the West Country one, remembering how much you like it. West Country butter  is  a step up. Though nothing beats a good Yorkshire curd, if you can get it. Remember Old Man Hemmings? Used to sell it at the market in Saltaire… Anyway. New York. You were saying about New York? Oh, yes! I was telling Gareth about it yesterday, actually. The museums were incredible, naturally, but it was just the  energy  of the place, you know? Non-stop. And the bagels… honestly, I think I lived on bagels and coffee for a week. It’s just so… loud. Loud’s good sometimes, isn't it? Gets the blood flowing. I've never been, you see. Always meant to, but something always came up. Always teaching, or marking, or… well, life. You planning on going back anytime soon? Not immediately. It was a work trip, and frankly, a bit exhausting. Speaking of exhausting, I keep seeing those adverts for flying lessons at Fairwood. Have you ever considered it? Flying lessons?! Eluned, are you daft? Me? In a tiny aeroplane? I'd rather wrestle a badger. Absolutely not. I’m quite happy with my feet firmly on the ground, thank you very much. Though… young Tim down the road, he’s been going for a while. Says it's exhilarating. Exhilarating and terrifying, I imagine! I just… I always thought it would be freeing. A different perspective, you know? Like when we were living in Japan. Remember the train journeys? Seeing the countryside just  fly  past. Though that was marginally less risky. Japan…now there's a place. We were bairns when we went there, weren’t we? Still finding our feet. That little ramen shop in Kyoto… that’s a memory I hold onto. It's funny how some smells just transport you straight back. Speaking of holding onto things, have you seen when the refuse collection is this week? I don't want to be caught out. It’s Thursday for recycling, and Friday for general waste, I think. I’ve got it on the calendar somewhere… Oh, actually, I need to check.

Right, okay. This is…suboptimal. Honestly, I think I’ve been cursed by the Scrabble gods. Again. "Q" without a "U" is just cruel, isn't it? Serves you right for being late, Leo. You missed tile distribution. Karma, darling, karma. Besides, you always get the dodgy letters. It’s a running joke. Late? He’s  always  late. Remember that time in first year, Leo, you missed your 9am lecture because you were convinced it started at ten? Professor Davies was not amused. Okay, okay, I get it. I’m perpetually tardy. It wasn’t  entirely  my fault this time! The train was delayed. Seriously delayed. Apparently, a sheep wandered onto the tracks. A  sheep , Ben! You can’t make this stuff up. A sheep? That's… distinctly Welsh. Fitting, considering we're in Wales playing Scrabble. Though, honestly, a delayed train is hardly a new excuse, is it? It’s a legitimate excuse! And it’s not like I do it on purpose. Honestly, I'm starting to suspect I have some kind of internal clock malfunction. Maybe you just need to rethink your entire morning routine. Speaking of routines… did you finish that reading for Semiotics, Leo? The one on the etymology of words? Almost. I got stuck on the section about the word ‘disaster’. Apparently, it originally meant ‘ill-starred’ – relating to the position of the planets. It’s fascinating, but also slightly terrifying that we blame cosmic forces for things going wrong. Sounds about right. My nan always said if you broke a mirror, you'd have seven years of bad luck. Superstition runs deep, you know? And speaking of words, did anyone else notice how ridiculous English spelling is? Like…'though', 'through', 'tough', 'thought'. What even  is  the rule? It’s a historical mess, isn’t it? All those Norman French influences. We just kind of… cobbled it together. Plus, you’ve got people like Samuel Johnson deciding which spellings would stick. Absolute power corrupts, even in lexicography. It's funny, isn’t it? My little sister is learning to spell, and it's just… relentless. "Is it 'ei' or 'ie'? Why is there a silent 'k'?" It's exhausting. She prefers picture books anyway. She’s obsessed with 'The Gruffalo’ at the moment. 'The Gruffalo' is a classic! Julia Donaldson is a genius. My younger cousin used to demand it be read to him at least five times a day.

Lovely cuppa, eh, Margaret? Just what a body needs on a day like this. Feels right chilly, even with the fire on. It is nice, Arthur. Though I think you put a bit too much milk in again. It's practically beige. Beige is a perfectly respectable colour! And I like a creamy tea. Reminds me of me nan, she used to make it just the same. Thick enough to stand a spoon up in, she did. Your nan could get away with murder. She had that way about her. Remember when she convinced the butcher to give us extra sausages 'cause it was young Timmy's birthday? Even though it wasn’t? Oh, I do! Old Mr. Henderson, bless his soul, didn’t stand a chance. She had a gift, that woman. A real gift for getting what she wanted. Though, I reckon I get me charm from her side o’ the family. Charm? Arthur, you once tried to barter a chipped teacup for a new set of gardening shears. A minor setback! And that teacup was  vintage . The man clearly had no appreciation for quality. Anyway, what are you knitting now? Another one of them colourful blankets for the grandchildren? Yes, this one’s for little Lily. She loves purple, the clever thing. It's rather fiddly, this pattern, lots of little bobbles. My fingers aren’t what they used to be, you know. Keeps me busy though. Better than just…sitting. Better than sitting and worrying, you mean. You still fretting about David? A little. He's been so quiet on the phone lately. Just…brief. Says he’s busy with work, but…he used to call just to chat. To tell me about silly things. Like what Brenda in accounts was wearing. Men! They're all the same. They get a bit of responsibility and suddenly they think they're too important for a good natter. He's prob'ly just got a new girlfriend. Arthur! Don't say things like that. Well, it's the truth, isn't it? They do. Still, he’s a good lad, David. A bit headstrong, like his father, but with a good heart. You raised him well, you did. I just worry. Things are so…uncertain these days. Everything feels like it’s changing so fast. Remember when life was simpler? When a holiday meant a week in Great Yarmouth, and the biggest excitement was winning a goldfish at the pier?

Right, that was… glorious. Absolutely glorious. Honestly, Sarah, you’ve outdone yourself with this roast. The gravy is particularly good. Is there… is there sherry in it? Glad you enjoyed it, Dad. Yes, a good splash of cream sherry. Old Mrs. Higgins, from the village, swore by it. Said it gives it a depth of flavour you just can’t get otherwise. And Carol, you barely touched your Yorkshire pudding! I’m saving room, dear. Honestly, I’m stuffed. It’s just… I’m trying to be a  little  more mindful. Started using that app, you know, the ‘StepWise’ one. It's infuriatingly cheerful, but it does guilt me into walking a bit more. StepWise? What’s that, some sort of fitness tracker? Waste of time, if you ask me. All these gadgets. I did just fine for sixty years without needing a blinking phone to tell me I haven’t moved enough. Though, I suppose a walk would have been good after all this… It’s not just a tracker, Dad. It links to your food diary too, so you can see where you’re going wrong. I’ve been using it a little and it’s actually quite helpful. Though I did have to lie about the biscuit consumption this afternoon. For science, obviously. Oh, you and your 'science'! It’s good to have a bit of balance, isn't it? Although, talking of biscuits… I saw old Mr. Peterson at the village shop this morning, looking absolutely furious. Apparently, they've put the price of digestives up  again . The cheek! Outrageous! Daylight robbery, I tell you. Everything’s going up. Still, at least we’ve got the promise of that new train station. Though, knowing our luck, it’ll never actually open. Remember all the fuss when they first announced it? Five years ago, was it? Seems like a lifetime. They said it would be open last summer, then this spring… Now they’re saying October. Honestly, I’ll believe it when I see a train pull in. It would make getting to Exeter so much easier, though. Especially for Carol and the school runs. It would be a godsend, wouldn't it? Although, I'm still not convinced it's going to be worth the disruption during the construction. Remember the traffic chaos for months? It took me an hour to get to the surgery last November.

…and honestly, the portion size was ridiculous. I ordered a burger, right? Standard burger, nothing fancy. And it came with, no exaggeration, a mountain of chips. Like, you could’ve built a small fort out of them. Proper Cornish portions, innit? You should come down to St. Austell sometime, we redefine ‘generous’. They practically  insist  you finish everything. Mum’d have a fit if you left a single chip. I appreciate the sentiment, but I think my arteries would stage a protest. It was good though, really good. Just… a lot. So, how was your weekend? Anything exciting happen down in the wilds of Wales? Besides battling chip mountains, of course. Pretty chilled, actually. Ben and I tried to get tickets to that new horror flick, ‘The Silent Echo’, but it was sold out everywhere. Annoying. We ended up just playing a load of FIFA. I absolutely  destroyed  him, by the way. Destroyed him? You and FIFA, name a more iconic duo. You’re relentless. I’ve been meaning to jump back into it myself, but Uni’s been… a bit much lately. That Shakespeare seminar yesterday was brutal. Shakespeare? Ugh. Still doing that? I thought you’d escaped that torture after A-Levels. Oh, I wish. It's part of my English Lit module. Yesterday was focusing on ‘Hamlet’ – specifically the soliloquies. Professor Davies decided to show us a clip of David Tennant doing it on the BBC. It was… intense, to say the least. Brilliant, obviously, but intense. David Tennant  is  good. Even when he’s brooding about being Danish royalty. Better than reading the stuff, I reckon. Though, to be fair, I haven’t willingly read Shakespeare since sixth form. I was more of a ‘notes’ kind of guy, remember? Winging it all the way. Oh, I remember. Your notes were… minimalist. A single word per act, if I recall correctly. "Death," "Revenge," "Bit depressing." Accurate summary! Speaking of depressing, have you seen what's going on with the Premier League table? My lot are properly floundering. I swear, if they don't sign a decent striker in January… Don’t even get me started. It’s been a chaotic season. I’m trying to remain optimistic about City, but even they’ve had a few wobbles. It’s wide open, which is… intriguing, I suppose. It's probably good for the league, keeps things interesting. Interesting for everyone except people who actually support teams!

…and honestly, the presentation could have gone  so  much better. Old Mr. Henderson kept interrupting with these really detailed questions about… spreadsheets. Spreadsheets, Liv! Like I'm some kind of Excel wizard. Oh, Henderson. He’s a menace. Absolutely a menace. Still, good on you for getting through it. Project Co-ordination sounds…stressful. Is it at least  interesting  stressful? Interesting is… a generous word. It’s mostly just chasing people for updates and trying to make sure everyone remembers what they’re supposed to be doing. It pays the bills, though, which is the main thing, isn't it? How’s the marketing world treating you, then? Still surrounded by influencers and avocado toast photoshoots? Sadly, yes. Though less avocado toast than you’d think. More…algorithm tweaking and painstakingly crafting captions for things nobody cares about.
