Though, we  are  launching a new campaign next month, focused on sustainable packaging. Which, I’m actually quite excited about. It feels a bit more…meaningful. That’s good! You need something meaningful. All that social media stuff can’t be healthy for the soul. Speaking of healthy… how’s your knee? Last I heard you were struggling with it after that netball match. Oh, it’s…okay. Still a bit dodgy going down stairs, which is a problem considering how much I seem to be navigating stairs these days. Physiotherapy helped a bit, but I think I just need to accept I’m officially getting old. Twenty-seven is the new thirty, apparently. Don’t be ridiculous! Twenty-seven is still practically a child. I’m twenty-four and I feel ancient sometimes, but that’s just because Mum keeps asking when I’m going to ‘settle down’ and find a nice young man. Oh, mothers. Mine's on the same wavelength. It’s always subtle digs about how all my cousins are married with kids. It’s exhausting. Have you… heard anything from Ben recently? Oh… um. No. Not really. He messaged me a couple of weeks ago, just to ask how things were, you know, ‘as a friend’. Very polite. Very… distant. Right. “As a friend.” The classic. That sounds pretty final. How are you, actually? You seem… quieter than usual when you mention him. I’m fine. Honestly. It’s just…weird, isn’t it? We were together for nearly three years, and now it's just… radio silence. We ended things amicably enough, I think.

Right, milk first for me, always. Though Mam always said that’s barbaric. She was a tea purist, you know? Hot water, bag, brew,  then  milk. Never the other way around. Oh, your Mam and her rituals. Mine just wanted it strong enough to stand a spoon up in. Different ends of the spectrum, aren't they? Though, honestly, I’m leaning towards your Mam’s method these days. Feels…proper. Are you still trying to get that Monstera to perk up? It’s looking a bit…dramatic. Dramatic is putting it mildly. It’s actively  sulking . I’ve tried everything! More light, less light, misting, talking to it… honestly, I feel like a right fool. It was thriving when I got it, all big, happy leaves. Now it's just…flappy and brown-edged. You’ve got the Midas touch with plants, what’s your secret? No secret, really. Just not overthinking it. People kill plants with kindness, you know? Too much water is the biggest offender. And they need to be repotted eventually. Have you checked the roots? Sometimes they get totally pot-bound and just…give up. I did repot it a few weeks ago, actually. Bigger pot, fresh compost… thought I was doing the right thing. Maybe I  over -composted it? Is that a thing? It can be. Too much feed can burn the roots. And what compost did you use? Some of that stuff is a bit…aggressive. Oh, God, I don’t even remember. It was on offer at the garden centre. Probably something super-charged. Right, noted. Less is more. Just like your cooking, actually. Simple, but always tastes amazing. I'm still dreaming about that roast chicken you did last month. That was nothing special. Just a good quality bird and some decent herbs. You make it sound like I’m a Michelin star chef. You're the baker in this house, though. Those scones you made for my parents…they were asking for the recipe for weeks. Aye, well, scones are in my blood. Mam made them every weekend, without fail. It was a whole production. Rolling pin, cold butter, precise cutting… she’d inspect them with a critical eye. If they weren’t perfectly round, they got binned. Absolutely binned. That sounds…intense. No room for imperfection! We were a bit more relaxed in my house. My Dad could barely boil an egg, so anything vaguely edible was celebrated.

Oh, this is… robust. Didn’t realise Brenda was experimenting with a new blend. How was your weekend, Gareth? Anything more exciting than battling the slugs in the vegetable patch? You know me, Alistair. Slug warfare is the highlight of my week these days. Though, I  did  manage to get the roses pruned. They were looking a bit unruly. Yours are always immaculate, I notice. What’s your secret? Beyond employing a small army of gardeners, naturally. No army, I assure you. Just a consistent schedule and a rather expensive organic pesticide. It’s a losing battle, of course. They always win eventually. Speaking of losing battles… did you see that game on Saturday? Absolutely dreadful. Which one? There were a few on. Though I confess, football isn’t my great passion. More of a rugby man myself. The Manchester United one. Honestly, the youngsters now… all flash and no substance. Rashford’s lad was pictured causing some trouble down in town, wasn’t he? A bit embarrassing for the club, and for the father, I imagine. It's becoming a pattern, isn't it? These footballers’ children seem to think they’re above the law. Aye, it’s the ‘second generation’ problem, isn’t it? They’ve grown up with privilege and don't understand the value of earning things. Reminds me a bit of the snooker players, actually. Ronnie O’Sullivan’s son is trying to follow in his footsteps, but it’s a completely different game for those kids. No grit, no hunger. That’s a good point, Gareth. The hunger is key. Though, I suppose it's hard to replicate a truly difficult upbringing. My own father, growing up in Cairo… well, that was a different world entirely. No silver spoons there. He’d have had a fit if I’d even  thought  about complaining about a lukewarm cup of coffee. Your father sounds like a character. Mine was a miner, down in Tredegar. Hard man, but fair. Always said a good day's work never killed anyone. He’d be horrified by some of the excuses these students come up with for late submissions. Tell me about it. The justification letters alone are a work of fiction. ‘My grandmother’s goldfish was unwell’. Honestly. I've started marking, and it’s… disheartening. The standard seems to be slipping year on year. I spent two hours yesterday trying to decipher a particularly convoluted essay on post-structuralism.

Honestly, this week has been  exhausting . Mr. Henderson is breathing down my neck about the quarterly reports, and honestly, I think he just enjoys making life difficult. It’s like he actively seeks out things to nitpick. Is Mr. Henderson the grumpy man who smells of old paper? That’s… surprisingly accurate, actually. Yes, that’s him. He  does  smell of old paper. And disappointment, probably. Morning, you two. What’s the Henderson-related drama this time? Sounds serious. Just the usual. Reports, deadlines, soul-crushing bureaucracy. It’s nothing new, darling. Though, this time he questioned my font choice.  My font choice , Liv. Seriously? The font? That  is  petty. What did you say? I calmly explained the rationale behind using Arial, highlighting its readability and accessibility. He just muttered something about needing to ‘project a more dynamic image’. Honestly, the man lives in the 1980s! Arial is nice. It’s… sensible. Like when Grandma knitted me a sensible cardigan. Exactly, poppet. It’s sensible. Now, enough about work. We need to finalise plans for Millie’s Christening. Have you spoken to Auntie Carol about doing the flowers, Liv? Yeah, I did yesterday. She's happy to. She’s got that amazing garden, so she’s thinking lots of wildflowers and greenery. She was asking about the colour scheme, though. Did you have something specific in mind? I was thinking something pastel. Maybe a pale lavender and cream? Not too fussy, you know? Millie’s first birthday party was a pastel explosion, I don't want it to look like a repeat. And we should definitely get that cake from Mrs. Peterson, the one with the sugar roses. She’s amazing. I liked the pink cake! It had sprinkles! You did, didn’t you? Perhaps we can have a small pink cake  as well , just for you. A little side-cake. Good idea, Mum. That’ll avoid a meltdown. Have we figured out the guest list properly? I think Grandpa's trying to invite half the village. Don’t even mention it. He keeps adding names. I had to tactfully explain that the village hall only holds a certain number of people. He’s convinced Cousin Brenda’s third husband deserves an invite, despite us barely knowing him. Is Cousin Brenda’s husband nice? Does he bring biscuits? I've met him once, he was... quiet. I don’t remember any biscuits, to be fair.

Honestly, this weather is  shocking  for May. It feels like November out there. Remember that wedding, Sarah? Auntie Brenda’s? It rained sideways all day. Oh god, yes! And Uncle Derek’s wig nearly blew into the buffet. That was… a sight. Poor Auntie Brenda was mortified, but secretly amused, I think. Wig? What’s a wig? Is it like hair but… not on your head? It is, darling. It’s a bit like a hat, but made of hair. Some people wear them if their hair falls out, or just to try a different look. It was a very… dramatic look for Uncle Derek. He thought it made him look younger. It didn’t. No, it absolutely did not! Speaking of dramatic, how’s work, love? Still battling the teenagers trying to sneak energy drinks? You have  no  idea. Honestly, it’s exhausting. Had one trying to buy a can this morning with his little brother’s ID. So brazen! And then the manager wants me to upsell loyalty schemes… it feels pointless half the time. They just want the Red Bull. Oh, retail. It’s a special kind of… perseverance training, isn't it? I remember when I was doing my postgraduate research, I considered a part-time job in a shop just to have some 'real world' experience. Thank goodness I didn't. I’d have lasted about five minutes. Mummy, can I have another biscuit? Please? Of course, sweetie. You've been a very quiet builder. Right, so, New York. I've been having another look at hotels. Everything is so… expensive. I was hoping we could get something with a bit of a view, you know, overlooking Central Park? That would be amazing! But yeah, it’s going to be a hefty price tag. Maybe we could compromise and look for something a bit further out, but with good transport links? We could save a lot of money and still see everything. That’s sensible. We don’t need to be  in  the park to appreciate it. And we definitely need to factor in money for shows. I was thinking about trying to get tickets for Wicked. Wicked? Is that like a witch? A  real  witch? It’s a musical, darling. With singing and dancing, and a story about witches. A pretend witch. And we have to go to one of those proper American diners. The ones with the red vinyl booths and the mile-high pancakes.

Right. Okay. This is…this is it. The mess. Don't judge, honestly. It  looks  worse than it is. Mostly. “Mostly”? That’s reassuring, Liam. Looks like a small paper blizzard landed in here. What  is  all of this? Is this… all the data from the fieldwork? Yeah, pretty much. And the initial transcription notes. And about three different iterations of the coding scheme. And… honestly I’ve lost track of what’s what half the time. I’m starting to see numbers in my sleep, I swear. Oof. Okay, significant. You said your supervisor wanted a full breakdown of the thematic analysis by Friday, right? That’s… ambitious. Ambitious is an understatement. He wants a preliminary report, draft conclusions, the works. He’s all ‘push yourself, Liam, reach your potential!’ Easy for him to say, he’s not staring into the abyss of qualitative data. Classic Professor Davies. Always encouraging the existential dread. So, what’s the biggest stumbling block? Is it the sheer volume, or are the themes just… muddy? It’s a bit of both, to be perfectly honest. The interviews were good, really good. But people are… messy, aren’t they? They bounce around, contradict themselves, and then try and backpedal. Coding it’s been a nightmare. I started with a really tight, structured scheme, but it just wasn’t  fitting  the data. So I loosened it, then it felt too broad. Now I think I’ve got something workable, but I’m terrified I’ve missed something crucial. Show me. What’s the current coding scheme looking like? Maybe a fresh pair of eyes…a geographically opposed pair of eyes, seeing as you’re proper Northern and I’m a London boy… can spot something? Alright, here. So the main themes are… ‘Sense of Place,’ ‘Community Resilience,’ and ‘Perceptions of Change.’ I’ve then got a bunch of sub-themes under each of those. Like, under ‘Sense of Place’ I’ve got ‘Local Identity,’ ‘Nostalgia,’ and ‘Attachment to Landscape.’ It feels… okay. But I'm not fully convinced. Hmm. ‘Perceptions of Change’ feels a bit broad, doesn’t it? Especially considering you're looking at the impact of the new developments on the local area. Maybe break that down further? Like ‘Economic Impacts,’ ‘Social Disruption,’ and ‘Environmental Concerns’? That’s… actually really good. I hadn't thought of splitting it that specifically. It makes a lot more sense.

…and then, honestly, I was presenting to a room full of…garden gnomes. All judging my quarterly report. Little knitted hats and everything. It was terrifying. Garden gnomes? Seriously, David? That’s a new one. You and your work stress manifesting in bizarre dreams. I had one last night where I was trying to teach a class of squirrels Shakespeare. Mummy, Mummy! Look! It’s a dragon! A  fire  dragon! Oh, wow, Lily! That’s amazing! Is he breathing fire at the garden gnomes? No! He’s breathing fire at the bad guys! I want juice. And I want a biscuit. Right, juice and biscuits it is. I’ll sort that. It’s funny, isn’t it? How vivid dreams can be. I woke up genuinely stressed about disappointing a bunch of ceramic ornaments. It is. I think it’s because they tap into all sorts of anxieties. The squirrels were definitely representing overly critical parents, I reckon. And the difficulty of getting anyone to appreciate iambic pentameter. Speaking of anxieties… I was looking at houses again online last night. Ones with bigger gardens. Oh-oh. Here we go. The ‘bigger garden’ equals ‘dog’ conversation, is it? Maybe. I just…imagine us with a dog. A big, goofy Labrador. Running around in a proper garden. It seems…nice. We could call him Winston! No! Sparkles! A sparkly dog! A sparkly dog, right. Look, we’ve talked about this, haven't we? It’s not just the garden, it's the time. And the money. And frankly, the sheer responsibility. You know how chaotic mornings are  now  getting these two ready for school. Add a puppy into the mix… I know, I know. It's just… a little part of me keeps picturing it. I saw a listing for a place near the park in Comberton, four bedrooms, decent garden… it was way out of our price range, obviously. Everything is way out of our price range around here! Comberton is lovely, but it’s ridiculously expensive. Although… I did see something about the Lottery increasing again. Maybe… just maybe… You’re suggesting we rely on the Lottery to fund our dog and dream house? Just saying, a girl can dream! And if we did win, you bet I'd be getting that Labrador, and you could have a garden big enough to get lost in. Honestly, I’d probably quit teaching.

Honestly, I’m still aching all over. It feels like I’ve been run over by a bus, not just…tripped over a rogue paving slab. You’re still going on about that? It happened yesterday, love. I thought you were being dramatic  then , but you’re milking it now. Though, to be fair, it  was  a particularly nasty slab. Really sticking up. Someone needs to report that. Milking it? Milking it?! I nearly broke my wrist! And my knee feels like it's full of gravel. I definitely considered A&E, you know. Properly. A&E? For a grazed knee and a slightly sore wrist? Seriously, Elsie? They’re swamped as it is. You’d have been sat there for six hours, next to someone with something  actually  serious. Well, it  felt  serious at the time. I thought I’d done something proper. Remember how I went pale? And I couldn’t even  bend  my fingers? You always go pale when you graze yourself. It’s a family trait, isn’t it? Remember when your grandad scraped his elbow gardening? Turned whiter than a sheet. And you could bend your fingers, you dramatically flexed them while complaining about the pain. That's different! He’s…grandad. It’s an age thing. And I wasn’t dramatically flexing, I was testing the range of movement! It's important to assess injuries, you know. I’ve read things. Being a Corpus Administrator, I deal with medical texts all day! I'm basically a semi-professional medical expert. Right. A semi-professional medical expert who almost went to A&E for a scrape. Look, I’m glad you’re okay, genuinely. But A&E is for emergencies. Broken bones, head injuries, things like that. Not…tripping. Okay, okay, I get it. But it really did hurt! And I’m worried about internal damage to my knee. You can’t  see  inside, can you? What if I’ve torn something? Elsie, you’d know if you’d torn something. You’d be unable to walk. You’ve been perfectly capable of getting to the shops, complaining about the price of bread, and generally being a menace all morning. That’s because I’m pushing through the pain! Brave face and all that. I’m trying to be stoic. It’s a North East thing, you wouldn’t understand. Down south, you’re all soft. Oh, here we go. The North-South divide.

… Honestly, the state of things. Another reshuffle. Do they  ever  actually get anything done, these politicians? Feels like rearranging deckchairs on the Titanic, doesn’t it? Titanic’s a bit dramatic, Arthur, isn't it? Though, I grant you, watching them is… exhausting. All promise and no delivery. Heard on the radio this morning they’re still arguing about the fishing quotas. Absolutely ridiculous. My brother-in-law, Colin, well he’s beside himself. Says it’ll ruin his livelihood. Poor Colin. He's a good man. Always willing to lend a hand. It's the small businesses that always get squeezed, isn’t it? Speaking of which… I was thinking again about that idea I mentioned. The tutoring centre. Oh, right. The one for the older students? The ones who need a bit of a boost for their A-levels? Exactly. I’ve been doing a bit of research. There’s a real gap in the market around here, you know? Plenty of places for the little ones, but once they hit sixteen, it’s much harder to find focussed, individual support. Especially in maths and sciences. I was thinking, a small room, maybe three or four students at a time… I'd do the teaching, naturally. You’d be brilliant at it, Arthur. You always were a fantastic teacher. The kids loved you at the school. Still talk about your physics demonstrations, apparently. Mrs. Higgins told my daughter just last week. But…starting a business, that’s a different kettle of fish altogether. It’s not like marking essays and setting exams. I’m not completely daft, Geoffrey. I’ve thought about the practicalities. The initial investment, finding a suitable space…that’s where I was hoping you might be able to lend your expertise. You always had a good head for figures. And knowing the local council rules… that’s a minefield. Flattery will get you everywhere, my friend. I  am  rather good at navigating bureaucracy, I’ll admit. Though I’m a bit rusty these days. Been more focused on keeping the shop afloat than starting new ventures. Things have been…quiet, as you know. Still, I’m happy to have a look at your numbers, see what it would take. That would be wonderful, Geoffrey. Truly. I haven't got a detailed plan yet, just a few scribbles in my notebook. I was thinking of starting small, just evenings and weekends.

…and honestly, the floral wallpaper in here is a  choice . It feels like my nan's living room, but…with more sticky floors. It’s…characterful. Woolwich pubs are rarely minimalist chic, are they? More ‘lived-in’, shall we say. It's a proper boozer, that's for sure. Remember that place near Mum's, The Red Lion? Even more floral. Oh, God, The Red Lion. That was an experience. Though, I think their roast potatoes were genuinely legendary. Right, food. Are we doing food here? I’m starting to feel a bit peckish. They’ve got a menu, I think. I glanced at it. The usual pub grub. Burgers, fish and chips… maybe a pie? I'm not ravenous, but a bit of something would be good. What are you leaning towards? Hmm. Pie is always tempting. Though, I had a rather substantial lunch, thinking I wouldn't need dinner. Famous last words. Is that…is that  Happy Valley  on the telly? It is! Didn't realise they were rerunning it. Sarah Lancashire is incredible, isn't she? Absolutely phenomenal. That final series was…intense. Intense is an understatement! I was practically hiding behind the sofa for the last two episodes. The way she portrays Catherine Cawood…it’s just brilliant. Properly raw. She’s got that incredible ability to convey everything with just a look. It makes me think about university, actually. Remember that acting workshop we both took as an elective? Utterly mortifying. Oh, don’t! I’d blocked that out. You and your…method acting. Trying to  become  the chair. Hey! It was about embodying an inanimate object! It was a challenge! Although, in retrospect, probably best I stuck to admin. What did  you  get up to in that workshop? I mostly tried not to make eye contact with anyone. I remember feeling desperately self-conscious. I was never comfortable with being…performative. Which is ironic, considering I spend my life listening to people  being  performative and writing it down. True. It's a strange job, transcribing. A sort of…professional eavesdropper. Do you still get interesting cases? Some. Mostly it’s endless meetings about marketing strategies. Thrilling, I assure you. Though, I did have a rather dramatic police interview last week. Quite a lot of shouting. Good practice for a bit of  Happy Valley  immersion, I suppose. Are you cold? You’ve got that thin coat on again.

…ach, it was mental, honestly. The midges were somethin’ else. Like a grey, buzzy cloud followin’ ye around. I thought I’d be driven daft. Thought I was losin' the plot, I did. Midge season in the Highlands. A rite of passage, Jamie. You knew what you were signing up for. And you took your fancy camera with you, didn’t you? Worth braving the beasties for a good photograph? Aye, well. That's the thing, isn't it? I  thought  I'd be gettin’ a good photograph. I’d planned this whole shot, see? Loch Maree, sunset, that ruined castle silhouetted against the sky… postcard stuff. But the light was just…off. And every time I tried to set up, a midge was landin’ right on the lens. So, the Highland romanticism didn't quite pan out? Not even close. Ended up with about twenty blurry pictures of nothin’ much, and a serious itch. I swear, they were goin’ up my nose! And the rain came in, o’ course. It always does, doesn’t it? Goin’ for a weekend o' landscape photography, ended up shelterin’ in a wee bothy with a farmer and his sheepdog. Sounds…cozy. Did you at least get any decent photos of the sheepdog? They often have character, those old dogs. Actually, aye. Old Angus, that was the dog’s name, was a star. Perfect model. Stoic, weathered face… captured the spirit o' the Highlands, he did. Ironically, that's the best photo I got the whole trip. It’s up on my Instagram, if ye want to see. I’ll have a look later. I’m still trying to get the hang of Instagram, to be honest. It’s all a bit… ephemeral for me. I prefer printing things, having a physical record. Remember darkrooms? That smell of the chemicals… a proper sensory experience. I remember ye talkin’ about it. You were always the artistic one, weren’t ye? I’m more of a point-and-shoot kind of guy. Though I am tryin' to learn more. I've been watchin’ some tutorials online about composition. Apparently, the ‘rule of thirds’ is a big deal. It is a good starting point. But don’t get too hung up on rules, Jamie. The best photography comes from breaking them, from seeing things differently. Are you still using that Canon EOS you were telling me about? Aye, still got it.

Right, so this week is… a bit of a juggle, isn’t it? I've got that meeting with Mr. Henderson on Tuesday, the one about the garden club fundraising. Honestly, the man talks for  England . And then Nan's appointment on Wednesday. I’m driving her, naturally. She insists she's fine to get the bus, but you know what she's like. Oh, bless Nan. She’ll say she’s perfectly capable and then complain for a week about the youngsters being rude on the 38. Tuesday and Wednesday are fairly quiet for me, thankfully. Just lesson planning and marking. Although, little Leo drew a picture of me with six eyes today… I’m not sure how to take that as constructive criticism. Six eyes! Oh, Leo. He’s a character. Likely just experimenting with anatomy, love. Don’t read too much into it. It's just, thinking about everything… and then there’s the nursery situation. Have you had any luck with viewings? That’s what I wanted to talk to you about, actually. I called Little Acorns again this morning. Still a waiting list. She said they’re having an open day next Thursday, said I could pop along and have a look, no pressure. But the list is  long . Apparently, everyone wants Little Acorns. It’s the only one round here with a forest school area, you know? A forest school! That sounds lovely. A bit muddy, perhaps, but lovely. We didn’t have those when your father and I were picking nurseries for you. It was all brightly coloured plastic and sing-song routines. Goodness, thinking back… were you happy there, love? I was fine. It was… okay. Mostly I just remember wanting to come home. But honestly, for Oscar, I want something more. Something where he can actually get messy and explore. It’s just… the thought of going back to work full-time and him being on a waiting list, or stuck in a place I’m not happy with… it’s awful. It  is  awful. Don't beat yourself up about it. It’s a perfectly normal worry. We’ll sort it. Perhaps we should look further afield? There’s that Little Sunbeams one near Sutton Coldfield, your Auntie Carol recommended it. I did have a look online. It's a bit of a drive though, isn’t it? And I’d feel terrible leaving Oscar with someone so far away.

Right, so you will  not  believe the day I've had. Honestly, it's been a proper circus. Old Mr. Henderson decided  today  was the day to complain about the canapés at the regional business awards… canapés, Liam! Like, seriously? Sounds about right for a business awards do. Always someone moaning about something. What was wrong with ‘em? Too much dill? Not enough prawn? He said the smoked salmon was “too pink.” Too pink! Like it’s a crime against nature or summat. I had to spend a good twenty minutes placating him while trying to sort out the AV setup 'cause the projector decided it didn’t fancy working. Honestly, I’m knackered. You always get the interesting ones, don’t you, Anya? It's the nature of the beast with events. I had a minor crisis at the factory today. Apparently, the new labelling machine is misprinting the batch numbers, and our quality control team are having a fit. Less…pink salmon complaints, more potential product recalls, though. So, swings and roundabouts, I suppose. Swings and roundabouts that give you grey hairs, more like! It’s just... draining. And people just assume because it’s ‘events’ it’s all glitz and glamour. They don’t see the frantic calls and the last-minute fixes. Did I tell you about the time the bouncy castle nearly took flight at the summer fete? No way! A bouncy castle taking flight? That  is  a story. Oh, it was terrifying! The moorings came loose in a gust of wind, and it was bobbing around like a giant, colourful balloon. Luckily, a couple of blokes managed to wrestle it down before anyone got hurt. But the look on the kids’ faces… priceless. And the complaints! “My juice went everywhere!” Honestly. Kids are brutal critics. You get used to it. Speaking of things going everywhere… how are things with Ben, Anya? You were looking a bit down last time we spoke. Oh, Ben. He’s…being Ben. It's just...he doesn't  get  my job. He keeps saying I should just “relax” and not stress so much. Like it's a choice! He thinks it's all parties and free canapés. He doesn’t see the pressure. And he’s started making comments on what I wear for work. What sort of comments? Oh, you know, “Is that really appropriate for a business meeting?” or “Are you sure that skirt isn’t a bit short?”.

…and that new fella at the shops, Doris, honestly. Barely a 'good morning' to be had. Used to be Old Man Hemmings, lovely chap, always a bit of a chinwag. This one just…scans yer groceries like you’re a nuisance. Oh, they’re all like that now, aren’t they, Arthur? No time for pleasantries. It’s all rush, rush, rush. Makes you miss the old days, doesn’t it? When Mrs. Gable used to run the village shop… she knew everyone’s business and a good brew was  always  on offer if you were feeling a bit poorly. Mrs. Gable… now  there  was a woman. Knew exactly how many sugars everyone took, even before they did! I remember young Timmy Harrison trying to sneak an extra biscuit, and she caught him every time. A hawk, that woman. But a kind hawk. Speaking of brews, Arthur, is this Earl Grey? It’s lovely. Not too strong, just how I like it. You always make a good cup, dear. Well now, Eileen, you’re a kind soul. It's Twinings, of course. Wouldn’t touch anything else. Got a special little tin, see? Keeps the flavour better. Doris here prefers builder’s, doesn’t she? Builder’s is perfectly respectable, Arthur! It’s a proper cup of tea. None of this fancy ‘darjeeling’ or ‘oolong’ nonsense. Gives you a bit of  oomph  to get on with things. Though, I must admit, Earl Grey  is  rather nice on a summer afternoon. It's all about the leaf, really. And the water, of course. Needs to be just off the boil, not a rolling boil, that ruins it. Learned that from my mother. She was a stickler for a proper cuppa. Used to say it solved all the world’s problems. Your mother was a wise woman, George. She always had tea ready for us when we were at the school fete. Remember how she'd do those little finger sandwiches? Cucumber and cream cheese… Ah, the fetes! That was a good time. Everyone together, raffles and cakes and dodgy coconut shy prizes. They don’t have them like they used to. Everything’s all…packaged now. No community spirit. Exactly! It's all online now, isn't it? Everything delivered to your door. Where’s the fun in that? I miss the days when you actually had to  go  somewhere, see people, have a chat.

Honestly, Mum, these are  exactly  how I remember them. Absolutely perfect. You haven’t lost your touch. Oh, stop it, you're making me blush. It's just a roast, isn't it? Though, I did use that Maris Piper variety you always said was best. I’ve been meaning to ask, how are things going with the new students, then? Any particularly…spirited ones? Spirited is one word for it. I have a student who insists on referring to Nietzsche as “Nick.” It’s…a choice. And another who tried to argue that postmodernism is just an excuse for not having a coherent argument. Oh, that’s brilliant! Sounds like you're keeping them on their toes. I had one last term who thought Foucault was a type of French pastry. You lecturers have all the fun. Dealing with complaints about broadband speeds all day is significantly less intellectually stimulating. Though, I did have a chap yesterday who was  convinced  we were deliberately slowing his internet down because he’d been to a protest. A protest? What about? Something about fracking, apparently. He was going on about corporate greed and the destruction of the Welsh countryside. Honestly, I just wanted him to reset his router. Oh, Caerphilly is lovely, though. I remember visiting with Dad when we were little. Such a beautiful place. Did your Auntie Brenda ever get that gallery space sorted? She was talking about it for ages. She did! Finally. She had a launch last month. Quite fancy, lots of local artists showcasing their work. It was a bit…intense, actually. Lots of very serious people talking about ‘the socio-political commentary’ in watercolour landscapes. Sounds about right. I went to a similar thing in Shoreditch last year. Everything was aggressively minimalist and overpriced. You could practically feel the artists judging your taste. Speaking of London, have you finalised that hotel booking for the conference, David? I thought you were going to try and find somewhere decent near the Southbank. I have. It’s…functional. Let’s put it that way. It was either that, or pay a king’s ransom for something with a view. Apparently, everything within a five-mile radius of the Tate Modern is now exclusively inhabited by hedge fund managers. It's ridiculous, isn't it? The prices in London. Remember when we could get a pub meal for under a fiver?  That  was a good time.

Right, operation unpacking is… underway. Honestly, the airport was a  nightmare . Did you even notice I was gone, or were you too busy saving lives? Saving lives is a strong term, but yeah, it was a busy week. I noticed! Missed having someone to yell at me for leaving mugs everywhere. How was Spain? Actually, don’t tell me it was all perfect sunshine and sangria. You always find  something  to complain about. Okay, you got me. The sangria  was  pretty good. But the hotel room was… aggressively beige. And there were these Germans who insisted on doing synchronized swimming in the pool at 7am. Synchronized swimming! Who does that on holiday? It felt like a personal attack on my sleep schedule. Oh my god, that’s brilliant. Synchronized swimming! You’re a magnet for eccentric holidaymakers, aren’t you? Anything else traumatizing? Not traumatizing, just… mildly irritating. The all-inclusive buffet was 90% different variations of ham. Like, smoked ham, glazed ham, ham with pineapple, ham pretending to be chicken… it was a ham-pocalypse. Sounds horrific. I mostly dealt with Mr. Henderson trying to convince everyone his toe wasn’t actually blue, it was just "a funny shadow." It took three nurses and a very stern doctor to convince him he needed to see someone. So, equally bizarre. Speaking of bizarre, how was Liam? I didn’t see any holiday snaps with him on your socials. Oh. Liam. Right. Look, it’s… complicated. We had a bit of a 'discussion' before I went away. A 'discussion' involving a LOT of raised voices and accusations about whose turn it was to empty the dishwasher. Apparently, that's a symbol of commitment issues. The dishwasher? Seriously? He broke up with you over the dishwasher? Not  directly  over the dishwasher. It was… a catalyst. Apparently, I’m ‘emotionally unavailable’ because I don’t find analysing cleaning rotas ‘stimulating conversation’. I mean, come on! That’s… ridiculous. He sounds exhausting. Honestly, you’re better off without him. Remember Ben? He always emptied the dishwasher without being asked. Ben, the saint. Although, I also remember Ben leaving his wet towels on the bed. Everyone has flaws. But Liam... he was just a lot. A lot of opinions, a lot of needing to be right, a lot of… beige. Just like that hotel room. Well, consider your life officially beige-free. So, good riddance to Liam and his dishwasher-related grievances.

…and honestly, seeing her yesterday, even with the positivity she’s trying to project, was just… gutting. She’s lost so much weight, hasn't she? And the fatigue. She just kept drifting off mid-sentence. It is awful, isn’t it? Sarah’s always been so vibrant, so  full  of energy. It’s just… cruel. Did she mention how the new chemo is going? She said it’s…managing the pain a little better, but the side effects are harsher this time. More nausea, she said. And the hair loss is progressing quickly. She was trying to make light of it, talking about beanies, but… you could see it was getting to her. It’s just not fair. We need to make sure we’re doing  something . Are we still on for next Saturday, taking round that lasagne? Definitely. And I was thinking, maybe a film night the week after? Something completely mindless, just to take her mind off things. Anything she's been wanting to see? I know she mentioned that new rom-com… the one with Ryan Reynolds? Oh, she’d love that! Yes, definitely. And maybe we could rally some of the others? Just… not a huge group. She gets overwhelmed easily now. Six, max, I think. Sounds good. Right. Distraction over, shall we attempt to be practical for five minutes? Have you had a look at that estate agent’s new listings in the village? The one I sent you the link to? Briefly. Honestly, my brain feels a bit mashed up thinking about mortgages and square footage right now. But yes, I skimmed. That Old Vicarage looks… promising? Though I suspect it'll be way out of our league. It's ambitious, admittedly. But have you seen the photos? That garden… and the potential for a study for you. It's got that lovely, south-facing aspect. It's about half an acre, apparently. Half an acre! That’s… a lot of mowing. And hedges. You know how I feel about gardening. You can hire someone! We’re lecturers, not subsistence farmers. We can afford a little help. Plus, imagine the space for the dogs. And think about having room for your mum to come and stay more often. It would be fantastic for her. That’s true. She’s been saying how she misses having a garden. She'd potter around for hours if she had one.

Right, I need a vent. Honestly, this job… it’s not  all  bad, but some things just get on my nerves something chronic. Go on then, Liam. Let it all out. Long day already, haven't it? What’s chewing at ya now? Is it another student trying to sneak a guest in past curfew? Nah, not today. It's… the bins. Honestly, the bins. Students think they’re invisible, just chuckin’ stuff  around  the bins, not  in  them. Pizza boxes flyin’ about, half-eaten takeaways… looks like a bomb’s hit after a Friday night. And then  I  have to clean it up before anyone notices. It’s not in my job description, y’know? I’m a security officer, not a bin man! You’re telling me! It’s the same with the kitchens in the flats. I’ve seen sinks piled higher with dirty dishes than I’ve seen in a proper restaurant after a rush. They just… leave it. Like the cleaning fairies are gonna come and sort it. Cleaning fairies? More like long-suffering Life Support Officers, eh? You get landed with all that then, do ya? A fair bit, yeah. I’m meant to be helping with wellbeing and stuff, offering support, you know, but half my time is spent chasing people up about fire alarms being disabled and encouraging them to actually  wash  their dishes. It's demoralising, honestly. They pay good money for this accommodation, you'd think they’d treat it with a little respect. Respect seems to be a lost art these days. It’s not just the mess, though, is it? It's the entitlement. They think they can just do whatever they want and there’ll be no consequences. Had one lad last week trying to argue that he should be allowed to have a party at 3 am because “it’s his birthday”. Oh,  don’t  get me started on the parties. It’s a constant battle. Last weekend, I had to break up a gathering in Block C. They’d propped the fire door open with a chair! Honestly, it’s terrifying. What if there actually  was  a fire? Exactly! They don't think about that, do they? They just want to have a laugh, consequences be damned. And they always act so surprised when you ask them to be quiet or follow the rules. Like  you’re  the unreasonable one.

Honestly, it’s just  so  weird running into people from Kent when you're halfway across Europe. Like, in Bruges last year, I swear I saw Mrs. Higgins from down the road, queuing for waffles. Waffles! She hates waffles. Bruges is full of tourists, love. Bound to bump into someone. Though Mrs. Higgins and waffles… that  is  a bit of a shock. Reminds me of old man Peterson. He swore black and blue he'd never go near a package tour, then Doreen dragged him on one to Italy. Came back raving about it. Oh, package tours aren’t so bad, Dad. Especially if you’ve got bad knees like Doreen. Makes life easier. Though I preferred Antwerp, didn't we have a nice time in Antwerp last December? The Christmas markets were lovely. Antwerp was good! But the traffic was mental. Driving into the city centre was a nightmare. Brighton’s bad enough, but that was another level. You needed a nerve of steel just to get to a chocolate shop. Brighton traffic is a joke compared to London, you know. Used to take me an hour just to get across town. Still, Antwerp… nice buildings. Trying to understand the signs, though. My Flemish is a bit rusty, and that's putting it kindly. Never really needed it past ordering a beer. Well, you always excelled at  that  part, didn't you? I'm trying to learn a bit of Dutch, actually. Duolingo. It's… slow going. All those rolled 'r's! Good for you, darling. It's good to keep the brain active. I tried to learn Italian for that holiday to Tuscany, but it just wouldn’t stick. Ended up pointing and smiling a lot. Pointing and smiling gets you surprisingly far. Speaking of keeping the brain active, Gran was showing me photos from her trip to Herne Bay last week. She said the shopping was amazing! Apparently, there's a new market there. Herne Bay? Still a bit of a dump, isn’t it? Though I suppose it's improved a bit since… well, you know. It used to be where we’d go when we were kids, though. Buying those stick of rock, always getting sand everywhere. It's nice for a day trip, Dad. And Gran loves it. She needed a bit of a cheer-up after… everything. Yeah. It's been hard. Mum's been trying to keep busy, organising Leo’s birthday.

Honestly, Mum, it’s just  everywhere  on TikTok. Everyone’s talking about this Irish equality vote. It's all "Vote Yes, Vote Yes!" But no one actually explains  what  we’re voting on, like, properly. Right, well, it’s a bit more complicated than just a ‘yes’ or ‘no’, love. It’s about expanding the definition of family, isn’t it? So it’s not  just  about marriage. It's acknowledging care work, and recognising different types of families. People who foster, cohabiting couples… that sort of thing. But isn’t marriage just… marriage? Boy and girl? That's what Mr. Henderson said in RS. He mumbled a bit, though, when Sarah asked about two mums. Oh, Mr. Henderson, does he? Well, bless his heart. It’s not just about ‘boy and girl’ anymore, is it? Times change. And it's not  just  about same-sex couples wanting to get married, even though that’s a big part of it. It's about legal rights and protections for everyone in a committed relationship, regardless of gender. It’s about fairness. Fairness… like when Dad ‘accidentally’ eats the last biscuit? Is this fairness like that? No, not  exactly  like that, though your father is a biscuit thief of the highest order. This is bigger. This is about the law treating people equally. Remember when your Auntie Carol was having trouble getting benefits for David when she was looking after him? Because she wasn't technically his 'parent'? This kind of vote could help with situations like that. Oh yeah, I remember that. She was fuming. She basically  was  his parent though, she was brilliant with him. Still is. So this vote would help people like Auntie Carol? It could. It aims to recognise the value of care, whether it's paid or unpaid, and who’s providing it. It's tricky to explain in simple terms. Honestly, even  I'm  still wrapping my head around all the details. Your Dad’s been reading articles on it for days. He's quite passionate. Oh god. Does that mean another one of his long lectures? “Now, Liam, as a responsible citizen…” Ugh. Actually, talking about responsible citizens... Have you remembered it’s Grandma’s birthday next week? Oh,  don't  remind me! She’s already started asking what we’re planning. She wants a full-blown party, like her 70th. You know she gets ideas from those daytime TV shows, and suddenly expects a string quartet and a chocolate fountain.

Cor, this is a good bit of cheese and pickle, Doris. Not like that plastic stuff they try to pass off these days. Reminds me of what your Mum used to make. Oh, she did a lovely cheese and pickle. Always a generous spread, she was. More pickle than cheese sometimes, if I’m honest! Though, honestly, Arthur, you'd eat anything if it was free. Now, now, that's not fair. I 'ave standards, you know. Though a good bit o’ cheddar never went amiss. Speaking of standards… did young Timmy ever get that lathe sorted? He was moaning about a blunt parting tool last week. Timmy? Yes, he did. Turns out it wasn’t the tool itself, but the angle he was holding it at. A quick call to old Mr. Henderson down the workshop and he sorted him right out. Said he was trying to force it, not let the tool do the work. Beginner’s mistake, apparently. Henderson, eh? Good man, Henderson. Knows his stuff when it comes to metalwork. I used to spend hours in old man Pruitt’s shed as a lad, watching 'im turn things. Fascinating it was. Proper skill. They don’t teach that sort of thing anymore, do they? All computers and… and TikToks. TikToks! Don't even get me started. Little Emily was showing me one the other day - some boy dancing with a loaf of bread. Honestly. What are we coming to? The world’s gone mad, Doris, absolutely mad. Although, I saw a rather clever one about the correct way to peel a mango… Mangos! Now there’s something I’ve never been keen on. Too… slippery. Give me a nice Granny Smith apple any day. You know, reminds me of a story… Old Mrs. Higgins, down the lane, she had this hamster. Little fluffy thing. Oh dear, where is this going, Arthur? Well, her grandson, little scamp he was, thought it would be a good idea to… warm it up.  Warm it up ? In the microwave! Honestly! Little bugger thought the hamster was cold. Doris, you won’t believe the commotion. The screeching, the flashing lights… Mrs. Higgins nearly 'ad a heart attack! Arthur! You are terrible! A hamster in the microwave?! Did it… did it...? No, no, it didn’t die, thankfully. Just… rather distressed. And smelling faintly of popcorn, apparently. Mrs. Higgins had to take it to the vet, they said it had a bit of internal bruising, but it recovered.

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of it! Charging five pence for a plastic bag. Five pence! Like it’s going to solve anything. It just feels… punitive. It’s behavioural economics, isn’t it? Nudge theory. Make people  think  about whether they need a bag, and they’ll take fewer. Though I agree, it feels a bit petty. It’s not like the supermarkets are passing the money onto environmental charities or anything. Petty? Oh, you young ones. When I was a headmistress, we had to fight tooth and nail for even a small grant for decent art supplies. Five pence adds up. And frankly, people have become far too reliant on disposable everything. It's a good start, if a small one. I suppose. Though I saw old Mrs. Higgins at the checkout looking utterly flustered, rummaging for reusable bags and muttering about socialism. It was quite a sight. Speaking of flustered, did you see that article about the cat that climbed into a delivery van and ended up eighty miles away? Oh, yes! Brilliant. Apparently, it was quite happy, just helping the driver with his route. A proper little adventurer. Better than my day, which was mostly spent battling with the bank’s online security. It’s designed to protect you, but it feels like it’s designed to frustrate you more. Don't even  start  me on banks. I was looking at remortgaging, and the interest rates are…well, they’re just taking the mickey. How are people supposed to get on the property ladder these days? It's laughable. Remember when house prices were sensible? Sensible. My dear, that was before my time, practically. Even when we bought this place, back in… oh, goodness, 1978? It was a substantial sum, but nothing like the prices now. And we had savings! People seem to rely so much on debt these days. It's the only way for most, isn't it? Unless you come from money. Which, let's be honest, most of us don't. I was reading about the… the mess in American politics again. Honestly, it's like a reality TV show. Don't even! I try to avoid it. It induces such stress. I'd rather spend an evening failing miserably at a cryptic crossword. That’s a much more rewarding form of frustration. I had one clue today: “Ancient city's restless spirit .”

Honestly, you two. Another evening glued to those screens? It’s lovely to see you enjoying yourselves, it really is, but haven’t you even  looked  at your books today? But Mum! Kai just unlocked a new Spinjitzu burst! It’s  amazing . You have to see it. I'm building a Nether portal! It needs obsidian. Lots and lots of obsidian. It took me ages to find enough. Obsidian… right. Sounds… thrilling. But remember that library book I got you, Leo? The one about the Roman forts? You were so excited about it yesterday. Yeah, but Romans don't have creepers. No, I suppose they didn't. Though, I imagine facing a legion of Roman soldiers could be pretty creepy too. Look, I’m not saying you can’t play your games, I just… I worry you're missing out on other things. Reading opens up whole worlds too, you know? Different kinds of worlds. Minecraft  is  a whole world, Mum! I’ve got a house, and a farm, and I'm building a railway to connect it to Isla’s village. Yes, I know it’s a whole world, sweetie. A digital one. It's just... It feels like every time I turn around, it’s Lego Ninjago, or Minecraft, or Roblox. It's wonderful you're creative with it, but it feels like that’s  all  it is. But it's fun! And you can play with your friends. Finn showed me this really cool redstone trick today… it makes a secret door! That does sound clever, I’ll give you that. Redstone… is that like wiring? Kind of. It’s like electricity, but in Minecraft. You can make things happen. Like, I made a trapdoor that opens when you stand on a pressure plate! Impressive. You’re both very resourceful. But what about using your imaginations in a different way? Remember when you used to build amazing dens in the living room with blankets and cushions? We could do that again. That was when I was little. You're not  that  little! And you both still love building, right? Lego isn’t just on a screen, you know. We've got that huge box of bricks upstairs, the one your Grandad gave you. That's… old Lego. It doesn’t have any minifigures with cool weapons. It has potential! You can build  anything  with it. A castle, a spaceship, a whole city!

Honestly, this is just what I needed. A proper cuppa and a bit of a natter with my girls. It feels like ages since we've all been together like this, properly. Not just dashing past each other. It  has  been a bit mad, hasn't it? Work’s been… well, work. Peak season at the shop is a nightmare. Mrs. Higgins complained about the font size on the sale signs  again  yesterday. You wouldn't believe. Oh, bless Mrs. Higgins. She's a character. Though I'm pretty sure the font size hasn't changed since last Tuesday. How was Greece, Mum? You were so quiet about it when you got back – just a general ‘nice’ which isn’t very  you . It  was  nice. Very nice. But… complicated. Old Mr. Davies was there. From university. Remember I used to talk about him? The one I had the massive crush on? Vaguely. The one who went into accountancy? Always seemed a bit… beige. Beige is a  very  apt description. He’s… still beige. But he’s also… very successful. And surprisingly lonely. He kept trying to, well, reconnect. It was a bit awkward, to be honest. All talk of ‘what ifs’ and ‘roads not taken’. I ended up spending most of the week avoiding the breakfast buffet. Oh, Mum! That sounds… intense. And a bit sad. I’m glad you had a good time  despite  Beige-Accountant. Did you at least get to see some ancient ruins or something? We did, darling, we did. Delphi was breathtaking. Absolutely stunning. But even surrounded by mythology, I kept thinking about how things could’ve gone differently, you know? It’s silly, isn’t it? After all this time. Not silly at all. I think everyone wonders that sometimes. Especially when someone from the past pops back up. It’s just… human. Listen, though, are we still on for that pottery painting thing this afternoon? I need a complete brain break after yesterday. Had a customer try to return a candle  they’d burned halfway down . Honestly! Ooh, yes! Pottery painting sounds fantastic. I haven’t done that in ages. I could actually use something creative to focus on. Uni's been essays, essays, essays lately. My dissertation is looming like a very judgmental cloud. Absolutely. Pottery painting is a perfect plan. I don’t think I’m quite up to the exertion of anything too strenuous, to be honest.

Ugh, honestly, this chicken salad is…ambitious. It tastes like someone’s nan made it, and not in a good way. Too much mayonnaise. You always complain about the sandwiches, Jamie. Last week it was “too much pickle,” the week before, “not enough lettuce.” Just eat it. We’ve got Physics revision to avoid, remember? It  is  a bit much, though. My tuna and sweetcorn is decent, actually. They’ve upped their game since last term. Remember when old Mrs. Higgins ran this cafe? Everything tasted faintly of lavender. Lavender! That’s horrific. Still, better than the school dinners. Seriously, they tried to serve us something labelled “mystery meat” last Tuesday. It was beige. Just…beige. Beige is the official colour of school food. It's a scientific fact, I'm pretty sure. Speaking of horrors, did you hear about the new History teacher, Mr. Davies? Apparently, he used to be in the army. No way! Really? How did you find that out, Leo? Old Man Hemmings, the caretaker, told me. Says Mr. Davies keeps talking about “strategic deployments” and expects us to address him as “Sir”. It's a bit much, even for a History teacher. That’s…intense. I can see the kids taking the mickey out of that immediately. Imagine him trying to get us to polish our shoes. It does sound a bit over the top. Still, as long as he’s good at explaining WWI and WWII. My grandad fought in WWII, you know. He never really talked about it, but my nan said it changed him. Mine's grandad fought in the Falklands. He's super quiet, always reading. He always carries a little compass. Said it helped him ‘find his way back’. Pretty sad, actually. It is. It’s weird, isn't it? How war impacts people for decades. Anyway, less depressing subjects. Anyone seen the new series of  Galactic Frontiers ? Oh my god, yes! It's amazing! Rhys is such a good villain. Although, I think Anya's character is a bit underdeveloped. They need to give her more to do. Rhys  is  good. He's got that whole brooding, mysterious thing down. It's way better than that other sci-fi show,  Starbound . So cheesy.  Starbound  is a classic! You just don't appreciate good, camp sci-fi, Jamie. It's the peak of entertainment. Classic trash, more like. Speaking of trash… did you see what happened with Ben Carter and the Prefects yesterday?

…and then Mr. Davies  actually  said, "Newton would be turning in his grave!" Honestly, it was over a slightly wonky graph. A  slightly  wonky graph! Like, it wasn't even drastically off, just… not perfectly aligned to his ruler. It's ridiculous. Oh,  please . Mr. Davies is the king of dramatic pronouncements. Remember when Ben spilled water near the electrical socket and he went on about potential electrocution and lawsuits? It was a tiny splash! True, true. But still! It’s frustrating. He marks so hard on presentation. It’s supposed to be physics, not art! I understood the concept perfectly, the graph just… wasn’t pretty. He barely looks at the working. It's the same with Miss Harding in English. She's obsessed with semi-colons. Like, if you use a full stop instead of a semi-colon when a semi-colon  might  be acceptable, it's a mark off. It drives me mad! We're supposed to be analysing Shakespeare, not mastering punctuation minutiae. Oh God, don't even get me started on Shakespeare. I just… don’t  get  it. “Hark!” and “thee” and “thou” everywhere. It feels like a different language. I'm worried about the essay next week. She wants us to do a close reading of Lady Macbeth and… I just see a stressed-out woman. Exactly! She’s ambition personified, and a bit scary, yeah, but everyone bangs on about her guilt like it's the  most  original thing ever. And the reading lessons are so slow. We’ve been on three pages of  Macbeth  for a week! Old Man Hemmings in Year 9 reads faster. Honestly. And Mrs. Peterson, our form tutor? She's sweet, but she’s always asking about our 'emotional well-being' first thing in the morning. It’s a bit much before I've even had a chance to wake up. “How are we  feeling  today, children?” Like, I'm feeling tired, Mrs. Peterson. That's the feeling. Haha, yeah. She's trying, I guess. She’s new. Though she does spend ages talking about her cat. Marmalade, isn’t it? That’s the one. Honestly, sometimes I think Marmalade gets more attention than we do. Did you see Sophie Miller trying to flirt with James Davies in the canteen yesterday? Disaster. He completely blanked her and then started talking about quantum physics to Mr. Mitchell. Oh, no! Poor Sophie.

…and honestly, the library was  dead . Like, genuinely, two people in the entire postgraduate section. I managed to get a solid four hours in, which is a miracle. Needed it after that disaster of a pub quiz on Friday. Disaster is putting it mildly, Leo. You and Ben trying to argue about the capital of Burkina Faso for five minutes was…a choice. Did you at least win the bonus round? No! It was about 80s hair metal! Ben claimed to be an expert, then named three pop singers. I was mortified. You two are hopeless. Honestly. Though, I secretly enjoy watching you squabble. It’s entertainment. How was your weekend, Imogen? Apart from Leo and Ben’s public humiliation, of course. Busy, busy, busy. Wedding cake tasting for a couple getting hitched in August. It's horrifying how much fondant people want these days. My hands are still sticky. But, it's good money. I've actually been starting to look at flights… Oh? Anywhere exciting? You mentioned something vaguely terrifying involving castles last time? Transylvania! I found some ridiculously cheap flights to Bucharest. And I'm thinking of getting a train up to… Bran Castle. You know, Dracula's castle. Bit cheesy, I know, but I've always been fascinated with that area, and the scenery looks incredible. Transylvania, eh? Crikey. Be careful you don't run into any Strigoi. Strigoi? Right, are you launching into Australian folklore now, Rhys? Gotta keep you Brits on your toes. Strigoi are like, Romanian vampires. Nasty blokes. You need to know these things before you go gallivanting around spooky castles. We’ve got drop bears, you've got… well, bad pub quiz teams. It's all relative. Drop bears? Don't even joke! My cousin went to Australia and was genuinely terrified for the entire trip. She kept looking up in trees! She should be! They’re sneaky little devils. Nah, just pulling your leg. Honestly, it's a beautiful country. You should come visit, Imogen, after your Transylvanian adventure. I'd love to! It's just… expensive. And I need to save for, well, potentially very expensive eye surgery. Oh, right. The laser eye business. Seriously? You been looking into that for ages. Is it happening? Thinking about it. I had another consultation. Apparently, I'm a perfect candidate. The thought of not needing glasses is so appealing, especially when I'm trying to ice a three-tiered cake.

Right, so, this photo – honestly, Leo, you looked like a startled meerkat! And Maisie, bless you, covered head to toe in… what  was  that, exactly? Mud! It was  amazing  mud, Mummy. From the obstacle course! I went under the net and everything. I fell over. Lots. But I still finished! Even though my wellies felt… squelchy. Squishy is the word, darling. And yes, you were both brilliant. Though I’m still finding mud in the washing machine. Speaking of things covered in stuff… Did you two remember to tell Grandma about the party next Saturday? I did! I told her about the balloons and the cake, and that Uncle Ben might try to do a magic trick. Good girl. Your Uncle Ben’s magic is… enthusiastic, let’s say. I’ve told him no rabbits, though. Last time, the poor thing nearly had a heart attack. Now, let's talk music. I’m trying to make a playlist for the party. Any requests? No… questionable lyrics, mind you. Can we have the dinosaur song? The REALLY loud one? We can  consider  the dinosaur song, Leo. But perhaps not on repeat for three hours. Maisie, what about you? Anything you'd like to hear? Ooh! Can we have that song from Alice in Wonderland? The one with the Dormouse and the Mad Hatter? “The Unbirthday Song”? Of course! You've been obsessed with Alice lately. You were trying to have a tea party with the cat yesterday. He didn’t want cucumber sandwiches. He just wanted to sleep. Well, cats are like that. Right, playlist is taking shape. Now, about these photos… I was thinking of getting some family photos done professionally. Not just quick snaps on my phone. Something… nice. Maybe for Christmas cards? Do we have to wear matching jumpers? I  hate  matching jumpers. No matching jumpers, I promise. I was thinking more… casually coordinated. Maybe something outdoors? Comberton Woods would look lovely. Can I wear my fairy wings? And can we bring Bumble? You can  absolutely  wear your fairy wings, love. And Bumble is always welcome. But the photographer might not want him photobombing every shot. We'll need to negotiate. Can I be a knight? With my sword? And a shield? You can definitely be a knight, darling. We’ll have to be careful with the sword though, won’t we? No poking anyone. Speaking of things involving potentially dangerous objects… I’m thinking of booking another session on the aerial hoop.

Now then, this pizza's not bad, not bad at all. Though Martha used to make a right good one, she did. Used to put a pinch of nutmeg in the sauce, she did. Gave it a bit of…oomph. Oh, she did, Arthur. You’ve told us about the nutmeg a thousand times. It was lovely, though. Everything Martha made was lovely. Though I reckon this one’s pretty good too, considering it didn’t come from a proper Italian. It's a decent effort, yes. Though I suspect the quality is directly proportional to the amount of chocolate roulade we're about to demolish afterwards. Speaking of which, Lily, Chloe, are you two saving room? Hmm? Oh, yeah, definitely. Just…sorting something. Saving a tiny bit. It’s really rich, though, isn’t it? And I’m still a bit stressed about the Maths results. Results, eh? Now don't you fret about them, girl. I never did much for exams myself. Passed just enough to get by, and look at me now - livin’ the dream! Though admittedly, the dream involves a lot of telly and biscuits. Don’t encourage her, Arthur. It’s important to do your best, Chloe. Though, honestly, one exam isn’t the be-all and end-all. Remember your Auntie Susan? She completely bombed her history A-level, and now she’s a successful solicitor. That's true. It's more about resilience, isn’t it? Being able to pick yourself up. Though, Lily, you were saying earlier something about tweeting photos? What were you up to? Oh, just…a funny picture of Mr. Henderson’s hair. It was sticking straight up in the air. It looked like a dandelion clock. A dandelion clock! Good one! Old Henderson always was a bit of a card. Remember that time he tried to demonstrate a science experiment and set fire to his eyebrows? Oh, Arthur, don't start. Poor Mr. Henderson. He was a lovely man, really. A bit eccentric, perhaps. Though he did have a very unfortunate comb-over. It wasn't  that  bad. It just…moved in the wind. It certainly had a life of its own, I believe. Anyway, Lily, just be careful what you post online. You don’t want to get into trouble with the school. Speaking of which, I have parents’ evening next week. Another chance to hear about all the near misses and potential disasters.

Oh, blast it. I keep forgetting about the Cannon’s jump. It’s all so different from draughts, isn't it? You’re absolutely ruthless with it, Daniel. Gotta be, Mum! You've taught me enough about strategy over the years. Besides, you're a quick learner. You were saying earlier you remembered Grandad teaching you something similar when you were a girl? Oh, yes. Not  this  exactly. Grandad had a little board game, all worn and chipped. Something he brought back from… oh, now what was it? Not China, I don't think. Maybe India? He travelled a bit after the war. Anyway, it wasn't quite the same rules, more simplified. But the idea of protecting your General, that was always there. Speaking of travelling, did you see that piece about the weather in South Korea? Torrential rain, apparently. Poor things. Makes our little drizzle seem rather… tame. Yes, awful. Reminds me of that summer in ’68. Non-stop rain for weeks. Ruined the strawberry crop entirely. Though, to be fair, most of it was probably gone already. Slugs, you see. They had a field day. You're always talking about slugs, Mum. It's like a recurring theme in your life narrative! Have you thought any more about getting some of those copper rings for the strawberry beds? I have, I have. But they're so expensive, aren't they? It feels a bit silly spending a fortune on protecting a few berries. Though, thinking about it, the raspberries are doing rather well this year. You’ll have to come back and help me pick them when they’re ready. I’d like that. Anything to distract me from thinking about work, to be honest. Mr. Henderson was on at me all morning about call handling times. Says I’m not ‘optimising my efficiency’. Honestly! I’m talking to people with real problems, not robots. Sounds about right. Bureaucracy at its finest. It's why I'm grateful for the relative freedom of teaching. Though I did have a student today who argued that Shakespeare was ‘overrated’. Overrated? Shakespeare? The cheek! What did you say? I tried to steer him toward a bit of critical analysis, explained the historical context, the impact on the English language...He just kept saying it was ‘boring’ and preferred TikTok. TikTok! Is that what the young people are doing these days?

…and honestly, that Piotr, lovely boy, but he  still  confuses ‘used to’ with ‘be used to’. After all this time! I feel like I'm banging my head against a brick wall sometimes, even with the private students. It's rewarding, of course, but draining. How are your classes going, love? Anything particularly…challenging? Oh, don't even get me started. I had one student today, a young Korean guy, convinced that every sentence  needs  a subject. Trying to explain implied subjects in English…it was like explaining colour to someone born blind. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I'm actually teaching English or performing miracles. But it’s good money, especially with those student loans breathing down my neck. Student loans! Don't remind me. It's a scandal, isn’t it? My nephew, just finished his law degree, he's absolutely drowning in debt. He's looking at a lifetime of repayments. When  we  went to university, it was grants, a little bit of saving from my parents… nothing like this. I shudder to think what it'll be like for his children. It’s terrifying. I feel incredibly lucky my parents helped a little, but it’s still crippling. It definitely shapes your choices, you know? I wouldn’t have considered teaching abroad if it wasn’t for wanting to earn enough to chip away at it. Which, by the way, is partially why I’m here with you in Tarnow! It's significantly cheaper to live here than back home, and the work is…well, it's work. Tarnow. Not exactly the Riviera, is it? But lovely, all the same. Much more…relaxed than Cambridge. Though I do miss a proper cup of tea. This is… passable. So, you’re planning on staying here long-term? I don’t know about long-term. Maybe another year? It depends. I’m starting to think about pensions, which feels ridiculous at my age, but realistically, I need to start planning. The UK pension system is a joke, isn’t it? Especially for freelancers like me. I was looking at some Polish schemes, actually. They seem… surprisingly stable. Stable is good. You need stability. I’ve been trying to sort out my own pension, or rather, lack thereof, for years. It’s a nightmare. Never really worked, you see. Always dabbled in things, bit of translation, bit of tutoring… never enough to contribute properly.

…and honestly, the lecturer just kept going on about Bayesian statistics. Like, alright, it's important, but after an hour and a half, you just glaze over, yeah? It’s brutal. You still sticking with Maths then, Liam? No second thoughts? Nah, committed. Brutal as it is, I actually… enjoy the challenge, you know? Human Sciences sounds interesting, massively broad though, isn't it? What are you leaning towards specifically within that? Are you thinking Psychology, Sociology…? It’s the broadness that  is  the appeal, actually. I’m hoping to focus on the behavioural side of things, maybe with a bit of anthropology thrown in. Trying to understand  why  people do things, not just the equations of how things happen, if that makes sense. It feels… more relevant, I guess. Plus, less actual maths. Which, after A-Levels, is a definite win. Fair enough. Though you were pretty good at maths. Remember that integration problem Mr. Henderson set? You cracked that in like, five minutes. That was a fluke. Pure, unadulterated fluke. Anyway, enough about academic suffering. This mocktail is… surprisingly good. What are you having? Looks strong. It’s a Virgin Mojito. Thought I’d be sensible for once. We’re practically adults now, supposed to be making ‘responsible choices’ and all that. Though, seeing as everyone else here is on proper cocktails… it's testing my willpower. Tell me about it. My cousin keeps offering me a sip of his Old Fashioned. He's convinced it's the key to unlocking the secrets of the universe. Your cousin’s always been a bit… dramatic. Remember when he tried to make soufflé? The kitchen looked like a bomb had gone off. Oh god,  the soufflé . Mum’s still talking about it. He insisted on using, like, ten different cheeses. Apparently, it needed ‘complexity.’ It just needed proper instruction, and maybe someone to supervise. I'm a much better cook, you know. I can actually make a decent pasta carbonara. High praise! I can barely boil an egg without setting off the smoke alarm. I stick to things that come in boxes, generally. Or I just… don't eat. That's not a long-term strategy, mate. Honestly, I'll teach you. It’s not hard. We could even have a cooking competition. Loser buys the winner a pint… when we’re old enough, obviously. Deal. Though I'm already predicting defeat.

Honestly, Amelia, you’d think they’d have sorted this out by now. Another budget, another load of…well, fiddling about, really. Fiddling about? Dad, that sounds rather dismissive. It affects everyone, doesn't it? I was just reading something about the changes to National Insurance. It's all a bit opaque, to be honest. That's why I teach English, not economics. Opaque is a good word for it. Deliberately so, I reckon. Keeps folk from asking too many questions. Anyway, this NI increase… it’s meant to fund social care, they say. But where’s it  really  going? That's the question. When I was your age, National Insurance felt…solid. Like a promise. Now? It feels like a pot they dip into whenever something inconvenient needs paying for. You’re not wrong. It's hard to feel confident in those systems, especially when the news is constantly talking about mismanagement. I try to explain it to my students when we talk about persuasive language – how governments  frame  these issues to get public buy-in. It’s a bit cynical, I suppose. Cynical isn’t always wrong, love. I spent forty years looking at numbers. Balancing books. And governments… well, they’re not known for their balanced books, are they? It's always ‘borrowing’ or ‘future generations’. I remember when Thatcher… That’s another rabbit hole, isn't it? But the point is, there’s always a narrative. Always. And often, it’s a narrative designed to distract from the core issue. Like, they’re talking about helping families with the cost of living, but increasing taxes on working people at the same time? It feels contradictory. Exactly! It’s robbing Peter to pay Paul. And Peter usually ends up with less. See, and this is where it gets tricky. Income tax, National Insurance, VAT… it all feeds into the same big pot. Then they decide how it’s spent. Education, healthcare, defence… and, let's be honest, a fair bit gets swallowed up in administration and… well, I suspect some ends up in the wrong pockets. It’s just… the scale of it is so enormous. It’s difficult to grasp. I mean, I understand the principle of progressive taxation - those who earn more contribute more. But when you see the loopholes for corporations and the wealthy… Ah, loopholes! That’s where the  real  money is saved, Amelia.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I get is just  criminal . Like, people genuinely think replying-all to thirty people is a good use of anyone’s time. It's for a project that's barely started! Thirty? Oh, bless you. Sounds like a nightmare. Remember old Mr. Henderson at the school? He used to CC the entire teaching staff – and the  dinner ladies  – on anything remotely about the school fete. Anything. Oh god, that sounds chaotic. My boss, Sarah, she’s brilliant, she’s trying to get everyone to just… think before they email. She’s started these “Email Etiquette Tuesdays” - it’s slightly embarrassing, but genuinely helpful. Email Etiquette Tuesdays? That’s… something. Sounds very corporate. We just have passive aggressive messages in the staff room about people leaving dirty mugs. It’s a different kind of communication breakdown. Ha! Definitely a difference in scale. How’s school going, anyway? Still battling with Ofsted looming? Oh, don't even  mention  Ofsted. The anxiety is palpable. They've announced the date - the 18th of next month. Everything is just… tightened. No one’s smiling anymore. It’s all data, data, data. It’s exhausting just witnessing it, let alone  being  the ones inspected. That sounds awful. You always seem so calm though, I wouldn't have guessed it was hitting you so hard. Oh, I am. It's just...learned behaviour, I think. After thirty years in the system, you develop a sort of emotional armour. Inside, I’m flapping like a distressed pigeon, but on the outside, it’s all “Right, let’s review the safeguarding policy  again .” How’s Ben? Any progress on the flat hunt? Ugh, don’t even ask. It’s a disaster. Everything we like is either a shoebox or costs the equivalent of a small island. We viewed one yesterday - it had ‘potential’ apparently, which translates to ‘needs a complete gutting and a small loan’. Oh, those are the worst. ‘Potential’ is code for ‘prepare to spend every waking hour and all your money’. Have you tried looking further out of town? Maybe towards Wymondham? It’s a nice little place. We have, but the commute is killer. Ben's really trying to avoid going back to train travel if he can. He  hates  it. Says it saps his soul. He does have a flair for the dramatic, your Ben. Still, I can understand.

Aye, this recycling scheme is getting daft, pet. They’ve changed it  again . Now they want all the plastic bottles squashed, but last week it was ‘no, leave ‘em as they are, we’ve got machines for it’. Honestly, you’d think they were deliberately trying to confuse folk. Tell me about it, Grandad. It’s like a full-time job just figuring out what goes where. I saw Mrs. Henderson next door arguing with the bin men yesterday about a yoghurt pot. Apparently, it had ‘residue’. Sounds about right. Bureaucracy in action. Though, honestly, it’s a good thing they’re trying, isn't it? It’s just… inefficient. Progress, I suppose. Progress? It's a right headache is what it is. Makes you long for the days when everything went in the same bin, eh? Though I suppose we didn’t  know  any better then. Still… speaking of headaches, how's that job hunt going, lass? Any bites yet? Not really, no. Sent off about five applications this week. Mostly data analysis roles, a few corpus linguistics ones. Getting a lot of auto-rejections. It’s frustrating. It’s tough out there, definitely. Especially with that level of competition. Have you had anyone look over your CV? Maybe tailoring it to each job description might help? I can take a quick look if you like. I’m used to sifting through applications for grads at work. That would be amazing, actually, Tom. I’ve tweaked it a bit, but a fresh pair of eyes would be brilliant. I feel like I’m just throwing applications into the void. Aye, it’s a jungle out there now, isn’t it? Back in my day… well, things were different. Securing a post at the hospital was straightforward enough. Though, even then, there were politics. Remember old Dr. Henderson? Never gave anyone a chance unless they’d played golf with him! Times change, thankfully. Though, I suspect networking still plays a huge role, just in a different form. LinkedIn, things like that. Oh, LinkedIn is a nightmare. Everyone's a ‘guru’ and ‘passionate’ about something. It's exhausting. Anyway… less about my doom and gloom. Did you two manage to get tickets for The Lambton Worm this weekend? Aye, got 'em through Maggie. She works down at the Civic Centre, always gets first dibs. It's a good show, that. Proper Sunderland history.

Honestly, the kids were  brutal  this week. Honestly, brutal. Year 7s are just… a different breed after half term. Like they've forgotten how to sit still, or listen, or… breathe politely. Oh, tell me about it. Mine were practically feral. I think they just get energy from knowing they can wind you up. Did you have much disruption? Disruption doesn’t even  begin  to cover it. I tried introducing a new grammar point, the present perfect, and it descended into chaos. Paper aeroplanes, whispering campaigns about who fancies who, the whole shebang. It felt less like a classroom and more like a particularly unruly zoo enclosure. Sounds familiar. I attempted a creative writing exercise on descriptive language. Ended up with a story about a ninja unicorn fighting a zombie dinosaur. Which, delightful as that is, wasn’t exactly the point of the lesson. Oh god, that’s brilliant! But also… exhausting. It makes you question everything, doesn't it? Am I being too ambitious? Is the curriculum realistic? Should I just give in and let them write about ninja unicorns all day? Don't even think about it! Though, honestly, sometimes the peace is tempting. Speaking of ambitious, how are you feeling about the TEFL conference next month? Still going? I am, yes. Though I’m starting to have serious second thoughts. It’s in Birmingham, isn't it? That's a proper trek. It is a bit of a mission, yeah. But Sarah told me last year it was really good. Lots of practical workshops, networking opportunities… You know, the usual conference spiel. Networking… that's what I dread. The forced pleasantries, the collecting of business cards from people you’ll never actually contact again… It all feels so… performative. I get it. It can be draining. But you might pick up some good ideas. Especially with the new curriculum changes coming through. I’m going to try and snag a place on that session about incorporating technology into lessons. Mine are already glued to their phones, might as well use it to our advantage. That sounds sensible, actually. I saw a workshop advertised on using AI in language teaching. Seems a bit… futuristic, but possibly useful for differentiation. I’m always looking for ways to make life easier, let’s be honest. Anything that reduces my marking load is a win in my book. Totally. Have you thought about what you might present?
