I often drop my 'h's when I’m talking fast - don't tell anyone. Ah, see, that's what I noticed with you, Chloe. You’ve got a bit of a midlands twang, but it’s almost… softened? Like you’re consciously not  broad  midlands, if you get me. It’s like you're trying not to sound too “Derby”. No offence! None taken! It’s true, I do tone it down a bit. When I first came to Chester, people were constantly asking me to repeat myself. It’s just easier. Plus, my mum always said I sounded “too common” when I really laid it on thick. Your mum says everything is ‘too common,’ love. Ignore her. It's a lovely accent! Mine's proper Yorkshire, like. You can tell immediately where I’m from, even if I tried to sound posh. People always ask if I’m from ‘up north’ the minute I open my mouth. “Ey up, lass! Where’s tha’ from?”

Aw, for goodness sake, Wilf! Just pass it! Honestly, they're playing like they’ve never seen a football before. Is that even a strategy? Relax, love. It’s only a friendly. And it  is  a bit shambolic, I’ll give you that. Though, to be fair, the squad’s a bit experimental with the Olympics looming. They’re probably trying out different formations. Experimental shambles, more like. It's giving me anxiety just watching it. You know I get properly invested during footy. Remember the Euros last year? I practically didn’t move from this sofa for a month. How could I forget? You were fuelled entirely by biscuits and righteous indignation whenever something went wrong. You nearly took out the TV remote with a cushion, remember when Kane missed that penalty? Don’t remind me. Still haven’t forgiven him, a little bit. Though, to be fair, pressure's immense. Speaking of immense pressure, are you still stressing about your thesis deadline? Is it still looming like a… a very large, academic football? It’s... present. Let's say that. I’m in the throes of ‘minor revisions’ now, which apparently means rewriting half a chapter. But it’s good, productive stress. More productive than watching this, anyway. What are you making there? Still the scarf for… who was it again? Old Mr. Henderson from down the street? Aye, Mr. Henderson. He’s always bringing us apples from his garden, so I thought I’d knit him something to keep his neck warm. It’s coming along slowly. I’m attempting a cable knit, which is proving to be… ambitious. It's all tangles and dropped stitches. Sounds about right. You always aim high with your knitting. Last time it was that fair isle jumper for your mum, which took you six months and looked like a psychedelic map. It was  artistic ! She loved it. Regardless. It’s relaxing, though, isn’t it? When you finally get into a rhythm. More relaxing than watching this mess. I saw they're already announcing some of the team for the Olympics. Any predictions for gold medals? Cycling, definitely. And rowing. Always strong in those. I’m more interested in the athletics, though. Watching the 100m sprint is always a rush. It is, isn't it? Proper electric. Oh! Hang on. They’ve  actually  made a decent pass. Oh, and a shot!

…and honestly, the whole premise of the Bee Movie is just  bonkers . A bee suing humanity? Like, where do you even  start  with that legally? But Barry B. Benson was trying to help the bees! They were getting their honey stolen! I know, love, I know. It's a sweet story, but… massively unrealistic. Though, it did make me think about how much we rely on bees. Are you two remembering to look out for bees in the garden? I saw one on the lavender yesterday! I didn’t poke it though, ‘cause you said. Good lad. Very sensible. Right, speaking of things that feel a bit…removed from reality… this whole Royal thing. Did you see they’re charging a fortune to get into Hampton Court Palace now? Ooooh, Hampton Court! We went there last summer! It had a maze! It did, a very good maze. But still! Paying to walk around a place that, theoretically, belongs to  us ? It feels…odd, doesn't it? Does that mean if  I  was king, everyone would have to pay me to walk in my garden? Well, hypothetically, yes. But being king comes with a lot of responsibility, doesn’t it? It’s not just having a nice garden. I would be a queen! And I'd have a castle made of chocolate! A chocolate castle… that sounds sticky. And would you want to be queen if it meant you couldn’t just…choose what you wanted to do? It’s a lot of waving and smiling and attending things. I don't want to wave. I want to build Lego. Lego is excellent. Much more fulfilling, probably. You know, it always strikes me as odd how much focus there is on “royal fruits” and all that. Like, are they actually better? Or is it just…marketing? What are royal fruits? Oh, it's just a silly thing… it’s when they give a fruit variety a ‘Royal Warrant’ because the Royal Family likes it. Doesn’t mean it tastes any better than the one from Sainsbury’s. It just means someone paid to get the Queen to eat it! So, it’s like a bribe? That’s…a surprisingly astute way of putting it, yes. It makes you think, doesn’t it? I mean, I’m not a staunch Republican, but… the whole system. It just feels a bit archaic. Archaic? What does that mean?

Honestly, that tip was a  state . People just dumping everything. Old carpets, broken garden gnomes… you wouldn't believe it. And the smell! Aye, they’re never pleasant, are they? Though, better them than your garden, eh, Margaret? You were talking about clearing out the shed yesterday. Any progress? Progress? It’s a battlefield, Doris! A battlefield of rusty tools and things your Uncle Arthur insisted were ‘too good to throw away’ thirty years ago. I found a lawnmower that probably predates the war. Honestly. Gran, did Uncle Arthur fight in the war? Good heavens, no. He was far too young. Though he was in the Home Guard, apparently. Mostly, according to your grandfather, involved in ensuring the village pub didn’t run out of beer. Sounds like a man of priorities. Though I suspect a well-stocked pub  was  strategically important during those times. Helps morale, you know. You’re too kind, Andrew. He was a scoundrel, your Uncle Arthur, but a lovable one. Still, Margaret, you are getting on with the clearing, though? Because we  need  to talk about what you want to keep before we start thinking about downsizing. Downsizing! Don’t start on that again, Doris. I’m perfectly happy where I am. It’s just…a lot of stuff has accumulated. And truthfully, the garden is becoming a bit much. You could get a robot lawnmower, Gran! I saw one on YouTube. They’re brilliant. They just go around and around and… A  robot  lawnmower? Goodness me. What will they think of next? Sounds terribly impersonal. I like feeling the grass under my feet, the smell of it… They're not  that  impersonal, Margaret. They just take the strain off your back. Remember last year when you pulled a muscle bending over the roses? A minor twinge. Anyway, I’m not convinced all this technology is a blessing. I saw on the telly last night – this programme about social media and teenagers… utterly terrifying. These youngsters glued to their phones, not talking to each other. It's a double-edged sword, isn’t it? There are definite downsides, but it also connects people in ways we never could before. I mean, look at Liam here, researching robot lawnmowers! It’s research, Dad! For a school project. We’re doing a presentation on automation. Good for you, Liam. See, Margaret? It's not  all  bad. Speaking of projects, did you ever get around to looking at those auction catalogues I sent you?

Right, so I’m tellin’ ya, the Walker Art Gallery's car park is a  nightmare  now. They’ve put those little bollards up everywhere, thinkin’ they’re makin’ it pedestrian friendly. It just means you spend fifteen minutes circlin’ like a shark, then end up miles away near the Catholic Cathedral. Oh, don’t even  start  on the parking. I had to drop Mum off there last week. Honestly, it was stressful. Did you manage to get that lesson plan sorted for the conditionals? The Year 10s are killin’ me with their "woulds" and "coulds". Sorted-ish. I’ve got the framework done, but I was thinkin’ of basing one of the practice activities around… weddings, actually. Everyone's got an opinion on weddings, like, and it’s good for hypothetical language. “If I  had  the money, I  would  elope to Vegas.” That sort of thing. Oh, brilliant! That’s actually really clever. It’s relatable. Speaking of weddings… Sarah and Ben are finally setting a date. September next year. Her mum’s already started talkin’ about centrepieces. September? Good for ‘em. Honestly, I'm relieved they’ve finally got round to it. All those engagement parties… felt like it was draggin’ on forever. Still, September’s a nice time. Maybe we can actually get a decent parkin’ space for  that  then, now everyone's back at work. Don’t get your hopes up. It’ll be chaos. Listen, I had a really good day today. Old Mr. Henderson, the one with the severe anxiety, actually  laughed  during our session. He told me a joke! Small win, but still. That’s amazing, honestly. Seriously. That’s proper good work, love. He's a tough one, that fella. Makes me appreciate teachin’ teenagers – even when they’re bein’ right little… well, you know. Right little terrors? Yeah, I get it. Actually, that reminds me. I've been thinking more about applying for that Masters in Clinical Psychology at Manchester. The deadline is next month. Ooh, go on! That’s what you’ve been workin’ towards, innit? Manchester's a bit of a trek, though. Would that mean… movin’? That's the big question, isn’t it? It’s a full-time course, so financially it makes more sense to live closer. But I hate the thought of leaving here, of leaving  us  here. And leaving Winston! Winston would be traumatised. He’d spend all day lookin’ out the window, judgin’ passers-by.

Honestly, this canteen food is  criminal . I swear they've been serving the same grey sausage roll for, like, three years. You're dramatic, Liv. It's not  that  bad. Though, yeah, it's consistently… underwhelming. I brought a flapjack, want a bit? My Nan sent me a whole box. Oh, bless your Nan! Always looking out for us. Yes, please! Definitely better than whatever this is pretending to be chicken. So, did you catch that new episode of ‘Heartstopper’ last night? Ooh, yes! Finally! I was proper stressed waiting for it all week. Charlie and Nick are just… ugh, everything. Though, I'm a bit worried about Isaac. He deserves happiness too, you know? Totally! They handled his storyline really sensitively though, I think. It felt very real. It's so much better than a lot of the rubbish on Netflix, honestly. Like, I tried watching that new celebrity dating show everyone’s banging on about and it was instantly switched off. Just…performative nonsense. Oh god, 'Love Island: VIP Edition' or whatever it’s called? Yeah, I saw a clip. It was excruciating. All botox and perfectly sculpted abs. Gives me the ick. Seriously! It’s all just… curated. You don't get any genuine connection. It makes you question everything you see on Instagram, doesn’t it? It's like, is  anyone  actually real online? It does. My cousin, Maya, she’s obsessed with it. She spends hours editing her photos, and it’s just… sad. She's naturally gorgeous! Like, why bother? She’s convinced she needs a full face of makeup just to pop to the shops. It’s the pressure, innit? Everyone’s trying to live up to some impossible standard. I deactivated my TikTok last week. It was just draining. Too much comparison. Good for you! I keep saying I'm going to, but then I get sucked back in watching silly dances or people doing life hacks that definitely don’t work. Have you seen that one where people try to peel a boiled egg with a glass? Absolute chaos. Oh, I saw that! It’s a disaster every time! Speaking of disasters… how was your date with Ben from the History society? You were saying he was  really  into Ancient Rome. Oh, don’t even ask. He spent a solid hour explaining the intricacies of Roman plumbing. Roman…  plumbing , Liv! I was trying to subtly steer the conversation towards music, and he just launched into another monologue about aqueducts.

Right, so I finally beat that Gym Leader in Pokémon Violet. The one in Artazon, with the Grass types. Took me ages, though. His Lilligant was a proper pain. Oh, good for you, Leo! That’s brilliant, isn't it? Oisin was trying to catch a… well, I  think  it was a Caterpie, in the garden earlier. It ended up being a slightly grumpy-looking moth. Moth! More pasta! More pasta it is, my little explorer. Honestly, the things he tries to ‘capture’. It’s adorable. A moth counts, technically. It's a bug. Did you see that new trailer for the DLC? Looks insane. They're adding loads of new Pokémon and a whole new storyline. I saw you were buzzing about it on your video call with Gran earlier. Honestly, Leo, all this gaming… don't you ever get tired of it? We were trying to Skype your Dad earlier, but the connection was awful. He said he was stuck in a meeting. Nah, never! And yeah, Dad's always in meetings. It's a skill, being able to defeat people online while simultaneously hearing him drone on about spreadsheets. Seriously though, the DLC looks amazing. I'm thinking we could maybe… go for Ramen afterwards, to celebrate? Ramen sounds lovely. Though you’ll need to ask your father, won't you? I'm still trying to get my head around the price of everything these days. And speaking of needing things... you’ve grown again, haven't you? Those jeans are looking a bit… snug. Mum! Don't embarrass me! They're  skinny  jeans, they're supposed to be snug. Everyone wears them. Everyone at school, maybe. But they look like they're cutting off the circulation to your legs. Honestly, you remind me of a sausage in its skin. Very funny. It’s a  fashion statement ! And I'm not wearing them for you, alright? Never said you were, love. It's just… practical concerns. And before you launch into a lecture on self-expression, have you been practicing your guitar? I haven’t heard you play in days. I did a bit yesterday. I'm trying to learn that new riff by Arctic Monkeys. It's really tricky. Nearly broke a string. Gitta! Play gitta! He wants to hear the ‘gitta’, Leo. Maybe after dinner? Although, honestly, the volume… Oisin gets a fright. Alright, alright. Maybe later.

Oh, look at this. Honestly, I haven't seen this in… decades. It’s one of the gardening set bits. Remember that, Maureen? The one your Auntie Elsie got us for Christmas? Good heavens, you’re right! Pink, wasn't it? Mostly pink. And that ridiculous little wheelbarrow. I remember arguing with you over who got to pull the wheelbarrow. You always wanted it. Because  I  was the one with the vision! I was planning entire herbaceous borders, Maureen. You just wanted to fill it with pebbles. Pebbles were vital structural elements! Don’t be absurd. Besides, you were always bossing me around in the garden, even the pretend one. “Maureen, the delphiniums need more space!” Honestly. Well, someone had to have a sense of horticultural order! It wasn't  all  bossing. We did have fun. Though, looking at this now… it’s just…plastic. Faded plastic. It feels a bit sad, actually. It’s just a thing, Anon. It represents the fun we had. Don’t get all melancholy on me now. We’ve got a whole cupboard full of 'represents the fun we had' to get through. Honestly, half of this stuff should have gone years ago. I know, I know. It’s just… it's hard, isn't it? Letting go. It feels like letting go of… bits of ourselves. Did we ever actually manage to grow anything in that garden, do you recall? Apart from weeds, obviously. Dad’s ‘lawn’ was mostly weeds, if I remember rightly. Oh, the lawn. A constant source of his frustration. He'd spend hours mowing it, then the next day it was full of dandelions again. No, we didn't grow much. Mostly we dug holes. And then filled them in. And then dug them again. Oh! And the Bako! Did we find the Bako yet? Not yet. It’s somewhere underneath this mountain of questionable porcelain dolls your mother insisted on collecting. Honestly, I think she bought one every time she went to Blackpool. She loved her dolls. She said they were an investment. An investment in dust, more like. But the Bako… now  that  was fantastic. We built entire cities with that Bako. They were always very elaborate cities. With surprisingly efficient public transport systems, I recall. You were the architect. I was the civil engineer. I made sure the bridges wouldn’t collapse. Though, they usually did collapse.

Honestly, this is ridiculous. Even in October! I got bitten three times last night. Three! And Leo, predictably, ended up with one right on his forehead. Three? That  is  bad. I thought we were past the peak mosquito season. Maybe they’ve had a late bloom because of the warm spell. Poor little Leo. Did the cream help? Eventually. He was inconsolable for a good hour. Just a tiny red bump, but he treated it like a full-blown emergency. Honestly, I’m starting to consider investing in a mosquito net for the bedroom. It’s a bit extreme, I know. Not at all. If it buys you a peaceful night’s sleep, it's worth it. Remember Auntie Brenda and her netting in Cornwall? She was prepared for anything. Although, hers was more about midges than mosquitoes. Oh, Brenda. Always prepared. Speaking of prepared, did you manage to get tickets for The Lunar Landing next week? I saw they had a few released today. I tried! I was on it the  second  they went live. But the website completely crashed. Kept giving me error messages. I eventually gave up after about twenty minutes of refreshing. Looks like everyone and their dog wanted to see them. Ugh, that’s so frustrating. They’re supposed to be amazing live, aren't they? I’ve only listened to their album a couple of times, but your brother raves about them. Said it was the best gig he’s been to all year. He’s right, they are. Proper energy. I was really looking forward to it. It’s been ages since we’ve had a proper night out, just the two of us. Always seems to be something…Leo, work, sleep deprivation… Tell me about it. It’s a constant juggling act. Although, I did manage to book that pottery class I was telling you about. It’s next Saturday afternoon. It’s only a couple of hours, hopefully enough to feel vaguely human again. That sounds lovely, actually. A little bit of ‘me’ time. You deserve it. Though getting out of the house on a Saturday afternoon... that's ambitious. We’ll be lucky if we don’t encounter gridlock. Don't even  mention  the traffic. I had to drop Leo’s cousin off at Waterloo East yesterday after their visit and it was horrendous. Took me nearly an hour and a half to get from Clapham to Waterloo.

Right, that’s me officially knackered. Four hours on the course, chasing that little white ball around. Honestly, sometimes I think it’s actively mocking me. Sounds…intense. You’re red in the face. Did you at least beat old man Hemmings this time? He always gives you stick. Finally! Yes! He was going on about his back again, blaming the weather, the grass, the alignment of the planets… anything but his own swing. It was glorious. Though my arms feel like lead. I need a proper meal, not just those disgusting protein bars they have at the clubhouse. Oh, you say that, but you scarf them down like they’re gourmet chocolates. I saw your Instagram story. Speaking of which, you were on your phone  a lot  during your round, weren’t you? Did you get some good content? Gotta keep the sponsors happy, innit? A couple of quick updates, a little video of my winning putt… It’s all part of the job now. Plus, Mum keeps messaging me asking for updates. It’s relentless. Honestly, sometimes I wish I could just chuck the phone in the lake. You wouldn’t last five minutes. She'd hunt you down. Anyway, I've been trying to write my cover letter for that marketing assistant job. It's… agonizing. Every sentence feels clunky and desperate. It's like, how do you convincingly say "please give me a job" without sounding like a total beggar? Blimey, that sounds rough. What's the company? Maybe I can take a look? I’m surprisingly good at spotting a load of tosh, apparently. Years of listening to tour pros waffle on about technique. It’s this recruitment agency, "Synergy Solutions." They're working with a few different companies, supposedly. The problem is…they just seem to want buzzwords. ‘Synergistic approach’, ‘dynamic team player’… I feel like I'm writing in code. Honestly, I haven’t felt this stressed since my dissertation. Yeah, recruitment agencies are a joke. Remember when I was trying to sort out some sponsorship deals after leaving sixth form? Felt like I was selling my soul. Honestly, I almost went back to Barbados to just…chill. Don't even joke about that. I've been having  those  thoughts, too. Just disappear to somewhere warm. Maybe learn to make cocktails? Though, knowing my luck, I'd end up running a poorly-managed bar in Skegness.

Ah, that’s the ticket. Proper soup. Beats the…the ‘technical difficulties’ we had with dinner last night, wouldn't you say, Mary? Technical difficulties is putting it mildly, Liam. Trying to wrangle a toddler and a takeaway pizza simultaneously is a logistical nightmare. Honestly, I thought I was going to lose a shoe. Can I be on my phone a bit longer? Just finishing a level on this game. It’s  really  hard. Daniel, the dinner table is a device-free zone, remember? We talked about this. Real life interactions are important, you know. Especially when your grandad is visiting tomorrow. He won’t be impressed seeing you staring at a screen. But, Dad! It's a limited-time event. I  need  to get the reward. Let him have five more minutes, Liam. He's been good this afternoon with his homework. Besides, it’s nice to have a bit of peace while Leo’s entertaining us. Twinkle, twinkle, li-li-little… spoon! A spoon, is it? Well, that's a new verse. He's a poet, that one. Right, five minutes, Daniel. Then phone away. I was actually meaning to ask, Mary, did you manage to sort out the cloud storage for those photos from the holidays? I’m running out of space on my laptop again. Oh, don’t even mention it. It was a whole saga. Google Photos decided my account was “suspicious” and locked me out. It took an hour on the phone with someone in Bangalore, and frankly, I’m still not convinced it’s all sorted. They kept asking me security questions about my first pet… I didn't even  have  a pet growing up! Bangalore, is it? Story of our lives these days. Everything’s outsourced. You’d think a company as big as Google could manage a simple photo backup. It’s just… frustrating, you know? Keeps me in a job, I suppose, troubleshooting things like that at work all day. Speaking of frustrating, Ben just beat me at that game. So unfair. He always gets lucky. Now, Daniel, don’t be a sore loser. It’s just a game. You'll get him next time. Did you finish your history reading? That’s more important than virtual battles, you realize. Yeah, I did it. It was about…the Tudors. All kings and beheadings and stuff. Pretty gruesome. It is, isn't it?

Honestly, I still can’t believe he slept in his pants  again . Little terror. Oh, bless him. It's not hurting anyone, is it? And it’s warmer, I suppose. Though I did find a rogue sock in the fruit bowl this morning. Mummy! He used  my  pink block for the castle wall! It’s a REALLY strong wall! And it’s not pink, it’s…rose gold! Rose gold, is it? Right. Sounds very architecturally sound. Look, you two, play nicely. We’re trying to have grown-up conversation here, which is hard when discussing pants-wearing children. He’s just testing boundaries, isn't he? Like his father. Hey! I resemble that remark. It's just comfort, pure and simple. I used to sleep in my cricket whites when I was a lad. Don't judge. Cricket whites? Right. Well, at least pants are a little less… fragrant after a day in the field. Anyway, about the house. I’ve been doing a bit more thinking, actually, and sketching. Oh, good. Let's hear it. I’m still leaning towards extending back over the utility room, but I’m open to persuasion. It needs more space, definitely. Especially with these two growing like weeds. I was thinking… what about up? Into the loft? We could get a really amazing master suite up there. Proper beams, velux windows, even an ensuite. Up? Hmm. Loft conversions are… disruptive, aren't they? All the dust, the mess. And the structural work. Plus, wouldn't we lose some storage? We could build in eaves storage. Loads of it. Think about it - a big, bright room with views over the garden. It would be  lovely . I’ve been looking at some inspiration online… Scandinavian minimalist, lots of light wood… Can we have a slide in our new room? A secret slide that goes straight into the garden? A secret slide?! Now  that’s  ambitious. Honestly, where did you even get that idea? I saw it in a book! It was a princess castle and she slid down to escape the dragon! Well, a slide might be a tad tricky, love. But we can think about fun things. Maybe a little reading nook? A reading nook is sensible. A slide is a health and safety nightmare. Although… …a fireman’s pole? Now  that  could be cool. A fireman's pole? Seriously? Are we building a children’s play area or a grown-up retreat?

…and honestly, the decorator said ‘sage green’ was  the  colour this autumn. Sage green! It looks like sick, Alun, frankly. Sick. I told him I wanted something with a bit more…oomph. A proper terracotta, perhaps. Something reminiscent of Tuscany. Tuscany, is it? Trying to recreate the Italian countryside in Surrey, are we, David? Bold move. Sage green isn't  terrible , mind. It's…restful. Though I can see your point about the oomph. My wife, Bronwen, she’s currently obsessed with Farrow & Ball’s ‘Railings’. It’s almost black, the entire downstairs would be enveloped in gloom. Gloom is not what one needs in a study, Alun. No. It needs to be inspiring! Speaking of inspiring… have you heard anything further about the funding bid for the particle physics project? The one with the simulated Hadron Collider collisions? It’s a rather long shot, I admit, but the preliminary data is…promising. Ah, yes. The Big Bang in a box, as young Emily called it. I did chase up Professor Davies in the Research Grants office this morning. He said it’s gone to the secondary review panel. Apparently, they’ve had a deluge of applications this quarter. He was…non-committal, to put it mildly. Said something about prioritizing projects with ‘immediate societal impact.’ Immediate societal impact? What could be more impactful than understanding the fundamental building blocks of the universe? Honestly, these committees. They’re obsessed with things that’ll make headlines, rather than actual breakthroughs. They’d fund a study on the optimal angle for Instagram selfies before they’d give a proper grant to something like this. You’re not wrong there, David. Though, I did see a piece about a university receiving funding for a project analyzing the emotional response to cat videos. So…perhaps your observation has merit. Have you considered amending the proposal to emphasize potential spin-off technologies? Something about medical imaging maybe? They love that sort of thing. I did briefly mention the possibilities for advancements in medical scanning, but it felt…forced. It’s not the primary focus. It's the physics, Alun! The pure, elegant physics! Though, if it helps our chances… I suppose I could expand on that section. It’s just a bit disheartening, to be honest. I've poured a considerable amount of time into outlining the modelling techniques. It is. But you know how it goes.

Right, Operation Lego Sort is… not going well. Honestly, it’s like a plastic brick explosion in here. Elsie, darling, are you  sure  you haven't been mixing all the sets again? No! I was building a Hogwarts castle! It  needed  grey bricks from the pirate ship! And I needed this for a… a Turtle lair! A really strong Turtle lair! A Turtle lair, of course. And Hogwarts requires pirate ship grey. Perfectly logical. Look, the idea is to get everything back in its original boxes. Remember? We’ve got City, Ninjago, Star Wars… it’s a tiered system of organisation. But Star Wars doesn't  need  a whole box! It's just a few tiny ships. Elsie, there’s a Millennium Falcon in there. A  relatively  large Millennium Falcon. Trust me, it needs a box. Speaking of needing things, have either of you finished your Easter eggs yet? I feel like I'm wading through chocolate wrappers too, alongside the Lego. I saved a bit of the caramel one! Can I have it after I finish the lair? You can have it after you’ve helped sort  some  Lego. A fair trade, don’t you think? It wouldn't hurt to have a bit of help. It’s like… like a Simpsons episode, this. Endless chaos, and no one actually getting anything done. I like The Simpsons! The yellow man is funny. He is, isn’t he? Though sometimes a bit… chaotic. Like this room. Actually, it reminds me a bit of Granny's house right now, with all the dust sheets and furniture moved about. Granny’s house smells like biscuits. It does! And paint, currently. They’re redoing the living room, aren't they? All that wallpaper stripping… it's a mammoth task. She's having a new fireplace put in. It's going to be really cosy. Is it going to be like Hagrid's hut? With a big fire? Maybe not  quite  like Hagrid's hut, darling. A little bit more… refined. Though Granny does love a good roaring fire. We’re promised a sneak peek next weekend, if the builders have made good progress. Can we take the Turtles to Granny’s? They need to see the new fireplace! We can certainly ask. Though I’m not sure Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello and Michelangelo would particularly appreciate floral wallpaper. Anyway, back to the bricks. How about this: If you both sort one container each, we can  all  go to the cinema on Saturday?

…and honestly, the paella was just…sad. Like, someone had  heard  of paella and then just kind of…assembled things. Not a socarrat in sight! It was all just mushy rice and suspiciously pale prawns. Oh, no. The cardinal sin of paella! No socarrat? That  is  tragic. Welcome back to reality, then. England and its distinct lack of properly cooked rice. How was the rest of Spain though? Beyond the paella disaster? It was brilliant, honestly. Barcelona was amazing – the architecture, the vibe… I even managed to brush up on my GCSE Spanish a little bit. Mostly just ordering tapas, let’s be real, but still. And Valencia was lovely, despite the paella incident. Did you have a good week with your mum? You seemed really excited about it. It was…good. Exhausting, definitely. Mum’s mum – Nana – is getting a bit more forgetful, you know? It's just a lot of repeating things, making sure she’s taken her meds, that kind of stuff. It’s lovely to spend time with them, truly, but it's also a big reminder of… things. Work feels almost relaxing afterwards, truthfully. How are things at the office? Still battling the rogue printer and Mr Henderson’s spreadsheets? Oh, the printer is  still  a menace. I swear it has a personal vendetta against me. And Mr. Henderson… honestly, that man lives in a world of colour-coded chaos. We've finally kicked off the Johnson account though, which is good. It's a big one, means a lot of late nights for the next couple of months. Sarah’s been absolutely amazing helping me get everything organised – she's a lifesaver. Sarah’s brilliant. She always is. She’s proper organised. I’m glad you’ve got her on your team. Sounds stressful though. You need to make sure you actually  take  some time off when things calm down. Remember what happened last year? You ended up practically living on coffee and willpower. I know, I know. Lesson learned. Probably. It’s just… I feel like I need to prove myself, you know? It’s a promotion-level project, and I'm still relatively new in the role. You  are  more than capable, Chloe. They wouldn’t have given it to you if they didn't think so. And honestly, all that proving-yourself stuff sounds exhausting. Speaking of exhausting… I bumped into Liam the other day.

Right, that’s a proper brew. Always better at your Mam and Dad’s, isn’t it? Though, don’t tell ‘em I said that. They'd never let me live it down. Yeah, it’s good tea. Better than school dinners, anyway. Which isn’t saying much. Aye, Brenda makes a good cuppa. Though, I still reckon my Victoria sponge is superior. Remember that one I made for young Thomas’s christening? A right showstopper that was. Showstopper is right, Elsie! Near as big as the baby himself, it was. Had to get two people to carry it. Oh, you two. Always the memories. Thomas is a grown man with a family of his own now, you know. Time flies, doesn’t it? Speaking of which, Leo, have you finished sorting out that essay for Mr. Harrison? The one on quadratic equations? Ugh, don’t remind me. It’s…progressing. I think. He wants us to explain them like we’re talking to a five-year-old. Trying to make sense of the ‘x’ and ‘y’ is hard enough, let alone explaining why it matters. Well, think of it like… building with Lego. You’ve got blocks, right? And you need to figure out how many blocks you need to make a certain shape. That ‘x’ is just a space for a block that you haven’t put in yet. Lego, huh? That’s… surprisingly helpful, actually. Still think Mr. Harrison's a bit mad, though. Mad? Teachers were sensible in my day. We didn’t question a thing. Just did as we were told. Mind you, we didn’t have all these fancy computers and gadgets either. We used slates and chalk! And a good clip round the ear if you misbehaved! Things were simpler then. Now, Arthur, let’s not glorify the past  too  much. It wasn't all rosy. Still, Elsie, you're right. Things are different now. Leo’s generation has a lot more pressure. Tell me about it. Everyone's talking about uni applications. Feels like my whole life's riding on these exams. University is all well and good, but don’t forget a trade, love. A good trade will always put bread on the table. My brother, Brian, he was a plumber. Always busy, always earning good money. Aye, Brian could fix anything. Remember when the boiler packed in at the church hall? Brian had it sorted in an afternoon.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit…dark. Not in a good, Disney-villain dark, but just…sad. Even for a story about a boy who doesn’t grow up. But Tinkerbell was pretty! She sparkled  lots . She  was  pretty, wasn't she? A proper little firework. Though I always felt a bit sorry for her, getting so jealous all the time. Jealous of Wendy? Why? Wendy was boring. She just…sat there. Well, Peter was paying Wendy a lot of attention, telling her stories. Tinkerbell wanted his attention too. It’s a bit complicated, isn't it? Like when you and your brother are fighting over a toy. Oh. Like the Lego spaceship. When  he  wouldn’t let me have a turn. Exactly! It's a bit like that. Now, you two have been watching a lot of Peter Pan films lately, haven’t you? Have you seen the really old one, the Disney one from 1953? Mmmhmm! With Captain Hook and Smee! Smee is funny. Smee  is  funny. He’s a bit hapless, isn't he? Always messing things up. And Captain Hook, well, he’s a proper villain. But did you know that J.M. Barrie, the man who  wrote  the original Peter Pan story, used to visit the children in Great Ormond Street Hospital? Great Ormond Street? The hospital? That's right. He used to tell them stories, and he actually  gave  the copyright to Peter Pan to the hospital! So all the money made from the play and the books goes to help sick children. Isn’t that brilliant? Wow! He gave them  everything ? Well, the rights to it, yes. It means they can keep helping children for years and years. It’s a really lovely thing to have done. So Peter Pan helps real kids? Not just Wendy and John and Michael? Exactly! He helps real kids. It's a way of his story…living on and doing good. Now, you two also watched that  Pan  film didn't you? The one with Levi Miller? That one was different! Peter Pan didn’t  know  he could fly at first. It was different alright. It was… a reimagining. A bit of a departure from the original story. It tried to explain  how  Peter Pan became Peter Pan, didn't it? Showing him as an orphan taken to Neverland… And Tiger Lily was a fighter! She was really good with the bow and arrow.

Right, nearly there then. Just past Cullompton, isn’t it? Feels like a proper trek to Exeter airport every time, even though I  know  it’s not. Used to think Southend airport was a long way… this is a different league altogether. It is a bit of a slog, Dad. Especially with the M5 traffic. Glad I wasn’t driving! You’re doing brilliantly, though. And honestly, it’s nice to have a bit of family time before Sarah disappears to Barcelona for a week. It really is. Feels like she just got back from her summer course. Time flies, doesn’t it? Remember when she was tiny and we lived in that little cottage near Crediton? She used to insist on wearing wellies  everywhere , even to the supermarket. Oh, I remember. And the mud… the  amount  of mud we had to deal with. That cottage was lovely, though. Proper chocolate box. Though a bit… drafty, wasn’t it? Still, a lot better than that pokey flat we had in Taunton. God, that was grim. Taunton was… an experience. At least we had a garden in Crediton, even if it was perpetually soggy. Mum, you spent  hours  out there trying to get roses to grow. Well, a girl’s gotta have a hobby! And the roses were worth it when they bloomed. Though I suspect the soil was mostly clay. Still, it was a good few years there, wasn't it? Before we moved down to this side of Devon properly. Good years. Good years. I miss being closer to the sea, mind you. Southend was… well, it was home, wasn’t it? Even with all its… peculiarities. Still, this is nice. Quiet. Plenty of cream teas to be had. You’d move for a cream tea, Dad. Honestly. Although, speaking of nice and quiet, have you managed to get any decent sleep lately? You were looking a bit knackered yesterday. Oh, it’s just this internal clock, you see. Used to getting up at six for work, even though I’m supposedly ‘retired’. It’s a nonsense, really. Wake up, potter about, read the paper… then feel guilty for not being productive. It's a vicious cycle. You need to break that habit, dear. We've talked about this. Maybe try a bit of mindfulness? Or just… allow yourself to sleep in. You deserve it. Mindfulness… sounds a bit new-age for an old Southend boy like me.

Honestly, this sun. Lovely for the dahlias, mind you, but a bit much for a working party, even one as…well, as  good  as this one is turning out to be. Thought I was prepared, proper hat and all. Aye, it’s a scorcher, isn’t it? Didn't expect it to get this warm, not in September. Been at it long, have you? I’m Arthur, by the way. Retired from the Nationwide, mostly managing accommodation for staff. Delighted to meet you, Arthur. I’m Beatrice. And yes, a good little while now. Been helping clear some of the rhododendrons – a right jungle they’d become. Used to be quite the artist, myself, mostly watercolours. Antiques a bit too, ran a little gallery for years. Though my back doesn't appreciate the bending now, not like it used to. Funny, isn’t it, how your body remembers what it  could  do. I know that feeling. Used to be able to spend all day on my feet showing people around properties. Now, a little walk up this hill is enough to get me puffing! Though truthfully, it’s nice to be  doing  something. Beats sitting around, I say. My wife, bless her, used to say I needed a hobby. Wives are usually right about those things, aren’t they? Mine, Eleanor, was always the practical one. She’d have organised this working party, I assure you. Down to the last biscuit. She… she passed a few years back. Hospice care was wonderful, truly. So calm. It’s funny the things you remember. She always said my hands were too delicate for gardening, but I'd sneak out to deadhead the roses anyway. Ah, I’m sorry to hear that, Beatrice. Losing a wife… It leaves a hole, doesn't it? Mine went ten years ago now. Cancer. We didn’t have children, so it was just…quiet, afterwards. Made me appreciate the volunteer work even more, I think. Something to fill the time, and something  useful . Exactly. Useful. And good company. Though I do occasionally think about what Eleanor would make of all this talk about… well, everything. Especially this business with the ME event next year. Honestly, the committee. They’re getting themselves in a right pickle over representation. The ME event? You mean the Midlands Exhibition? I’ve heard murmurings. What’s the fuss? The fuss is, they’ve got a panel, see, mostly blokes, talking about…well, everything!

Right, so I was thinking, maybe we  could  ditch the all-inclusive in Tenerife and actually… do Italy? Italy? That’s a bit of a jump from poolside cocktails, isn't it, love? Not that there’s anything  wrong  with poolside cocktails, mind you. After the year you’ve had, you deserve a spot of sunshine and doing absolutely nothing. I  know  I deserve it, Mum. But doing absolutely nothing feels… a bit… wasted? I need something to  look  forward to that's a little more... stimulating. Tenerife feels… predictable. I’ve done all-inclusive before. It's always the same. Plus, I keep seeing these photos of Tuscany, and Florence, and… oh, the food! Ah, the food. That  is  a good argument. You’ve always been a bit of a foodie, haven’t you? Remember that time you tried to make paella in your tiny student kitchen? The smoke alarm nearly sent the whole building up. Don't remind me! It was a disaster. But this would be different. Cooking classes, wine tasting… exploring little villages. I’ve found a couple of agriturismos that look amazing. Proper farm stays. Agriturismos, fancy! Sounds expensive. Tenerife was looking rather reasonable, remember? Especially with the early bird discounts. It is a bit more, yeah, but not massively. And I've been saving. And if we go self-catering for some of the time, rather than eating out every night, it could balance out. I was thinking maybe a week in Tuscany, then a few days in Florence? We could get the train. The train? Oh, darling, you know I’m not the most coordinated person. I'm picturing me, dragging a suitcase up seventeen flights of stairs with no lift, while you’re effortlessly navigating the Italian rail system. I’ll handle the suitcase! And the rail system. Honestly, Mum, it's actually very efficient. I've been researching it. And you’d love Florence. All the art, the history… you always enjoyed art history at school. I did, didn’t I? Mr. Henderson was a lovely man, terribly enthusiastic about the Renaissance. Though, to be honest, I remember being more focused on dodging paper airplanes during his lectures. But Florence… It has been a long time since I’ve really  looked  at art. Exactly! And we could take a walking tour, see the Duomo, cross the Ponte Vecchio. There are these amazing leather markets...

Right, so I’ve been looking at the bank statement again, and… honestly, Dad, fifty quid to ‘GlowUp Gaming’? Seriously? What  is  GlowUp Gaming? Ah, that. That’s young Leo. He was round the other day, showing me this new… online thing. Apparently, it’s for extra lives or something in a game. Said he’d lost a bet to him. Lost a bet  to  Leo? Leo’s twelve! And fifty quid? I thought we agreed no more lending money, especially not for virtual… whatever. Now, now, don't get your knickers in a twist. It’s Leo. He’s a good lad. And it's not lending, exactly. More of a… contribution towards his digital lifestyle. He promised to wash the car for a month. A month of car washes for fifty pounds? That’s… generous to Leo, certainly. It just feels like everyone's always asking for something. Remember Auntie Bev phoning up last week about needing help with her boiler? Bev and her boilers. Always something. Look, family’s family. Besides, I did alright with that contract at work. The Henderson project came in under budget, so the boss was well pleased. Might even be a bonus coming my way. That's brilliant, Dad! Properly made up for you. Henderson’s a massive account, isn't it? All those new warehouses near Derby? Biggest we've had in years. It's been long hours though, that’s for sure. All meetings and spreadsheets. Makes me appreciate a quiet cuppa and a bit of the cricket. Did you catch any of the England match yesterday? Bits and pieces. I was stuck in the library, finishing up an essay on post-structuralism. Honestly, after wrestling with Derrida all day, cricket felt… well, slightly less challenging. Although Root was on fire. That cover drive was something else. Root  is  class, isn't he? Reminds me a bit of Viv Richards, the way he just… dominates. Although no one will ever truly be like Viv, mind. He was a different breed. Remember watching him play back in Barbados? The atmosphere was electric. I’ve seen footage, yeah. Proper iconic. You’ve got loads of stories about that era, though, haven’t you? You should write them down. A proper memoir. 'From Bridgetown to the Black Country' or something. Don't be daft. Who'd want to read about an old man rambling on about cricket?

Right then, you two. Still gettin’ on alright with this…Skype, is it? Never did trust these modern contraptions, always thought they’d be listenin’. Though, truth be told, I ‘aven’t got much to ‘ide these days, ‘ave I? Just a bit of dodgy knee and too many memories. Oh, Arthur, you and your suspicions! It's perfectly safe, dear. And lovely to  see  you both. Though it's not quite the same as a proper cuppa and a natter, is it? This screen makes you look awfully pale, David. Are you feeling alright? Just the lighting, Brenda. And yes, perfectly fine. Just marking essays, you know how it is. Though, actually, one of the projects  did  involve the students making miniature globes. Found it quite sweet, really. All painting tiny continents. Got me thinking about places… Globes, eh? Used to ‘ave one meself, years ago. Proper big one. Sat in the corner of the livin’ room. Used to spin it and pretend I was goin’ everywhere. Never actually  did  go anywhere though. Not proper places, anyway. Just Blackpool a couple of times. Blackpool was lovely! Remember that stick of rock, Arthur? The one that lasted for weeks? And we tried to win a teddy bear on the pier…never did, did we? We always ended up spendin’ all our money. We did, didn't we? Always were a bit…easily led by flashing lights. Still, better than stayin' cooped up. Though I couldn't manage all that walkin' these days. This leg…it’s a right nuisance. You should really look into getting a better support for it, Arthur. There are some excellent lightweight braces now. Might make a trip to Yorkshire a bit more feasible? You always said you wanted to see the Dales. Yorkshire, eh? Always sounded a bit…grim up north, didn't it? All stone and sheep. Brenda, you’ve been, 'aven’t you? What was it like? Oh, Arthur! It’s  beautiful . Dramatic landscapes, lovely little villages…and the people are so friendly. We did a walking holiday there years ago, stayed in youth hostels. Don't think your knee would enjoy that though, dear. Hostels aren’t what they used to be, mind you. More like small hotels now. Though the communal washrooms… You two. Always finding something to reminisce about. It reminds me of one of my students asking me if people actually used to  sleep  in rooms with strangers.

Right, so I’ve been lookin’ at flights again. Honestly, it’s a right mess, isn’t it? Every time I check, the prices have jumped up another tenner. I swear the airlines are just… takin’ the mickey. Tell me about it! I had a similar issue trying to book Mum’s trip to Barcelona. It’s like they have an algorithm specifically designed to stress people out. What dates are you looking at again? And where are you tryin' to go? Crete. We were thinkin’ the 14th to the 21st of July. Basic package, just flights and the apartment. I thought bein’ flexible would help, but nothin' seems to be makin' a difference. Everything's either gone up or is full of ridiculous stopovers. I don’t mind a quick change in Amsterdam, but bein’ routed through, like, Bulgaria? No thank you. Bulgaria, seriously? They  are  pushing it. Have you tried EasyJet and Ryanair separately, rather than through one of those comparison sites? Sometimes you get a better deal cuttin’ out the middleman. Though, then you have to factor in baggage allowance… the usual nightmare. Aye, I’ve had a look. Ryanair was… well, Ryanair. They wanted extra for a window seat  and  for me to print me boarding pass at home. Honestly! And EasyJet wasn’t much better, they were addin’ on charges for everything. I'm startin’ to think we should just stay 'ere, go to Blackpool or somethin'. At least I know what I’m gettin’ there. Blackpool? From wanting a sun-soaked beach holiday to Blackpool! That's quite a downgrade, isn't it? Look, let me have a quick go after dinner? I'm pretty good at sniffing out deals. My Master’s in Operations Management apparently translates to "can find a cheap flight", who knew? You’re an angel, you are. Seriously. I’m startin’ to get proper stressed about it. It's supposed to be a chillin’ holiday, not a major logistical operation. Me mam keeps sayin’ "you should've booked months ago", but honestly, I thought June was still early enough. Mums are always right, aren’t they? Even when they’re not. But honestly, it feels like everything’s more expensive now. I've been lookin’ at gettin’ a new sofa, and the prices… forget about it. It's like everything is inflated. Heard a bloke on the radio talkin’ about “shrinkflation” the other day – apparently they’re makin’ chocolate bars smaller but keepin’ the price the same!

Honestly, Maureen, it’s getting ridiculous. Absolutely ridiculous. They’ve upped the direct debit again. For what, I ask you? For the privilege of  having  money with them? Oh, banks. Don’t get me started, Arthur. I switched to Monzo a couple of years ago, and it’s been…a revelation. Transparent fees, no hidden charges, and you can actually  talk  to someone if you have a problem. Not like trying to get through to Barclays. It’s a digital bank, though, is that something you’d consider? A digital bank? At my age? I’m barely comfortable with this mobile phone Doreen bought me! She says it’s ‘essential’ for keeping in touch with the grandchildren, but all I ever seem to do is accidentally video call people. And then there’s the battery…it vanishes quicker than a biscuit at a toddler’s party. You and that phone, Arthur! It is a nightmare, isn’t it? I’m with O2, and they're not much better. Always trying to upsell me something. “A bigger data package, Doreen! You  need  a bigger data package!” As if I’m running a business from my handbag. They all do it, don't they? It’s just relentless. But honestly, Monzo’s app is really user-friendly. They send you notifications for every transaction, so you know exactly where your money is going. It’s really helped me budget. Budget? Humph. I've  always  budgeted. That's what an accountant does! It’s just… things are more expensive now. Dreadfully so. Remember when you could get a proper loaf of bread for under a pound? Now it’s… well, I haven’t even  looked  at the price of bread lately. I suspect it’s a small fortune. Don't even mention supermarkets, Arthur. I went to Sainsbury’s last week. A head of broccoli cost nearly three pounds! Three pounds for a  broccoli ! I nearly had a word with the manager. It's daylight robbery. They're blaming it on the weather, you know. All the floods in Spain and Morocco affecting the fruit and veg supply. But I suspect it’s a bit more than just the weather. It's pure greed. Greed, that's it exactly. They're all at it. The banks, the supermarkets…even the energy companies. It’s a conspiracy, I tell you. A conspiracy to bleed us dry!

…and honestly, the beaches in Mozambique are just  unreal . Like, picture postcard stuff. Not a grey, drizzly bit of North Sea in sight. Though, I do miss a proper Greggs sausage roll when I’m out there, mind. You and your sausage rolls, Liv! You’ve been gone five minutes and all you can talk about is Greggs. Mozambique sounds lovely though, proper escape. I’m still trying to decide where to go this summer. Somewhere hot, definitely. After these shifts, I need sun. Sun’s good. I’m leaning towards going home to Ireland, actually. Mam's been on at me for ages to come back and help with the sheep. Sheep? You  help  with sheep? I thought you were terrified of animals, Aisling! I remember that spider incident in first year… That was one spider, Chloe! And it was HUGE. Sheep are…different. They’re fluffy. And Mam really needs a hand. Besides, Fresh air is needed, and away from all the hospital smells. Honestly, the smell is the least of it. Try the emotional weight. Animals are therapeutic though, I suppose. I spent my childhood on a farm, so I'm used to them. My auntie’s got alpacas now. Alpacas! They’re like fluffy, grumpy llamas. Alpacas sound bizarre. But kind of amazing. I once tried to ride a camel in Namibia. Big mistake. Let’s just say my backside wasn’t happy for a week. Oh, Liv! You’re a disaster tourist. Always getting into scrapes. But seriously, Namibia…that sounds incredible. Did you see much wildlife? Loads! Elephants, lions… everything. The sunsets were insane. But the food was…interesting. A lot of game meat. I'm quite picky, you know? Give me a good roast dinner any day. Now  that  we can all agree on. I swear, a roast with proper Yorkshire puddings is my ultimate comfort food. Mam makes the best. She’s got a secret ingredient, she won’t tell anyone what it is. My Nan always puts a little bit of mustard powder in hers. Gives it a real kick. Though, I'm a bit of a foodie, I like to experiment. I made a leek and potato soup the other day with smoked paprika. It was unexpectedly good. Smoked paprika? Sounds fancy. My mam’s cooking is…traditional. Lots of stew, lots of potatoes. It’s hearty, if nothing else. She makes the best soda bread, though.

Honestly, this perspective is  killing  me. It just doesn’t… feel right. It looks all wonky. Let me see. Oh, yeah, it’s a bit off, innit? You’ve got the vanishing point all wrong, I reckon. You’re trying to do the hallway again, aren’t you? Aye. Trying to. It's supposed to be dramatic, all leading to the closed door, really atmospheric. But it just looks like someone’s built a wonky corridor in Minecraft. Bit harsh, but fair. You always were better with landscapes, weren't you? Remember those paintings you used to do of Porthcurno beach? Proper stunning. Oh, God, don't remind me. That was before I decided I needed to be a tortured artist and only paint depressing interiors. It’s a phase. A very frustrating phase. Speaking of phases… how's the essay coming on? Still wrestling with post-structuralism? Wrestling is an understatement. It’s more like being pinned to the mat by it. Derrida is actively mocking me, I swear. I’ve written and rewritten the introduction about ten times. Trying to sound clever and end up sounding like a twit. You’re not a twit! You’re brilliant. Just… sometimes academic writing needs you to actively  not  sound like a normal person. It’s weird. Trust me, I had to do it for my personal statement. It's just... what’s the  point  of it all? Like, we spend years learning this stuff, writing essays, getting degrees… then what? Just… a job? Is that it? Woah, heavy stuff for a Tuesday afternoon. Don’t suddenly have an existential crisis on me. Sorry. It just gets me thinking, you know? My nan was talking about her friend, Elsie, the other day. Elsie's eighty-something and she's just… bored. Says she regrets not doing more when she was younger. Not necessarily ‘big’ things, just… things she  wanted  to do. Painting, learning an instrument, something. That’s a bit sad, innit? It makes you think about what we’re all rushing  towards . Being old and regretful. Exactly! And it’s not like we’ve got loads of time to figure it all out. We're nearly twenty already! Feels like yesterday we were stressing about A-Levels. Tell me about it. Mum keeps asking about ‘career prospects’ which is just… ugh. Like, I don’t  have  a five-year plan! I just want to make nice things and not worry about money.

Honestly, this butternut squash is putting up a fight. You’d think it was personally offended I was trying to make soup. Sounds about right. They’re deceptively solid. Need a hand? You're attacking it like it stole your last biscuit. No, I’m good, just… venting. Long day. The client wants the whole project re-scoped  again . Honestly, it’s like they don’t know what they want until they see a near-finished product and then decide it’s all wrong. Ugh, that's the worst. People who don't understand the concept of briefs. How was Sarah, though? Did she finally get that shift sorted at the hospital? She did! Managed to swap with Ben. She was so stressed about it. Said she was dreading having to explain to Mr. Henderson  again  why she couldn’t cover his overtime. You know how he gets. Like a grumpy badger. Oh, bless her. He’s a nightmare. Honestly, sometimes I think he actively enjoys making people feel uncomfortable. Being a nurse must be exhausting enough without having to navigate  that . It’s good she’s got a good shift though, means we can actually do something this weekend. Exactly! I was thinking… remember Liam and Chloe are back from their backpacking trip on Friday? They mentioned wanting to go out for a proper meal. Fancy joining? We could finally try that new Italian place, ‘Bella Notte’? Everyone’s been raving about it. Bella Notte, yeah! I’ve seen pictures, it looks gorgeous. Friday sounds amazing. I really need a proper catch-up with them. It feels like ages since I've properly  seen  anyone outside of work. It’s all just faces through masks and quick chats in the breakroom. Tell me about it. Work's been relentless. Though, on the bright side, I think Mark finally asked Emily out.  Finally ! What took him so long? It was painfully obvious to everyone but them. Did she say yes? She did! He apparently took her to that little jazz bar in town. She posted a story with a ridiculously happy face and a cocktail. It was…cringey, in a good way. That’s lovely! They’re both so sweet. Though, it makes me think about… well, you know. Don’t even. Let's not go there. My brain is fried enough without revisiting the disaster that was Ben and I. Sorry, didn’t mean to open old wounds.

Right then, let's get this consent form sorted for the seminar. I've had a proper look through it, and frankly, it feels a bit… heavy-handed, doesn't it? All this legal jargon. Are we sure we need to state the potential for ‘emotional distress’ arising from discussing cross-cultural misunderstandings? It feels a bit much for a Tuesday afternoon session on business etiquette. I did flag that with legal, actually. They insisted. Apparently, there was a case last year where someone was quite upset during a similar workshop – something about feeling personally criticised when a communication style was discussed as 'ineffective’. They’re covering themselves. It's tedious, but… it's the world we live in now. Tedious is an understatement. It feels like we’re preparing people for a therapy session, not a seminar on exporting to Japan! Though, I suppose it  could  get a bit… lively when we start unpacking some of the differences. Especially around directness. Lively is one word for it. I remember a student a few years back, German chap, practically exploded when I suggested a more indirect approach to negotiating. “Unprofessional!” he declared. Though, that  was  a one-on-one tutorial, thankfully. Still. I think we need to be very careful how we phrase things on that form. Perhaps add a line about the seminar being a discussion of  general  tendencies, not judgements of individuals? Good idea, I’ll add that. "This seminar explores common communication patterns and is not intended to offer individual assessments or criticisms.” That sound alright? Aye, that's better. Right, form sorted -ish. Let’s move on to the actual seminar content. I was thinking we could structure it around three main sections: high versus low context cultures, non-verbal communication – gestures, eye contact, that sort of thing – and then finally, the practicalities of virtual communication across borders. Sounds sensible. I'm happy to take the high/low context bit. It’s my favourite, honestly. I’ve got some cracking case studies about misunderstandings in Germany and the US. You know, the German directness versus the American politeness. It always gets a good reaction. I can handle the non-verbal. I did some research on that for a module last year, and I’ve got some good visuals – photos of gestures that have vastly different meanings in different cultures. A thumbs up is a perfect example. So innocuous here, deeply offensive elsewhere.

Honestly, that seminar was… something else. Honestly, the questions they were asking! Like I hadn’t  considered  Foucault’s influence on post-structuralist architecture. It's first year undergrad, Ben, not a doctoral defence! You and your architectural theory. You do love to torture them, don't you? Gently, of course. The benevolent dictator of the seminar room. It’s not torture! It’s… challenging them. And it’s frustrating when they just want the easy answers. Where's the critical thinking? It feels like marking essays is just endless re-writing of Wikipedia articles. I know the feeling. My ‘Introduction to Political Philosophy’ group had a collective meltdown over Machiavelli today. Apparently, anyone who suggests politicians might be a bit… self-serving is inherently cynical. Oh, bless. They’ll learn. The hard way, probably. It’s just... draining. All that optimism. It reminds me a bit of when we first got here, doesn’t it? Everything was so full of potential. It does. Though I think we both underestimated just  how  much potential bureaucracy a Chinese university could hold. Still waiting on that research grant approval, by the way. Ugh, don't even. I checked again this morning - still “under review”. It's been "under review" for three months! Honestly, it's impacting everything. I can't even properly start planning the final stage of the project without knowing if we have the funding for the specialist software. I heard Professor Zhang complaining about it at the faculty meeting. Apparently, there’s a backlog because someone in the finance department decided to implement a new, incredibly complex, digital approval system and hasn't bothered to train anyone how to use it. Classic. It’s always something. It just feels… limiting. Remember how easy things were back at UEA? Annoying, yes, but  easy  in comparison. Massively. And… it makes me think about the house again. Oh? What about it? Don't tell me you've been looking at Rightmove again. We agreed, no house-browsing until at least the end of the academic year. I wasn’t  actively  browsing, I swear. But a colleague was talking about the property market in Norwich, and it just… got me thinking. He said prices have gone up again, but not as drastically as in London, which is a plus. And he sent me a link to a really lovely little cottage in Old Catton.

Honestly, this is lovely, Mum really  did  make the best shepherd’s pie. It just doesn't taste the same when I try to recreate it. It’s probably all the love she put into it, isn't it? Or a secret ingredient. Mmmhmm. Definitely the love. Though knowing Gran, she probably just shoved an extra knob of butter in. She wasn’t shy with the dairy, was she? Remember that time she tried to convince me butter was a vegetable? Oh god, yes! "It comes from a cow, therefore it's practically a salad!" She was… unique. It's a shame the house is being sold. I know it needed work, but it just feels…wrong. All our childhood summers crammed in there. It does. But realistically, it was too much for anyone to manage. And honestly, the amount of stuff Mum and Dad accumulated over the years… it just needed a clear out. Speaking of which, did you see the state of the attic? It was like an archaeological dig. Don’t even  start  me on the attic. Seriously. Aunt Carol’s collection of porcelain dolls! Who needs thirty porcelain dolls?! And all the old furniture… where do you think it's all going? Some of it's being donated, I think. Apparently, a local antique shop took a few pieces. Though I suspect the floral sofa is destined for a landfill. It wouldn't fit in my flat, and frankly, wouldn't  match . I'm thinking of getting a new sofa anyway, something… minimalist. Minimalist? You? The boy who hoarded Lego until he was sixteen? People evolve, sis. I’m a sophisticated engineer now. Speaking of evolving, have you seen that new series, ‘Automated’? It’s on Channel 4. It's all about the impact of robotics on industry. It’s a bit scary, actually. No, I haven’t. I’ve been drowning in marking. Year 11 History essays… they are the bane of my existence. Robotics, huh? Sounds… relevant to your work. Massively. It’s not just manufacturing, it’s everything. They were talking about automation in agriculture – urban farming initiatives using robots to monitor crops, optimize yields. It’s wild. We're designing systems for similar things, though on a smaller scale. It's less 'terminator' and more 'precise agricultural intervention'. That’s…slightly reassuring. Still, the thought of robots taking over all our jobs is a bit unsettling.

Honestly, this risotto is  fighting  me tonight. It’s supposed to be creamy, not… gluey. You say that every time you attempt risotto, Ben. It’ll be fine. Just needs more wine, probably. And a bit less stressing about the perfect consistency. It’s Tuesday night, not a Michelin star inspection. Easy for you to say, you’re a chopping machine. I’m wrestling with starches and Arborio rice. It feels representative of my whole week, actually. Fighting a losing battle. Oh, here we go. What’s up with the research? Still battling the ethics committee over the control group parameters? Worse, actually. Data analysis is…messy. Really messy. I thought, you know, with a relatively simple correlation study, things would be clearer. Turns out teenagers, and their relationship with social media and body image, is  not  simple. No, I imagine not. Teenagers are inherently complex. And social media just amplifies everything. What’s the core problem? Is the sample size too small? No, the sample size is decent. It’s just…the results are all over the place. A tiny, almost statistically insignificant link between hours spent on ‘influencer’ focused accounts and negative body image. Which feels… underwhelming. I was hoping for something more concrete, something that really illustrated the impact. Well, maybe that  is  the impact. It's not a massive, glaring issue for everyone, but a subtle, pervasive influence. It’s not necessarily about a direct ‘before and after’ effect. It could be more nuanced than that. You’re always so focused on getting a neat, tidy result, Ben. Sometimes life—and data—isn’t like that. I know, I know. My supervisor keeps saying that. He says I need to embrace the ambiguity. Easy for  him  to say, he’s already a professor. He doesn't need to publish another paper to secure funding. Fair point. It's a pressure cooker, academia. Speaking of pressure cookers, how was your mum's birthday yesterday? Did she enjoy the garden centre trip? It was… Mum. She enjoyed seeing us, obviously, but she spent the entire time subtly hinting that she expected a power washer for her patio. Apparently, old Mrs. Higgins next door got one. Oh, bless her. The competitive spirit is strong with your mum. Did you give in and suggest getting her one? I tried to steer the conversation towards a nice set of gardening gloves, but she was having none of it.

…and then young Timmy, bless ‘im, he built this whole castle – a proper fortress, it were – right on the tide line. I told ‘im, I said, “Timmy, boy, that ain’t gonna last five minutes.” And didn’t, of course. Gone in a flash. Just… gone. Reminded me a bit of things, that did. Oh, Arthur. Don’t start with the metaphors again. It was a sandcastle. A lovely sandcastle, I’m sure, but just a sandcastle. You’re letting the sea get to you, even when we’re  talking  about the sea. It  is  a powerful image, though, isn't it? Especially given… well, you know. You’ve been a bit quiet since Maureen called yesterday. Quiet? I’m never quiet! I’m just… contemplatin’. That’s all. Maureen just… she just brought up all sorts of things. About the house. About money. Always about money with her. She's worried sick about you both, Arthur. And honestly, you haven’t exactly been making it easy. Sticking your head in the sand, so to speak. I’m not stickin' me 'ead in the sand. I’m just… seein’ how things play out. Sellin’ the house… it feels like givin’ up, don’t it? All them memories… Me and Ethel, raisin’ the kids there… It's a big decision, certainly. But holding onto it when you’re struggling just doesn’t make practical sense, does it? And Maureen has a point; the repairs are getting more and more extensive. You'd be pouring money into a bottomless pit. And you’ve barely left the house in weeks, Arthur. Honestly. It's not healthy. You used to love getting out, even just for a potter around the village. I used to. Things are different now. It's… it’s hard to explain. Feels like a weight, all the time. Like there’s a grey cloud followin’ me around. Sounds a bit like you're getting a bit down, Arthur. Are you sure you’re alright? Honestly? Have you considered talking to someone? There are some really good services available, even just for a chat. They've got volunteer groups, things like that. Talk to someone? What good would that do? They wouldn’t understand. They don’t know what it’s like to… to just feel… useless. Useless? Arthur, don’t talk like that! You’re not useless. You were a wonderful husband to Ethel, a fantastic father… Ethel’s gone, and the kids have got their own lives.

Honestly, I don’t know  what  I’d do without this stuff anymore. Honestly. It's a lifesaver. Ooh, what is that? Another one of your fancy Korean skincare things? You've built up quite the collection, you have. Looks expensive. It is a bit, alright. It’s a sleeping mask. It's got…snail mucin in it. Snail  what  now? Snail…mucus? You're putting snail slime on your face? It doesn't  sound  great, does it? But honestly, it’s amazing. It’s supposed to be incredibly hydrating and good for repairing skin. My skin’s been so dry lately with the heating on. You wouldn’t believe the difference. Well, I’ll believe you’re telling me it works, but I don’t think I could bring myself to smear snail goo all over. I’m more of a…simple cleanser and moisturizer kind of girl. Though, my skin  is  feeling a bit rough. Winter’s awful, isn’t it? It is. And I used to be exactly the same as you, honestly. Just basic stuff. But then I started watching those beauty YouTubers – don’t judge! – and they were all raving about these things. I thought, “What have I got to lose?” No judgement! I watch a few myself, mostly for make-up tutorials. I’m trying to get better at doing a smoky eye. Sarah at the Post Office did mine for her wedding and it was gorgeous, but I can’t recreate it to save my life. Oh, Sarah’s wedding! How was it? I didn’t get to go, did I? It was lovely. Proper fairytale wedding. She looked stunning, obviously. And the cake… massive. Anyway, back to beauty. Have you seen what’s happened with nail varnish lately? Everyone's doing these gel manicures. Oh, I’ve seen them. They look amazing, but the thought of all that UV light… and I read something about the removal process being really damaging? Yeah, that’s what worries me. I get my nails done, but I always just have a normal manicure. Though, I did try those stick-on gel nails the other week. They were alright for a couple of days, but they started peeling. Such a faff. A faff is the word! I tried them once, too. Didn’t last five minutes. I just can't be bothered with all the upkeep. I’m hopeless at maintaining anything, really.

…and honestly, the parking situation around the World Museum is  criminal . I was only nipping in to pick up a resource pack for the year 9s, right? Fifteen minutes, max. Came out to a parking ticket. A  parking ticket , Liam! For seventeen quid. Seventeen! Seventeen quid? That's rough, even for Liverpool city centre. You'd think they'd cut museums a little slack, wouldn’t you? Encourage people to use ‘em. What were you getting for the year 9s anyway? Something on Ancient Egypt? You're always bangin’ on about Ancient Egypt. Nearly. It's a pack on Victorian Liverpool. Trying to get them to connect with the city, you know? Seeing as half of 'em have probably never been to Albert Dock. It's a good resource, loads of primary source images. Just a pain in the backside getting hold of it. How’s work been? Dealing with any… particularly challenging cases this week? Don't even  start  me. Had a safeguarding referral yesterday involving a lad, fifteen, living in… well, let's just say the conditions weren’t great. His mum's struggling, battling a few things. It's the same old story, isn't it? System's stretched, everyone's overworked. Makes you wonder what the point is sometimes, to be honest. Blimey. That sounds… heavy. You’re a good egg for doing it, though. Really. Takes a certain type. I just shout at teenagers about the correct use of the semicolon. Comparatively, it’s a breeze. Don’t undersell yourself, mate. Keeping fifteen year olds engaged with semi-colons is a public service in itself. Speaking of stressful things, you still thinking about that Masters application? Got the interview scheduled? Yep. Next Tuesday. I’m petrified. It’s for Applied Linguistics, at Lancaster. Seems a long way to go for an interview, mind. But the course is brilliant. Designed for practicing teachers like me. Lancaster… that’s ambitious. Good on you, though. You’ll smash it. You always do. You’ve been talking about this for ages. It'll be a proper kick up the backside, though, won't it? Balancing work and study. That’s the scary part. And the money, obviously. Tuition fees are ridiculous. I've been crunching the numbers, trying to figure out how I'm going to afford it all. Might have to cut back on… well, everything, really. No more impulsive vinyl purchases, for a start.

Honestly, it’s just…exhausting, isn’t it? This whole blended family dynamic. Not the kids, they’re lovely, genuinely. It’s… navigating everything  around  them. Tell me about it. Though, thankfully, my navigating mostly involves persuading a tiny human that broccoli  is  a friend, not the enemy. But I get what you mean. It’s a lot of layers. How are things with Mark and his ex, actually? Last I heard it was…tense about the school trip? Tense is putting it mildly. She’s decided that because little Leo is ‘sensitive’ he can’t possibly go on a residential trip with…well, with anyone who isn’t her. Apparently, the thought of him being away for two nights is causing  her  sleepless nights. It’s just…controlling, you know? And Mark is, as always, trying to be the peacemaker, walking on eggshells. It’s wearing him thin. Oh, bless him. He's such a good man, Mark. He just wants everyone to be happy. But sometimes peacemaking just enables the…drama, doesn't it? It’s hard when it impacts Leo. He was so excited about the trip. Exactly! He was practically packing his suitcase weeks ago. And now…it's all been shut down. I tried to gently point out to Mark that constantly accommodating her anxieties isn’t healthy for anyone, least of all Leo, but…you know how he is. He hates conflict. I do. It’s a very…British thing, I think. Avoidance at all costs. My mum was the same. Although, admittedly, she wasn’t navigating a complex co-parenting situation, just…life in general. It’s funny, isn’t it? We spend so much time trying to please everyone, we forget to ask ourselves what  we  actually want. Precisely! And it's impacting me too, of course. I feel like I'm constantly tiptoeing around, trying to be supportive of Mark without getting sucked into the vortex of his ex’s issues. It's draining. I feel like I’m losing a bit of  me  in all of this. Remember when we used to just…go to art galleries on a whim? Or spend an afternoon browsing bookshops? Oh god, yes! Before tiny humans and blended families. Those were the days. It feels like a lifetime ago. Though, to be fair, even  before  Jasper, finding time for those things was a struggle. It's easy to lose yourself, isn't it?

…and honestly, the way they wrote off that storyline in  Line of Duty ? Criminal. Absolutely criminal. It felt like they just…ran out of ideas, didn’t they? You’re still on about  Line of Duty ? It was ages ago, love. And, realistically, they  always  do that. Build it up, build it up, then a pretty underwhelming reveal. It’s their whole schtick. But this was  different . H was supposed to be… significant! Not some bloke turning out to be connected to a previous case that barely anyone remembered! It felt like a slap in the face to anyone who actually invested. Fair enough. I haven't revisited it, so I can’t really comment. I've been trying to wade through all the nature documentaries on iPlayer. Needed something a bit…calmer after a week of fieldwork samples. Honestly, staring at pond water for eight hours straight does things to your brain. Sounds…pleasant. I've been obsessively scrolling Pinterest again. Don’t even ask. Oh god, not the wedding boards again, are they? No! Well, a little. But it’s mostly just…rustic baking ideas. And tiny house designs. I think I'm having a mid-life crisis, but I’m only twenty-six. It's terrifying. I even saved a pin about fermenting vegetables.  Fermenting vegetables , Mark. You, fermenting vegetables? That's a visual. You struggle to keep a basil plant alive. Hey! That was a particularly unforgiving windowsill. And the cat kept trying to eat it. Anyway, it’s just… escapism, alright? Work is proper hectic at the moment. This new research grant, it's brilliant, genuinely, but the admin is relentless. I can imagine. Funding applications are my nemesis. Speaking of hectic, have you heard from Sarah about her birthday? She was hinting at wanting to do something big this year. I think she’s thinking a weekend away. She sent me a Pinterest board… unsurprisingly. Mostly pictures of fancy spa hotels and cocktails with little umbrellas. It looks expensive. Typical Sarah. Always aiming for maximum glamour. She’ll probably end up in Skegness, knowing her luck. Remember that time she tried to throw a ‘sophisticated’ garden party and it rained sideways for three days? Oh, don't remind me! The gazebo nearly took flight, and everyone ended up crammed into the kitchen wearing bin bags as hats. It was legendary. Have you got her something yet?

Oh,  this  one is nice. Look, David, brushed chrome, three lights… a bit modern for the dining room, maybe? But it's only £35.99 with free postage. Hmm. It  is  a bit… stark, isn’t it? I was thinking something with a bit more… warmth? We’ve got all the wood in there, you know? Something that complements it. Though £35.99  is  a steal. What’s the lumen output on that one? Let me see… Oh, it says 600 lumens. Is that good? I honestly have no idea about lumens. I just pick things that look pretty. 600 lumens is… alright. It’ll brighten the room, but probably won’t be enough for proper dining, especially when we’ve got a roast going and need good light to see what you’ve cooked! We need something closer to 800, I’d say. Plus, think about the bulb fitting. Is it a bayonet or an Edison screw? We’ve got a mix of both still. You and your technical specifications!
