Honestly, you sound like my father. Right, let’s filter for 800 lumens. And… Edison screw, because that's what I remember using last time I changed a bulb. Although, to be fair, I mostly just shout at you to do it. I am the designated bulb changer, it's true. It's a burden I bear with grace. Okay, filtering… Right, that one. The one with the frosted glass shades. That’s a bit more like it. 850 lumens, Edison screw, and it’s £42. Ooh, I like that. Very… cosy. Though forty-two pounds is creeping up, isn't it? We were hoping to spend under forty on a fitting. It’s all adding up, isn’t it? Lights, new curtains… and then there’s the potential… house. Don’t remind me. I was back on Rightmove earlier. It’s a dangerous habit, that. Especially when I’m supposed to be working. Found anything tempting? Anything remotely resembling our dream cottage with the big garden and the Aga? Tempting, yes. Realistic, no. I found one in Market Harborough. Four bedrooms, decent sized garden… but it's got a shared driveway and it’s ridiculously overpriced for the area. They want nearly half a million for it. Half a million! In Market Harborough? They’re having a laugh. What’s wrong with our little house, anyway? It just needs a bit of… freshening up.

Honestly, this coffee is a bit weak, isn't it? I swear, I made it exactly how I always do. Maybe the beans are getting old. You always say that, Sarah. It's perfectly fine. You're just a coffee snob, admit it. How was your shift yesterday? Still manic at the hospital? Manic is an understatement. Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was a mermaid and tried to ‘swim’ out of her bed. Took three of us to gently persuade her otherwise. Honestly, some days I question my life choices. Though, seeing Mr. Patel finally get to video call his daughter in Australia... that makes it worthwhile. Oh, bless Mr. Patel. He talks about her constantly. Makes you realise how important those connections are, doesn’t it? This shift at the bungalow was… eventful. Eventful how, Chloe? More wandering, I presume? Old man Hemmings gets up to mischief, doesn’t he? Worse. Brenda, the agency carer, left his lunch unattended for  five  minutes, and he swapped it with Mrs. Lewis’s prune compote. The look on his face when he realised was priceless, but honestly, the mess… it was everywhere! Oh, you're kidding! Prune compote warfare? That’s… something. It’s always the quiet ones, isn’t it? My Mum always said that. Your Mum would have loved the chaos, she really would. Speaking of Mums, has your sister, Carol, had any luck with that job application? The one at the council? That’s what I was going to ask  you  about! She's heard nothing. She’s proper stressed. Says the online application process is a nightmare – all those competency-based questions. I told her to just be herself, but she worries she's not 'corporate' enough. It’s awful, isn't it? Designed to weed people  out , not find the best person. I'm having a look myself, actually. Something a bit more stable than agency work. The hours are killing me. You are? What are you looking at, love? Mostly admin jobs, receptionist roles. Anything with regular hours, really. Saw one at that new veterinary surgery near the station. Thought about it, actually. I always loved animals. Oh, that’s interesting! You'd be brilliant with animals. Remember when we found that stray kitten down by the river, Chloe? You practically raised it single-handedly. That little scamp, Winston! He ended up with a lovely family, didn’t he?

…Honestly, this is brilliant, love. You do a roast chicken sandwich  so  well. It’s a national treasure, it is. Flattery will get you everywhere, David. Though it’s hardly a culinary masterpiece, is it? Just chicken, stuffing, cranberry, and a bit of mayo. Don’t undersell it! Anyway… speaking of needing comfort, I was reading this article this morning. Apparently, the whole ‘blue light filter’ on your phone before bed? Mostly rubbish. Oh really? I've been a dutiful filter-user for years! What  does  work then, according to this font of wisdom? The interesting bit was about temperature. Apparently, your core body temperature needs to  drop  to fall asleep properly. So, a cooler room is good, obviously, but they’re saying a warm bath or shower an hour or two before bed can actually  help  – because your body then cools down afterwards. Makes sense, doesn't it? That's… actually quite clever. I always feel sleepy after a hot bath, but I just assumed it was post-relaxation bliss, not physiological temperature regulation! I'll definitely give that a proper go. Though, knowing you, you’ll be rigging up some complicated cooling system for the bedroom next. Hey, I’m just a proactive sleeper! Remember that camping trip we did in the Peak District? I spent a whole day perfecting the airflow through the tent to minimise condensation. Oh,  please . “Perfecting airflow.” You were mostly rearranging guy ropes for three hours and then complaining it was still damp. And getting us hopelessly lost on the way back to the car. Lost? We weren’t lost! We took a… scenic route. A very long, scenic route involving a field full of sheep and a farmer who looked seriously unimpressed. Scenic routes don’t involve turning a twenty-minute walk into a two-hour ordeal, David. You and your insistence on not checking the map. It's a recurring theme. Remember Rome? Rome was different! The streets were a… labyrinth. Honestly, those city planners need a talking to. No logical grid system. And the signage… non-existent. It’s not my fault I have a strong sense of direction, even if it consistently points towards adventure. Your “strong sense of direction” led us on a three-hour detour to a rather questionable industrial estate. We ended up asking for directions from a man selling knock-off handbags. He was very helpful!

…and then, honestly, Mr. Nibbles just  launched  himself off the top of the cage. Full-on, dramatic dive. I thought he'd broken something. No way! Your hamster is a menace. A tiny, fluffy menace. Honestly, you need to post a video. It would go viral. Was it a calculated jump? Like, did he  think  he could make it to the bookshelf? Hamsters are surprisingly intelligent, you know. I read this article… Oh, here we go. The hamster conspiracy theories. He probably just misjudged it, love. They're not exactly known for their spatial awareness. Mine once tried to stuff an entire carrot into his cheek pouches. Looked like a furry balloon. He definitely didn’t calculate it. He was chasing a sunflower seed. A  single  sunflower seed. It was pathetic, really. He landed on the bedding, totally fluffed out, then just…carried on eating it like nothing happened. They’re so resilient, aren’t they? It’s weird. Like little, armoured tanks. Speaking of resilient... have you guys seen the new lad in the history seminar? The one with the ridiculous hair? Oh, the one who looks like a startled fox? Yeah. What about him? Well, he was presenting today, right? And some bloke actually asked him, completely straight-faced, if it was difficult being a ginger in the sun. You are  kidding  me! What did he say?! He just blinked. Like, a very slow, deliberate blink. Then he said, "I apply factor 50, thank you for your concern." The entire lecture hall lost it. Oh, brilliant! That’s amazing. People are awful, aren't they? It's always the gingers. It’s like they're fair game for awful jokes. It’s the lack of melanin, I reckon. People feel emboldened to say things they wouldn't dream of saying to someone with a normal hair colour. It's a societal thing. We need to analyse it. Oh, don't start with the societal analysis, Elara. It's just being a knobhead. Some people are just knobs. I dated a ginger once, lovely bloke, incredibly pale, always burning. We had to get him a hat even on cloudy days. My cousin, Liam, is ginger. Proper fiery red. He used to get called 'Rusty' at school. He hated it. He dyed his hair black when he was sixteen, then bright blue for a bit. It suited him, actually. It's just… the  audacity  of that question in the seminar.

Right, that  should  solidify my position here. Honestly, this is going to take ages, isn't it? We’ve been at this for… three hours? Feels like three days, more like. And you think  that’s  solid? Wait ‘til your Uncle Dave gets a run at you. He’s a ruthless sod in Risk, you know. Absolutely no sentiment. Reminds me of… Genghis Khan, actually. Oh, don’t even  start  comparing Dave to Genghis Khan, Geoff! You always do that when he’s winning. It’s a bit dramatic, isn’t it? And honestly, you've barely got anything on the board yourself. Dramatic? I’m stating a historical fact! The man understood territorial acquisition! Anyway, I’m building a defensive line. Slow and steady wins the race. Unlike some people who rush in, guns blazing... Hey! I’m being strategic. It's about taking risks. You’re playing it so safe you’ll be here ‘til Christmas. Speaking of which, Mum’s already going on about the Christmas lists. Apparently, little Leo wants a… remote control dinosaur that  talks . Oh, bless him. He’s obsessed with dinosaurs at the moment. And apparently, it has to have “realistic roaring sounds”. Honestly, everything is about realism with children these days. When I was little, a plastic dinosaur was  sufficient . Realistic roaring sounds… Sounds like my wife when I forget to take the bins out. Speaking of things needing updating, has anyone seen my glasses? I swear I left them on the table. Everything’s blurry. Under the instructions for the game, I think. You were squinting at them earlier trying to decipher the bits about card exchanges. Ah, there they are. Thanks, lad. Right, back to world domination. You know, I always preferred the old version of this game. The maps were better. More… epic. I always thought the maps looked the same. It's the little plastic armies that are the fun part. Though, remember when Aaron tried to play with us last year? He was convinced Australia was a single territory and kept putting all his troops there. Oh god, that  was  a disaster. He was so determined. “But it’s all desert! One big desert!” He just didn't get the concept of borders. He’s a bright lad, Aaron, but geography isn’t his strong suit, is it? Reminds me of when I tried to explain to someone from the States that Bedford isn't near London.

…and honestly, Professor Davies just looked  so  disappointed when I said I was still unsure about the dissertation topic. Like I was personally offending him with my indecision. Honestly, the man thinks existentialism is a personality trait. Oh, Davies. He's a trip, innit? He once tried to explain the meaning of life using only biscuits and a sticky post-it note. But look, you’re allowed to be unsure. It’s… uni? That’s kinda the point, isn’t it? Figuring things out as you go along. What are you even considering? Still history? I  thought  history. But then I was looking at jobs afterwards…and it's either teaching – which I don't think I have the patience for – or museum work, which is ridiculously competitive. And Mum keeps sending me links to ‘sensible’ jobs. Accountancy, of all things! Like I’d survive a spreadsheet. Your Mum's a menace. She was trying to set me up with her friend’s son who’s a chartered accountant last time I was home. Said he was ‘stable’. Stable?! I’d rather wrestle a badger. Exactly! Stable is code for…beige. I was talking to Chloe the other day, she's already applied for a training contract at a law firm. She's terrifyingly organised. Chloe always was a machine. Remember in sixth form when she colour-coded her revision notes by historical significance? I was just hoping to remember  anything  at that point. Don’t compare yourself to Chloe. Honestly. It’ll ruin your day. What about something completely different? Like, you’re brilliant at photography. Could you do something with that? I've thought about it, but it feels… risky. Like a hobby, not a career. And Dad would have a fit. He wants me to follow in his Footsteps, be a proper, respectable architect. Your Dad wants everyone to be an architect. He tries to design our takeaway boxes. It's a bit much. Look, careers aren't set in stone, are they? You're 21! You’ve got ages to mess things up and change your mind. Easy for you to say, you know exactly what you want to do. Veterinary science, right? You've always wanted to be Dr. Doolittle. It’s not  always  been vet sci. I went through a phase of wanting to be a pop star. Terribly embarrassing photos exist. I even tried to learn the ukulele.

…and then Mr. Davies actually said, “The socio-economic impact of the Industrial Revolution wasn’t  just  about factories, it was about…people’s  lives .” Like, no duh, sir. We all knew that. It felt so condescending. Davies does have a habit of stating the blindingly obvious, doesn't he? Ours is banging on about the ethics of gene editing again. Honestly, it's like he thinks we’re all gonna be designing super-babies in our bedrooms. Seriously! It’s a biology project, not a sci-fi convention. Though, I did read this article about CRISPR… it’s pretty mind-blowing what they can do now. Potentially cure genetic diseases and all that. Yeah, but that's the thing, isn't it? 'Potentially'. And who gets access to that 'potential'? It'll be the rich, obviously. Always is. It's just… another way to widen the gap. You’re going down a dark path, mate. It's supposed to be about the science, not… well, inequality. It  is  about inequality! Everything is! Even this project. Like, we're both doing A-Levels, we’ve got decent schools, we're worrying about uni applications… there are kids our age who are worrying about where their next meal is coming from. It feels a bit… detached, doesn’t it? I guess. It's just… a bit overwhelming to think about everything at once. I saw a thing on the news the other day about food banks being overwhelmed. It's grim. Dad was saying that even people  with  jobs are needing to use them now with everything being so expensive. Exactly! It’s not just ‘those people’ anymore, is it? It’s everyone. Even my Uncle Raj, he’s a builder, and he was saying work’s been really slow, and materials are through the roof. He was proper stressed. That's rough. So, back to the project…are you actually making progress with the ethics bit? I'm just stuck on the historical context for the Industrial Revolution. It all blurs together after a while - steam engines, child labour, squalor… I'm skimming. Honestly. It's just a load of philosophical waffle. I’m focusing on the potential benefits, hoping Davies won't notice I haven't really tackled the downsides. What about your research? Found anything good about the impact on Slough? Actually, yeah. I found some stuff about how Slough became a trading hub, because of the canals.

…and honestly, the whole recording process was a nightmare. Not technically, mind you. Old Mr. Hemmings at the studio is a wizard, truly. It was  me . I just…freeze. Utterly. He kept having to say, “Right, Penelope, from the top,” and I’d just stare blankly, forgetting what I was supposed to be saying about, of all things, prize-winning marrows! Marrows? Seriously? Is that what you're doing now? Voiceovers for vegetable competitions? Don't laugh, darling! It’s surprisingly lucrative. Apparently, the Surrey Horticultural Society wants to up their online presence. And Mr. Hemmings knows I used to do a fair bit of radio work years ago. But still. Standing in a soundproof booth, talking intimately about the virtues of a 'Long Green Improved' marrow… it felt rather absurd. I can imagine. Sounds…intense. I spent most of yesterday avoiding Mrs. Higgins next door. Oh, not again. What’s she been up to now? Still complaining about your music? Worse. She cornered me about “finding a nice young man”. Apparently, Derek from number 23 is a ‘good sort’. He’s practically ancient! And he collects garden gnomes. Derek and the gnomes. Good grief. You'd think people would learn. Still, bless her heart, she probably just wants you to be happy. Though a battalion of garden gnomes isn’t exactly my idea of bliss either. Happy? I'm trying to navigate the benefit system and avoid well-meaning but incredibly irritating neighbours! Happiness feels a long way off. Actually, speaking of feeling… everything aches. Oh, don't tell me your back’s playing up? You really must book that physiotherapy appointment. I told you about Mrs. Abernathy’s physio, didn’t I? Brilliant woman. Got me moving again after that awful incident with the garden gnome… ironically. The garden gnome? What happened? A long story involving a slippery path and a particularly hefty gnome. Let’s just say my left knee hasn’t been the same since. These joints, honestly! They’re a constant reminder of getting older. Tell me about it. Even just getting up off the sofa feels like an Olympic sport. It's probably all the sitting around, though. I need to  do  something. You do. Something gentle to start with. The physio will suggest exercises. And perhaps we can go for a little walk in the Shalford park tomorrow? We could grab a coffee afterwards.

Right, this gravy  needs  more flour, doesn’t it? Honestly, you London lot wouldn't know a proper gravy if it slapped you in the face. It's gotta be proper thick, like… like building paste, almost. Building paste? Honestly, Maisie, you’re exaggerating. It looks perfectly… serviceable. And coming from someone who once tried to make Yorkshire puddings in a microwave, I think your gravy opinions are slightly suspect. That was  one  time! And I was under pressure! University deadlines, okay? It’s not the same. A proper gravy elevates a roast dinner. Elevates it! Yours always seems a bit…watery. No offence. None taken. It's just a preference, I guess. I prefer a gravy you can actually  pour , not one that threatens to anchor the whole meal to the plate. So, how’s work been? Still battling conference centre chaos? Oh, don't even  start  me. Last week was… a special kind of hell. Some tech conference, right? Hundreds of blokes in hoodies talking about blockchain. I swear, if I had to direct one more man to the charging points, I was going to scream. Sounds… stimulating. At least you're never bored. My job is fairly repetitive. Production schedules, quality control, making sure everything runs smoothly. It’s… safe. Predictable. Sometimes I miss the chaos of uni, to be honest. Safe is good! Especially when you’re trying to, you know,  adult . I’m starting to think ‘adulting’ is a scam, though. Like, who decided we all needed mortgages and pension plans? I’m proper overwhelmed thinking about it. Tell me about it. I’ve been looking at flats lately, just… browsing, really. The prices are insane. You get a cupboard for half a million. It’s utterly ridiculous. And then there’s the whole deposit thing… it feels impossible. It  is  impossible! Mum and Dad helped me a bit with a deposit for this place, thankfully. But even then, it's… a lot. And this place isn't exactly Buckingham Palace, y'know? It's a decent enough little flat, but it's on the edge of town. Cambridge is pricey. Lewisham's bad, but this is… another level. Did you manage to get away at all this summer? I went back home for a week with my family, which was nice. My little cousin is obsessed with TikTok now. Terrifying. Ooh, TikTok! Don’t get me started.

Honestly, I still can't get over  Everything Everywhere All at Once . It was… a lot. Like, a beautiful, chaotic, existential lot. Right? I felt genuinely  exhausted  after that film. In a good way, though. It was brilliant, wasn’t it? Michelle Yeoh is a legend. Exhausted is the word. I’m usually pretty good with sci-fi weirdness, but that one just kept layering on the weirdness. Though I have to admit, the hot dog fingers got me. Proper laughing. Oh, the hot dog fingers are iconic now, aren’t they? My little sister, Maisie, has been walking around pretending to have them all week. It's disturbing. Did someone say hot dog fingers? Honestly, it's a masterpiece of visual comedy. I saw a TikTok about the bagel everything, it was amazing. Maisie’s seen it too then? Blimey, you’re exposing the youth to some heavy stuff! I was expecting  Barbie  to be the most mind-bending thing she’d watch this month. She watched  Barbie  with us last week. Loved it, naturally. Said Ken was “a bit dim, but cute.” She’s eleven, so…  Barbie  was… something. Visually, it was incredible. I wasn’t expecting it to be so…philosophical, actually. I thought it was going to be a fluff piece. Exactly! It was a really clever critique, hiding in a bright pink package. It made my dad surprisingly thoughtful, too. He was going on about patriarchy for a good hour afterwards. My Da would just be complaining about the price of the tickets. He'd say, "It’s just a doll, what’s all the fuss about?" He’s old school. My nan wouldn’t have lasted five minutes. She’d be muttering about “modern nonsense” and asking when they're going to make a decent period drama again. She’s obsessed with  Call the Midwife .  Call the Midwife  is good! I watched a few episodes with my grandma. It's properly moving, though. I cried. Oh, you will  always  cry at  Call the Midwife . That’s its entire purpose. Speaking of moving, has anyone seen  Past Lives ? I'm thinking about going this weekend. I’ve heard really good things! Apparently, it’s heartbreaking. Yeah, a few people at uni have mentioned it. Slow burn, apparently? It’s supposed to be beautifully shot, though. I'm usually more of an action film kinda guy, to be honest.

Honestly, Mum, Paris was  amazing  but getting back… a disaster. Absolute chaos at Charles de Gaulle. Oh dear, was it? I thought things had calmed down a bit after all the strikes. What happened, love? You sounded bright as a button on the phone, just a bit… frazzled. Frazzled is an understatement. It was the queues, mostly. Security, then passport control, then luggage… and then someone decided to have a full-blown meltdown because their connecting flight had been cancelled. It was like a domino effect of stress. Paris sounds…intense. I had a blissfully quiet weekend, actually. Just binge-watched bad reality TV and attempted to bake sourdough. Key word: attempted. It looks like a hockey puck. Oh, bless you. Sounds perfect, actually, compared to my experience. And don't even  ask  about trying to navigate the Metro with a suitcase. Oh, the Metro  is  a beast. Remember when your Auntie Carol got completely lost down there? Ended up in some tiny village outside the city. Don’t remind me! That was mortifying. Anyway, the city itself was incredible, though. We did all the touristy things – Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Notre Dame… it’s just… getting there and back felt like an endurance test. Oh! And I managed to acquire a souvenir. An entirely unintentional one. Ooh, a real souvenir? Did you accidentally shoplift a miniature Eiffel Tower? Very funny. No, it’s… considerably less glamorous. I tripped. Tripped? Where? Are you alright? I’m fine, Mum, honestly. Just a bit bruised. We were walking along the Seine, admiring the bridges, and there was this… cobblestone. A particularly treacherous cobblestone. And bam. Down I went. Scraped my knee pretty badly. Oh no! Did you at least have a romantic falling-into-arms moment? Nope. I landed squarely on my knee. Thankfully, Liam – you know, the guy I went with – helped me up, but it’s throbbing now. I think it might be more than just a scrape. Liam, yes, the architect. Nice young man. You should get it checked, darling. Don't want it getting infected. I’ve got some antiseptic cream upstairs. And a bandage, of course. It’s always something with you and your clumsiness. Remember that time you broke your arm falling off a roundabout when you were eight? Mum! You hold onto that story for dear life, don’t you? It was  one  roundabout incident, and I was showing off.

Morning, Chloe! Just grabbing a coffee before the 9am. How was your weekend? Anything exciting happen? Oh, hi Ben! Morning to you too. Honestly, pretty chilled. Went to Chichester with my Mum on Saturday. She's been wanting to go to the cathedral for ages. It was… nice. Bit touristy, but Mum loved it. How about you? Did Bedford beckon? Bedford didn’t beckon, sadly. Actually stayed  in  Brighton. Shocking, I know. Just needed a proper lie-in and a bit of peace and quiet. I’ve been meaning to ask, how are things going with the new trainees at the shop? Still having to smooth things over after…well, you know,  that  incident with Dave and the till? Don't even  mention  Dave. Honestly. He’s on a final warning now, thankfully. I spent most of Sunday filling out incident reports. It’s exhausting, being a supervisor sometimes. You wouldn’t believe the things people try to get away with. Thankfully, the others are good. Sarah’s really picking things up quickly, and she actually asked me about referencing styles the other day - reminded me of uni! Speaking of, how’s the TEFL course going? Still drowning in the British National Corpus? Drowning is a polite way to put it. We’re looking at passive voice constructions at the moment. It’s… subtle, isn't it? How something seemingly innocuous can completely change meaning. I spent an hour yesterday trying to explain it to a group who were convinced it was just ‘lazy English.’ It’s moments like that I question my life choices. Tell me about it. Trying to explain grammar to people can feel like banging your head against a wall. Although, remember old Mrs. Higgins in our undergraduate degree? She could make even the most Byzantine syntax sound…almost accessible. Oh God, Mrs. Higgins. A legend. I still think about her lectures sometimes. Though, honestly, I wouldn’t put myself through creative writing again. The feedback was brutal. You and I both know we’re better at  analysing  writing than producing it. Absolutely. I think I'm better at the organisational side of things, honestly. Which is fortunate, considering. Payday’s Friday, right? I’m counting down the seconds. Need to contribute something towards the student loan this month, plus I promised my sister I’d help with…well, never mind. It’s a long story involving a dodgy ex and a questionable proposal.

Right, so you  have  to keep an eye on it. It’ll look like nothing’s happening for ages, then suddenly…boom. All the water’s gone and it’s sticking to the bottom. Ruined. Absolutely ruined. Oh dear. Sounds stressful. My mum never made rice like that, she always used one of those electric rice cookers. No fuss at all. Though, she wasn’t much of a cook generally, to be fair. Everything tasted…beige. Beige? That’s a good way of putting it. Electric ones are okay, I guess. Not the same though, is it? This is proper rice. Speaking of proper, are we having enough spice in this curry? I chucked in a decent amount of chilli powder, but… I think it's good. Remember when we went to that Indian place in Bournemouth last year? The one with the voucher? It was  way  too hot, even for you, and you pretend you can handle anything. I was sweating buckets. Little Leo here wouldn’t have stood a chance. Bournemouth! God, that was a mission. Getting there, finding parking…and yes, that curry practically melted my face off. I think they just threw in a jar of jalapenos. Still, the voucher made it worth it, didn't it? Saved a good tenner. It did. Everything’s so expensive these days. I'm trying to be better about meal planning and not wasting food. It’s shocking how quickly meat goes off. I bought some chicken last week and it was… questionable, by Wednesday. Ugh, yeah. That’s the worst. The smell… Anyway, back to the rice. Right, it’s bubbling nicely now. We’ll put the lid on and leave it for fifteen minutes. No peeking! It  does  look…fluffy. You’re a rice master, you are. It's funny, isn't it? How much we think about seemingly small things like rice. It's not like it's a fancy ingredient. It’s all about the details, innit? It’s the same with everything. Like, look at all this stuff they put in processed food. Ridiculous amounts of salt and fat. It’s no wonder everyone’s ending up with…well, you know. Don't get me started. I read something the other day about how some food companies are deliberately adding things to make food  more  addictive. It's appalling. It reminded me of… oh, this is silly, but it reminded me of something I saw on a documentary about jellyfish.

Right, so then Mr. Henderson, bless ‘im, actually  asked  if I’d applied for any jobs this week. Like he’s me dad or summat. I just… stared at ‘im. He's a postie, what does  he  know about job huntin’ these days? Honestly, Liam, you need to at least  pretend  to try and answer. It’s for your own good, and it stops Brenda at the Jobcentre naggin’ you. She’s got a voice like a foghorn, that woman. Brenda is a character, definitely. She tried to get me to do a course in basket weaving last year. Basket weaving! Said it was ‘transferrable skills.’ Transferrable to… what, exactly? Selling baskets down the market? Though, actually, with how many tourists we get in summer… might be a viable business idea. Aye, and I’ll be runnin’ it, will I? Look, it’s just… demoralisin’, innit? Sendin’ out CVs into the void. Everythin’ wants experience, but how am I supposed to  get  experience when no one’ll give me a chance? I’ve a degree, for crying out loud. A proper one, from Lancaster. It’s brutal, yeah. But you’ve been lookin’ for, what, nearly a year now? Maybe you need to broaden yer horizons a bit? Not just applyin' for fancy marketing jobs. Broaden me horizons to what, then? Workin’ at Booths stackin’ shelves? No offence, Chloe, but I didn't go to uni to stack shelves. No one  wants  to stack shelves, Liam, but it’s money, and it’s a foot in the door. I started at the Co-op after graduating. Least it gave me somethin’ to talk about in interviews. And it paid the bills. Speaking of bills… Did anyone see that documentary on telly last night about the energy prices? Absolutely terrifying. Me mum’s already started frettin' about winter. Oh God, yeah. It was mental. It's gonna be a long winter, that's for sure. Honestly, I'm worried about bein' back home for Christmas. The heating's always on full blast, it's like a sauna. And Dad moans every time the bill comes. My nan’s the same. Says we’re livin’ in the dark ages again. She remembers when you could leave the lights on all the time. Happy days, apparently. Though, she also remembers when everything cost tuppence, so… You’ve got a point. It’s all relative, isn’t it?

Oh, this is proper good, this is. You really outdid yourself, ANON. Honestly, after a day chasing venue managers, a home-cooked meal is just… bliss. Glad you like it, love. It’s nothing fancy, just a simple carbonara. Though, truth be told, I had a bit of help from a YouTube tutorial. My cooking skills peaked at scrambled eggs about twenty years ago, and they’ve been steadily declining since. Don’t sell yourself short! It’s better than anything I could whip up, and believe me, my attempts are usually disastrous. Last time I tried baking a cake, it ended up looking like a geological formation. Solid as a rock, that thing. Sounds impressive…ly inedible. So, venue managers, eh? Still battling with them for dates and demands? It sounds stressful. You have  no  idea. This conference in November? The keynote speaker wants the stage decked out like a spaceship. A spaceship, ANON! And the AV team are saying it'll take a week to build, and the venue wants double the usual rate for the extra rigging. Honestly, sometimes I question my life choices. All this for people to sit in a room and listen to someone talk about data analytics. Sounds… ambitious. Data analytics  and  spaceships. It’s a bit much, innit? Remember when I used to complain about having to choose between Coronation Street and the snooker? Seems like a simpler time. Oh, you and your soaps. Mum always said you could recite entire storylines. Seriously, it was scary. But yeah, simpler definitely. Although, even  you  used to get worked up about the local cricket team. That’s different! That’s a matter of local pride! Anyway, you need to stand your ground with these people. You're the coordinator, aren’t you? You’re supposed to be in charge. Don’t let them walk all over you. I try. It’s just… politeness. I’m naturally polite. Yorkshire folk are bred to apologise even when  they're  in the right! It's a curse, honestly. I end up saying “Sorry, but could you  possibly  reconsider the spaceship?" instead of "Actually, that's ridiculous, and we haven’t got the budget!” That’s your problem right there. You need to toughen up. Being nice is good, but it doesn't pay the bills. Speaking of toughening up, are you still going to that yoga class? You were saying it was helping with the stress.

Right, who’s on washing up duty tonight? Honestly, this kitchen looks like a bomb’s hit it. It's always the same after a roast. Not me! I've got, like, loads of homework. History essay on… ugh, Hitler. It’s so boring. Hitler boring? That’s a new one. Actually, it  is  a pretty weighty topic for a homework assignment. Don’t skim over it, alright? It’s important to understand how… well, how awful he was. I’ll do it. Less awful than Hitler, definitely. Though the washing up isn't exactly a party. Bless you, Leo. You're a star. Just remember to actually  wash  them, not just swill them. And Daniel, try and at least  pretend  to look at your homework. It’s due when? Thursday. But Mrs. Davies said we could have an extension if we showed effort. So, I’m strategically showing effort… by thinking about tennis. Ah, tennis. You practicing with Mr. Henderson still? He’s a good coach. Yeah, he's alright. He keeps going on about my serve needing more ‘oomph’. Honestly, it’s fine. “Oomph” is important in a serve, darling. You need that power. It’s like marketing – needs impact! Speaking of impact, have you seen your father’s attempts to grow a moustache? Hey! It’s coming along. It’s… subtle. A distinguished grey fleck. It looks like a dust bunny glued to your face, Dad. Sorry. Oh, Leo! You’re terrible. He's modelling himself on some dashing Victorian detective, apparently. It’s all because of that Agatha Christie box set he got for his birthday. It  is  a good box set! And a refined gentleman  does  require a subtle moustache… it’s about gravitas. Gravitas? You look like you’re trying to be a villain. Like, a really bad one. He’s been showing me his Instagram feed for ‘inspiration’. Apparently, there’s a whole community dedicated to facial hair. It’s terrifying. He’s started following accounts with names like 'HandlebarHeroes' and 'WhiskerWarriors'. It's research! I need to understand the craft. Does he  tell  these 'WhiskerWarriors' about his operation manager job? That’d be awkward. Probably. Daniel, have you spoken to Chloe lately? You were supposed to be going to the cinema with her this weekend, weren’t you? Oh, yeah... Chloe. Um… we kind of… postponed. Postponed? Why? Is everything alright? It’s just… she's been really busy with rehearsals for the school play.

Right, are we nearly there yet? Honestly, this traffic is a nightmare, even for a Saturday. Feels like everyone in Greater Manchester is heading to Macclesfield today. Not too far, Mum. Just past the roundabout and then it's pretty much straight on. You've been saying that for the last ten minutes though! Are you still stressing about fitting that sideboard in? Well,  am  I? It’s a solid oak sideboard, love. Not some chipboard nonsense. It needs to go in the dining room, and if it doesn’t fit… well, that's a whole heap of bother. I told Brenda at the shop I needed precise measurements, didn’t I? She just waved her hand and said, “Oh, it’ll be fine, love.” Brenda knows nothing about my dining room. Brenda always was a bit like that. More interested in a chat than actual selling. Remember when she tried to sell me a bright orange kettle? Said it was “very modern”. Oh, don’t I just. Honestly, that woman. Anyway, if it doesn’t fit, it’s going straight back. And I’m not taking it back on my own, I can tell you that. It’ll be  you  two. Honestly, Mum! You’re already planning my weekend. What about my essay? Essay can wait. Solid oak furniture cannot. Speaking of things needing shifting… did you ever get round to taking those old curtains to the tip? Not yet. It feels like such a mission, honestly. And I need Dad’s van. I could drop ‘em next week, if you like. Doctor’s appointment in Macclesfield, could swing by. Although, that tip is always a mess, isn’t it? Last time I was there, half the staff were just stood around chatting. It's a disgrace. You pay your council tax… Honestly. Anyway, did you hear about poor Sarah and her family? Sarah… oh, from uni? The one who’s always stressed about exams? No, not that Sarah. Sarah from the book club! Her husband, Mark, he’s really poorly. Apparently, they’re saying it could be… well, you know… dementia. Early onset. It’s just awful. They have those two little girls, don't they? Terrible news. She’s such a lovely woman, Sarah. Always bringing biscuits to the meetings. It's heartbreaking when it happens so young. My aunt Elsie… it was a slow decline, took years.

…and honestly, the whole thing just feels so…random. Like, one minute I'm presenting the Q3 projections, the next I'm being told my role is ‘at risk of redundancy’. At risk! As if it’s a dodgy weather forecast. Oh, darling. That’s awful. Absolutely awful. I had a feeling things weren't brilliant at StellarTech, they’ve been quiet on the funding front haven’t they? But redundancy… that’s a shock. How many others? Apparently, they’re looking at cutting three positions in my department. Three! It’s a small team, Mum. And I’ve only been there a year. Feels a bit unfair, to be honest. They said consultations start next week. It  is  unfair. You’ve worked so hard getting that graduate job. Remember all those applications? All that fretting? Don’t let them just brush you aside. You have rights, you know. And your dad’s good with that sort of thing, he can have a look at your contract, make sure they’re doing everything properly. Thanks, Mum. I will definitely ask him. It’s just…disheartening. I actually  like  working there. Okay, the office is beige bordering on depressing, and Gary in accounts smells perpetually of tuna, but it's a good team. Well, you're a capable girl, you'll find something else. Don't dwell on it too much right now. What are we doing this weekend? I was thinking we could finally go to that garden centre near Diss. I need to get some lavender for the front, and I saw some lovely hydrangeas. Oh, that sounds nice. Though, truthfully, I was hoping to maybe hit the gym a couple of times. I’ve been really trying to be consistent with it, building up to being able to actually  lift  something respectable. I feel so feeble at the moment. You’re not feeble! You always were a bit of a bookworm, preferred a good novel to climbing trees, but you're perfectly strong enough. Though, I do think a bit of exercise would do you good, especially with all this stress. Remember your Grandad? He swore by a good walk every day, kept him going until he was ninety-two! I do. And he ate a biscuit with  every  cup of tea. A seriously unhealthy amount of biscuits. Which reminds me, I’ve been terrible with my diet lately.

This is good, Mum. Really good. Better than school dinners, definitely. Glad you like it, darling. It’s just a simple tomato and basil sauce, but sometimes simple is best. And yes,  definitely  better than school dinners. They haven't improved since  I  was at school, I reckon. More! More! Easy there, little man. You've already got half the jar on your face. Right, Leo, we need to actually  discuss  the summer. It's creeping up, isn’t it? School finishes next week. I know! It's gonna be brilliant. No more Mr. Henderson droning on about the Tudors. Although…he did do a pretty good impression of Henry VIII. Fascinating. But we need a plan, Leo. You can't just spend the entire six weeks glued to the telly watching  Stick with Mick . Though, I admit, that programme is… surprisingly addictive. Hey! Mick’s awesome! He builds dens and goes on adventures. I’ve been trying to build a den in the garden, but it keeps collapsing. Well, building a structurally sound den is a skill, it takes patience. Maybe we could look up some proper den-building techniques online? Or ask Mr. Davies next door, he's pretty good at DIY. Good idea. Although, I was thinking more about hanging out with Finn. He’s going to try and learn some Japanese. Japanese? That’s…ambitious. Where did  that  come from? He says he wants to be an anime artist when he grows up. And you need to know Japanese to understand what they’re saying, obviously. He’s trying to teach me some phrases, but it sounds like gibberish. Like… “Konichiwa” or something? I keep saying it wrong. Well, it’s a tricky language, I’ve heard. Good for Finn, though, taking on a challenge. Maybe I should try learning something new too. Although, concentrating with  this  one… is a full-time job. You could learn the guitar again! You used to be really good. You even played in a band, didn't you? Oh, that was a long time ago, darling. A  very  long time ago. Before your…well, before life got complicated. It’s probably all rusty now. But maybe, just maybe… We could dig it out of the attic. Cool! And we could go swimming more. Remember last summer, we went to the lake every week? I do. That was lovely. It’s just… getting  to  the lake with everything.

Right, so, this bit's brilliant, innit? Absolute tension. Proper Hitchcockian stuff. Though, honestly, I still reckon  The Birds  is scarier. Is it, though? This is proper psychological, like.  The Birds  was just… birds. A lot of flapping and pecking. This is gettin’ under yer skin. Though I do appreciate a good avian assault, I’ll admit. Reminds me of me nan's garden, actually. She loved pigeons. Your nan and pigeons… classic. You always find a way to bring it back to Birkenhead, don't you? Speaking of things that inspire low-level fear, I had the dentist today. Oh, no. The dreaded dentist? What happened? Didn't you just get a filling like, last month? I did. Apparently, it was a  slightly  bigger cavity than they initially thought. And now they’re talking about a root canal. A ROOT CANAL, Liam! I nearly leapt off the chair. The sound of the drill...it's a uniquely horrible experience. Makes you question the very fabric of existence. Dramatic, much? They give you the good stuff, do they? The gas and air? They offered. I declined. I wanted to  feel  the fear, apparently. Method acting for life, I suppose. Helps with the writing, having a good existential crisis. It gives it… depth. Right, ‘cause wrestling with dental torment is totally conducive to crafting award-winning prose. You're a weirdo, you know that? Actually, thinking about escaping pain… remember that disastrous holiday to Greece we took in uni? Oh, god. Don’t even. The sunstroke, the questionable kebabs… and your attempt to learn Greek by just shouting louder in English. Hey! It got me served, didn’t it? And it was a truly cultural experience. Although, I maintain that the taverna owner was actively taking the mick. He just kept bringing me more ouzo. Said it was “for the spirit.” More like for silencing your attempts at language acquisition. You sounded like you were trying to summon a demon, not order a beer. Speaking of spirits, you still reading that weird historical fiction thing? The one with all the druids? Aye, still at it. It’s… a slog, honestly. The prose is a bit flowery for me. But the research is fascinating. Apparently, ancient Britons had some seriously messed-up rituals. They would… well, I won’t bore you with the details. It involves mistletoe and sacrifices. Right, maybe I’ll stick to crime novels.

Honestly, this week has just  flown  by. Feels like yesterday we were arguing about whether to put milk in first, and now it's nearly the weekend again. How's the little 'uns been at school, love? Any drama? Oh, Mum, you know they're always little dramas. Year twos are at that stage where everything is a crisis. Little Timmy didn't share his crayons, Maisie thinks someone looked at her funny… the usual. But honestly, it’s really rewarding. I’m starting to feel like I’m actually  making  a difference, you know? It’s a nice feeling. It is. I remember you always being good with children. Even as a little one, you were organising all the cousins, playing teachers… it suits you. And you’re settling in alright at the school then? They seem a decent bunch? They are. Really supportive colleagues, which is brilliant. And the Head is lovely, really forward-thinking. We've been talking about implementing some new reading schemes. It's just… a lot. It’s a big step up from the training, actually putting everything into practice. Long hours too, planning and marking. Oh, I imagine. Teaching isn’t for the faint of heart. You’ll get used to the workload, though. You always were a hard worker. Speaking of work, I’m still dithering about what to do. Honestly, I’m starting to think I just need a complete change. Somewhere hot, preferably, where I don't have to think about spreadsheets. Oh? You’re actually considering leaving? What are you thinking of doing? Have you been looking at anything? Nothing concrete yet. Just…dreaming. Maybe a little cottage by the sea somewhere? Or finally doing that Italian course I always talked about. Actually, that reminds me, we need to start thinking about summer holidays. Have you got anything planned? Perhaps we could all go somewhere. That sounds amazing! I hadn’t really thought about it yet. I was thinking maybe just a week in Cornwall with a couple of friends, a little recharge before September hits. But going away with everyone would be lovely. Though, with the christening coming up... Oh, yes! Little Leo's christening. How are preparations going? Has Sarah sorted out a venue? She's been a bit quiet lately. She's stressed, bless her. She found this beautiful little church in Tamworth, but getting a date that works for everyone is proving tricky.

…and honestly, the Year 10s are just…a handful this year. It's not even the disruptive behaviour, though there's plenty of that, it’s the sheer  lack  of engagement. I feel like I’m talking to a wall sometimes. They just want to be on their phones. Oh, darling, tell me about it. It’s the same at the primary school. Though with mine, it’s all about Roblox and Minecraft. They can tell you the entire back story of every character, but ask them to spell ‘because’ and… blank stares. I’m starting to think education is a losing battle. It feels like that sometimes, doesn't it? I mean, I  love  teaching languages – getting them excited about different cultures, opening their minds – but it's hard when they're just not willing to meet you halfway. Did you ever think, back when we were training, it would be like this? Absolutely not! We were all so idealistic. Remember all the talk about 'learning through play' and 'student-centred approaches'? It's all well and good in theory, but when you have thirty kids who haven’t had a decent night’s sleep and are fuelled by sugar… it goes out the window. How’s Alfie doing with his French? Is he still determined to be a Parisian baker? He is! Honestly, he’s got a real aptitude for it. He’s already picking up phrases and correcting my pronunciation, the little cheek! It's quite sweet. He's been watching French cooking shows, everything. It’s the only thing that motivates him to do his homework. Though, he did ask me if croissants were a healthy breakfast... apparently, he read something about saturated fat. Oh, children! They’re so wonderfully logical, but utterly oblivious. Speaking of oblivious, Rupert is convinced he’s going to be a professional footballer. He spends hours in the garden practicing penalties. Honestly, the noise! It’s driving Brenda round the bend. Brenda still going strong with the gardening, then? Last time I saw her she was trying to grow orchids in a greenhouse attached to the shed. Oh, she's obsessed. It’s become her whole life since she retired. She's even started selling cuttings at the local farmers market. A little business venture of hers! Gets her out of the house, at least. She’s always complaining that Rupert doesn’t visit enough.

Honestly, this charoset is banging. Proper banging. Your nan really knew what she was doing, didn't she, Liv? It's way better than anything I’ve had before, even at Rabbi Klein’s Seder last year. Too much apple, not enough walnut in his, if you ask me. Oh, stop it, Leo, you're making me blush! It  is  Nan’s recipe, passed down, you know? She used to make a massive batch, enough to feed the whole of Golders Green. And really, it’s all about the balance, isn’t it? Apple for the mortar, walnuts for… well, I forget the mortar explanation, truthfully. Just tastes good, yeah? The mortar represents the hard labour the Israelites endured in Egypt, darling. A very important symbol. Though I agree, Liv’s nan always had the perfect consistency. Not too wet, not too dry. Like a good editor, you need just the right touch. It  is  good. Reminds me of something my Gran used to make, though hers definitely didn’t have dates in it. More of a… fruitcake consistency, really. Not quite the same vibe. So, anyone got plans for after Passover? I was thinking of finally heading to Italy. Been meaning to for ages. Italy? Ooh, nice one, Tom! Florence? Rome? Venice getting a bit… much, innit? Full of tourists. I’m trying to convince a mate to finally come to Paris with me. He keeps going on about the football, but I'm like, ‘Mate, there's more to life than Arsenal!’ Paris is lovely! Though I spent most of my time scouting out bakeries last time. Found this tiny place in Montmartre, unbelievable croissants. Seriously, I think I gained a stone just eating pastries. You and your pastries, Liv. It’s a vocation. Speaking of vocations, Leo, how’s the postgraduate work treating you? Still deciphering the mysteries of… what is it again? Fluid dynamics? It's alright. It's a slog, right? Endless equations. Had a lecture on Bernoulli’s principle today. My brain nearly exploded. Honestly, sometimes I think I should've just followed my mum and become a solicitor. Way less maths. Though, probably more stress. Honestly, it's a toss-up. Tell me about it. Engineering isn't exactly relaxing. I've been dealing with stress tests on some new bridge designs. Trying to make sure they can withstand everything from gale-force winds to… well, a rogue Ortolan flying into it, apparently.

…and honestly, the ending of  The Diplomat  just felt  rushed . Like they’d realised they hadn’t left enough breadcrumbs and just crammed everything into the last episode. What did you two think?      Oh, I agree, completely! I was yelling at the telly, honestly. All that build-up with the bombing, and then it just… fizzled? It needed another series, at least, to properly explore all that. Though, to be fair, I’m saying that about most things these days. Everything’s a mini-series now, isn't it? No patience for a slow burn anymore.      I actually quite liked the unpredictability of it all. I mean, I  was  expecting a different outcome, but it wasn't terrible. Though, I do find myself increasingly distracted when watching things. I keep reaching for my Kindle!      That’s exactly it, isn’t it? The pull of a good book. I’ve just started a new Kate Atkinson,  Transcription . It's got that same sort of layered mystery she does so well. So far, it’s brilliant. Though, I confess, I did download a sample onto my Kindle first. Just to see if I liked her style.      Oh, I love Kate Atkinson! But I still prefer the feel of a proper book. The smell, the turning of the pages… it’s just… comforting. I tried eBooks for a while, a few years ago, when my eyesight started playing up, but I really missed it. It felt like I wasn't  reading ; I was just consuming text.      I can see that. I do like the convenience of eBooks, especially when travelling. Less to carry. But I agree, nothing beats a physical book. I’m currently reading a biography of Ada Lovelace. Fascinating woman. Got it second hand, it's beautiful old hardback.      Ada Lovelace! Brilliant choice. I remember reading about her in university. A real visionary. It’s funny, isn't it, how history often overlooks the contributions of women? Speaking of history… how are your Mum and Dad getting on with their move? Last I heard, it was all a bit chaotic.      Chaotic is an understatement. Dad keeps “finding” things he absolutely  must  keep, things I’m fairly sure he hasn’t used since the 1970s. Mum’s trying to be practical, but it's hard when he's digging up memories with every dusty box. She’s been quite stressed.      Oh dear. Moving is awful.

Right then, operation ‘Get Connected in Finland’ is a go. Honestly, getting these shipped over was a palaver. Nearly ended up with them stuck in some DHL depot in Dusseldorf. You and your logistical nightmares, Dad. I swear you could make ordering a pizza an international incident. Are they the… the sparkly purple ones I picked out online? Sparkly purple. The youth of today, eh? Very… striking. Yes, they are indeed. Though honestly, they all look the same to me once you’ve squinted at the tiny instructions for half an hour. I swear the font size is designed for ants. Don’t start! You’ll need my assistance then, obviously. You know I’m the tech wizard of the family. Remember when you thought Bluetooth was a dental condition? A perfectly reasonable assumption! It  sounds  like a dental condition. Anyway, point is, I need a hand. I’m thinking of switching completely away from Nokia finally. It’s been a good innings, mind you. Loyal as a labrador, that Nokia 3310 was. Could’ve used it as a weapon if needed. A weapon? Dad! But honestly, it's time. They’ve been… well, relics for years. This is a massive step for you. What finally pushed you over the edge? Honestly? The mapping. We were trying to navigate that little village near Kesälahti yesterday, and the Nokia just… gave up. Kept insisting we were in a field of sheep. And you know how much I dislike sheep. This new one has got all sorts of fancy GPS. Apparently. That’s what the young man in the shop said anyway. Flashed a lot of jargon about ‘satellites’ and ‘triangulation’. Okay, mapping is a very good reason. Especially when you try to drive through a farmer’s field. Right. Let’s get these going. Do you want me to set yours up completely, or just walk you through it? I can transfer all your contacts, photos… Transfer the photos? Oh, crikey. There's a lot of photos of… well, everything. Mostly gardens and buildings. And the cat, obviously. A  lot  of photos of Winston. Don’t judge. No judgement! Winston is adorable. Okay, so full setup then. Have you got your SIM card? The one we got at the airport? It's… Here we are. It’s like finding a needle in a haystack sometimes. Everything's miniaturised these days. Back in my day, phones were the size of bricks!

Right, so a Red Panda is basically a tiny bear-raccoon… thing? They’re brilliant, aren’t they? Like, seriously adorable. They are lovely. Though, a bit… impractical as pets, wouldn't you say, Leo? Imagine trying to house-train  that . Mum! I wasn’t suggesting we  get  one! Just… appreciating. Though, imagine a Red Panda in the garden. It would be amazing. Better than Mr. Fluffernutter, honestly. Roo-roo! Malamooche! Good boy! That’s right, Finn. Malamooche is a very good boy. He’s protecting us from the imaginary tigers, isn’t he? Leo, be careful with Finn, he thinks Malamooche is real competition for your affections. I know, I know. He's got good taste, though. Malamooches are proper fluffy. Better than any cat, even. Speaking of animals… what do you reckon Amelia would think of a Red Panda drawing for her birthday? That's a lovely idea, actually. She adores animals. Though, she’s also rather fond of your cat, isn’t she? Remember when she spent a whole afternoon trying to build a fort  with  Winston? Nearly gave me a heart attack thinking he’d get stuck. Winston loves attention. He'd probably  let  her build a fort around him, the fluffy opportunist. Anyway, back to Amelia’s party... are we still going with the bowling? Yes, bowling is confirmed. I booked the lane for Saturday afternoon. We should probably start thinking about getting a cake. Chocolate, definitely. She mentioned something about wanting a chocolate cake with raspberries. Raspberry and chocolate… sounds good. Can  I  help decorate it? Maybe with little bowling pins? We’ll see. Last time you “helped” decorate a cake, it looked like a small explosion had happened in the kitchen. No offence. Hey! I was experimenting with edible glitter! It was advanced baking. Panda! Red! Yes, Finn, a red panda! Isn’t it pretty? Now, Leo, while I finish this laundry, could you perhaps brainstorm some party games? Something that isn't just screaming and running around? Hmm… we could do a ‘pin the tail on the bowling pin’ thing. Or maybe a scavenger hunt? I found this cool website with printable clues. It's all about hidden treasure, proper swashbuckling stuff. A scavenger hunt sounds good. As long as it’s contained to the garden. I don't want to spend the whole afternoon looking for clues under the sofa. Oh, and we need to think about the holidays.

…and honestly, Gran, you wouldn't  believe  how many fairy lights Dad put up this year. It looks like Blackpool Illuminations in our front garden. He’s gone proper mental, he has. Oh, your father. Always a bit… enthusiastic, wasn’t he? Though I do miss those displays. It’s not the same without him fussing over everything. Makes it feel a bit… quieter. Yeah, it’s a bit different without your Dad being the Christmas light architect. Though, to be fair, the sheer  amount  he used to use was a fire hazard, innit? Fire hazard is putting it mildly, lad. I swear he was trying to signal the passing aircraft. Still, a good show. Reminds me of Christmases down in Bognor. Used to have a proper community spirit, we did. Everyone decorating, carol singers… you don’t see much of that anymore. It's not like that up north, not really. More…low key. We’d have a big family do, but it’s more about the food and telly than the decorations, I think. Mum makes the best roast potatoes, though. They’re legendary. Roast potatoes are good, yeah. But my Lola – that’s my grandma – her  lechon … now  that’s  Christmas dinner. Crispy pork, slow-roasted for hours. It's a Filipino thing. Loads of family, massive portions, everyone talking at once. It’s chaos, but it’s brilliant. Oh, that sounds lovely! We always had a traditional Christmas dinner, of course. Turkey, stuffing, sprout – though I always secretly hated sprouts. Your grandfather insisted on them, though. Said it wasn’t Christmas without them. He was a very stubborn man, your grandfather. Stubborn? Now  there’s  an understatement. He once spent three days arguing with a postman about the correct way to deliver a parcel. Three days! That sounds  exactly  like my grandad. He once got into a full-blown debate with a shop assistant about the price of a bag of barley. Said it was daylight robbery. They’re all the same, these old fellas, eh? Always have an opinion, and they're always right, according to them. It’s interesting, though, isn’t it? How different things are even  within  Britain. You’ve got your northern Christmases, your southern ones, then you throw in traditions from the Philippines… it’s a right melting pot. It is, isn’t it? And it’s good, I think. Keeps things interesting.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of audio I’m getting through this week is ridiculous. It’s all these university lectures – apparently, everyone decided to record everything at once. It's fascinating stuff, actually, mostly history, but my ears are  aching . How was your day, darling? Anything exciting happen in the world of administration? Exciting is… a strong word. It was mostly spreadsheets and trying to convince Brenda that yes, we  do  need to update the filing system. She’s been using the same one since the nineteen nineties. Honestly, you’d think she’d be resistant to progress, but it’s more like she’s actively hostile to it. Brenda sounds delightful. Still stuck in her ways, I presume? She hasn’t changed a bit since we all worked together at the council, has she? Not a jot. A force of nature, is Brenda. A slightly terrifying, paper-based force of nature. Anyway, enough about work. This lasagne smells divine, actually. Did you make it with that smoked mozzarella you found? I did! It makes all the difference, doesn’t it? A little bit of smokiness lifts the whole thing. I was thinking, after this, we could finally start that new detective series everyone’s talking about?  Happy Valley ? I've heard such good things. Oh,  Happy Valley  is brilliant! Sarah, you're in for a treat. It’s beautifully grim, and the lead actress… phenomenal. Really gets under your skin. Though, be warned, it’s not exactly light viewing. Grim is good, sometimes. After a day dealing with Brenda, I appreciate a bit of darkness. Is it one of those where you spend the whole time trying to guess who the culprit is? I'm terrible at those. Always wrong. It's more about the characters, I think. The police work is solid, but it’s the internal stuff, the personal lives, that really grabs you. It’s not just ‘whodunnit’, it’s ‘why did they do it, and what’s it costing them?’ Exactly. And the Yorkshire landscape is just…stunning. It’s almost a character in itself. It adds to the bleakness, you know? Speaking of bleakness, I’ve been trying to finish that biography of Edgar Allan Poe. It’s fascinating but seriously depressing. The man was a mess. Oh, Poe. A classic. I remember reading ‘The Raven’ at school and being utterly captivated. Though, I confess, I haven't ventured beyond that.

Honestly, Doreen, this council. They’re at it again. Another planning application for building on that green space down by the river. Can you believe it? Mmm. Heard something about that on the radio, Arthur. Not surprised, though, is it? They’ve got their eye on every bit of undeveloped land round here. Think of the money they’d make. Money, that’s all they think about. That field’s been there forever. Old Man Hemmings used to keep sheep there, remember? Lovely sight that was, in the summer. Now they want to put up…what was it? Another estate of those pokey little houses. Good morning, you two. Arthur, still battling the council, I see? And Doreen, a new project on the needles? Morning, David. Just keeping my hands busy. And yes, Arthur's in a right state about the field. Honestly, it's the only bit of countryside left that's not overrun with concrete. It’s not just  a  field, David! It’s…it’s part of the character of the place. They’ll ruin it, I tell you, ruin it. They said something about “affordable housing”. Affordable for who, I ask you? Not for folks like us, that's for certain. Look, I understand your concerns, Arthur. Trust me, I do. But getting worked up about it won’t change anything. These things are generally a done deal before they even announce them. But we have to  try ! We can write letters, go to the meetings… We've done that before, dear. Remember the library? They went ahead and closed it anyway. We signed petitions, we wrote to the MP… didn't make a jot of difference. That was different. That was… that was just cost-cutting. This is about greed! It's often both, Arthur. Look, I actually spoke to Councillor Bailey yesterday. Casual conversation, really. He mentioned the development. He says there's a real pressure from central government to meet housing targets. It's not as simple as just a local council being greedy. Pressure?! What about the pressure on us to have a bit of green to look at? To have somewhere nice to walk? I can’t walk far these days, you know. My knees… Now, Arthur, don't start on your knees. You know they flare up when you get agitated. Have some more tea. Agitated? I  should  be agitated! It’s a disgrace, that's what it is.

Right, so, the pub’s booked for Friday. The Eagle, 7:30? I managed to get the little room at the back, should be… less chaotic. Anyone got strong objections? The Eagle’s good. Easy enough for everyone to get to. Sounds perfect, Claire. Though, if we’re aiming for ‘less chaotic’, maybe we should send out a strongly worded email about leaving Horace alone this time? Oh god, yes. Last time was… a near disaster. Poor Horace. You're talking about the potted plant, right? I only just joined the team a couple of months ago, and the Horace stories are  legendary . Apparently, someone tried to give him a little hat? A  tiny  cowboy hat. It was Amy from marketing. She thought it would be ‘cute’. Horace did not appreciate it. He nearly toppled over. We spent ten minutes rescuing him. Sorry I’m late, the printers were being…difficult. What’s all this about Horace needing rescuing? Is he staging a rebellion against office décor again? Something like that, Sarah. Amy tried to accessorise him. Oh, Amy. She’s…enthusiastic. Right, so, Eagle Pub, Friday? Good. I’ve been meaning to properly celebrate finishing that phonological analysis report. It nearly killed me. It did look brutal, honestly. Speaking of near-death experiences, did anyone see that poor wasp struggling in the car park this morning? It was flipped on its back. Oh, I did! I tried to help it, but it just buzzed at me aggressively. I think it was a lost cause. I always feel terrible for those. I watched one the other day trying to build a nest  inside  a vending machine. Just relentless. Nature, eh? I'm a bit of a soft touch, I admit. I used to rescue earwigs from the bath when I was little. My mum used to go mad. That’s sweet, Lucy. Though earwigs are…a different story. Honestly, Sarah, have you seen the state of the floral arrangements outside the main entrance recently? They're lovely but there are  so  many bees getting trapped. Good point. I'll flag it with facilities. They’re usually pretty good about that sort of thing. They had to rescue a bird that got stuck in the air vents last year. It involved a complicated system of mirrors and a very patient security guard. Seriously? That sounds…intense. Cambridge is wild, innit? Right, back to Friday...

Ugh. Honestly, history is  killing  me this week. Mrs. Davies is obsessed with the Tudors. Like, we’ve done three lessons on Henry VIII’s wives already. Three! Tell me about it! I’m drowning in Geography. Mr. Harrison’s decided we need to know the population density of every village in the Amazon rainforest.  Every  village. It’s ridiculous. I’m pretty sure knowing that won't help me pass my GCSEs. Seriously! It’s all just…memorising. I mean, I get the importance of history, but does anyone  actually  remember all those dates and names? I just end up picturing Anne Boleyn getting her head chopped off on repeat. It's grim. Oh, that's awful. I keep zoning out in Geography. I just start thinking about what I'm having for dinner, you know? My mum’s making roast chicken tonight, which is a major win. Ooh, lucky! Mum’s attempting some sort of Moroccan tagine. It usually tastes a bit…suspect. Last time she made it, it tasted vaguely of cinnamon and sadness. Cinnamon and sadness! That's brilliant! Mine tried to make paella last month, and it was basically just yellow rice. She’s a good cook generally but exotic cuisine isn’t really her forte. Anyway, back to torture… Have you started the English essay yet? The one on  Romeo and Juliet ? Don't even  mention  Shakespeare! I’ve got the intro written, but I’m completely stuck on the actual argument. Like, what’s the point of all that teen angst? Everyone just needs to communicate better! I actually don't mind  Romeo and Juliet . It's just…long. And all the ‘thee’s and ‘thou’s - it's exhausting. I’m trying to argue that the feud between the families is more to blame than fate. What about you? I was thinking of doing something about how Juliet's completely stifled by her parents, but I feel like everyone does that one. It's so predictable. Mrs. Peterson would probably roll her eyes so hard they’d fall out. True. You need something a bit more…original. Have you thought about Friar Laurence? He’s a bit of a disaster, isn’t he? Constantly coming up with terrible plans. Ooh, that  is  good! Like, he's supposed to be the voice of reason but he accidentally causes everyone to die! Classic. I could totally work with that.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails about the new data protection policy is just… relentless. It's the same information, reworded five different times, sent to everyone. I swear, I spend half my day archiving 'important updates' that are anything  but  important. Sounds brutal, El. Same here, though thankfully not policy related. It’s just… endless meetings about meetings. We're supposed to be streamlining the logistics for the Henderson project, but we’re spending all our time  talking  about streamlining. It’s a bit circular, isn't it? Oh, you two. Work, work, work. You’d think you lived to breathe spreadsheets. Back in my day, we just…  did  things. Less fuss. Though, admittedly, a lot more shouting. Mum! Don't tell me about the shouting again. I still have nightmares about Mr. Henderson from your stories. No relation to  my  Henderson project, I assume? Heavens, no! Mine was a Henderson who ran the biscuit factory. A right tyrant, that man. Couldn’t tell a digestive from a custard cream if his life depended on it. But hey, it paid the bills. Speaking of bills...how’s your flat going, El? Still no leaks after that storm last week? Thankfully not! Bit of damp on one wall, but nothing a dehumidifier can’t handle. It's just...finding the time to actually  decorate  it. I keep promising myself a weekend, but then work throws something else at me. I was thinking of maybe getting that seagrass rug you have, Mum. It looks so cosy. That rug  is  nice. Comfy underfoot. Although, maybe not the best choice if you've got a cat… Jasper would have it shredded in five minutes. You’re right. Jasper is a tiny, fluffy agent of chaos. Maybe a slightly more practical option. What about your mum, Mark? Have you managed to get her settled into the new assisted living place? It's… it’s going. She has her good days and her bad days. She misses the garden terribly, even though she barely used it. Says she can't smell the roses anymore. It's heartbreaking, honestly. She keeps asking when Dad’s coming to take her home. Oh, love. It’s awful, isn’t it? It doesn't get any easier. But she's lucky to have you thinking of her, making sure she's comfortable. Remember when your grandfather was like that?

Honestly, this is just… relentless. It's like as soon as one thing's sorted, three more pop up. Specifically, this operation. The hospital keeps sending me different forms for the payment plan. It’s infuriating. Oh, love, that sounds awful. Hospitals are the  worst  for paperwork. Is it the same with everything, or just the operation costs? Are they being difficult about direct debit? It’s everything! The initial consultation, the scans, the actual operation... each one feels like a separate battle with bureaucracy. And yes, they’re being incredibly slow to set up a direct debit. They want a deposit upfront, which is fine, I paid that. But then they want quarterly payments, and the forms keep changing! It's all a bit…stressful, when I’m already worrying about recovery. Well, you know, don't be afraid to just ring them up and  demand  to speak to someone who knows what’s going on. Sometimes a bit of firmness is all it takes. I had trouble with the building society last year, thought they'd overcharged me. Went right up the chain, and suddenly everything was sorted. You’re probably right. I’m just…exhausted, I think. And then there’s Leo. He got detention  again  yesterday. Oh, Leo. What was it this time? Still messing about in science? Worse, actually. Apparently, he and Jamie were caught…well, it was a prank, but a bad one. They swapped all the labels around in the art room. Paint with the glitter, clay with the watercolours…Mrs. Davies was not amused, apparently. Oh, bless. Boys will be boys, eh? Though, swapping labels  is  a bit mischievous. Is he remorseful at least? He says he is, but honestly, I think he just hates being stuck in after school. Detention doesn’t seem to be doing any good. I’m starting to wonder if I should just let him face the consequences and… not intervene as much. It’s a tricky one. You don’t want him thinking he can get away with anything, but constant battles aren’t good either. Have you spoken to his dad about it? Briefly. He thinks I'm too soft on him. He remembers his own school days being far stricter. Honestly, sometimes I think we’re raising two different children. Men! They always think a firm hand is the answer. You’ve got to remember he’s a teenager, hormones are raging.

Right, I’m officially brain-fried. History of Art is trying to actively  kill  my brain cells, I swear. How’s the revision going for you, Liv? Still buried in organic chemistry? Don't even. It's…a process. Honestly, I think I understand less  now  than I did before I started revising. It’s just layers of confusion building on top of more confusion. At least your subject matter is pretty. All I see are swirling molecules and reactions that defy logic. How was work last night? Busy as usual, I imagine? You have  no  idea. It was chucking it down, proper biblical rain, and everyone decided the best place to be was huddled in the pub. Old Man Hemmings was in, telling the same story about catching a five-pounder down at the docks in ‘67, and Brenda nearly started a fight with a hen party. Standard Friday, really. Sounds…charming. Still, beats staring at benzene rings. God, I wish I could just…not have to worry about money for a bit. Uni's expensive, even with the loan. Tell me about it. I’m working every weekend  and  most weeknights practically just to keep afloat. Postgrad is a beautiful thing, academically, but financially? It's a right mess. I'm thinking of picking up another shift, maybe Tuesday night. It's grim, though. Another shift? You barely sleep as it is! You'll burn out, Jess. And you need to actually  have  time to, you know,  study  for your Masters. What is it again, Medieval Literature? Aye, Medieval Lit. Focusing on Chaucer, mostly. It’s fascinating, proper absorbing when I get the chance to delve into it, but trying to translate Middle English after a ten-hour shift serving pints and listening to people complain about the football… it’s a different kind of challenge, let me tell ya. I can imagine. It's just… frustrating, isn't it? Like, I'm working my butt off trying to get qualifications that are supposed to lead to something better, but in the meantime, everyone's already  doing  something. Like your job - you're earning, you're gaining experience, you’re…well, you’re socialising, even if it’s with Old Man Hemmings. I'm just…floating in a sea of textbooks. Don't be daft, Liv. You're doing amazing. And honestly, bartending isn’t all it’s cracked up to be.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of these things is a miracle anyone ever finds what they need. Right, anyone actually  booked  anything exciting for their holidays yet? I'm staring at Ryanair and feeling distinctly uninspired. Exciting? Ha! Exciting costs money, lad. I’ve got a week in Blackpool booked. It’s…traditional. And the grandkids love it. Plus, you can’t beat a good stick of rock. Blackpool, is it? That's grand. I haven’t been to Blackpool in donkey's years. I’m going home to County Clare, thank goodness. Me mother’s not getting any younger, and I need to spend a bit of time with her. Fresh air, a bit of craic… much better for the soul than arcades, I reckon. Blackpool is… an experience. I admire your dedication, Margaret. I'm escaping the city completely. We've rented a cottage in the Cotswolds. Trying for ‘quaint’ and ‘peaceful’. Fingers crossed it doesn’t rain for the entire fortnight. It’s always a gamble, isn’t it? Cotswolds sounds lovely, David. A bit… pastoral for me, perhaps. I need a bit of sun. Though, ‘sun’ and ‘Ryanair’ rarely appear in the same sentence, do they? I was looking at somewhere in Spain, maybe, but the thought of all the lads on stag dos… Oh, you’ll get that anywhere nowadays, even Blackpool! Last year there was a hen do dressed as Teletubbies.  Teletubbies , I tell you. It was something else. Oh, that  is  a sight! Reminds me of a wedding I went to back home… the groom’s best man decided to give a speech entirely in Klingon. No one had a clue what he was saying. It went on for a good five minutes! Klingon? Good grief. That’s…dedicated. Or possibly just fuelled by too much whiskey. That's brilliant! See, this is why I need to go away, to avoid hearing stories like that at work. It messes with my sense of reality. I'm thinking maybe Majorca. Relatively calm, decent beaches… Majorca is alright. Gets a bit crowded though, doesn't it? Heard the sangria's a bit watered down these days too. You're better off making your own. My auntie Vera has a recipe... it's a secret, of course. She guards it with her life. Says it's the only thing that gets her through winter. Speaking of secrets, there’s a little pub near my mother’s cottage… they make a Guinness that could raise the dead.

Honestly, I still can't believe how dodgy that call was. Absolutely scandalous! The ref’s lost the plot, hasn’t he? Which call? Oh, the penalty? Yeah, a bit soft, I reckon. But honestly, both sides are playing pretty rough. It’s a derby, what do you expect? They’re all at it. Soft?! Soft?! It was a blatant dive, Mark! He tripped over his own feet and expected a free kick! My grandad would be turning in his grave. He’d be saying “Look at that, lass, a disgrace!”. He was a Mackem through and through, you know. Wouldn't stand for this. Right, grandad’s ghost weighing in on the football. Fair enough. Still, Newcastle  are  playing well. Gotta admit that. They’ve got a bit of fire about them today. Fire? They're relying on dodgy decisions and hoping for the best! Honestly, this is why I get stressed watching football. It’s not about skill anymore, it’s about who can con the referee the best. You always get stressed. Remember that Champions League final a few years ago? You were practically vibrating. I thought the sofa was going to suffer structural damage. That was different! That was Liverpool! And it  was  a travesty what happened. This is just… frustrating. Speaking of needing something strong, are we ordering anything? I could murder a takeaway. I skipped lunch prepping for that presentation tomorrow. Takeaway? Good shout. What are you fancying? Chinese? Indian? The usual Friday night ritual? Ooh, Indian sounds good. But… you know what I've been craving? A proper, greasy, gut-busting burger. Like, a really American one. None of this gourmet burger nonsense. I want a triple cheeseburger with bacon, proper chips, and a milkshake. The kind that sticks to your ribs. Woah there! That's a step up from your usual healthy quinoa and avocado. You alright? That sounds… intense. I  am  alright! Just having a moment of weakness. Uni life and salad leaves have clearly repressed my true, Northern self. Remember when we went to that diner in Sunderland? That was heaven. Massive portions, endless coffee… Vaguely. I remember being impressed by the sheer volume of food. And possibly slightly intimidated. Birmingham portions are a little more… restrained. Restrained?! You call those little chips  chips ? They’re potato sticks! They don't even hold enough sauce! Honestly, it’s a crime against carbohydrates.
