It feels a bit colonial to push for ‘correct’ pronunciations when the whole point of language is that it  changes  and varies. That's a really important point, actually. One of the things I'm working on now is looking at how non-native speakers perceive different accents. There's a lot of preconceived notions about what sounds ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ that are tied to social class and prestige. Oh, totally! I was working with an author from Bradford last month and her accent was  fierce . Proper strong Yorkshire. And some of the editors were… hesitant. Said it might be ‘difficult for some readers to understand.’ Honestly! It’s beautiful! It's  real ! Aye, I get that. It’s the same back home in Sunderland.

…and honestly, the BBC drama last night? Utter tosh. All style, no substance. Beautifully filmed, mind you, the cinematography was  lovely , but the plot…paper thin. You know I'm a sucker for a good historical drama, but that just felt… manufactured. Oh, you and your historical dramas, Alistair. You’re such a snob! I quite enjoyed it. It was a good bit of escapism, wasn’t it? Something to switch the brain off with after a long day wrestling with data. Besides, my mum  loved  it, and you know trying to disagree with her on telly is a path to certain doom. Touché. Mothers are always right. Though I maintain a solid grounding in historical accuracy is  not  too much to ask. It's the lazy writing that gets to me. They just assume people won’t notice the anachronisms. It’s insulting, really. Speaking of insulting, have you seen what they’re charging for streaming services now? It’s highway robbery! Tell me about it. I’m perpetually cycling through subscriptions just to catch the things I want to watch. And then inevitably forgetting to cancel and getting charged for another month of something I haven’t touched. The internet’s brilliant, don't get me wrong, for research and everything… but it's become a bit of a chaotic mess, hasn’t it? A complete and utter mess. It’s like the Wild West, isn't it? Everything's algorithm-driven, curated to keep you scrolling, rather than actually providing anything of value. Remember when you used to just  discover  things? Find a band, or a book, or a film completely by chance? Vaguely. It feels like a lifetime ago. Though, I did stumble across this fascinating documentary series online about the Sami people in northern Scandinavia. Absolutely brilliant. Completely changed my perspective on… well, pretty much everything. Oh, really? The Sami? I’ve read a bit about their culture, but nothing in depth. It’s incredible how many different cultures exist, isn’t it? And how little most people know about them. I always feel a bit of a fraud when I try to talk about cultural understanding. My experiences are so…limited, really. Predominantly European, upper-middle class. That’s fair enough. Nobody expects you to be an expert on everything. But it’s good you’re thinking about it. It makes a difference. It’s funny, isn't it?

Right, that’s a proper brew. Thanks, love. Though I still say your nan makes it better, doesn't she, Arthur? She puts a pinch of bicarbonate of soda in, you know. Makes all the difference. Aye, she does, Margaret. A pinch of magic, that woman. Always has. Though I reckon half the ‘magic’ is she pretends it’s a secret and makes a fuss about it. Oh, don't be daft, Arthur. It  is  a secret! And it makes the water softer, you see. All the Hull water's a bit harsh, even now. Harsh water? Sounds rubbish. Is that why everyone in Hull has hard skin? Now, don’t go being cheeky, lad. It just means it’s got more minerals in it, that's all. Though, your nan has a point. It's not the same as back home. So, how was school today, Ethan? Anything exciting happen? Nah, same old. Mr. Henderson droned on about the French Revolution. Honestly, it's just heads getting chopped off for, like, ever. Why do we  need  to know this? Oh, it's important to know about history, Ethan! Helps you understand why things are the way they are now. Though, I never paid much attention in history myself, to be honest. More interested in dodging my mum's chores. You always were a little scamp, Doris! Remember that time you painted the cat blue? Oh, don't bring that up! It was a perfectly good shade of blue, and Marmalade didn't seem to mind at first. It was Mum who minded. She nearly had a fit! Goodness me. That  was  a story. Right, back to more mundane matters. I was thinking about getting the gutters cleaned next week. Arthur, you've been saying yours need doing for ages. Aye, I have. Keeps putting it off though. My balance isn't what it was, y’know. Don’t fancy climbing up a ladder these days. I could probably do it. I'm quite good at climbing. Mrs. Peterson next door keeps complaining about leaves in hers too, so I could do both. Get a bit of pocket money. You? Climbing a ladder? Ethan, you barely reach the top shelf in the kitchen! I’ve grown since then! And I could get a longer ladder. Proper sturdy one. Oh, I don't know about that, dear. Ladders are dangerous things. Best to leave it to a professional.

Honestly, this air is… different. Even to yesterday. It feels cleaner after that little rain shower. Did you manage to get all your marking done this afternoon, then? Mostly. I finished the essays for the second years, thankfully. Just the dissertations looming now. The sheer  volume  of them is terrifying. I swear, every year they get longer. You had a good session with your students? It was alright. Bit of a slow one, to be honest. Had to spend ages explaining the nuances of post-structuralism to a student who seemed convinced Derrida was a brand of coffee. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if I’m getting through. Oh, bless him. You’re a saint. At least it gives you a story for dinner. Look, let me show you something. Remember old Ben from university? Ben…tall, always wore that ridiculous striped scarf? Vaguely. What about him? He sent me these photos. He finally made it to Patagonia! We always said he’d go one day, completely disappeared off-grid for a bit, and now look at him – mountaineering. The photos are incredible. Oh my goodness, that’s breathtaking. Look at those glaciers! He always was a bit of an adventurer, wasn't he? I remember him trying to build a raft to float down the River Cam. And nearly getting arrested! He’s posting daily updates. Says he’s completely disconnected from everything, no signal, no Wi-Fi, just…mountains and fresh air. Seems incredibly peaceful. Makes you think, doesn’t it? It does. Makes me think about how glued we are to these things. . Although, honestly, being able to video call Mum every week is worth it. I’d have missed her 60th terribly if we weren’t here. Absolutely. And the students need us to be accessible. It's just... a balance, I suppose. Speaking of travel, are you still thinking about going to Japan next summer? We talked about it ages ago. I am! I’ve been doing a bit of research. Kyoto looks amazing. I’d love to see the temples and gardens. The culture just fascinates me. It would be a nice change from… well, from everything here, as lovely as it is. It would be. It's such a different world. We could do a proper deep dive into the food scene too. Remember how much we enjoyed that ramen place in London? Oh, don’t even  start .

Honestly, my head is  still  pounding. Like, properly pounding. Did you see Chloe trying to do that… that TikTok dance on the table? Embarrassing doesn't even cover it. Oh my god, yeah! I thought the table was gonna collapse. She nearly took Liam with her. He looked genuinely terrified. Though, to be fair, Liam looks terrified most of the time. True, true. He's a sweet boy, but definitely not built for chaos. Speaking of chaos… I think I accidentally told Ben I liked his… haircut.  No way . Ben with the… the sculpted side bits? You didn’t! I did! It just… slipped out. He was talking about his barber and I just blurted it out. Now he keeps looking at me. It's awkward. He even  touched  his hair when he was talking to me after that. Oh, girl. You've opened a can of worms. He’ll think you're angling for something. You know he’s got a thing for girls who like ‘alternative’ styles, right? All the ripped jeans and band t-shirts? Ugh, I know! I usually go for… less sculpted. More messy bun and comfy jumpers. This is  not  me. I think I need a distraction. Did you manage to see Jess last night, even for a bit? Briefly. She was glued to Kai. Honestly, I’m starting to think they’re actually an item. Remember how she said he was ‘just a friend’ last week? She was practically hanging off him. I knew it! I called it! She denies everything, but Kai’s got that puppy-dog look that melts everyone. My Nan always says you can tell a good lad by how he treats his mum, and Kai’s always talking about making his mum tea and doing her shopping. Your Nan's wisdom strikes again! Mine just tells me to marry a doctor. Apparently, financial security is the key to happiness. Although, she did help me sneak biscuits after bedtime when I was little, so she's not  entirely  focused on practicality. Classic Nan logic. Mine's obsessed with my cousin's Labrador, Winston. She keeps saying I need a dog. "It'll get you out, darling! You need fresh air!" Like going to a club isn't fresh air. Different  kind  of fresh air, admittedly. Tell me about it. My mum keeps trying to set me up with her friend's son.

Honestly, this is lovely, love. Peas and chips… haven’t had a proper plate of this in ages. Feels… comforting, doesn’t it? Like being a child again. Though Maureen would have had us eating something far more “sensible.” Sensible being boiled everything until it lost all colour and flavour, I presume? Your mum was a woman of strong opinions on nutrition. Aye, she was. Everything had to  do  something. Strengthen the bones, build the blood… never just  taste  nice. Though, she made a cracking apple crumble, I'll give her that. She did, didn’t she? She’d say crumble was 'fruit encased in fortification'. Now, about your grandmother… have you managed to sort out a lift for her on Friday? She’s been ringing me every hour on the hour asking if you’ve ‘got a plan, darling’. I have, I have. Kev’s offered to pick her up from the station. He said he doesn't mind, and it saves you a trek all the way to Penrith. He’s even promised to help her with her bags. Though knowing Kev, he’ll probably try to talk her ear off about FIFA. Oh, that man and his football. Honestly, he thinks he's the next Messi. Last time he was over, he spent the entire evening trying to convince me that offside is actually a very complex rule. Very complex for  him  to consistently get wrong, anyway. He’s a good lad, Kev. Enthusiastic. And truthfully, the offside rule  is  a bit of a nightmare. Even I struggle sometimes, and I’ve got a degree in… well, something completely unrelated, but still. A logical mind! It's less logical and more… a moving target. He was going on about 'tactical fouling' just yesterday. Apparently, it's a crucial element of modern gameplay. I just nod and smile. It’s easier. Easier for you, maybe. It drives me mad. All that shouting at the television. It's no way to behave. Reminds me of your Uncle Patrick when the Republic were playing. He once threw a cup of tea at the telly during the Italia '90 World Cup. No way! Really? Oh, absolutely. Splattered all over the screen. Maureen nearly had a fit. Said it was a waste of a perfectly good cuppa. Patrick always was a bit… dramatic. Still, don’t blame him entirely. Some of those refereeing decisions back then were scandalous.

…and honestly, the way he was fiddling with it, I just  knew  something was going to break. Laptops are not Lego, Dad! Honestly, trying to ‘upgrade’ the RAM with a butter knife… Now, now, don’t exaggerate. It wasn’t a butter knife, it was a flat-head screwdriver. Perfectly serviceable. Just needed a little… persuasion. He was convinced he could fix it himself and save a fortune. It’s the principle of the thing, isn't it? Anything broken equals a DIY challenge. That’s men for ya. My George tries the same with everything. Last week it was the washing machine. Said a bit of WD-40 would sort it. Ended up flooding the kitchen. Exactly! And then  I  have to spend three hours on tech support trying to explain why forcing things isn’t always the answer. Speaking of things not working, has anyone noticed how awful the water tastes lately? Oh, god, don’t get me started. I’ve been buying bottled water. It tastes… metallic. Metallic? It tastes like chlorine to  me . Remember when you could just drink straight from the tap? Proper London water, that was. They say it's all the run-off from the farms. And with these bin strikes, everything’s just getting… worse. Honestly, the smell on the street is dreadful. It's a disgrace, isn't it? I saw a rat the other day, bigger than my cat! It’s lucky we’re up here, second floor. Speaking of lucky, are you still trying to get your mum’s old Blackberry working, Sam? You were wrestling with it earlier. It’s… a challenge. Getting the contacts transferred is a nightmare. It's like ancient technology. Voice recognition doesn’t even  recognise  my voice. It thinks I’m speaking Swahili. Blackberry? Good grief. I’m still trying to understand this Sat Nav my granddaughter bought me. I ended up in Worthing instead of Worthing  town centre  last week! Oh, bless you. Sat Navs are the devil's work. Always taking you the scenic route. Honestly, I prefer a good map. You're brave, Carol. I get lost walking around Brighton without Google Maps. Remember that time we took a ‘shortcut’ through the Lanes and ended up completely turned around? How could I forget? We walked in circles for an hour, convinced we were going the right way. It was raining, of course.

…Honestly, it’s just grey. Perpetually grey. I didn’t realise how much I  needed  a good dose of Vitamin D until I came here, and even then… November in Poland isn't exactly the Riviera, is it? Did you check the football results? Man United were playing, weren’t they? Yeah, I did. While marking essays, naturally. They drew. 1-1 with Bournemouth. Absolutely typical. Honestly, I don't know why I bother. It just winds me up. But hey, at least it’s something to distract from the existential dread of impending exam results. How are you holding up with the SAD, though? You were pretty low last time we spoke. It’s… manageable. The coffee here helps. This Tram place does a surprisingly good latte, don’t you think? Proper foam. It’s just… Cambridge is so  bright . Even when it’s raining, there’s a quality of light. This feels… dull. And the short days! It feels like I’m living in permanent twilight. I got a message from Aunt Carol this morning, asking about the weather. She insists it’s “balmy” in Dorset. Balmy! Aunt Carol always thinks it’s balmy in Dorset. She’s permanently in rose-tinted glasses. Listen, have you been speaking to that student of yours, Marek? The one who was struggling with the past perfect? Oh, Marek. Bless him. Yes, I did a Zoom call with him yesterday. He’s still finding it tricky. It’s not the grammar itself, it's the  concept  of time. He keeps translating it directly from Polish. I feel so responsible for them all doing well in their exams, you know? It’s silly, really, as I’m only doing a few hours a week, but I genuinely worry if they won't understand. I know exactly what you mean. That’s the nightmare of this job. You pour everything into them, and then it all comes down to one test. I've got a girl, Anya, who’s convinced she's going to fail her speaking exam. She’s perfectly fluent, but her confidence is shot. I've been trying to reassure her… It's exhausting, isn't it? Makes me thankful I’m ‘semi-retired’. Though ‘unemployed’ is probably more accurate. Still, at least I don't have the pressure of marking essays and preparing lesson plans. Although… Mum keeps suggesting I volunteer on a farm.

Right, I swear, this gravy is fighting me. It’s either too thick or too thin, there’s no in-between. It's like trying to predict the weather back in Doncaster, honestly. One minute sunshine, the next… torrential downpour of lumpy gravy. Sounds stressful. Gravy  is  important though, innit? Can't have a roast without decent gravy. Mine’s always a bit…beige. Never quite gets the colour right. Beige is…optimistic, Liam. Sometimes yours looks positively grey. Honestly though, Amelia, you’re overthinking the gravy. It'll be fine. You always fuss. It's the Yorkshire in you, I reckon. Everything needs to be  just so . It’s not fussing! It’s…standards! And it  is  the Yorkshire. My nana would have my hide if I served up lukewarm gravy that looks like dishwater. Speaking of standards, I had a nightmare at work today. Oh yeah? What happened? Another bridezilla demanding a swan made of ice for the centrepiece? You told me about that last time. Worse. Mr. Henderson, the CEO of that tech company we're doing the conference for next month? He wants…a ‘rustic-industrial’ theme. Rustic-industrial? What even  is  that? Sounds like a shed. Exactly! It’s a contradiction in terms! He sent me mood boards full of exposed brick, fairy lights strung across metal beams, but then wants it all “high-end and sophisticated.” I spent two hours on a phone call explaining that you can't have tweed bunting AND minimalist chrome sculptures. He just kept saying “Think…Steampunk, but approachable.” Steampunk? Is that all the gears and goggles stuff? That sounds…a bit much for a business conference. A  lot  much. I’m pretty sure he hasn’t actually thought this through. And the worst part? He specifically said “I want something…different. Something the delegates  won't  have seen before.” Like no one’s ever had a conference, ever. Men. Honestly. They have these grand visions, no practical understanding, and expect you to just…magic it into existence. Honestly, it's the same in my job. Trying to get production to understand that 'urgent' doesn't mean 'whenever you get around to it'. Tell me about it. On the building site, you say 'quick' and they take it as a suggestion. I was chatting to Dave the other day – he’s been trying to get a date with Chloe from the bakery.

…and honestly, it's just a bit  odd , isn’t it? How they’ve laid this place out. It’s almost… regimented. All these squares of lawn, lines of trees. Not very natural, is it? Bath parks, they're all a bit more… flowing, you know? Less… precise. Hmm, you’ve got a point. It's a bit brutalist, almost. Though I suppose in the middle of London, you need some order. And look at 'im go! That little chap's determined to catch one of those pigeons. Reckon he stands a chance? Zero. Absolutely zero. They're far too wily. Though it's nice to see a kid actually  doing  something rather than staring at a screen. Speaking of wily, did you hear about Old Man Hemmings getting duped by one of those charity chuggers again? Gave ‘em fifty quid, the poor sod. No way! Again? He needs to learn to just walk on by. They’re persistent little blighters. Changing the subject slightly – do you remember Mrs. Chen and her husband coming to visit last year? She was saying something about parks in China being… different again. Oh, yes! Lovely couple. They were fascinated by the lime trees here, weren’t they? Said they didn’t have anything quite like them back home. She was telling me about the parks in Chengdu, near where her sister lives. Apparently, they're obsessed with pandas. Pandas, aye. It's the national symbol. But they've got more than pandas, haven't they? I was reading an article about wildlife reserves they’ve established, trying to bring back the numbers of… what were they? Asiatic black bears? Apparently, they’d dwindled drastically. That’s right, the moon bears. Awful what’s happened to their habitats. And the landscape itself… she described some utterly stunning places, mountains and stuff. It sounded a world away from Devon, that’s for sure. Beautiful, but… you’d need a proper 4x4 to get around some of those roads, she said. Devon’s bad enough sometimes! Trying to navigate those narrow lanes in a normal car feels like playing Russian roulette with a tractor. Speaking of travelling, you still thinking about getting over to the Isle of Wight for a weekend? Maybe. It's a bit of a faff, getting the ferry and all that. And then driving around – I heard the roads are even narrower than Devon.

Right, this playlist is a disaster. It's all… beige. Seriously, Leo, who puts smooth jazz on a road trip playlist? It’s supposed to be belters, anthems, not something my gran listens to while she's doing crosswords. Hey, don’t disrespect Kenny G. It’s… calming. And you said you wanted something ‘chill’ for the drive. This  is  chill. Chill for a dentist’s waiting room, maybe. We’re going to the Lakes, we need something with a bit of… oomph. Something to sing along to when we’re bombing down those windy roads. Remember that time we tried to do karaoke in Blackpool?  That  needs to be the vibe. Oh god, don’t remind me. Your rendition of Bohemian Rhapsody nearly got us thrown out. And honestly, I think the karaoke machine just gave up on life. Look, I just thought you'd be tired after the early start. I was trying to be considerate. Aw, you  are  a sweetheart, you really are. But considerate doesn’t equal Kenny G. I’ll just… override it. . Found it. “Road Trip Bangers - Do Not Touch!”. See? Carefully curated. Featuring a disproportionate amount of early 2000s pop-punk because it’s scientifically proven to improve mood. Scientifically proven? By whom, exactly? You and a questionable YouTube algorithm? Don’t question the science, Leo. Just… listen. Better, isn’t it? Infinitely less beige, I’ll give you that. Though, prepare for me to judge your musical taste relentlessly. This is… intense. Good. That's the point. So, are we sticking to the plan then? Check-in at the B&B’s at four, hike up Catbells tomorrow, and then… what did you say about that pub in Keswick? The Dog & Gun. Apparently, they do a really good Cumberland sausage pie. And a decent selection of local ales. We could have dinner there on Saturday night. Unless you’d rather try that fancy Thai place you found online? Oh, the Thai place looks amazing, but after a hike, a proper pub grub is calling my name. Cumberland sausage pie it is. You know, I’m already feeling less stressed just being out of the city. Work has been mental. Tell me about it. They’re breathing down my neck about this new bridge design. Apparently, it’s “not innovative enough”. Like, what do they want? A bridge that  flies ? They always want something impossible.

Right, so then Brenda – you remember Brenda from uni, always wore those massive scarves? – she  insists  her cat, Winston, is psychic. Honestly. She’s convinced he predicted her boyfriend dumping her. Winston the psychic cat, eh? Sounds a bit… optimistic, doesn’t it? My Nan reckons she can tell the weather with her knees, but I don’t go runnin’ to her for the forecast. Oh, well, people cope in different ways. I think Brenda's just a bit heartbroken. Speaking of heartbroken, how  are  you, Liam? You’ve been a bit quiet since… well, since everything with Chloe. I’m alright. Just… busy. Work’s been mental, loads of overtime at the site. Keeps me outta trouble, I suppose. Busy? Or avoidin’ phone calls? I saw her post on Instagram, lookin’ all happy on a weekend trip to Brighton with… Mark. Mark from her pottery class. Yeah, I saw that too. Look, it’s fine. I knew it wasn’t goin’ anywhere long-term. Too many… differences. Differences? Like what? You two seemed pretty solid for a good six months. Just… different lifestyles, yeah? She’s all artsy, goes to life drawing, vintage shopping, talks about 'finding herself’. I like a pint down the pub, footy, workin’ with me hands. Not exactly a match made in heaven, is it? It wasn't like it was serious. Still, must sting a bit seein’ her with someone else so quickly. Especially Mark. He always did have a bit of an artist vibe, didnae he? I always thought he was a bit… pretentious. He is, a bit. But Chloe likes that. She likes… thoughtful. I’m just… straightforward. I say what I mean, do what needs doin’. She wanted someone to debate existentialism with over oat milk lattes. I just want a roast dinner and a good game. Right, I can see that! It’s good you recognize it wasn't a good fit, though. Better to end things now than drag it out. It’s just… have you actually  talked  to her properly since it ended? Or are you just basing it on Instagram updates? We had a chat, the night it ended. She said she needed someone who understood her… creative process. She used that phrase. “Creative process”. I don’t even know what that means! Sounds like she’d been readin’ too many poetry books. Seriously though, maybe a proper conversation, just clear the air?

…and then  he  had the audacity to ask me if I’d “considered a Gantt chart” for the social media rollout. A Gantt chart, Chloe! It’s Instagram posts, not building the Shard! Oh, bless him. Who was this charting enthusiast? Mark from Marketing again? He sounds…enthusiastic. Enthusiastic is one word for it. Oblivious is another. It's Mark. Always Mark. He thinks everything can be solved with a spreadsheet and a strongly worded email. I swear, he once tried to schedule a ‘brainstorming session’ with allocated time slots for ‘idea generation’ and ‘critique’. That  is  peak Mark. Honestly, you’d think after six months he'd realise you run a pretty tight ship already. How did you respond? Did you unleash the sarcasm? I was remarkably restrained, actually. I just blinked at him and said, “Mark, it’s pictures of cats. We’re good.” He looked completely bewildered. I think it momentarily short-circuited his brain. Good. Some people need short-circuiting. Long day at work then? You have no idea. The entire morning was spent putting out fires because Sarah in Sales decided, completely unilaterally, to promise a competition prize that we don’t even  have . And then there was that whole debacle with the influencer… Oh god, don’t tell me. The one you were worried about being a bit… problematic? "A bit" is an understatement. Turns out her last sponsored post was promoting a detox tea that’s been flagged by the Advertising Standards Authority. My boss is not impressed. Apparently, due diligence extends beyond a quick Google search. Ugh, that’s a nightmare. You’re basically a professional damage control officer, aren’t you? Seriously, they should pay you double. Speaking of stressful situations… how’s Liam taking everything? You haven't mentioned him much lately. That’s… complicated. Complicated like ‘ran out of milk’ complicated, or ‘everything is falling apart’ complicated? Definitely leaning towards the latter. We…we broke up. Oh, Liv! No. What happened? I thought things were going alright. You seemed…happy. I  was  happy. Or, I thought I was. It just… fizzled. He said he needed “space to figure things out.” Space to figure things out usually involves a questionable amount of time on FIFA with his mates, as far as I can tell. Oh, that's awful. The 'space to figure things out' line is such a cop-out. Was it sudden?

…and so, the Green Knight, he just  appeared  in the middle of King Arthur's Christmas feast. Can you imagine? Just walked in, all green, even his horse! Was he a scary green? Like…slime green? A bit like slime green, I suppose. But a really  regal  slime green. All shimmering and powerful looking. Not like the goo you find under the sofa. Did Arthur fight him? Well, that’s the thing, isn't it? He didn’t  immediately  fight him. The Green Knight proposed a…a game. A strange game. He said anyone could strike a blow at  him , but they had to agree to meet him in a year and a day, and let him return the blow. Ooh! That’s a bit like dare, isn’t it? But…deadlier. You could say that. Much deadlier. Sir Gawain, Arthur’s nephew, took up the challenge. He bravely swung his axe… and lopped off the Green Knight’s head! WHOA! I know, right? Dramatic. But… the Green Knight just picked up his head, held it, and reminded Gawain about the return blow in a year and a day. That’s really creepy. Why would he  want  someone to chop his head off? That’s a really good question, Lily. That’s part of what makes the story so fascinating. Some people think he was testing the knights’ courage, their honour. Some think he was a spirit, a test sent by Morgan le Fay, the sorceress. Is Morgan le Fay evil? That’s another brilliant question, Leo. It's complicated. She wasn’t necessarily…  evil  in the way a truly wicked villain is. She was powerful, and she often used her magic to challenge Arthur and his court. Perhaps she thought they were getting too proud, too complacent. She thought they needed a lesson. So she’s like… a trickster? Exactly! A very powerful trickster. And often, in old stories, it's not about good versus evil being clear cut. It’s more about…balance. About challenging what people  think  is right and wrong. But Gawain  had  to go and let the Green Knight chop his head off, right? That doesn’t sound very balanced. It doesn't, does it? And that’s where the story gets really interesting. Gawain spent the whole year travelling to find the Green Knight. He faced all sorts of hardships, and temptations… He was tested, not just physically, but morally too.

…and honestly, the logistics of it all. A film set  at  the school? It's ambitious, isn’t it? Did she say what it was for, exactly? Something about a historical drama. Apparently, a local production company is using the school grounds as a stand-in for… well, I don't know  what  exactly. Victorian London, maybe? She was mostly excited about being an extra. Said she got to wear a bonnet. Mummy! It  still  hurts! Oh, sweetheart. Let me see. Where does it hurt exactly? Still that spot? Yeah! Right… here. I tripped over Leo’s Lego. Again. Leo and his Lego. It’s a minefield, that room. Did you put some ice on it, love? Yes! But it doesn't make it better. Can I have a biscuit? Sweetheart, let's get you settled on the sofa with an ice pack  and  a biscuit. Then we can see if it’s still sore later. Can  I  have a biscuit too? Even though my leg doesn’t hurt? Alright, alright. Everyone gets a biscuit. Saves me arguing. I could use one myself, actually. Long day wrestling spreadsheets. Prospect Research being particularly demanding today? You have no idea. Old Man Hemmings wants a full breakdown of all charitable donations over £500 in the last quarter, cross-referenced with postcode data... it’s a nightmare. Seriously considering taking up basket weaving. You and basket weaving? I can't see that. Although, honestly, after grading thirty sets of Year 6 history essays, I'm starting to understand the appeal of something… repetitive and brain-deadening. See? We're all in the same boat. Speaking of repetitive… I was thinking of hitting the gym tonight. Been a bit lax lately. Oh, good for you! I haven’t been in ages. I keep  meaning  to, but then the marking piles up, or someone needs help with their homework… I know the feeling. I'm thinking just a quick thirty minutes on the treadmill. Not aiming for marathon runner, just trying to keep the heart ticking over. Although… those running machines are  evil , aren't they? All that impact. They are. I always feel about ninety years old after ten minutes. I prefer the cross-trainer. Less jarring. Fair enough. I might give that a go. Just need to mentally prepare myself for the sheer… effort. Mummy, when are we going to get doughnuts? You promised!

…and honestly, Arthur, the waiting list at the surgery is just getting ridiculous. Three weeks to see a nurse about a persistent cough! Three weeks! Back in my day, you’d be seen the same afternoon. Though, admittedly, you probably wouldn’t  need  to see anyone the same afternoon, what with everyone being generally fitter. Fitter? Don’t make me laugh, George. We were all smoking like chimneys and eating lard in everything. Fit as fiddles, we weren’t. It's just they’re swamped now, isn’t it? More people, fewer doctors. And everyone expecting to live to be a hundred and fifty. Exactly! It’s unrealistic. And the paperwork! My daughter, she's a nurse now, you know. Says half her time is spent filling out forms, not actually  nursing . It's criminal. Right mess. Speaking of messes… did you see the council’s latest plan for that eyesore down on the seafront? They're talking about another block of flats. Honestly, when will they stop? Brighton’s turning into one giant concrete jungle. I did. Dreadful. Though, I suppose we need somewhere for all the Londoners fleeing the city, don't we? Though I can’t understand why anyone  would  want to leave London. Money, mostly, I reckon. And a bit of peace and quiet. Though they won’t find much of that here in the summer. Anyway, I was reading something the other day, an article about the Green Party actually gaining some traction in the local elections. Seems more folks are finally waking up. The Greens? Hmm. I’m all for looking after the planet, mind you, absolutely. But some of their policies… well, they seem a bit… impractical, don’t they? All that talk of closing off roads and banning cars. How's old Mrs. Higgins supposed to get to the shops? She relies on the number 1 bus, and even  that's  unreliable these days. They’ve got a point about reducing pollution, George. We’ve got some of the worst air quality in the country here. Though I agree, practicality is key. My nephew, young Daniel, he works for a renewable energy company now. Solar panels mostly. He says it's booming business. Says folks are finally realising it's not just a fad. Good for him. It's good to see young people finding work in something worthwhile. Still, wishing he'd gone into teaching like his Aunt Millie wanted.

…and honestly, the variegated string of hearts is just  thriving . I nearly killed it last winter, thought it was a goner, all droopy and sad. But I repotted it, gave it a bit more bright, indirect light, and now look at it! It's sending out these lovely little heart-shaped leaves everywhere. You wouldn't believe. You and your plants. It's a full-time job, isn't it? My flat's a cacti graveyard. I think they resent my lack of…enthusiasm. I water them when I remember, which is clearly not enough. Oh, cacti are different! They  want  to be neglected, practically. It’s the drama queens like the string of hearts you’ve got to watch. Speaking of drama, have you seen what she’s wearing today? Professor Ainsworth. That…floral monstrosity? Oh, good lord. It  is  something, isn’t it? Like a garden exploded on her tweed jacket. Is that…pansies? With sequins? I think they  are  sequins! Honestly, it’s a bold choice. She’s usually so…sensible. Maybe she’s having a mid-life crisis. Though, at her age, is it mid-life or…late-life? Existential questions over pints and questionable floral arrangements. Sounds about right for a Tuesday in Cambridge. Did you manage to sort out the ISA transfer yet? I was meaning to ask. Nearly. The paperwork is a nightmare, honestly. So many forms asking for the same information, just in slightly different ways. It’s designed to put you off, I swear. And the automated phone service is an absolute labyrinth. I spent twenty minutes just trying to talk to a human being. Tell me about it. Dealing with financial institutions is designed to induce stress. Part of the system, I reckon. Keeps people reliant. It's all rather… cynical when you think about it. Speaking of cynical, did you catch that Trump rally footage last night? Oh, please no. I actively avoid it. It’s just…exhausting. Like watching a slow-motion car crash. The relentless negativity. I know, I know. But it’s…fascinatingly awful, don't you think? The sheer magnetism he has with a certain demographic. It's terrifying. I was reading an article about the algorithms boosting his content on social media, even with the ‘fact check’ labels attached. It’s just… feeding the echo chamber. Everyone getting more and more entrenched in their own beliefs.

Honestly, this is bliss. Mum’s roast was… Mum’s roast. Intense. But blissfully intense. And getting out of London for a weekend is a lifesaver. The students are  determined  to test my patience this term. You say that every term, love. They always seem to find new and inventive ways, don't they? What’s the current flavour of student rebellion? Existential dread layered with TikTok trends? Pretty much. Though this week it’s been relentless questioning of the validity of art history. Apparently, it’s all ‘Eurocentric’ and ‘problematic’. Not that I disagree with the need for a broader perspective, but it’s like they’ve just discovered the concept of bias. It's exhausting trying to steer them away from just… dismissing everything pre-2000. Sounds familiar. I get that with film studies. Everything pre-Marvel is just “slow” and “boring”. Though, I did have a student argue, and I quote, that ‘Citizen Kane’ was just a rich bloke showing off. Oh, good lord. They’re something else. It makes you wonder about the impact of constant stimulation, doesn’t it? Everything’s a 15-second clip. It’s like they can't process anything nuanced. Which, ironically, is what good art  is . It's the violence too. I was talking about Hitchcock yesterday and one of them genuinely couldn't understand why  Psycho  was considered a landmark rather than just… shocking. They’re used to so much gratuitous violence. It’s normalised. It's true. And the way it's presented. Everything’s about shock value, no subtext, no psychological tension. It’s all just… bang, blood, repeat. Remember how terrified we were of the Daleks? That was  genuine  terror, built on suggestion and clever sound design. Absolutely. And we weren’t desensitised by twenty-four-hour news cycles showing actual atrocities. It feels… different. Speaking of different, did you see that documentary about killer whales? It was fascinating. Oh, the one about their hunting techniques? I started it, but Mum wanted to show me photographs of the garden gnomes, so… my attention was diverted. Apparently, Brenda the gnome has a new hat. Brenda always needs accessorising. But the orcas… they’re employing coordinated hunting strategies, learning from each other, passing down knowledge through generations. It's like a marine culture. Truly incredible. And slightly terrifying, when you think about it. It is. Intelligent animals. Makes you think about what else we don’t understand about the natural world.

…Now this one, this is Doreen and Arthur, down at the pier in Cromer. Must be, oh, 1968, I reckon. Arthur was always a bit of a character, him. Always had a plan, always involved something…dodgy, usually. Remember that time he tried to run a little hostel in Great Yarmouth? Oh, Arthur! Don't get me started. A hostel! The man couldn’t organise a tea party, let alone a respectable lodging house. I remember Brenda telling me it was overrun with… well, let's just say a  certain  type of holiday-maker. And the complaints! Brenda nearly had a breakdown dealing with the, the  issues . Hostels are surprisingly complex to manage, actually. It's not just about beds and breakfast. You've got security, liability, the constant turnover, differing expectations... it’s a lot like running a small school, in some ways. Keeping everyone happy, safe, and reasonably behaved. You need a very specific skillset. Skillset? Arthur had enthusiasm! That’s what he had. And a healthy disregard for planning. He wanted to make a quick buck, that’s all. He thought everyone wanted to be near the seaside, didn't factor in they might also want… cleanliness, and a modicum of quiet. Look, here’s that picture of you and Derek in your school uniforms. Goodness, you both look so serious! What were you studying, Bernard? Something to do with…engines, wasn't it? Engineering, aye. Tried to be clever, I did. Thought I’d build things, make things. Didn’t quite pan out, did it? Too much fiddling, not enough…sticking at it. Though, I did once take apart a clock and actually got it working again. That was a triumph. Engineering’s fascinating. My nephew's doing aerospace engineering at Bristol. They're working on some incredible projects now – sustainable aviation fuels, new wing designs… it's lightyears away from taking apart a clock, but the fundamental principles are the same. Problem-solving, understanding how things work. Sounds complicated. My dad, now  he  was a practical man. Run that little butcher’s shop in Costessey for years. Always up before dawn, getting the meat in. Proper hardworking fella. Not like today’s youngsters. Your dad was a lovely man, Bernard. Always a kind word. And your mother, bless her, ran that little sweet shop right next door. They  both  worked themselves to the bone. I remember going in there as a girl, spending my pocket money on those little sherbet lemons.

Honestly, Liam, I'm starting to wonder if we’re actually  teaching  them how to write academically, or just marking errors. This batch is…rough. So many basic structural issues. Yeah, it’s a perennial issue, isn’t it? Cambridge attracts brilliant minds, absolutely, but ‘brilliant’ doesn’t always equate to ‘articulate on paper’, especially when it comes to the conventions of academic writing. It’s a different skillset entirely. Exactly! And it feels like we assume they  should  already have it. Like, arriving at university is a magic switch that flips and suddenly everyone knows how to construct a coherent argument with proper referencing. It's just… not realistic. It’s a bit of a cultural expectation thing too, I think. What do they learn in A-Levels these days? Is there enough emphasis on extended writing? I remember when I was an undergrad, we had dedicated workshops. I’ve heard similar complaints from students who’ve come through the state system. Not enough dedicated practice. So many are brilliant at analysis in class – insightful comments, really clever ideas – but when they get to translate that to an essay... it falls apart. It's frustrating for them, I think, as much as it is for us. It must be. It's a shame. You know, ironically, I was  really  good at spotting that sort of thing in my previous life. Oh, right! You were in recruitment, weren't you? I always forget. What did you recruit for again? Initially, it was mostly finance roles in Sydney. But I ended up specializing in graduate schemes for large corporations. And a huge part of the job wasn’t actually judging their financial acumen – it was judging their communication skills. Their CVs, cover letters, how they presented themselves in interviews. Honestly, a LOT of bright, qualified people would fall at the first hurdle because they couldn't articulate their abilities effectively. That's fascinating. It makes sense though. They can  do  the job, but can’t  sell  themselves doing it. So, you were essentially pre-screening for academic literacy, albeit in a professional guise? Absolutely. Though we definitely didn't call it ‘academic literacy’. It was just ‘professional communication’ – but the underlying skill set is very, very similar. Being able to structure an argument clearly, support your assertions with evidence, tailor your language to your audience…it’s all the same stuff. The stakes were different, of course.

Right, I officially can’t look at another graph. My brain’s turned to mush. Tell me about it. Statistics is the devil’s work, innit? I'd rather be explaining the benefits of extended warranties on washing machines all day. At least  that  makes sense. You say that, but I bet some people argue about washing machine warranties with the same intensity as arguing about… well, anything statistics-related. You're probably right, actually. People are weird. Oh, hey, you two haven't met Zara, have you? Zara’s in my sociology seminar. Hi! No, I don’t think so. Nice to meet you both. I'm Zara. I'm doing my Masters in Environmental Management. This library is…intense. It's always packed. Liam. And this is Chloe. I’m just stuck here trying to survive this module. I work at Curry's, so escaping into the world of consumer goods feels a lot easier than formulaic equations, you know? Chloe here is a proper academic, doing her Masters in History. She's trying to convince me that the Wars of the Roses were actually  thrilling  and not just a bunch of blokes hitting each other with swords. Hey! They were strategically brilliant! And the political intrigue was  fascinating . It's basically a medieval Game of Thrones. Anyway, Zara, where are you from originally? You've got a lovely accent, if you don't mind me saying. Oh, thank you! I was born in India, actually, but I moved over here when I was pretty young. Grew up mostly in Birmingham. It's quite different up here, isn't it? Salford's got a… vibe. Different how? Birmingham's a proper city. Loads going on. It is! It's just… warmer, maybe? And the food's better. No offence to your chips and gravy! But a proper biryani is hard to beat. No offence taken! I  love  chips and gravy. It's a northern staple. Though I will admit, a good curry is a mood booster. I’m from Bradford, so we have a pretty strong South Asian community there. It’s fantastic. What about you, Liam? Where are you from? Near Preston. Proper countryside. Sheep everywhere. My mum kept trying to get me to learn to shear them when I was a kid. Didn't take. I'm useless with animals, to be honest. I once tried to feed a pigeon a crisp

Right, so then Uncle Barry starts goin’ on about his time in the Falklands again. Honestly, you'd think he single-handedly won the war, the way he tells it. It’s always ‘Me and my lads…’, never ‘We and the entire British armed forces…’ Oh, bless him. My grandad was the same about the Second World War. Every family gathering was basically a condensed history lesson, heavily biased toward his own exploits. It’s a thing with that generation, I think. Needs to feel…significant. Significant and…slightly embellished, more like. He was a cook, love! A very good cook, apparently, but not exactly stormin’ the beaches. Still, he gets proper het up if you question his stories. Anyway, what were you readin’? You had your nose buried in somethin’ earlier. Looked fancy. Oh, this? It's a new film magazine.  Sight & Sound . It’s a bit… intense. Loads of really analytical pieces, dissecting cinematography and symbolism. It's fascinating, but sometimes I just want to read a review that says “It was good, go see it!” without a three-page essay on the director’s childhood trauma. Sounds a bit much, doesn't it? I prefer somethin’ lighter. I was flicking through  Stylist  earlier, at Mum’s. Mostly adverts and ‘Ten Ways to Boost Your Confidence’ articles, but it’s a good distraction. Though, honestly, having everything reduced to a 'life hack' is a bit depressing. Completely. It’s like, are we all just constantly striving to optimise ourselves? What happened to just… being? Speaking of distractions, you still into all that computer stuff? Last I heard you were building your own rig. Oh aye! Still at it, actually. Finally managed to get a decent graphics card, though it cost me a fortune. It's a beast, though. Runs everything. I’m tryin’ to teach meself some game development now. It’s a right steep learnin’ curve. Game dev? That’s ambitious! I could barely manage Minesweeper. I’m more of a… user. I need things to  just work , you know? My job's stressful enough dealing with production schedules and supply chains without adding debugging code to the list. Tell me about it. Coordinating conferences is a headache. Everyone wants somethin’ different, and they all think their somethin’ is the most important. This last one nearly did me in. Some bloke insisted on a specific shade of blue for the room lighting.

Honestly, that was a  brutal  game. My legs feel like jelly. Tell me about it! I thought I was going to pull a hamstring in the third quarter. Though, watching you nearly take out poor old Mr. Henderson was… entertaining. Sorry about that! He just got in the way. He really shouldn't be standing so close to the court if he doesn’t want a rogue elbow to the ribs. Anyway, less about almost geriatric assault and more about… well, everything. I need to vent. Oh, lay it on us. Is it work? Another client wanting a ‘modern farmhouse’ aesthetic in the middle of London? Worse. It's  dating . Or rather, the distinct lack of it. I swear, dating apps are just… a parade of men who list ‘hiking’ and ‘craft beer’ as their personality traits. It's exhausting. Hiking  and  craft beer? That's practically the national hobby at this point. You’re aiming low if that's what puts you off. No, it's the hollowness of it! It’s like they didn’t even  think  to put anything else. And then they message with just "Hey".  Just “Hey” ! Ugh, the "Hey" brigade. They think minimal effort equals intriguing mystery. It's just lazy. I had one ask me if I could "design him a cool shed" on the first message. A  shed . Seriously? A shed? That’s… impressively direct. Though, maybe he was testing your professional boundaries disguised as flirtation. I doubt it. It was more likely a cry for help fuelled by too much Strongbow. Speaking of which, I think I need another one. This is all very stressful. I’ll get the round. So, what about that guy from the gallery opening last month? The one who kept talking about Wes Anderson films? Surely he was better than shed-requesters and “Hey” senders? Oh, Leo. He was…  intense . Everything was a metaphor for something else. He spent half an hour explaining how my scarf represented the existential dread of late-stage capitalism. No way! That’s amazing! You should have just nodded and said, “Profound.” I tried to change the subject to the weather! It didn't work. He reframed the weather as a commentary on climate anxiety. It was…a lot. Right, okay. Clearly, Leo is a lost cause. It’s just… what  is  everyone in London doing? It feels like all the remotely interesting people vanish as soon as you cross the M25.

…and honestly, the energy bills this month are  criminal . I swear they just pluck numbers from thin air. Did you see what British Gas is charging now, Dad? Criminal is right! Back in my day, a tenner covered everything. Everything! Now, you're telling me it's…hundreds? For a little heat and light? Daylight robbery, that is. It's not  just  the gas, Dad. Electric’s gone up too. And water rates. It all adds up. Liam's been really good at trying to find cheaper providers, but it’s a minefield. Oh, I know, love. Same at my place. You try and save where you can, don’t you? I’ve started using those energy-saving lightbulbs, and I turn everything off at the wall. Every single thing. Old habits die hard though, I confess. Still leave the telly on standby sometimes. It's okay, Mum. We all have our weaknesses. I’m still hopelessly addicted to buying cycling accessories. I don’t  need  another pair of cycling gloves, but…they were on sale! They were a lovely shade of blue, though. They really match the bike. Which, by the way, is taking over the living room. It’s not taking over! It's strategically positioned for easy access. Plus, we can talk about our trip to Brighton! Remember we were saying about cycling along the seafront? Brighton? Oh, lovely place. Though a bit…packed, isn't it? Used to go down there on day trips as a lad. Fish and chips on the pier, the whole shebang. Still remember the smell. And the arcades! Lost a fortune in those arcades. Oh, George, you and your gambling! Your mother always said you’d gamble away everything you earned. She wasn't wrong, bless her. Though she enjoyed a little flutter herself, mind you. A harmless bit of bingo. We were thinking of taking the train down to Brighton, actually. Liam’s been saying he wants to visit the Royal Pavilion. Have you been, Mum? Oh, ages ago. It’s quite…flashy, isn't it? All that gold and those pagodas. Not really my cup of tea, if I'm honest. I prefer something a bit more…rustic. Like this flat, actually. It's really cosy. Though, that kitchen could do with a bit of attention, couldn't it? We’re planning on doing the kitchen next year, Mum. It’s a bit…dated.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data is mental. Like, terabytes of transcribed speech. It’s all for building better speech recognition models, but sometimes I feel like I’m drowning in ‘umms’ and ‘ahhs’. You wouldn’t believe the things people say. Sounds…intense. More intense than designing bridges, I reckon, though that has its own stress points. I swear, if I have to look at another load calculation for a retaining wall this month… Still, at least it’s  tangible . You can  see  the bridge. You can’t exactly  see  a better algorithm, can you? Exactly! It’s all abstract. I tell me mam I spend my day looking at text files and she just nods and offers me a biscuit. She thinks I’m fixing computers or something. Speaking of which, have you seen the state of broadband here in Cambridge? I was trying to upload a small sample dataset last night and it was glacial. Back in Sunderland, it was faster. And that’s saying something! No kidding. It’s a rip-off. I keep meaning to switch providers, but then I get distracted by…well, anything, really. Work mostly. How's your flat hunt going, by the way? Still looking? Don’t even get me started. It's a joke. Trying to find anything remotely decent for under £1200 a month is impossible. I went to see a place yesterday… it was basically a glorified cupboard with a shared bathroom. And they wanted six months’ rent upfront! Honestly, how are people supposed to manage? It's insane, isn't it? My dad keeps going on about how he bought his first house for the equivalent of £10,000 back in the day. And it wasn't a shoebox! He’s thinking of maybe helping me out with a deposit. He’s convinced property is still a good investment, despite everything. He’s got that whole 'bricks and mortar' mentality. Your dad’s got a point, I think. It's just…the getting  onto  the ladder is the killer. I saw something online today about the government’s new scheme, Help to Buy or something. Seems a bit of a sticking plaster, though, doesn’t it? Just drives up prices further. It does. All it does is allow people to borrow more money. It’s not addressing the fundamental problem of supply and demand. It is all a bit depressing, to be honest.

Honestly, this shift last night was  something  else. Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was convinced the curtains were plotting against her. Spent a good hour assuring her they weren't sentient beings, you know? Oh, bless her. You get all sorts, don't you, Mum? It's the night shifts, isn't it? Everything feels… heightened. I’m just glad I’m chained to a laptop and not responsible for anyone’s wellbeing. Though sometimes my clients feel like they're trying to plot against  my  sanity with their briefs. It’s true, the nights are…different. Though, I had a lovely moment with Mr. Davies this morning. His granddaughter came to visit and he just beamed. Little things like that make it worthwhile. Though, the agency is putting us all on mandatory training next week. Something about “safeguarding vulnerable adults”. As if we don’t already! Is that the one where they make you role-play difficult scenarios? Because I  hate  those. Makes my stomach churn. I had one last month where I had to pretend a service user was accusing me of stealing, and it just felt so awful. Oh, don’t even get me started on the training! It’s always the same, isn't it? Endless powerpoints and scenarios that barely reflect real life. And the presenters… they’ve never actually  done  a day's care in their lives. It's the same with marketing training, honestly. “Think outside the box!” they say, whilst simultaneously outlining a very specific, rigid strategy. It’s just… frustrating. Speaking of frustrating, have you heard anything from Aunt Carol? Still no word about the party? Not a peep. I texted her yesterday, just checking if everything was still on, and she didn't even read it. Which is Carol, really. Always last minute.com. I’m hoping she hasn’t decided to go all out and hire a bouncy castle again. Remember last year? Oh my god,  the bouncy castle . Uncle Barry nearly broke his hip trying to get on it! And the neighbours were furious about the noise. I think old Mr. Peterson threatened to call the police. He did! He was absolutely livid. Honestly, Carol means well, she just gets… carried away. She's always wanted to be the life and soul of the party. It stems from feeling overlooked as a kid, I think. Her brother got all the attention.
